# Robot-in-operation (Output)

## Function

The signal outputs to the external device that the robot is in operation (executing more than one task ).

## Usage

The signal is used to light the robot operating indicator lamp of the external operating panel.  
Since the signal is turned OFF with STOP ALL PROGRAMS, it outputs to the external device that all programs are stopped.

## ON Conditions

The signal will be turned ON while executing the program and also in the Wait State with a condition branch or timer command.  
However, this signal will not turn ON while [Supervisory tasks](000492.html) or [TP panel tasks](001852.html) are running.

## OFF Conditions

The program will be turned OFF with STOP ALL PROGRAMS.

STOP ALL PROGRAMS means the operation of the ROBOT STOP or STOP button of the teach pendant or the mini-pendant and INSTANTANEOUS TOP (ALL TASKS), STEP STOP (ALL TASKS) and ROBOT STOP inputs.

# Single-Cycle End (Output)

## Function

The signal outputs to the external device that a single-cycle of the program is completed.

1. The single-cycle end signal will be output upon reading END of the program. However, it will be output earlier than the end of the actual robot operation because the Robot Controller pre-reads the program.
2. The single-cycle end signal will be output on the premise that only one program is executed at a time. If two or more programs are executed simultaneously (multi-tasks), the single-cycle end signal will be turned ON immediately after any of the programs reads an END command.

## Usage

The signal is used to operate another equipment in synchronization with a single-cycle end of the program.

## ON conditions

The signal will be turned ON when the program is read to the end.

## OFF conditions

The signal will be turned OFF immediately after the program starts to run.

# Robot Error (Output)

## Function

The signal outputs to the external device that a problem, such as a servo error and a program error, occurs with the robot.

## Usage

1. The signal is used to turn ON the robot external operating panel error indicator lamp.
2. The signal is used to help the PLC clear an error in response to a Robot Error signal.

## ON Conditions

This signal turns ON when an error which error level is 3 or higher occurs.

For details about error level, refer to "[Error Levels](000494.html)" of ERROR CODE.

## OFF Conditions

As shown below, the signal will be turned OFF under the following conditions.

1. When Clear Robot Error is input from the external device and the existing error is cleared.
2. When the existing error is cleared by operating the **Cancel** key of the teach pendant or the mini-pendant.

# Robot Warning (Output)

## Function

The signal outputs to the external device that a minor error has occurred with an I/O command or during servo processing.

## Usage

1. The signal is used to light the robot warning indicator lamp of an external operating panel.
2. The signal is used to help the PLC clear an error in response to a Robot Warning signal.

## ON Conditions

This signal turns ON when an error which error level is 1 or 2 occurs.

For details about error level, refer to "[Error Levels](000494.html)" of ERROR CODE.

## OFF Conditions

As shown below, the robot-warning signal will be turned OFF under the following conditions.

1. When Clear Robot Error and Operation Preparation Start signals are input from the external device and the existing error is cleared.
2. When the existing error is cleared by operating the **OK** or **Cancel** key of the teach pendant or mini-pendant.

ID : 1033

# Dead Battery Warning (Output)

## Function

The signal indicates whether the voltage of the encoder backup battery has decreased.

## Usage

The signal allows you to know the battery replacement timing, which is the time when the battery voltage has decreased.

## ON Condition / OFF Condition / Timing Chart

The timing of battery voltage monitoring differs between robot models, which also have different ON and OFF conditions and timing charts.

### VM Series, VS Series, VS-6556/6577 Series, HM Series, HS Series, XR Series, and XR2

Monitoring timing
:   The function monitors the voltage of the encoder backup battery when the robot controller turns on.

ON condition
:   The signal will turn on if you turn on the robot controller with its encoder backup battery voltage decreased.

OFF condition
:   The signal will remain off if you turn on the robot controller with its encoder backup battery voltage not decreased.

Timing chart
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001033_2.png)

### HSA1 Series, HSR Series, and VP Series

Monitoring timing
:   The function keeps monitoring the voltage of the encoder backup battery while the robot controller is on.

ON condition
:   The signal will turn on if the encoder backup battery voltage decreases while the robot controller is on.

OFF condition
:   The signal will remain off if the encoder backup battery voltage does not decrease while the robot controller is on.

Timing chart
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001033_1.png)

# Error No. (Output)

## Function

When an error occurs, the signal outputs the error number in a 3-digit (12-bit) hexadecimal code.

The displayed error code is not output as it is. This command will convert the existing error code displayed on the error dialogue to RC7M's error code which has the same meaning of the existing error code.

For the error code correspondence, refer to the "[Error Code](001075.html)".

In the version 1.6.\* or later, an error code displayed in the error dialog can be directly output by specifying the error output range. For details, refer to "32bit Error Code Output IO No" in the "[Displaying and Changing I/O Parameters](001769.html)" under the OPERATION GUIDE.

## Usage

The signal is used to display an error number on the external device.

## Output Conditions

The signal will be output when an error occurs.

## Clear Conditions

The signal will be cleared when *Clear Robot Error* and *Operation Preparation Start* signals are inputted or by operating the Cancel key of the teach pendant or mini-pendant. When this signal is cleared, all states will become OFF (0).

# Operation Preparation Start (Input)

## Function

* By turning ON (short) this signal, input signals to „ described in (1), (2), input conditions and operation will be detected and the robot will automatically start to operate. Input these signals with the system output *Robot Power ON Complete* turned ON.
* By turning ON (short) *Clear Robot Error*, an error that has occurred will be cleared.

## Input Conditions and Operation

Before inputting an operation preparation start signal, turn ON (short) inputs (1) to (3) below.  
Note that CAL execution (input) is for the compatible mode-use only.  
Switching CAL execution causes no effect on operations because RC8 series controls no robot that requires CAL.

### (1) Motor Power ON (Input)

By turning ON (short) the operation preparation start signal with this signal turned ON (shorted), the power to the motor will be turned ON. However, this signal can be used only in the Auto mode.

### (2) SP100 (Input)

By turning ON (short) the operation preparation start signal with this signal turned ON (shorted), SP100% will be set.

### (3) Program Reset (Input)

By turning ON (short) the operation preparation start signal with this signal turned ON (shorted), all programs will be initialized.

By turning ON (short) the operation preparation start signal with all inputs (1) to (3) turned ON (shorted), (1) to (3) will be executed one by one. Inputs (1) to (3) will also become valid when part of them are executed by the teach pendant or mini-pendant.

For the input timing of the operation preparation start signal and (1), (2) see the figure given below.

The operation preparation start signal and (1), (2), will be turned OFF (falling) upon turning ON of the servo ON (output) is turned ON.

Although the robot is made to execute all items at start-up, execute only necessary items at the time of recovery from suspension during operation to reduce recovery time.

ID : 1038

# Program No. Select (Input)

## Function

The program number to be executed can be specified from the external device by inputting this signal.

## Input Conditions and Operation

1. This signal is executable only in the external mode. In other modes, an error will be displayed, and the terminal motor power will be turned OFF.
2. As shown in the table given on the next page, the program No. select signal is made up of eight bits of 20 to 26 and the parity bit.
3. Input a decimal program number by converting it into binary 20 to 26 and parity bit.
4. "Short" represents the bit value = 1, "open" represents the bit value = 0, and the parity bit is odd parity.
5. As shown below "Timing chart", input the program No. select signal before the program start signal (1 msec. or more), and hold the state until the robot starts to operate. If this condition is not met, an error will be displayed, the power to the motor will be turned OFF.
6. Input 1 or 0 as the parity bit so that the total of 1's existing in the eight bits of 20 to 26 and the parity bit will be odd.

   Example: When the program number is 15, the bit status of 20 to 26 is (001111), and the total number of 1s is four, an even number. Set 1 as the parity bit to make the total number of 1s five, an odd number.

1. The bit value =1 represents short, and the bit value =0 represents open.
2. The program numbers executable from the external device are limited to Program No. 0 to 127.
3. Invalidation of the parity bit is not recommended.

## Timing Chart

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Example of Program No. Select Signals

|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Input signal** | | | **Program No. (decimal)** | | | |
| **1** | **15** | **26** | **65** |
| **2****0** | **=** | **1** | **1** | **1** | **0** | **1** |
| **2****1** | **=** | **2** | **0** | **1** | **1** | **0** |
| **2****2** | **=** | **4** | **0** | **1** | **0** | **0** |
| **2****3** | **=** | **8** | **0** | **1** | **1** | **0** |
| **2****4** | **=** | **16** | **0** | **0** | **1** | **0** |
| **2****5** | **=** | **32** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **0** |
| **2****6** | **=** | **64** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **1** |
| **Parity** | | | **0** | **1** | **0** | **1** |

The figure below shows an example of a program No. select signal sequence circuit considering parity.

ID : 1039

# Program Start (Input)

## Function

This signal starts the program specified with the program No. select signal from the external device.

## Input Conditions and Operation

By switching the status of this signal from ON (open) to ON (shorted) in external mode, operations (1), (2) and (3) described below will take place. (The status of the signal must be switched from OFF to ON.)

### (1) Before Executing or Completing the Program

 If the program start signal is input (switched from OFF to ON) when the robot has not yet completed the program or is at rest after it has completed a cycle of the program, the program No. select signal will be read, the program will execute a cycle, and the robot will come to a stop.

Input the program No. select signal before the program start signal (1 ms. or more), and hold the state until the robot starts to operate. If this condition is not met, ERROR will be displayed, the power to the motor will be turned OFF.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

The program start signal requires program start preparation time (50 ms. or more) before input from OFF (open) to ON (shorted).

The program start signal must remain OFF (open) during the program start preparation time. If it is turned ON (shorted) during that time, the next cycle will not start to run.

To start a new cycle, the status of the external start signal must be switched from OFF to ON before each cycle.

### (2)Step-stopped Status During Program Execution

When the status of the program start signal is switched from OFF to ON with the program step-stopped, the program will resume from the step following the suspended step and stop at the cycle end.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

To cancel the execution of the remaining steps of a step-stopped program and start it from the beginning, input a program reset signal, a program No. select signal and a program start signal at the same time. For further information, refer to "Program Reset (Input)".

### (3)Instantaneous Stop Status During Program Execution

When the status of the program start signal is switched from OFF to ON with the program immediately stopped, the program will resume from the suspended step and stop at the cycle end.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

To cancel the execution of the remaining steps of an instantaneously stopped program and start it from the beginning, input a program reset signal, a program No. select signal and a program start signal at the same time. For further information, refer to "Program Reset (Input)".

## Example of Program Start Signal Rise (ON) and Fall (OFF) Timing

### **** Example of Program Start Signal Rise (ON) Timing

The figure below shows how to make the program start signal rise with robot system outputs (external mode output and single-cycle end output).

|  |
| --- |
|  |

The program start signal for the first cycle rises as soon as the external mode becomes valid and the conditions of the peripheral devices are met. The program start signal for subsequent cycles rises after output of a single-cycle end signal.

### Example of Program Start Signal Fall (OFF) Timing

#### How to make the program start signal fall with a robot system output (program start reset output).

When the robot program starts to run, a program start reset signal is output. The external device receives it and makes the program start signal fall (OFF).

|  |
| --- |
|  |

#### How to make the program start signal fall with the simplified method (1 shot method using a timer).

|  |
| --- |
|  |

1. Although the 1 shot method is easy, the timer setting for falling to raise the program start signal in the middle of the preceding cycle is difficult.<br />  
   Use this method only to raise the program start signal after the robot stops at the end of each cycle.
2. The status of the robot-in-operation, program start reset and single cycle end output signals changes in sequence after the program start signal is input (T1 -> T2 -> T3 in the figure given on the next timing chart).  
   The change of the status of these signals takes place within 100 ms. after the program start signal rises (ON).

|  |
| --- |
|  |

# Program Reset (Input)

## Function

By turning ON (short) this signal, any program can be forcibly executed from the beginning in a step-stopped state and a suspended state.

Generally, a step-stopped or suspended program resumes from where it stopped.

## Input conditions and operation

### When issued with the Program Start

1. The figure below shows the input conditions and an operation timing chart.
2. Use the program reset signal together with a program No. select signal, and input it before the program start signal (1 msec. or more).
3. Turn OFF the program reset signal after the robot starts to operate (after a program start reset signal is output).
4. A program No. select signal is required to execute the same program number as the suspended one from the beginning.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

### When issued with the Operation Preparation Start

1. The figure below shows the input conditions and an operation timing chart.
2. Input Program Reset before Operation Preparation Start (1 msec. or more).
3. After turned ON, this signal may take a maximum of one second for initializing all programs. During the period, do not input signals to the robot.

|  |
| --- |
| Input conditions and operetion of program reset signal |

# Step Stop (All Tasks) (Input)

## Function

Input this signal to step-stop the program being executed from the external device. All tasks will be step-stopped.

## Input conditions and operation

1. If the status of this signal is changed from ON (shorted) to OFF (open), the robot will stop all tasks immediately after the ongoing step is completed, and the Robot-in-operation signal will be turned OFF. However, External Auto mode will remain valid, and the suspended program will be resumed by inputting a program start signal. See the figure given below.
2. Turning OFF (open) this signal when inputting a program start signal makes the robot stop step by step.
3. Internal operation with the teach pendant is valid only when the status of this signal is changed from ON (shorted) to OFF (open).
4. For resuming the program after a step stop, refer to "Program Start (Input)."

# Instantaneous Stop (All Tasks) (Input)

## Function

Input this signal to instantaneously stop the program being executed from the external device. All tasks will instantaneously stop.

## Input conditions and operation

1. If the status of this signal is changed from ON (shorted) to OFF (open), the robot will instantaneously stop in the middle of the ongoing step, and the Robot-in-operation signal will be turned OFF. However, Auto mode or external mode will remain valid, and the suspended program will be resumed by inputting a program start signal.
2. Internal operation by the teach pendant is valid only when the status of this signal is changed from ON (shorted) to OFF (open).
3. For resuming the program after an instantaneous stop, refer to "Program Start (Input)."
4. The minimum required pulse width is 50 msec. or more.

## Timing chart

| Minimum Instantaneous Stop Pulse Width |

# Clear Robot Error (Input)

## Function

The robot can recover from a stopped state, resulting from a robot error by turning ON (shorted) the operation preparation start signal with this signal ON (shorted).

## Usage

The signal is used to clear an error that brought the robot to a stop.

## Input conditions and operation

1. When a robot error occurs, clear the error display on the teach pendant or mini-pendant and the external output *Error Number* to ready the robot to operate.
2. When the *Clear Robot Error* signal is turned ON (shorted), other input signals (*Motor Power ON*, *CAL Execution*, *SP100* and *Switch EXT Mode*), which are to be used in combination with the *Operation Preparation Start* signal, will be ignored. To turn ON the power to the motor after a robot error is cleared, turn OFF (open) the *Clear Robot Error* signal after turning OFF the *Robot Error* signal (output) as shown below.
3. Input the *Clear Robot Error* signal before (1 msec. or more) the *Operation Preparation Start* signal.

## Timing chart

| --- |
| Input Conditions and Operation of Clear Robot Error Signal |

# Interrupt Skip (Input)

## Function

If this signal is turned ON (shorted) during execution of the robot operation command within the range between INTERRUPT ON and INTERRUPT OFF in the program, the operation of the ongoing step will stop and the next step will start.

## Input conditions and operation

If this signal is turned ON (shorted), the robot will immediately stop the ongoing operation and start executing the next step.

# Continue Start (Input)

## Function

Turning the program start signal ON when this continue start signal is ON will resume the current program being on halt.

## Input conditions and operation

This signal is executable only in external mode. If this signal is on, program numbers will be ignored at execution of Program start and the current program being on halt will be resumed. If Continue Start Permitted signal is not ON, the controller will issue an error.

# [RC3 Compatible Mode] Types and Functions of System Output Signals

The table below lists the system output signals used in the compatible mode.

For information about system output signals common for all allocation modes, refer to [[Common for all Allocation modes] Types and Functions of System Output Signals](002649.html).

| Application | Signal name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up | [Robot Power ON Complete](001022.html) | Outputs when preparations for operation are ready to start. |
| [Auto Mode](001023.html) | Outputs when the robot is in auto mode. |
| [Servo ON](001024.html) | Outputs when the power to the motor is turned ON. |
| [CAL Complete](001025.html) | This signal is for the compatible mode-use.   RC8 series robot controller are not necessary CAL, therefore this function always turns OFF automatically after boosting. |
| [External Mode](001026.html) | Outputs when the robot is in external mode. |
| Program pre-execution check | [Teaching](001027.html) | Outputs when the robot is in manual or teach check mode. |
| Program execution | [Program Start Reset](001028.html) | Outputs when execution of the program starts in response to the program start signal received. |
| [Robot-in-operation](001029.html) | Outputs when the robot is in operation (the program is being executed). |
| Program end | [Single Cycle End](001030.html) | Outputs when the program completes one cycle. |
| Error/Warning | [Robot Error](001031.html) | Outputs when a failure (such as a servo failure and program error) occurs in the robot. |
| [Robot Warning](001032.html) | Outputs when a slight error occurs. |
| [Dead Battery Warning](001033.html) | Outputs when the voltage of the encoder backup battery or memory backup battery lowers. |
| [Error No.](001034.html) | An error number will be outputted in BCD code if an error occurs. |
| Continue | [Continue Start Permitted](001035.html) | Outputs when Continue Start is enabled. |
| SS function | SS Mode | The signal of SS (Safe Start) Function which is equipped with the RC7 robot controller.   This signal is always OFF because the RC8 series robot controller does not have SS function. |

System output signals are checked every 8 ms.

# [RC3 Compatible Mode] Types and Functions of System Input Signals

The table below lists the system input signals to be used in compatible mode.

For information about system input signals common for all allocation modes, refer to [[Common for all Allocation modes] Types and Functions of System Input Signals](002652.html).

| Application | Signal name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start-up | Motor Power ON and [Operation Preparation Start](001037.html) | Turns the motor power ON. |
| CAL Execution and [Operation Preparation Start](001037.html) | This signal is for the compatible mode-use.  Switching CAL execution causes no effect on operations because all robots controlled by RC8　series do not require CAL. |
| SP100 and [Operation Preparation Start](001037.html) | Sets the speed to 100%. |
| [Program Reset](001041.html) and [Operation Preparation Start](001037.html) | Initializes all programs on halt. Starting a program after initialization will execute the program from the beginning. |
| [Program No. Select](001038.html) and [Program Start](001039.html) | Executes a specified program. |
| Program execution | [Program Reset](001041.html), [Program No. Select](001038.html) and [Program Start](001039.html) | Cancels the current program and starts executing a specified program from the beginning. |
| Stop | [Step Stop](001042.html) | Step-stops all programs by opening signals. |
| [Instantaneous Stop](001043.html) | Instantaneously stops all programs by opening signals. |
| Error clear | [Clear Robot Error](001044.html) and [Operation Preparation Start](001037.html) | Clears an error. |
| Program interrupt | [Interrupt Skip](001045.html) | Interrupts the execution of the current step and starts the next step. |
| Continue start | [Continue Start](001046.html) and [Program Start](001039.html) | Executes continue start. |

* Two or more signal names listed in the signal name field indicate that they should be used in combination.
* System output signals are checked every 8 ms.

# Overview

Mounting a PROFIBUS-DP slave board in the robot controller enables the controller to communicate with external devices according to the PROFIBUS-DP–compliant communications protocol.

As a slave unit, the robot controller can exchange I/O data with PROFIBUS-DP–compliant field devices of different manufacturers.

For details about PROFIBUS, refer to the
PROFIBUS website as shown below.

* PROFIBUS
  International: <http://www.profibus.com/>

## Operating Environment

To use a PROFIBUS slave board, you need to prepare an expansion board (PROFIBUS slave board) and a function expansion license certificate. For details, see "[Options for Robot Controller](001971.html)
"or "[Optional Function and License](005476.html) ".

> ### Expansion Board
>
> The table below lists the configuration of PROFIBUS slave board.
>
> PROFIBUS slave board is installed in a PCIe slot which is one of an expansion slot in the robot controller. Mini-I/O connector kit is used as an input signal of the safety circuit.
>
> | No. | Components | Description | | |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 1 | PROFIBUS slave board  (including Nos. 2) | Product form ;   * Shipped after mounted on the controller with license * Shipped separately as a spare part with license * Shipped separately as a spare part without license | | |

# Installation of PROFIBUS Slave Board

A PROFIBUS slave board is built in an expansion slot of a robot controller.  
A robot controller equips two expansion slots. From these slots, use a connector for PCI Express board to connect PROFIBUS slave board. For about the way of connection, refer to "[Installing Expansion Board](001347.html) ".

1. When turn the controller power ON after this installation, "Shutdown since driver installation of the new device was completed." is displayed on the teach pendant. Press "OK" to shutdown the robot controller, then turn the motor power ON when "It is now safe to turn off your computer" appears. After reboot is completed, set the Project property setting and the Field bus parameter setting with WINCAPS, and then send these parameters to the robot controller.
2. For safety reason and to prevent damage to the devices, disconnect the power cable of the controller or shut down the power supply to the controller from the facilities before disconnecting or connecting cables.

PROFIBUS slave board also can be used in combination with other extension boards. Selectable allocation mode differs depend on the combination of the extension boards.

For available allocations, see "[Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode](001325.html)".

# LED Display

The state of LED is described as follows.

| LED | Color | State | Status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS | Green | Light up | Normal | Unit is in normal condition |
| Green / Yellow | Blink | During start-up | During start-up |
| Yellow | Light up | During start-up | During start-up |
| - | Light out | No power supply | Power supply of the controller is off |
| COM | Green | Light up | Normal | Network in normal condition (communication established) |
| Red | Light up | Network disconnected | ・The size of I/O modules is inconsistent  ・The order of I/O modules is different |
| Blinking at regular intervals | Stop | On halt or communication error |
| Blinking at irregular intervals | Not set | Not set |

# Project Property Setting

To use a PROFIBUS slave board as an I/O expansion board, you need to register the following information from WINCAPSIII.

From the [Project] menu, point to [Property] to open the Property window, and then click .[I/O] tab. For details, refer to "[Configuring a Project](004406.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001061_1.png)

## Assign

### Device

|  | Setting value |
| --- | --- |
| Device | "PROFIBUS Slave" or "[Parallel] + [PROFIBUS Slave]" |

### Mode

"Standard" indicates the Standard mode, and "Compatible" indicates the RC3 Compatible mode. For details about allocation modes, refer to “[Functions in Individual Allocation Modes](001326.html) ”.

|  | Setting value |
| --- | --- |
| Mode | "Compatible" or "Standard" |

## Options MiniIO

### Power source

If the total maximum capacity of Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Parallel I/O is 1.3 A or lower, the internal power source is available.

|  | Setting value | Defalt setting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Power source | "External" or "Internal" | External |

## Options PROFIBUS

### Input / Output Setting

For about the number of IO points, refer to “[Quick Reference Table for the Number of Input/Output Slots](001463.html)".  I/O can be added or removed by one byte; this will determine the maximum number of I/O.

|  | Setting value (byte) | Default Setting (byte) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input setting | "8", "12", "16", "20" or "32" | 8 |
| Output setting | "8", "12", "16", "20" or "32" | 8 |

### Node Address

|  | Available range | Default Setting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node address | 1 to 125 | 1 |

# Obtaining a GSD File

A GSD file, which is read in the network configuration software of PROFIBUS master, is used to establish, manage, and design networks on your PC.
  
Since this file has been installed in your robot controller, connect your PC to the robot controller and then access the following URL to download the file into your PC.

* GSD file name and its location

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| URL | http://<RC8 IP Address>/eds/ |
| File name | RC800DD6.GSD |

<RC8 IP Address> is an IP address of the RC8 robot controller

You can check your robot controller’s IP address with a teach pendant. For details, see “[Displaying and Changing Communication Settings Screen](001783.html)”.

## Setup of PROFIBUS Master Configurator Software

Please keep the following in mind when you configure PROFIBUS master configurator software.

* I/Os expressed in the PROFIBUS master configurator are viewed from the master device.
* When configuring the robot controller on the PC with the PROFIBUS master configurator software, set the same module as one selected on the teach pendant screen.
* To set RC8 I/O module on PROFIBUS master configurator software, enter n byte Output con for Slot 0, and n byte Input con for Slot 1.

1. The robot controller may use a coherent type of module only. The GSD file contains both programs for coherent and incoherent types, so be sure to choose the program exclusive to the coherent type. (The program name contains a "con" string.)
2. Some master device programs use special functions when exchanging data with a coherent type of module. For details, refer to the instructions manuals prepared for master devices

# Service Function Menu

Operation path : [F2 Arm] - [F12 Maintenance] - [F12 Service]

To perform this operation, set the user level "[Maintainer](001772.html)".

Display the menu associated with servive function.  
 Press [F12 Service] to display [Service function] screen shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001073_1.png)

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [[F1 Acceleration Limit]](001074.html) | Set the maximum acceleration limit. |
| [[F3 Motion]](003283.html) | Set the speed limit for safety control (maximum speed at the manual operation). (This function is available in Ver.2.5.\* or higher) |

# Maximum Acceleration Limit Setting

Operation path : [F2 Arm] - [F12 Maintenance] - [F12 Service] - [F1 Acceleration Limit]

Set acceleration limits of each axis.  
Press [F1 Acceleration limit] to display [Acceleration Limit Settings] as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001074_1.png)

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [F1 Prev] | Display the previous page of the currently displayed [Acceleration Limit Settings] screen. |
| [F2 Next] | Display the next page of the currently displayed [Acceleration Limit Settings] screen. |
| [F3 Jump To] | Displays numeric keypad.  Enter the acceleration limit value limit of the axis to display and select with numeric keypad, and press [OK] to move to the acceleration limit value of the target axis. |
| [F5 Edit] | Select the acceleration limit value of the axis to change, and press [Edit] to display numeric keypad.  Enter the value with numeric keypad, and press [OK] on the numeric keypad to change it.  Press [OK] in [Acceleration Limit Settings] window to confirm the changed value. |

# ERROR CODE

For the error code, refer to "[ErrorList.pdf](img/001075/ErrorList.pdf)"  
For each error level, refer to "[Error Levels](000494.html)"

With regard to the RC7's error codes which are output to "[Error Read(0100)](001014.html)" in Standard Mode of the System Input/Output Signals or "[Error No. (Output)](001034.html)" in RC3 Compatible Mode, refer to the "RC7 codes" section.

## Error [81608FFF]

Error [81608FFF] stands for an error which is not supported by RC8 series.  
This error occurs when provider-used program is executed.  
For details, see "[Provider Errors](005122.html)" in the "PROVIDER GUIDE".

## How to Refer to Error Codes

In an error code with eight digits, the upper two digits may change as described below. Therefore, when you search an error code from the error code table, use the lower six digits.

### Error Code System

abcccccc

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| a [The first digit from the left] | The first one digit will be used to distinguish robots when two or more robots are controlled.  The error code table attached to this manual includes errors that start from eight.  8: A master robot. A robot if only one robot is used.  9: The first robot in slave robots.  A: The second robot in slave robots.  B: The third robot in slave robots. |
| b [The second digit from the left] | This digit expresses an error level from 0 to 5.  Note that the same error may be different error levels in normal tasks and supervisory tasks.  The error code table attached to this manual expresses the errors in normal tasks only. |
| c [The third or lower from the left] | These digits express the error content. |

Example)  
Error code "8150006B"  
8: Robot is a "Master".  
1: Error level is "Level 1".  
50006B: The error content is "Command isn't executable while program is edited".

## How to Output Error Codes to I/O

| Mode | Output timing | Destination | Output area and format |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Standard mode | Executing "[Error Read (0100)](001014.html)", which is an I/O command, will output an error code. | RC7 code  (16bits output) | On the status area of the system output, an RC7 Code will be displayed. You can check an RC7 Code in the Error Code Tables.   In the Error Code Table, if an outputted error's RC7 Code cell is empty, 230\* will be issued (the asterisk represents an error level). |
| RC8 series code  (32bits output) | When an error occurs, an error code written in the Code column in the Error Code Table will be outputted to the user output area you have specified. |
| RC3 Compatible mode | [Output automatically when an error occurs.](001034.html) | RC7 code  (12bits output) | The lower 12-bit of the RC7 Code in the Error Code Table will be outputted to the error area of the system output. (Example: 0x2187 >0x187)  In the Error Code Table, if an outputted error's RC7 Code cell is empty, 30\* will be issued (the asterisk represents an error level). |
| RC8 series code  (32bits output) | When an error occurs, an error code written in the Code column in the Error Code Table will be outputted to the user output area you have specified. |

To use an RC8 series Code (32-bit output), you need to specify the output area beforehand.  
For details, refer to "32bit Error Code Output I/O No." in the "[Displaying and Changing I/O Parameters](001769.html)" under the OPERATION GUIDE.

# Changes from RC7M

The following table shows changes from RC7M.

## Hardware

| No | Change | Reason | Measure | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Motor and encoder cable](000815.html) is for RC8 exclusive use | Space-saving | Purchase newly |  |
| 2 | [Power cable](000816.html) is for RC8 exclusive use | Space-saving | Purchase newly |  |
| 3 | RC7M Global spec. is equivalent to Standard spec. of RC8. | Globalization | For details, refer to [manuals](001317.html) |  |
| 4 | Safety I/O connector is integrated into Mini I/O connector | Enhance Usability | For details, refer to [manuals](001370.html) | No change of I/O assignment |
| 5 | Add Protective stop (2 systems) | Enhance Usability | For details, refer to [manuals](001370.html) |  |
| 6 | Mini I/O's internal/external power supply method change is performed by TP | Enhance Usability | For details, refer to [manuals](001345.html) | Short socket for changing power supply is not shipped with RC8 since it is not used. |
| 7 | Include one PCI board.(RC7 has three boards) | Space-saving | For details, refer to [manuals](001317.html) | A piece of PCI express is added |
| 8 | Protect external wiring of I/O with self recovery fuse | Enhance Usability |  | If short-circuit is likely to occur, shunt by self recovery fuse and display the short point on the pendant screen. |
| Fuse and other IC for output are not shipped because the circuit is back to normal condition without parts replacement when short-circuit resolved. |
| 9 | [Field network board](001317.html) is RC8 exclusive use. (DeviceNet, CCLink, PROFIBUS, EtherNet/IP) | Globalization | Purchase newly |  |
| (DeviceNet, CC-Link, PROFIBUS, EtherNet/IP) |
| 10 | [One driver board controls two axis](001357.html) | Space-saving |  | Driver board replacement is for two axis each |
| 11 | Free of controller's memory backup battery replacement | Easy of maintenance |  | RC7M requires to replace the memory backup battery every two years.  RC8 requires [the internal clock battery](005907.html) replacement only once every ten years. |

## Software

| No | Change | Reason | Measure | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | TP display | Enhance Usability | For details, refer to [manuals](001674.html) | Basic menu compositions are not changed. |
| ([layout, color, icon, etc.](001702.html)) |

| (Approach direction of tool coordinate is downwards from flange) |
| 5 | Integrate internal auto mode and external auto mode into one. | ISO-compliance | For details, refer to [manuals](001527.html) | Internal/External mode of RC7 and before was Denso-proprietary specification |

# The Setting of the Deadman Switch Linkage Function

Operation path : [F6 Setting] - [F3 Pendant and Panel] - [F7 DSW interlock]

Set the deadman switch linkage function.  
When pressing [F7 DSW interlock], [DSW interlock] screen is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001079_1.png)

| Keys other than function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| Motor power ON | When this option is enabled, motor power turns on at the timing of pressing the deadman switch in manual or teach check mode. |
| Motor power OFF | When this option is enabled, motor power turns off at the timing of releasing the deadman switch in manual or teach check mode.  Note:This option button is displayed and effective only when using the safety I/O less specification.  Other than Safety I/O less specifications, motor turns off whenever the deadman switch is released. |
| Display Arm traverse key | When this option is enabled, the arm traverse key is displayed in the right side of the display during pressing deadman switch in manual or teach check mode. |
| Display Jog dial speed | When this option is enabled, you can change the robot speed to the custom speed value by the jog dial during the arm traverse key is displayed (a state of deadman switch is pressed) in manual or teach check mode. |
| [Jog dial speed selector](005767.html) | Once [Open] button is pressed, the [Aux] window that sets the custom speed values will be displayed. |

For the Mini pendant, you can set the motor power ON/OFF-linkage with the parameter setting of WINCAPSIII.
(This is available Var 1.8.\* or later)

No.19: Interlock motor off and deadman SW (0: Enable, 1: Disable) (This item is displayed only when the Safety I/O-less specification is used)  
No.20: Interlock motor on and deadman SW (0: Disable, 1: Enable)

For details about the way of setting, refer to "[Configuring Parameters](004407.html)" of WINCAPSIII GUIDE.

# Output Signal During Program Stop Process

When the entire program has stopped such as an emergency stop or instantaneously stop and others, the program cannot reboot in a certain period of time. If reboot the program, an error message "Command is not executable during program stop process " occurs.

To activate the stop processing condition acquisition by IO, go to [F4 I/O] [F6 Aux][F5 I/O Parameters] then specify the user output number in [No 127 Running Stop Processing IO No].

This signal turns ON when the specified IO is during program stop process.

# Actuator Type Setting and Changing

To change the actuator type, go to the Hand Initializing settings screen.

When replacing the electric gripper to the same model, the parameter initialization is not necessary though; you need to clear the referenced machine information.

Route : Basic screen - [F9 hand] - [F12 Aux] - [F1 Initial settings]

###### 1

Press [F1Initializing settings] to display [Initializing settings]window.  
Select the actuator type from the Inti Parameter then press[Initialize].

The message shown below appears. Press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001081_2.png)

###### 3

If all the settings are successfully completed, the message below appears. Press [OK].  
If an error occurs, fix the error and select the actuator type again.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001081_3.png)

# Removing the Electric Gripper

Before removing the electric gripper control board from the robot controller, be sure to disable the electric gripper.

If the robot controller is removed before disablement, an error shown below occurs.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001082_1.png)

Route : Basic screen - [F9 Hand] - [F12 Aux] - [F2 Parameter]

###### 1

Press [F2 Parameter] to display the screen below. Select the hand number to be activated.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001082_2.png)

###### 2

Click [Edit] then change the value to "0" and press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001082_3.png)

###### 3

The message shown below appears.
Press [OK] then reboot the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001082_4.png)

# Setting DHCP

## Key

[COM] (Effective
in Manual mode)

## Operation

###### 1

Press [COM] to call up the "COM Setting" screen shown below which lists communications settings for the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001085_1.png)

###### 2

Choose "IP address" with the up and down cursor keys and then press [OK]. IP address setting screen appears as shown below.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001085_2.png)

###### 3

Choose "DHCP" with the up and down cursor keys then press [OK].
"DHCP setting screen" appears as shown below.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001085_3.png)

Choose desired state of DHCP("Disable" or "Enable") with the up and down cursor keys then press [OK] to change DHCP setting.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

ID : 1088

# Setting the next Battery Replacement Date

## Access

[Aux]—[Maintenance]—[Ctrlr Batt], [Encdr Batt]

## Operation

Set the next replacement date of the internal clock battery and encoder battery of the robot controller.

When the replacement day comes, appears on the screen periodically.

###### 1

The "Battery Replacement"
date screen appears as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001088_1.png)

###### 2

Choose an input field with the right and
left cursor keys, then enter new data (next replacement date) with the numeric
keypad.

Press the [OK] key to establish the new setting.

Normally, the replacement cycle of the controller battery (for the internal clock) is every 10 years, and the encoder battery is every 2 years.
(refer to the Installation & Maintenance guide)

After replacing each batteries, set the next battery replacement date from the controller.

When replacing the controller battery (for the internal clock), set 10 years later from the current time of the controller.

When replacing the encoder battery, set 2years later from the current time of the controller.

# Adjusting the Air Pressure Balance of the Z-Axis (For 4-axis Robots)

## Key

[AUX] (Effective
in Manual mode)

## Operation

HM standard type robot adjusts the air pressure.

H\* series robots except HM standard type and XR robots do Gravity Offset Compensation. (Ver.2.2.\* or higher)

To adjust the air pressure balance of
the Z-axis, you need to turn the motor power on.

### HM Standard Type Robot

###### 1

Press [AUX] to call up the
"Aux. Function" menu shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_1.png)

###### 2

Vertically scroll the screen with
the up and down cursor keys to choose the "ArmAux"

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_2.png)

###### 3

Press [OK]. The "ArmAux" window appears.

Press [Cancel] to abort adjusting the air pressure balance of the Z-axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_3.png)

###### 4

If you choose
"Z-Balance" and press [OK], then the "Z-Balance" window
appears as shown below.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

Adjust
the air pressure balance so that the indicator line comes within the OK range of
the gauge.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_4.png)

Press [OK] in the state of motor power on. If the motor remains off, a message "Turn ON motor" will appear.

###### 5

Press [OK]. The following screen
will appear.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_5.png)

###### 6

Press [OK] or [CANCEL] to
complete the air balance adjustment procedure.

### H\* Series Robots (except HM Standard Type ) or XR Robot (Ver.2.2.\* or higher)

Follow the same procedure as HM standard type robot by Step 3.

###### 4

Select "Z-Balance" and press [OK]. "Execute GrvOffset?" appears.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_6.png)

###### 5

Confirm the following notes and press [OK].

* Turn ON Motor.
* The robot fully stops.
* The robot can be moved by external force; that may result in the error.

Press [OK] in the state of motor power on. If the motor remains off, a message "Turn ON motor" will appear.

###### 6

Once Gravity Offset Compensation completed, a message will appear. Press [OK] to complete the air balance adjustment procedure.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001089_7.png)

# Displaying the Encoder Reference Position

Operation path : [F2 Arm] - [F12 Maintenance] - [F2 Encoder] - [F2 Encoder reference]

To perform this operation, set the user level "[Maintainer](001772.html)".

Display the encoder reference position state.  
Press [F9 Encoder reference] to display the following [Encoder reference position] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001090_1.png)

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [F6 Clear] | Clear the encoder reference position. |

If perform encoder reference position clear operation, a serious error occurred in the encoder is cleared.
However, keep in mind that this operation could cause abnormal operation of the robot.

# Vision-Robot Coordinate Calibration

A calibration mentioned here is to calculate the conversion matrix which converts visual coordinates (X,Y) into robot coordinates (X,Y,Z), and then save the calculation result into Cal data tables. There are 32 Cal data tables controlled by different numbers ranging from 0 to 31. For about the format of Cal data table, see [Vis.CalTrans](000641.html) command.

There are two ways for calibration; Simple calibration by means of the TP panel. Calibration with numerical input by means of the teach pendant.

## Calibration by Means of TP Panel

Refer to "[Visual Calibration Procedure with a TP Panel](005105.html)".

## Calibration by Numerical Input

Refer to "[Visual Calibration Procedure by Numerical Input](005665.html)".

# 6th-Axis CALSET Position (Clean Room Type Robot)

The position of the 6th-axis of VS-\*\*\* series of robots (Clean Room Type) is determined by special Jig. The 6th axis is a boundless rotation joint, so checking the number of rotations of the axis is not necessary.

To setup, follow the process below.

1. [CALSET Jig Installation](#book1)
2. [Positioning](#book2)

## CALSET Jig Installation

###### 1

Set the 6 axis to the place drawing below indicates. (Near the 0 degree)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001094_1.png)

###### 2

Mount the CALSET jig.  
Tightening Torque; 8.8 +/- 1.7 Nm

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001094_2.png)

## Positioning

Rotate the CALSET jig clockwise, touch the pin to the bolt slightly.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001094_3.png)

# Precaution for 4-axis Robot Posture

For a 4-axis robot, set the approach vector of target posture to a downward direction from the flange as shown below.

* For P-type ([Position Type](000456.html)), set the Rx element to 180 degree, Ry elements to 0 degree.
* For T-type ([Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html)), set the approach vector to V(0,0,-1) .

Unless you set other than above, error "0x83201525L：Destination posture is not realizable in this robot type" occurs and operation cannot be performed.

# Login

## Access

[AUX]-[Login]

## Operation

###### 1

Press [AUX] to display [Auxiliary function option list].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001096_1.png)

###### 2

Choose "Login" with the up and down cursor keys, then press [OK]. "Login" screen shown below appears.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001096_2.png)

To log in with specified user level, choose the user level for login, then input the password and press [OK].

In the initial setting, the password is as follows.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Operator] | 5593551 |
| [Programmer] | 5596045 |
| [Maintainer] | 5596060 |

You can change your “[login password](005950.html)” with a teach pendant.

You cannot change it with a mini-pendant.

If your login password includes an alphabetic letter, you can enter alphabetic letters with a mini-pendant.

E.g. A login password including an alphabetic letter

1． The following describes how to enter letters on the password entry screen.

- Number: Press a numeric key once

- Alphabet: Press a numeric key in succession

To enter the letter “a”, press the numeric key “2” five times in succession.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001096_3.png)

2． Pressing the left and right cursor key “▶” moves the cursor one space to the right, allowing you to enter the next alphanumeric letter.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001096_4.png)

3． Repeat 1 and 2 to finish entering the password, then press [OK] to log in.

If the user level is Operator or Programmer, the user level is maintained after the power off.   
 If the user level is Maintainer, the user level is not maintained after the power off. In this case, the user level will be Programmer after the power off.

To re-login together with changing user level from a higher level to a lower level, password is not required.

Choose "Option" with the up and down cursor keys and then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_2.png)

###### 3

Choose "Extension" and then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_3.png)

License list setting window appears as shown below.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_4.png)

If no selectable license key exists,the following message appears.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_5.png)

### Function menu

Press [OK] on the License list setting window to call up the "Function menu list" as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_6.png)

Differences according to the user level are shown below.

|  | Detail | Add | Remove |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operator | ● | - | - |
| Programmer | ● | ● | - |
| Maintainer | ● | ● | ● |

#### License details

Choose "Detail" with the up and down cursor keys and then press [OK]. Detail information window appears as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_7.png)

Differences according to the user level are shown below.

* -License key
* -License state
* -Registration date (for fixed-term license only)
* -Expiration date (for fixed-term license only)

Differences according to the user level are shown below.

|  | License key display |
| --- | --- |
| Operator | 1234-5678-90AB-\*\*\*\* |
| Programmer,Maintainer | 1234-5678-90AB-CDEF |

#### Add License

Choose "Add" with the up and down cursor keys and then press [OK]. "Add License" window appears as shown below.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_8.png)

Input alphanumerics with numeric input keys and then press [OK] to confirm the license addition.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

When license addition fails, "Add License" window displays again.

When license addition fails, following messages appear.

|  | Messages |
| --- | --- |
| License cannot be handled by the teach pendant | The license is not allowed. |
| When fixed-term license has expired | Invalid license. |
| When addition successfully complete | Success! |

#### Remove the License

Choose "Remove" with the up and down cursor keys and then press [OK]."License delete confirmation" window appears as shown below.

To abort setting, press [CANCEL].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001099_9.png)

If the license delete fails, the following message appears.

|  | Messages |
| --- | --- |
| When delete is prohibited  (User level is "Maintenance" or lower and fixed- term license) | Removing is not allowed. |
| When delete successfully complete | Success! |

# I/O Information Display

Operation path : [F4 I/O] - [F6 Aux] - [F1 I/O Information]

Display CIFX board (DeviceNet slave board, CC-Link remote device board, etc.) information.   
Press [F1 I/O Information] to display the following [I/O Information] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001100_1.png)

For details, refer to the table below.

| Descriptions | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alloc Mode | Device | Display Device name. |
| Mode | Display Alloc Mode. |
| Detail |
| CIFX Device No. | Display CIFX Device No. |
| CIFX Serial No. | Display CIFX Serial No. |
| CIFX Hardware Revision | Display CIFX Hardware Revision. |
| Firmware Type | Display Firmware Type. |
| Firmware Version | Display Firmware Version. |
| IP Address (\*) | Display configured IP address. |
| Subnet mask (\*) | Display configured Subnet mask. |
| Gateway (\*) | Display configured Gateway. |
| MAC Address (\*) | Display MAC address. |
| Node Address (\*) | Display configured node address. |
| Bit Rate (\*) | Display configured communication speed. |
| Name of Station (\*) | Display configured station name. |
| Type of Station (\*) | Display configured station type. |

\* : Several types of CIFX boards can be displayed.

When I/O information acquisition fails, the following message will appear on the Detail section.  
"Not have detailed information."

# Setting R-axis Motion Space Limit

Operation path : [F2 Arm] - [F12 Maintenance] - [F9 Motion range of R axis]

Set the R-axis motion space of the XR robot.  
Press [F9 Motion range of R axis] to display the following [Motion range of R axis] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001101_1.png)

To change the setting, choose desired R-axis motion range and then press [OK] to confirm.

After setting change, operate the robot at a low speed to confirm the software motion limit works as intended.

# Installation Guide for Upright Setting of RC8 Controller (Standard)

When placing the controller in the upright position, it is recommended to use customer-prepared parts to fix the controller to the wall and floor as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001110_1.png)

## Items Prepared by Customers

| Type | | Ａ | Ｂ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Placement direction | | When the wall locates bottom side of the controller. | When the wall locates upper side of the controller. |

| Stand | [Fixing stand for upright setting](img/001110/rc8_stand.pdf) | |

| Stand | [Fixing stand for upright setting](img/001110/rc8_stand_UL.pdf) | |
| Fixing bolt for facilities | | M6 x 9 bolts (common for both types) | |

## Setting Procedure

There are two types of screws, large and small, on each side panels.  
Please remove large screws which are circled on the below image.

Fix the fixing stand for upright setting to the side panel which is immediately next to the power supply connector.

Fix the controller to the facilities' floor with 6 pieces of M6 bolts, and to the wall with 3 pieces of M6 bolts.

# Commands for Conveyor Tracking

| Commands | Functions |
| --- | --- |
| [TrackAbsApproach](003133.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), perform a robot task motion that moves a robot arm to the approach position which is apart from the reference position by specified distance. |
| [TrackAbsMove](003134.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), perform a robot task motion that move a robot to the designated target position. |
| [TrackAbsMove S](003135.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), perform a robot task motion of [free curve interpolation](005030.html) where a robot passes through designated path points. |
| [TrackApproach](005346.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), move a robot arm to the approach position that is apart from the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) by specified distance. |
| [TrackArrivalTime](005351.html) | Return the estimated execution time in which a [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) arrives at the specified limit of the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange). |
| [TrackBufferDelete](005671.html) | Using an index number obtained by [TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html), delete data of the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
| [TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html) | Take out index numbers of data stored in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), and then return them as an array. |
| [TrackBufferRead](005492.html) | From the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), read out specified data. |
| [TrackBufferSort](002285.html) | Change the sorting order of data within the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
| [TrackConveyorSpd](005349.html) | Obtain the current speed of the conveyor or the turntable. |
| [TrackConveyorVector](002224.html) | Obtain the [conveyor vector](002221.html#conveyorVec) that has been calculated at the conveyor calibration with [vector type](000455.html) data. |
| [TrackCount](005347.html) | Return the number of data within the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
| [TrackCurBufferSort](002286.html) | Return the currently selected [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) for sorting method of data with a [variant type](005067.html) data array. |
| [TrackCurMotionRange](002674.html) | Check whether the target position of the [robot task motion](002221.html#operation) is within the robot motion range. |
| [TrackCurPos](005348.html) | Obtains the current position of the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) by [position type](000456.html). |
| [TrackCurStartArea](002225.html) | Return the currently selected [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange) with a [variant type](005067.html) data array. |
| [TrackDepart](005350.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), move a robot arm from the current position to -Z direction of the tool coordinate. |
| [TrackDraw](003049.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), move a robot arm from the current position to the specified position with Travel distance. |
| [TrackEncoder](005494.html) | Obtain the encoder value of the conveyor or the turntable. |
| [TrackInitialize](005354.html) | Initializes the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), then starts trigger detection. Executing this command to a slave robot connects it to the master robot when you use the conveyor tracking system with coordinated multiple robots. |
| [TrackInRange](005355.html) | Check whether the current position of the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange). |
| [TrackMinimumIntervalLength](005794.html) | Set a threshold value to prevent the registration of overlapped workpieces. |
| [TrackMotionRange](002675.html) | Check whether there is any point entering the robot motion range, on the path of the target position of the [robot task motion](002221.html#operation) when the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange). |
| [TrackMove](005356.html) | With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), move a robot arm to the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork). |
| [TrackMove S](002983.html) | This enables a robot to execute [free curve interpolation](005030.html) motion, while [tracking](002221.html#tracking) a [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) carried by conveyor or turntable. |
| [TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html) | In order to define the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin), specify the offset value from the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange). |
| [TrackPrepareData](002836.html) | TrackPrepareData deletes the duplicated data in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) among several workpice data detected by a vision sensor, rearranges the workpiece data in order from the most downstream one, and then return the data set.  This command deletes duplicated data and rearranges workpiece data before setting the workpiece data in the tracking buffer by [TrackSetVision](005376.html). The return value of this command will be used as arguments of TrackSetVision without any modification. |
| [TrackSetSensor](005375.html) | Store workpiece-related data detected by a sensor into [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
| [TrackSetVision](005376.html) | Store workpiece-related data detected by a vision sensor into [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
| [TrackShiftTarget](003048.html) | Change the target position of the tracking motion from Default position to the position specified by Offset value. |
| [TrackStandByPos](005352.html) | Return the coordinates when a [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) piece arrives at the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange). |
| [TrackStart](005377.html) | Starts the [tracking mode](002221.html#trackingMode). |
| [TrackStartArea](005490.html) | Configures the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange). |
| [TrackStop](005378.html) | Stops the [tracking mode](002221.html#trackingMode). |
| [TrackTargetOffset](005493.html) | Set the value for the "Minimum Interval Length of Work Detection", which is a parameter for the conveyor or circular tracking. |
| [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) | Read out workpiece data from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) and then set them to the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork). |
| [TrackTargetRelease](005567.html) | Delete data of the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork), or return the data to the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |

# Configuring the I/O Allocation Mode Parameter

## Type of I/O Allocation Mode

There are four types of allocation mode; Mini I/O dedicated mode, Compatible mode, Standard mode, All User mode.  
For each mode, input and output signals functions are different.  
For details about each mode, refer to "[Functions in Individual Allocation Modes](001326.html)" from RC8 SERIES ROBOT CONTROLLER MANUAL.

Available allocation mode is different depending on the I/O Expansion board used. For details, refer to the "[Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode](001325.html)" of RC8 SERIES ROBOT CONTROLLER MANUAL.

## How to Set the I/O Allocation Mode

If the allocation mode at the shipment is not the mode you intend to, change the allocation mode with WINCAPSIII. Regarding to operation procedures, please refer to "[I/O Mode Setting from WINCAPSIII](005271.html)" of START UP MANUAL.

For the way of checking currently selected I/O allocation mode, refer to "[Checking the I/O Allocation Mode](005272.html)" from START UP MANUAL.

If the controller has an I/O extension board that can be used in the RC3 compatible or standard mode as a factory option, the default is the standard mode.

## Pin Assignment, Port Number

For about pin assignment and port number, refer to "IO allocation" section on the user's manual of your I/O expansion board or each I/O.

## Other References

For about the overview of I/O and the installation, refer to "[General Information about the Interface](001322.html)" and "[Connecting I/O](001344.html)" from RC8 SERIES ROBOT CONTROLLER MANUAL, respectively.

For about I/O expansion board or each I/O, refer to the manufacturer's user's manual.

# Notes When Power is Turned On

After installing the RC8A robot controller, when the power is turned on for the first time, errors such as "854A1385" and "854A13D9" may occur repeatedly (This phenomenon does not occur for RC8A safety I/O-less specification).

If the setting of Mini I/O power supply is set to external power supply, when the power of the RC8A robot controller is turned on before external power supply, this error may occur (Factory setting of Mini I/O power supply is set to external power supply).

When an error occurs, follow the process below.

## External Power Supply of Mini I/O is Ready

Turn off the RC8A robot controller.

After that, turn on the external power supply of Mini I/O, and then turn on the power of the RC8A robot controller again.

## External Power Supply of Mini I/O is Not Ready

Change the setting of Mini I/O power supply temporarily to internal power supply, and restart it.

As factory default, the teach pendant is displayed in Japanese. If you want to set the power setting in other language, please set the language setting first.

### Language Setting

###### 1

Press [LOCK] and then clear an error.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001131_1.png)

###### 2

When the power is turned on for the first time, after pressing [LOCK] and clearing an error, a window to set language is displayed. Set any language.

If the window to set language is not displayed, follow the operation path below to change language.

Operation path : [F6 Setting]－[F3 Pemdant and Panel]－[F1 Language]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001131_3.png)

###### 3

Turn off the RC8A robot controller and then turn on the power again.

### Setting Mini I/O Power Supply to Internal Power Supply

###### 1

Press [LOCK] and then clear an error.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001131_1.png)

###### 2

Follow the operation path below.

Operation path : [F4 I/O]－[F6 Aux]－[F5 I/O Parameters]

[I/O Parameters] window is displayed. Change the [59 : I/O Power Mode] parameter to "1 : Internal" and press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001131_2.png)

###### 3

Turn off the RC8A robot controller and then turn on the power again.

# Preparation of Hardware

The force sensor–based force control function requires a force sensor, a force sensor cable, and other components in addition to our robot products.

You can use a force sensor made by the following manufacturers. Different hardware is required depending on the manufacturer of a force sensor you choose. In addition, only specific force sensors are available among those manufactured by these companies. For details, refer to the following links.

| Manufacturer | Connecting method | Contents of "Preparation of Hardware"  (link destination) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WACOH-TECH Inc. | RS-422A | [Hardware preparation for using force sensors of WACOH-TECH Inc.](005465.html)  To use a force sensor of this manufacturer, the robot controller software version must be version 2.2.\* or higher. |
| ATI Industrial Automation | Ethernet | [Hardware preparation for using force sensor of ATI Industrial Automation.](001133.html)  * To use a force sensor of this manufacturer, the robot controller software version must be version 2.11.0 or higher. * When using the Cooperative Control function, you cannot use a force sensor of this manufacturer. |
| SINTOKOGIO,LTD. | RS-422A | [Hardware preparation for using force sensor of SINTOKOGIO,LTD.](001138.html)  To use a force sensor of this manufacturer, the robot controller software version must be version 2.11.0 or higher. |
| Hypersen Technologies | Ethernet | [Hardware preparation for using force sensor of Hypersen Technologies](001231.html)  * To use a force sensor of this manufacturer, the robot controller software version must be version 2.22.\* or higher. * When using the Cooperative Control function, you cannot use a force sensor of this manufacturer. |

# Preparation of Hardware when Using ATI Industrial Automation Force Sensor

This page describes details of the devices required to use a force sensor manufactured by ATI Industrial Automation for the force sensor–based force control function.

* This manufacturer’s force sensors are available when the robot controller software version is Ver.2.11.0 or higher.
* If the cooperative control function is used, this manufacturer’s force sensors cannot be used.

# Force Sensor Mounting Stay

To install a force sensor to a flange of a robot, the dedicated stay (force sensor mounting stay) needs to be made by customers. This section describes the force sensor mounting stay in the following subsections.

* [Structure of Force Sensor Mounting Stay](#ID001134_Structure)
* [Key Point when Designing Force Sensor Mounting Stay](#ID001134_Point)

## Structure of Force Sensor Mounting Stay

The following shows an example of the force sensor mounting stay.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_1.png)

For the force sensor mounting stay, make multiple through holes as above so that bolts and dowel pins can be inserted.

To install the force sensor mounting stay to the flange of the robot, use dowel pins and bolts as shown below.

(Dowel pins and bolts should be prepared by customers)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_8.png)

To install the force sensor mounting stay to the force sensor, use dowel pins and bolts as shown in the lower-left figure.

In actual, install the force sensor mounting stay to the flange of the robot, and then install the force sensor. Therefore, dimension A in the lower-right figure needs to be high enough to tighten bolts.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_2.png)

## Key Point when Designing Force Sensor Mounting Stay

Dimension of screw on the flange surface and total mass of tool/stay/force sensor
:   For positions and dimensions for screw holes on the flange surface and holes of dowel pins, they are written in the dimensional outline drawing of the robot to be used.

    For the total mass of an equipment that applies payload to a flange such as a stay/force sensor/tool (hereafter, "tool-related part") and the position of its center of gravity, the upper limit differ depending on the robot to be used.

    For details, refer to the following links.

    |  | Robot series | Dimensional outline drawing / Precautions of tool-related part  (Link destination) |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | 6th axis | VM | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](000831.html) * [Precautions When Designing the End-effectors](000845.html) |
    | VS | * [Reference Drawings](000081.html) * [Precautions When Designing End-effectors](000038.html) |
    | VS-6556/6577 | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](005402.html) * [Precautions When Designing the End-effectors](005423.html) |
    | VP | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](000932.html) * [Precautions When Designing the End-effectors](000934.html) |
    | 4th axis | HM (including HMS) | * [Precautions When Designing the End-effectors](004593.html) * [Engineering-design Notes for Robot Hands](004604.html) |
    | HS (including HSS) | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](004738.html) * [Engineering-design Notes for Robot Hands (HS/HSS)](004750.html) |
    | HSA1 | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](002912.html) * [Engineering-design Notes for Robot Hands](002922.html) |
    | HSR | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](002427.html) * [Engineering-design Notes for Robot Hands](002431.html) |
    | XR | * [Outer Dimensions and Workable Space of the Robot Unit](004816.html) * [Engineering-design Notes for Robot Hands](004827.html) |

Dimensions of hole of force sensor
:   For positions and dimensions for the screw hole of force sensor and the hole of dowel pin, refer to the dimensional outline drawing of the force sensor to be used.

Positions of the screw holes of the flange and the force sensor are close
:   If positions of the screw holes of the flange and the force sensor are close (example: a pitch circle diameter (hereafter, "P.C.D.") of the screw hole of the flange and P.C.D.of the screw hole of the force sensor are very close), both bolts interferes each other as shown below. The standard stay cannot be installed. In this case, install the relay stay additionally.
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_4.png)
:   The following is an example of the force sensor mounting stay and the relay stay.
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_5.png)
:   First, install the relay stay to the force sensor.
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_6.png)
:   Next, install the force sensor mounting stay to the flange. After that, install the relay stay with the force sensor to the force sensor mounting stay.
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001134_7.png)
:   By designing positions of each hole of the force sensor mounting stay and the relay stay so as not to interfere each other, it allows to install as above.

# Parameter Setting and Communication Setting of Net Box

In the Net Box, the parameter regarding the function of the force sensor is stored.

Before executing the force sensor–based force control function, you need to specify the parameters for the function.  
 In addition, setting of the IP address is necessary to communicate through Ethernet.

Editing the parameter and communication setting of the Net Box is performed on the computer.

If you access to the Net Box from the computer through Ethernet communication, a web page generated by the Net Box is displayed on the computer. Edit parameter in that page.

The following figure is a system example when editing a parameter. If you use the PoE Ethernet switching HUB for supplying power to the Net Box, the DC power supply is not necessary.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001135_1.png)

Follow the procedure below to set.

| Item  (Link destination) | Procedure  (Link destination) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. [Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer](001136.html) | Perform the Ethernet connection setting of a computer so that the computer can communicate with the Net Box through Ethernet.  For details, refer to [Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer](001136.html). |
| 2. [Parameter Setting and Communication Setting](001137.html) | Access to the Net Box from the web browser on the computer, and perform the parameter setting and communication setting.  For details, refer to [Parameter Setting and Communication Setting](001137.html). |
| 3. [Communication Setting of Robot Controller](001145.html) | Perform the communication setting of a robot controller so that the robot controller can communicate with the Net Box through Ethernet.  For details, refer to [Communication Setting of Robot Controller](001145.html). |

# Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer

Perform the Ethernet connection setting of a computer so that the computer can communicate with the Net Box through Ethernet.

To do this, you need to know the IP address that is set to the Net Box.

This section describes on the assumption that the IP address of the Net Box is the factory default value (192.168.1.1).

The following explains the operation window of Windows10 as an example.

When an equipment other than the Net Box and the computer is connected through Ethernet network, if the equipment is DHCP server, the IP address of the Net Box may be changed automatically to the address other than above. For DHCP setting of the Net Box, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx).

###### 1

Perform the computer setting with the computer and the Net Box are not connected through Ethernet cable. If those are connected, remove them once, and connect them again after the computer setting completes.

###### 2

Perform the following operation from your computer’s desktop.

1. Select [Start] button.
2. Select [Setting] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_1.png)

###### 3

Select [Network & Internet].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_2.png)

###### 4

Select [Change adapter options].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_3.png)

###### 5

Select [Ethernet].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_4.png)

###### 6

Select [properties] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_5.png)

###### 7

Perform the following operation.

1. Select [Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)].
2. Select [properties] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_6.png)

###### 8

Perform the following operation.

1. Select [Use the following IP address], and then set the following values to [IP address] and [Subnet mask].

   |  |  |
   | --- | --- |
   | IP address | 192.168.1.100 |
   | Subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
2. Select [OK] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_7.png)

Above setting value is an example. If it is inconvenient in your environment in use, set another value that can communicate with the Net Box.

This completes the setting.
