# Parameter Setting and Communication Setting

Access to the Net Box from the web browser on the computer, and perform the parameter setting and communication setting.

To do this, you need to know the IP address that is set to the Net Box.

This section describes on the assumption that the IP address of the Net Box is the factory default value (192.168.1.1).

###### 1

Confirm that the computer and the Net Box are connected through Ethernet cable.

Confirm that power is supplied to the Net Box.

The following shows a connection example when using the DC power supply. If you use the PoE Ethernet switching HUB, the DC power supply is not necessary.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_5.png)

###### 2

Start the browser on the computer and access to the Net Box.

After starting the browser, enter "http://" and the IP address of the Net Box in the address bar, and press Enter key (In this example, enter "http://192.168.1.1").

(The following shows a display example of Internet Explorer)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_6.png)

###### 3

The browser page goes to the welcome page of Net F/T as shown in the following figure.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_7.png)

* If the account ID and password are requested, it might be due to the Proxy setting of computer. Set by the following steps so as not to use the Proxy.

  |  |
  | --- |
  | Windows operation path：[Start] - [Settings] - [Network & Internet] - [Proxy] |
  | (Up to [Network & Internet], it is the same operation as "[Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer](001136.html)") |

  When performing the above operation, the [Proxy] setting window will be displayed. Turn off "Use a proxy server" and click [Save].
* When it does not go to the welcome page after waiting for a while or the welcome page is not displayed correctly, if you press F5 key on the keyboard, it may be displayed correctly.

###### 4

Perform the parameter setting.

Click [Configurations] on the welcome page.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_1.png)

###### 5

1. Set [View Configuration] to "#1 – S1-580-20".
2. Select [GO] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_2.png)

###### 6

Edit the parameter of the subtitle [Configuration #1 (Active configuration)].

1. Confirm that [Calibration Select] is "#1 – FT14685".
2. Set [Force Units] to "N", and [Torque Units] to "N-m".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_8.png)

###### 7

Click [Apply] button at the bottom of the page.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_9.png)

###### 8

Once the window is updated, confirm that the values are "1000000" for [Counts per Force] and [Counts per Torque] in the subtitle [Configuration #1 (Active configuration)].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_10.png)

When the window is not updated after waiting for a while, if you press F5 button on the keyboard, it may be displayed correctly.

###### 9

Perform the communication setting.

Click [Communications] on the welcome page.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_3.png)

###### 10

(If you want to change the IP address of the Net Box, perform this step and then go to the next step). (If you do not change the IP address of the Net Box, skip this step and go to the next step).

Edit the parameter of the subtitle [Ethernet Network Settings].

1. Select "Static" for [IP Address Mode].
2. Set any value for each [Static IP Address], [Static IP Subnet Mask], [Static IP Default Gateway].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_11.png)

###### 11

Edit the parameter of the subtitle [Raw Data Transfer (RDT) Settings].

1. Select "Enabled" for [RDT Interface].
2. Select [Apply] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_4.png)

This completes the setting.

# Using a SINTOKOGIO Force Sensor

This page describes details of the devices required to use a force sensor manufactured by manufactured by SINTOKOGIO, LTD for the force sensor–based force control function.

* To use a force sensor of this manufacturer, software version the robot controller must be version 2.11.0 or higher.

## Available Force Sensor

The “ZYXer” Series force censor manufactured by SINTOKOGIO, LTD. is available.

### Operation-Checked Sensor

| Model number/model name | Rated load | | Outline drawing/specifications |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Translational force [N] | Moment [Nm] |
| ZYX080A501Z | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±500 | Mx、My、Mz : ±20 | For details, refer to [SINTOKOGIO, LTD.](https://www.sinto.co.jp/en/product/force-sensor/) website. |
| ZYX080A501 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±500 | Mx、My、Mz : ±20 |
| ZYX080S102 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±1000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±40 |
| ZYX100A102 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±1000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±45 |
| ZYX100S202 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±2000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±100 |
| ZYX125A102 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±1000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±75 |
| ZYX125S202 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±2000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±200 |
| ZYX160A302 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±3000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±120 |
| ZYX160S402 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±4000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±320 |
| ZYX200A352 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±3500 | Mx、My、Mz : ±260 |
| ZYX200S902 | Fx、Fy、Fz : ±9000 | Mx、My、Mz : ±600 |
| Common Specification For any model, data exchange between a robot controller and a force sensor is done via RS-422A communication.  The baud rate of RS422A communication is 46800bps in the standard model. You can change the baud rate to 92160bms when placing an order though, the baud rate of the robot controller is 46800bps at the maximum. Therefore, do not change it to 92160bps. | | | | |

Information of each force sensor written above is only a part of the entire information. For details, refer to [SINTOKOGIO,LTD.](https://www.sinto.co.jp/en/product/force-sensor/) website.

## System Configuration

The following image shows the system configuration.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001138_1.png)

Periodically check the force sensor.

| Components /  Manufacturer / Model(Part number) | Description |
| --- | --- |
| (1) Force sensor SINTOKOGIO,LTD.   * Refer to [Available force sensor](#ID001138_Outline). | Select a force sensor according to your application. |
| (2) Force sensor mounting stay (made by customer) | A stay for fixing a force sensor to the end of the robot arm.  For details, refer to "[How to Install a Force Sensor](001139.html)". |
| (3) Tool (selected by customer) | Select a tool according to your application. |
| (4) Tool mounting stay (made by customer) | A stay for fixing a tool to the force sensor.  Create a stay with referring to the outline drawing of [Available force sensor](#ID001138_Outline). |
| (5) force sensor cable SINTOKOGIO,LTD.   * Shipped with the force sensor.  Select appropriate length from 2ｍ, 5ｍ and 10ｍ. | A cable that connects the force sensor to the robot controller. Specify the length of the cable when you purchase the force sensor.  The cable end of the robot controller connection side is loose-wire. Connect individual wire of the loose-wire to the applicable pins on D-sub 9 pin connector (female).  For information about how to connect wires, refer to "[How to connect pins for D-sub 9 pin connector (female)](#ID001138_WiringTable)" in the bottom of this page. |
| (6) D-sub 9 pin connector (female) (selected by customer) | This connector connects the force sensor cable and the cable of the power supply device (see below) to the robot controller.  For information about how to connect wires, refer to "[How to connect pins for D-sub 9 pin connector (female)](#ID001138_WiringTable)" in the bottom of this page. |
| (7) Power supply device (DC5V) and wiring (selected by customer) | A power supply device and its wiring that feed electrical power to the force sensor.  Prepare device having the following specification.   * DC 5V ±5%   For information about how to connect wires, refer to "[How to connect pins for D-sub 9 pin connector (female)](#ID001138_WiringTable)" in the bottom of this page. |
| The following two devices are available for the Force sensor and robot controller connection.   |  |  | | --- | --- | | (8-1) RS-422A communication board CONTEC CO., LTD.  1ch type  COM-1PD(LPCI)H  2ch type  COM-2PD(LPCI)H  4ch type  COM-4PD(LPCI)H  (Either of them are PCI boards.) | Insert this board into the expansion slot of the robot controller for use.  For normal application, select 1ch type. If an RS-422A communication is used for other application than the Force sensor, select 2ch type or 4ch type.  RS-422A communication board needs arrangement before use. Please refer to "[RS-422A Communication Board Setting](018097.html)".  This board cannot be used together with any other PCI board.(Example: Electric gripper control board, paralell I/O board, EtherCAT master board) A PCI Express board can be used together.(Example: CC-Link remote device board, EtherNet/IP adapter board, PROFIBUS slave board) | | (8-2) RS-422A Micro converter CONTEC CO., LTD.  Model  COM-1PD(USB)H  (This device requires robot controller software version 2.5.\* or higher.) | Connect this converter to a USB connector of robot controller.  You need to perform necessary settings on this RS-422A micro converter before use. Refer to "[How to Use RS-422A Micro Converter](018098.html)" for details.  If this product is subjected to strong noise, Force sensor communication-related errors may occur.  In this case, take any measures for noise reduction with reference to "[Noise Reduction When Using RS-422A Micro Converter](018099.html)". | | |
| (9) Software license for the force sensor–based force control function DENSO WAVE Inc.  Force Sensor Compliance Control  Compliance function-activated  410002-735\*  License only  410002-736\*  Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control  Compliance function-activated  410002-898\*  License only  410002-899\* | These are DENSO products.  These licenses are required to use the force sensor–based force control function.  The force sensor–based force control function is classified into two types: “Force Sensor Compliance Control” and “Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control”.  Select a license for the type of function that you intend to use.  "Compliance function-activated" targets a newly purchased robot set. Ordering this option with a robot set will activate the function before shipment. Please order this option with a robot set.  "License only" targets a robot set that has been shipped without "Compliance function-activated" option. To use this function with such robot set, please order "License only". If you order "License only", you need to activate the function on your robot controller.  For how to activate the function, refer to “[Activating the Function](005932.html)”. |

### How to Connect Pins for D-sub 9 Pin Connector (Female)

Size of holes of force sensor

# System Configuration of Net Box-connection Type Force Sensor

The following image shows the system configuration.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001141_1.png)

When creating a system, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx) and perform it correctly and safely, in addition to the following contents.

Periodically check the force sensor.

| Components /  Manufacturer / Model (Part number) | Description |
| --- | --- |
| (1) Force sensor ATI Industrial Automation   * Refer to "[Available Force Sensors](001133.html#ID001133_Outline)". | Select a force sensor according to your application.  In the instruction manual of ATI Industrial Automation, the force sensor is described as "Transducer". |
| (2) Force sensor mounting stay (made by customer) | A stay for fixing a force sensor to the end of the robot arm.  For details, refer to "[How to Install a Force Sensor](001150.html)". |
| (3) Tool (selected by customer) | Select a tool according to your application. |
| (4) Tool mounting stay (made by customer) | A stay for fixing a tool to the force sensor.  Create a stay referring to the outer dimension drawing of the force sensor published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx). |
| (5) Transducer cable ATI Industrial Automation   * Accompanied with the force sensor | A cable to connect the force sensor and the Net Box.  When you purchase the force sensor, this cable will be accompanied.  Depending on the force sensor, some force sensors are integrated with a cable (a force sensor and a cable cannot be separated) (hereafter, "cable integrated type"). Nano and Mini series are the cable integrated type.  The length is different between the cable integrated type and other force sensors (hereafter, "cable separated type").   * Cable separated type  Standard : 10 m  Option : 0.3 m to 30 m * Cable integrated type  Standard : 1.8 m  Option : 0.3m to 5 m   Specify the length when you purchase the force sensor. |
| (6) Net Box ATI Industrial Automation   * Accompanied with the force sensor | An interface to connect a force sensor and a robot controller so as to be able to communicate between these devices.  When you purchase the force sensor, this product will be accompanied.  For details, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx). |
| (7) M12 to RJ45 adapter (purchased from ATI Industrial Automation. Or made by customer) | An adapter (a cable) to connect the Net Box and a robot controller through Ethernet cable.  You can purchase it from ATI Industrial Automation.  Or this can be made by customer.  For details, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx). |
| You need to supply electricity to the Net Box. You can select from the following two methods.   |  |  | | --- | --- | | (8-1) PoE Ethernet switching HUB (purchased from ATI Industrial Automation. Or selected by customer) | This can supply electricity to the Net Box and connect with multiple Ethernet cables.  You can purchase it from ATI Industrial Automation.  Or the selected HUB by customer can be used.  For details, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx). | | (8-2) DC power supply (purchased from ATI Industrial Automation. Or selected by customer) | This can supply electricity to the Net Box.  You can purchase it from ATI Industrial Automation.  Or the selected power supply by customer can be used. In that case, select a power supply that is fulfilled with the following specification.   * Voltage range : 11 V to 25 V * Maximum power consumption : 10 W   For details, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx). | | |
| (9) EtherNet cable (selected by customer) | This connects the Net Box and a robot controller through the M12-RJ45 adapter. Select an Ethernet cable that is fulfilled with the following specification.   * Ethernet cable more than CAT5 |
| (10) Software license for the force sensor–based force control function DENSO WAVE Inc.  Force Sensor Compliance Control  Compliance function-activated  410002-735\*  License only  410002-736\*  Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control  Compliance function-activated  410002-898\*  License only  410002-899\* | These are DENSO products.  These licenses are required to use the force sensor–based force control function.  The force sensor–based force control function is classified into two types: “Force Sensor Compliance Control” and “Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control”.  Select a license for the type of function that you intend to use.  "Compliance function-activated" targets a newly purchased robot set. Ordering this option with a robot set will activate the function before shipment. Please order this option with a robot set.  "License only" targets a robot set that has been shipped without "Compliance function-activated" option. To use this function with such robot set, please order "License only". If you order "License only", you need to activate the function on your robot controller.  For how to activate the function, refer to “[Activating the Function](005932.html)”. |

| (7) Power supply (24 V DC) (selected by customer) | A power supply to supply electricity to the force sensor. Select a power supply that is fulfilled with the following specification.   * Nominal voltage : 24 V * Voltage range : 12 V to 30 V * Maximum power consumption : 1.5 W |
| (8) Software license for the force sensor–based force control function DENSO WAVE Inc.  Force Sensor Compliance Control  Compliance function-activated  410002-735\*  License only  410002-736\*  Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control  Compliance function-activated  410002-898\*  License only  410002-899\* | These are DENSO products.  These licenses are required to use the force sensor–based force control function.  The force sensor–based force control function is classified into two types: “Force Sensor Compliance Control” and “Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control”.  Select a license for the type of function that you intend to use.  "Compliance function-activated" targets a newly purchased robot set. Ordering this option with a robot set will activate the function before shipment. Please order this option with a robot set.  "License only" targets a robot set that has been shipped without "Compliance function-activated" option. To use this function with such robot set, please order "License only". If you order "License only", you need to activate the function on your robot controller.  For how to activate the function, refer to “[Activating the Function](005932.html)”. |

# Parameter Setting and Communication Setting of Force Sensor

In the force sensor, the parameter regarding the function of the force sensor itself is stored.

Before executing the force sensor–based force control function, you need to specify the parameters for the function.  
 In addition, setting of the IP address is necessary to communicate through Ethernet.

Editing the parameter and communication setting of the force sensor is performed on the computer.

If you access to the force sensor from the computer through Ethernet communication, a web page generated by the force sensor is displayed on the computer. Edit parameter in that page.

The following figure is a system example when editing a parameter.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001144_1.png)

Follow the procedure below to set.

| Item  (Link destination) | Procedure  (Link destination) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. [Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer](001146.html) | Perform the Ethernet connection setting of a computer so that the computer can communicate with a force sensor through Ethernet.  For details, refer to [Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer](001146.html). |
| 2. [Parameter Setting and Communication Setting](001147.html) | Access to the force sensor from the web browser on the computer, and perform the parameter setting and communication setting.  For details, refer to [Parameter Setting and Communication Setting](001147.html). |
| 3. [Communication Setting of Robot Controller](001148.html) | Perform the communication setting of a robot controller so that the robot controller can communicate with a force sensor through Ethernet.  For details, refer to [Communication Setting of Robot Controller](001148.html). |

# Communication Setting of Robot Controller

Perform the communication setting of a robot controller so that the robot controller can communicate with the Net Box through Ethernet.

To do this, you need to know the IP address that is set to the Net Box.

This section describes on the assumption that the IP address of the Net Box is the factory default value (192.168.1.1).

###### 1

Perform the setting of the robot controller, with the robot controller and the Net Box are not connected through Ethernet cable. If those are connected, remove them once, and connect them again after the setting of the robot controller completes.

###### 2

With the teach pendant, perform the communication setting of the robot controller.

1. Perform the following operation.

   |  |
   | --- |
   | Operation path: Basic screen - [F6 setting] - [F5 Communication and Token] - [F2 Network and Permission] |
2. [Communication Settings] window is displayed. Select "Ethernet".
3. Set as shown in the following table.

   (Items other than below are not required to change)

   |  |  |
   | --- | --- |
   | DHCP | Disable |
   | IP Address | 192.168.1.10 |
   | Subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
4. Click [OK] on the [Communication Settings] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001145_1.png)

Above setting value is an example. If it is inconvenient in your environment in use, set another value that can communicate with the Net Box.

###### 3

This completes the setting.

After connecting the robot controller and the Net Box through an Ethernet cable, configure the force sensor–based force control function. For how to configure the function, refer to ["Parameter Setting”](005466.html).

# Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer

Perform the Ethernet connection setting of a computer so that the computer can communicate with a force sensor through Ethernet.

To do this, you need to know the IP address that is set to the force sensor.

This section describes on the assumption that the IP address of the force sensor is the factory default value (192.168.1.1).

The following explains the operation window of Windows10 as an example.

When an equipment other than the force sensor and the computer is connected through Ethernet network, if the equipment is DHCP server, the IP address of the force sensor may be changed automatically to the address other than above. For DHCP setting of the force sensor, refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx).

###### 1

Perform the computer setting with the computer and the force sensor are not connected through Ethernet cable. If those are connected, remove them once, and connect them again after the computer setting completes.

###### 2

Perform the following operation from your computer’s desktop.

1. Select [Start] button.
2. Select [Setting] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_1.png)

###### 3

Select [Network & Internet].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_2.png)

###### 4

Select [Change adapter options].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_3.png)

###### 5

Select [Ethernet].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_4.png)

###### 6

Select [properties] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_5.png)

###### 7

Perform the following operation.

1. Select [Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)].
2. Select [properties] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_6.png)

###### 8

Perform the following operation.

1. Select [Use the following IP address], and then set the following values to [IP address] and [Subnet mask].

   |  |  |
   | --- | --- |
   | IP address | 192.168.1.100 |
   | Subnet mask | 255.255.255.0 |
2. Select [OK] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001136_7.png)

Above setting value is an example. If it is inconvenient in your environment in use, set another value that can communicate with the force sensor.

This completes the setting.

# Parameter Setting and Communication Setting

Access to the force sensor from the web browser on the computer, and perform the parameter setting and communication setting.

To do this, you need to know the IP address that is set to the force sensor.

This section describes on the assumption that the IP address of the force sensor is the factory default value (192.168.1.1).

###### 1

Confirm that the computer and the force sensor are connected through Ethernet cable.

Confirm that power is supplied to the force sensor.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001147_1.png)

###### 2

Start the browser on the computer and access to the force sensor.

After starting the browser, enter "http://" and the IP address of the force sensor in the address bar, and press Enter key (In this example, enter "http://192.168.1.1").

(The following shows a display example of Internet Explorer)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_6.png)

###### 3

The browser page goes to the welcome page of Net F/T as shown in the following figure.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_7.png)

* If the account ID and password are requested, it might be due to the Proxy setting of computer. Set by the following steps so as not to use the Proxy.

  |  |
  | --- |
  | Windows operation path：[Start] - [Settings] - [Network & Internet] - [Proxy] |
  | (Up to [Network & Internet], it is the same operation as "[Ethernet Connection Setting of Computer](001146.html)") |

  When performing the above operation, the [Proxy] setting window will be displayed. Turn off "Use a proxy server" and click [Save].
* When it does not go to the welcome page after waiting for a while or the welcome page is not displayed correctly, if you press F5 key on the keyboard, it may be displayed correctly.

###### 4

Perform the parameter setting.

Click [Configurations] on the welcome page.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_1.png)

###### 5

1. Set [View Configuration] to "#1 – S1-580-20".
2. Select [GO] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_2.png)

###### 6

Edit the parameter of the subtitle [Configuration #1 (Active configuration)].

1. Confirm that [Calibration Select] is "#1 – FT14685".
2. Set [Force Units] to "N", and [Torque Units] to "N-m".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_8.png)

###### 7

Click [Apply] button at the bottom of the page.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_9.png)

###### 8

Once the window is updated, confirm that the values are "1000000" for [Counts per Force] and [Counts per Torque] in the subtitle [Configuration #1 (Active configuration)].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_10.png)

When the window is not updated after waiting for a while, if you press F5 button on the keyboard, it may be displayed correctly.

###### 9

Perform the communication setting.

Click [Communications] on the welcome page.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_3.png)

###### 10

(If you want to change the IP address of the force sensor, perform this step and then go to the next step). (If you do not change the IP address of the force sensor, skip this step and go to the next step).

Edit the parameter of the subtitle [Ethernet Network Settings].

1. Select "Static" for [IP Address Mode].
2. Set any value for each [Static IP Address], [Static IP Subnet Mask], [Static IP Default Gateway].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_11.png)

###### 11

Edit the parameter of the subtitle [Raw Data Transfer (RDT) Settings].

1. Select "Enabled" for [RDT Interface].
2. Select [Apply] button.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001137_4.png)

This completes the setting.

# Entering IP Address of Force Sensor

To communicate with a force sensor through Ethernet, you need to enter an IP address of the force sensor.

The following shows how to enter an IP address.

###### 1

Operation path : [F2 Arm]-[F2 Force Control]-[F5 Sensor]

Arm auxiliary functions window will be displayed. Press [F2 IP Address Setting]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005467_2.png)

###### 2

Enter IP address of the force sensor and then press [OK] button.  
![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005467_3.png)

### Confirmation of IP Address and Port Number

Press [F1 Sensor Setting] to display [Sensor Setting] window.

Check whether displayed IP address and port number is correct.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005467_4.png)

IP address and port numbers cannot be edited from the [Sensor Setting] window.

### Reconnection of the Force Sensor

When the connection between the robot controller and the force sensor is interrupted, press [F3 Connect Sensor] in the [Sensor] window.

# How to Install a Force Sensor

To install a force sensor to a flange of a robot, the dedicated stay (force sensor mounting stay) needs to be made by customers. Refer to "[Force Sensor Mounting Stay](001134.html)" and the following contents, create the force sensor mounting stay and install it to a flange of a robot.

Dimensions of hole of force sensor
:   For positions and dimensions for the screw hole of force sensor and the hole of dowel pin, refer to the outer dimension drawing in "[ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx)"

Positions of the screw holes of the flange and the force sensor are close
:   Mini40, Mini45 and Nano25 correspond to the case "Positions of the screw holes of the flange and the force sensor are close" that is written in "[Force Sensor Mounting Stay](001134.html)".

Others
:   For information other than above (cable bending radius, handling method), refer to the instruction manual published on [ATI Industrial Automation website](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_ModelListing.aspx).

# Parameter Adjustment

If you use a force sensor, after specifying parameters, you need to adjust the parameters according to your intended operation by using the equipment and the robot that actually performs force control.  
 As required parameters are different between the two functions, refer to an appropriate page according to your intended function when adjusting the parameters.

* If you use Force Sensor Compliance Control, refer to [Procedures for Adjusting Force Sensor Compliance Control](002161.html).
* If you use Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control, refer to [Procedures for Adjusting Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control](001180.html).

Using the monitoring functions for adjusting the parameters allows you to check feedback values from the force sensor and force control logs. For details of the monitoring functions, refer to [this page](001177.html).

# Parameter Settings for Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control

The following describes details of parameter settings.

* Specify the parameters for each force control number (parameter table number for the compliance function), and specify the control mode for each force control number as well.
* The force control is configured in three windows: [Force Control Setting], [Force Control Detailed Setting], and [Sensor Setting].
* The [ForceParam](005176.html) item names are written in [ ] in the “Item name” column.

* Setting the control force to a larger value will cause the robot to move faster. If the robot collides with a workpiece during the high speed operation, the robot or the force sensor may be broken down or damaged by excessive force. To ensure safety, increase the control ratio gradually from smaller to larger, and set the ratio to 0% for the direction of the force that you do not intend to control.

To prevent unexpected operation of the robot, after switching the force control numbers, make sure that the parameters for the switched control number are specified as intended.

## Force Control Setting

Operation path : Top screen - [F2 Arm] - [F2 Force Control] - [F6 Setting]  
 Select a force control number (parameter table number for the compliance function) from 1 to 10, and then press [OK].

| Item name | Unit | Range | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Control mode | - | 0, 1, 3 | Select "3" from the following control modes.  0: Compliance Function  1: Force Sensor Compliance Control  3: Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control |
| Control coordinate  [Coordinates] | - | 0, 1, 2 | Select one of the following coordinate systems.  0: Base coordinates  1: Tool coordinates  2: Work coordinates |
| Control force  [force]  (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ) | N | -5000 to 5000 | Determines the force to control the robot. The output force will not be greater than specified.  Lowering this value will cause the robot to follow the direction of a smaller external force.  Setting this value to 0 will cause the robot to always follow the direction of an external force. |
| Nm | -1000 to 1000 |

## Force Control Detailed Setting

Operation path : Top screen - [F2 Arm] - [F2 Force Control] - [F12 Detail setting]  
 Select a force control number (parameter table number for the compliance function) from 1 to 10, and then press [OK].

| Name | Unit | Range | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Position error allowance  [PosEralw=allowable position deviation]  (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ) | mm | 0 to 1000 | Determines the allowable positional deviation for the tool end.  Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control monitors how much the tool end has moved since the start of force control operation. |
| deg | 0 to 360 |
| Joint error allowance  [Eralw=allowable axis deviation]  (J1 to J8) | deg | 0 to 1000 | Determines the allowable deviation value for each axis.  Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control monitors how much each axis has moved since the start of force control operation.  The parameter is invalid if specified for an auxiliary axis. |
| Control rate  [Rate=control rate]  (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ) | % | 0 to 100 | Determines the rate of force control applied when Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control is used.  Basically, set the ratio to 100% for the direction of the force that you intend to control. Set the rate to 0% for the direction of the force that you do not intend to control. |
| Max speed  [SpMax=maximum translation speed] | mm/s | 0 to 10000 | Determines the maximum speed to be applied until the robot contacts an object. |
| Maximum rotation speed  [RSpMax=maximum rotation speed] | deg/s | 0 to 10000 | Determines the maximum rotational speed to be applied until the robot contacts an object. |
| Stiffness level of the contact object (X, Y, Z) |  | 0 to 3 | Determines the stiffness level of a contacted object when force is applied to the direction of each axis (X, Y, Z) in the selected coordinate system.  0: Stiffness level 0  1: Stiffness level 1  2: Stiffness level 2  3: Stiffness level 3  Setting a higher stiffness level enables the robot to respond to a stiffer object.  In adjusting this parameter, start from the initial value "3". |
| Stiffness level of the contact object (Rx, Ry, Rz) |  | 0 to 1 | Determines the stiffness level of a contacted object when force is applied to the rotational direction of each axis (X, Y, Z) in the selected coordinate system.  0: Stiffness level 0  1: Stiffness level 1  Increasing the stiffness level enables the robot to respond to a stiffer object.  In adjusting this parameter, start from the initial value "1". |

### Parameter adjustable only with Maintainer

If you log in with Maintainer, you can configure the following parameters in addition to the parameters in the table above.

| Item name | Unit | Range | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Opt mode | - | 0, 8 | Not used for Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control. |

### Parameter adjustable only in WINCAPSIII

The following parameter can be specified only in WINCAPSIII.

| Item name | Unit | Range | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Phase Shift Time  (X, Y, Z, RX, RY, RZ) | sec | 0– | Not used for Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control. |

## Sensor Settings

Operation path : Top screen - [F2 Arm] - [F2 Force Control] - [F5 Sensor] - [F1 Sensor Setting]  
 If the output values of the force sensor exceed “Contact detect force” or “Contact detect moment”, the force control will start based on the specified “control force”. In this page, assume that the force control starts when the robot is in contact with an object.

| Item name | Unit | Range | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Contact detect force for robust compliance control | N | 0– | When the absolute value from the force sensor exceeds this value, the force control starts based on "control force".  Set this value to less than "control force". |
| Contact detect moment for robust compliance control | Nm | 0– | When the absolute value from the force sensor exceeds this value, the force control starts based on "control force".  Set this value to less than "control force". |

* The robot always performs a compliant motion in the direction for which "control force” is set to 0. Therefore, the robot always operates with the force control working regardless of the parameter values specified in the [Sensor Setting] window.
* Set “contact detect force” and “contact detect moment” to the values equal to or greater than noises of the force sensor. If the parameters are set to the values less than the noises, the function fails to correctly detect a contact with an object.

### Contact with an object

Activating Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control will cause the robot to perform a non-force-controlled motion until a contact with an object is detected from the output values of the sensor.  
 The speed of non-force-controlled motion is determined by the following formula based on the specified value of "[maximum translation speed](#ID005469_maxspeed)" or "[maximum rotation speed](#ID005469_maxRspeed)", and "[control rate](#ID005469_control)".

* Non-force-controlled motion speed = (maximum translation speed or maximum rotation speed) × control rate

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001179_1.png)

As the robot moves at the non-force-controlled motion speed calculated from the specified parameters regardless of its internal and external speeds, it may move at high speed if the parameters are specified improperly. Be careful when specifying the parameters.

To change the speed of the robot motion, change the values of "[maximum translation speed](#ID005469_maxspeed)” or "[maximum rotation speed](#ID005469_maxRspeed)”, and "[control rate](#ID005469_control)". These parameters are described in "[Force Control Detailed Setting](#ID005469_Forcecontroldetails)".

# Procedures for Adjusting Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control

To configure Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control, change the value of the parameter "stiffness level of the contact object".

* The parameter “stiffness level of the contact object” can be changed with the teach pendant and WINCAPSIII. However, using both of the methods may confuse you and cause a risk of improper configuration. To prevent this, we recommend you to use only either of the methods.
* Parameters other than “stiffness level of the contact object” can be changed with both the teach pendant and commands. However, using both of the methods may confuse you and cause a risk of improper configuration. To prevent this, we recommend you to use only either of the methods.
* If a direction you intend to control and a direction specified by a robot motion command (such as Move command) as a robot motion direction are the same, the force control cannot be performed as you have specified by the control force, control rate and virtual damper. In this case, move a robot to the position where the control starts, and then skip the robot motion command with MotionSkip command.

## How to Adjust the Parameter

Adjust “stiffness level of the contact object” using the actual robot so that your desired amplitude and convergence time can be achieved.  
 Execute an actual operation and adjust the parameter to achieve your desired vibration and convergence time.

In adjusting the parameter, make sure that the following two conditions shown in the table below are satisfied.

You can check the amplitude and convergence time using force control logs.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001180_1.png)

| Number | Check points |
| --- | --- |
| (1) | The amplitude converges within the positive and negative allowable ranges of the target value that you have planned. |
| (2) | The vibration properly converges within the planned duration. |

For details of force control logs, refer to “[Acquiring, Displaying and Saving Force Control Log](005592.html)”.

### Correlation between stiffness level of the contact object, amplitude, and convergence time

If you change "stiffness level of the contact object", the responsiveness to "control force" will change as indicated in the table below.

| Stiffness level of the contact object | Convergence time | Amplitude |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Increase | Long | Small |
| Decrease | Short | Large |

### Precautions for adjustment

If the specified "stiffness level of the contact object" causes vibration, this means that the force control is failing.  
 Do not set "stiffness level of the contact object" to the level that causes vibration or lower.

Lowering "stiffness level of the contact object" excessively may cause the robot to be unstable and vibrate.

# Example Program of Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control

The following is an example program.

## Description of the Example Program

1. This is an example program for a fitting operation.
2. Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control is started when the robot brings a workpiece to the start position of the force control.
3. The force sensor value is reset (0N, 0Nm) when the force control starts.
4. Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control ends when the robot has moved the workpiece a predetermined distance.

## Example

```
Sub Main
'!TITLE "Fitting operation"
'
' Position to get workpiece		P[1]
' Force control starting position		P[2] 
' Once this travel distance is achieved, force control ends	F[1]

  Dim startPos As Position
  Dim rotStartPos As Position
  Dim snsrVal As Position
	
  TakeArm Keep = 0
  
  Move P, @e P[1]				'Position to get workpiece
  
  Delay 100
  
  hand0.Chuck 1					'Hand chuck
  
  Delay 100
  
  Move P, @e P[2]				'Starting position
	
  startPos = CurPos				'Set the current position as a starting position
  
  ForceSensor 0					'Reset sensor
  
  Delay 500
	
  ForceCtrl True, 1, Mode = 3			'Start Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control
	
  Do
  
  snsrVal = ForceValue(0)			'Acquire the sensor value
  
  'Condition for motion end
  'Wait until the tool end moves F1 mm from the force control starting position
        				
  If (Abs(PosZ(*)-PosZ(startPos)) > F[1]) Then GoTo StopProc 
  
  Loop
	
  StopProc:
  		
  ForceCtrl False				'End the force control
  
  hand0.Unchuck 0				'Hand unchuck
  
End Sub
```

# Connecting Robot Controller

Controller and robot are connected by the motor & encoder cable.

Make sure that the power of controller is OFF before starting settings.

## Connection in Robot Side

###### 1

Check and match the right and left side of connector of the motor & encoder cable and connector of the robot.

The connector cannot be plugged in if it connected wrong way.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001187_1.png)

###### 2

Insert the motor and encoder cable’s connector straight into the robot’s connector.

* The motor and encoder cable’s connector has a tab on each left and right side. These tabs ensure the sealing of the two connectors when fitted into the robot’s connector.
* Make sure that both tabs on the left and right sides click when fitted into the robot’s connector.
* In addition, move the cable’s connector left and right to confirm that the tabs have been fitted into the robot’s connector. (Refer to Figure 1.) If only one of the tabs is fitted into the robot’s connector, the cable’s connector will be significantly tilted. (Refer to Figure 2.)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001187_2.png)　![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001187_3.png)

## Connection in Controller Side

Refer to "[Connecting Robot](001339.html)" of RC8 SERIES ROBOT CONTROLLER MANUAL.

ID : 1189

# Resetting the Login Passwords

## Function Description

To reset the login passwords for the robot controller.

* The function resets the login passwords for the robot controller, not for WINCAPSⅢ.
* The function is available in Ver.2.16.\* or higher.

## Operation Procedure

###### 1

Start WINCAPSⅢ.

For details, refer to “[Starting Up/Shutting Down](004355.html)”.

###### 2

Press [Password reset] from [RC8 tools] in the [Tool] menu.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001189_1.png)

###### 3

Enter the IP address of the intended robot controller in the displayed IP address entry window, and then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001189_2.png)

###### 4

The following confirmation message appears. Press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001189_3.png)

###### 5

The following completion message appears. Press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001189_4.png)

Resetting the login passwords will restore them to the default. If you change a login password, enter the following default password in [Current password].

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| [Operator] | 5593551 |
| [Programmer] | 5596045 |
| [Maintainer] | 5596060 |

ID : 1191

# Consideration for Disposal

## Robot and Controller

When disposing of the robot, controller, and other products, treat them as industrial waste in compliance with the national and local laws and regulations.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Battery

The robot and controller contain lithium primary batteries.

| Battery type | |
| --- | --- |
| Robot | ER17500 (lithium thionyl chloride battery) |
| Controller | CR17335 (lithium manganese dioxide battery) |

When disposing of or recycling the batteries, observe the national and local laws, regulations, and instructions on recycling.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

### How to remove the battery

* VM robot: Refer to [here](000895.html).
* RC8 robot controller: Refer to [here](img/001191/001191_4.pdf).
* RC8A robot controller: Refer to [here](img/001191/001191_5.pdf).

In addition, observe the following precautions for disposal and recycling of batteries.

1. Batteries may present a risk of fire or chemical burn if mistreated. Do not recharge, disassemble, heat above 100℃ (212°F), or incinerate.
2. Dispose of or recycle a used battery promptly. Keep away from children. Do not disassemble and do not dispose of in fire.
3. Do not dispose of or recycle uninsulated batteries together with metals and any conductive items. Doing so may cause fire or explosion. Before disposing of or recycling batteries, make sure to insulate them by sealing their terminals with insulation tapes or other appropriate ways.

### Battery in optional devices / functions

IPC set for RC8 extension function contains a battery. For how to remove the battery, refer to "[How to Replace the Battery of IPC Set for RC8 Extension Function](002715.html)".

### Handling Batteries

* For how to handle lithium thionyl chloride batteries, refer to "[here (PDF)](img/000990/Precautions for battery.pdf)".
* The instructions for handling lithium manganese dioxide batteries are written in the service manuals. Contact our [service](001078.html) representatives.

ID : 1198

# Consideration for Disposal

## Robot and Controller

When disposing of the robot, controller, and other products, treat them as industrial waste in compliance with the national and local laws and regulations.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Battery

The robot and controller contain lithium primary batteries.

| Battery type | |
| --- | --- |
| Robot | ER17500 (lithium thionyl chloride battery) |
| Controller | CR17335 (lithium manganese dioxide battery) |

When disposing of or recycling the batteries, observe the national and local laws, regulations, and instructions on recycling.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

### How to remove the battery

* HSA1 robot: Refer to [here](002942.html).
* RC8 robot controller: Refer to [here](img/001198/001198_4.pdf).
* RC8A robot controller: Refer to [here](img/001198/001198_5.pdf).

In addition, observe the following precautions for disposal and recycling of batteries.

1. Batteries may present a risk of fire or chemical burn if mistreated. Do not recharge, disassemble, heat above 100℃ (212°F), or incinerate.
2. Dispose of or recycle a used battery promptly. Keep away from children. Do not disassemble and do not dispose of in fire.
3. Do not dispose of or recycle uninsulated batteries together with metals and any conductive items. Doing so may cause fire or explosion. Before disposing of or recycling batteries, make sure to insulate them by sealing their terminals with insulation tapes or other appropriate ways.

### Battery in optional devices / functions

IPC set for RC8 extension function contains a battery. For how to remove the battery, refer to "[How to Replace the Battery of IPC Set for RC8 Extension Function](002715.html)".

### Handling Batteries

* For how to handle lithium thionyl chloride batteries, refer to "[here (PDF)](img/000990/Precautions for battery.pdf)".
* The instructions for handling lithium manganese dioxide batteries are written in the service manuals. Contact our [service](001078.html) representatives.

# Robot Mount

The robot mount should be rigid enough. It is also advisable to mechanically join the robot mount with heavy equipment.

Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling). If the sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or slightly modify the robot speed.

## Maximum Reaction Force Applied to the Robot Mount

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001201_1.PNG)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Overturning moment Ml: | 3553 Nm |
| Torsional moment Mt: | 5178 Nm |
| Horizontal translational force Fh: | 14918 N |
| Vertical translational force Fv: | 2596 N |

Design the top plate structure so that it is independent from other top plate structures in the equipment.

# Classification of Users

When using a robot, classify the users as indicated below and make them take training necessary in their own classifications.

* Install robots and related devices in compliance with laws and regulations of each country and region.
* When transporting, installing, teaching, adjusting and maintaining, you need to wear protective gears (working clothes, safety shoes, safety glasses, hard hat and gloves) applicable to work, with keeping safety in mind.

## User Types

Users are classified into the following three types. Below is the scope of operations available to each user type.

### Operator

* An operator turns a robot on/off.
* An operator starts a robot program from the control panel.

### Programmer

* A programmer can perform what the operator can perform.
* A programmer can move a robot manually and put the positions into the memory.
* A programmer can create and edit the robot program.
* A programmer can check the connection with the peripheral devices of the robot and correct the connection setting.
* A programmer can work inside the safety fences, only when the following conditions are met.

  + A programmer has taken the robot operation training.
  + Safety measures when the worker operates inside the safety fences have been taken by risk assessment.

### Maintainer

* A maintainer can perform what the programmer can perform.
* A maintainer can transport, install, and remove the robot.
* A maintainer can move a robot manually.
* When an error occurs with a robot, the maintainer can eliminate the cause and bring it back to the operating status.
* A maintainer can work inside the safety fences, only when the following conditions are met.

  + A maintainer has taken the robot operation training.
  + Safety measures when the worker operates inside the safety fences have been taken by risk assessment.

## Training Required for Users in Each User Type

Following table indicates the training required for the operators, programmers, and maintainers.

| Operator | Programmer | Maintainer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Safety training of machinery including robots | | |
| - | Training to make the work of programmers to be performed safely | Training to make the work of maintainers to be performed safely |
| - | | Maintenance training of robots |

## Points to Consider

In handling the robot, take training necessary for your intended user type based on the comparison between the intended work and the scope of operations available to each user type that is shown above.

# Safety Performance of the Safety Functions

This page describes the safety performance of the safety functions.

The following are calculated under the worst conditions. In addition, the calculation is made under the condition that the mission time is 20 years.

## Safety Performance of the Safety Functions

### Safe Torque Off (STO)

| MTTFD  (year) | DCavg  (%) | PFH | PFDAV | PL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 163.2 | 99 | 5.31× 10-10 | 4.63 × 10-5 | e |

| MTTFD  (year) | DCavg  (%) | PFH | PFDAV | PL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

# What to Do After Using the Mirror Control Function

After using the Mirror Control function, perform the following for COBOTTA.

* EMGStop Confirm
* SLS Confirm

Master Control cannot be disabled unless EMGStop Confirm is executed.

Operation path: [F6 Setting] - [F10 COBOTTA] - [F8 Master Control] - [F4 EMGStop Confirm]/[F5 SLS Confirm]

## EMGStop Confirm

Before disabling the Master Control function, execute EMGStop Confirm.

###### 1

Press [F4 EMGStop Confirm] on the [Master Control] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_4.png)

###### 2

Press the Emergency Stop button for COBOTTA, and then press [OK] on the system message.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_5.png)

###### 3

Press [OK] on the displayed confirmation message.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_6.png)

###### 4

After executing EMGStop Confirm, disable Master Control.

Press [F1 Enable/Disable] on the [Master Control] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_7.png)

###### 5

Press [OK] on the displayed system message.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_8.png)

Next, execute SLS Confirm.

## SLS Confirm

###### 1

Press [F5 SLS Confirm] on the [Master Control] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_1.png)

###### 2

A system message appears. Send the SLS set values displayed on the message using the COBOTTA parameter tool, and then press [OK].

If you press [OK] before sending the SLS set values using the COBOTTA parameter tool, SLS Confirm will not be executed properly. In this case, start over from STEP1.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_2.png)

###### 3

Press [OK] on the displayed confirmation message.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001208_3.png)

###### 4

Set the external speed to 100% and operate all the axes of COBOTTA manually one by one to check if an over-speed error occurs. When checking for an error, move each axis approximately at the following angles.

| Axis | Angle |
| --- | --- |
| J1 | 20 deg |
| J2 | 20 deg |
| J3 | 30 deg |
| J4 | 35 deg |
| J5 | 90 deg |
| J6 | 270 deg |

After checking all the axes, send a speed monitoring threshold you want to set using the COBOTTA parameter tool.

This completes the procedure to follow after using the Mirror Control function.

# Robot Mount

## Maximum Reaction Force Applied to the Robot Mount

This page shows the maximum reaction force generated on the robot installation surface when the robot moves.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001209_1.png)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Overturning moment Ml: | 2006 Nm |
| Torsional moment Mt: | 2947 Nm |
| Horizontal translational force Fh: | 1538 N |
| Vertical translational force Fv: | 2433 N |

### Example of a Mount for a Floor-Mounted Robot

|  |
| --- |
|  |

1. When a robot operates at high speed, the robot mount undergoes large reaction forces. The mount must be rigid enough so that it will not vibrate or be displaced due to reaction forces. It is also advisable to mechanically join the robot mount with heavy equipment.
2. Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling). If this sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or slightly modify the robot speed.

### Example of a Mount for an Overhead-Mounted Robot

|  |
| --- |
|  |

1. When an overhead-mounted robot operates at high speed, the top plate structure undergoes large reaction forces. Design a vibration-proof mount so that its top plate will not vibrate due to the reaction force. In addition, ensure that the top plate for robot installation is structurally separate and independent from other part of the robot system/cell.
2. Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling). If this sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or modify the robot speed.

# Wiring an I/O cable to a GigE Camera

This page describes how to wire an I/O cable for vision tracking with a GigE camera manufactured by Basler.

## GigE Camera Connections and I/O Cable Pin Assignment

* Image of GigE camera connections and I/O cable

  | GigE Camera Connections | I/O Cable |
  | --- | --- |
  |  | Name: Basler Power-I/O Cable, HRS 6p/open, S |
  |  |
* Pin assignment and signal name (camera specifications: for acA2500-14gc)

  The pin assignment differs depending on the camera specifications. For details, refer to the Basler [website](https://docs.baslerweb.com/).

  | Terminal Number | Line | Signal Name |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 1 | ⁻ | 12 DVC camera power |
  | 2 | Line 1 | Opto-coupled I/O input line |
  | 3 | - | Not connected |
  | 4 | Out 1 | Opto-coupled I/O output line |
  | 5 | - | Ground for opto-coupled I/O lines |
  | 6 | - | Ground for camera power |

## I/O Cable Wiring

The following are the available I/O terminal numbers.

* For NPN type

  | Camera I/O Terminal Number | Mini I/O Terminal Number |
  | --- | --- |
  | 4 | 19 to 26 (User input) |
  | 5 | 66 to 68 (DC power source input/output 0V) |
* For PNP type

  | Camera I/O Terminal Number | Mini I/O Terminal Number |
  | --- | --- |
  | 5 | 19 to 26 (User input) |
  | 4 | 32 to 34 (DC power source input/output +24V) |

For information about the vision tracking configuration, refer to "[How to Configure Vision Tracking](001215.html)".

# How to Configure Vision Tracking

This page describes how to configure vision tracking when using EVP2.

Configure it using the pylon Viewer.

###### 1

From the Windows Start menu, open [Basler] - [Pylon Viewer].

###### 2

Click [Connect].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_1.png)

###### 3

Select the camera you want to connect.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_2.png)

###### 4

Open the camera table you selected under "Feature" and click [Digital I/O Controls].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_3.png)

###### 5

Select a Line that has the function of "Opto-coupled I/O output line" under "Line Selector". (\*1)

Next, set "Line Mode" to [Output].

\*1) For details of the Line that has the function of "Opto-coupled I/O output line", refer to "[GigE Camera Connections and I/O Cable Pin Assignment](001214.html#ID001214_GigECamera_Pin)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_4.png)

###### 6

Set "Line Format" to [Opto-coupled] and "Line Source" to [Exposure Active].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_5.png)

###### 7

Open "Configuration Sets".

Set "Configuration Set Selector" and "Default Startup Set" to [User Set 1], and set "User Set Load" and "User Set Save" to [Execute].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_6.png)

###### 8

Click [Execute] under "User Set Save".

Unless the [Execute] is clicked, the settings will be canceled.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_7.png)

This completes the vision tracking configuration.

# Checking the I/O Signal of Vision Tracking

The following two procedures are available to check the I/O output signal for vision tracking.

* Shoot with EVP2.
* Shoot with a GigE camera after performing the following steps with the pylon Viewer.

  ###### 1

  Click [Single Shot].

  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_8.png)

  ###### 2

  Set "Trigger Mode" to [On] and click [Execute] under "Generate Software Trigger".

  Unless the [Execute] is clicked, the settings will be canceled.

  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001215_9.png)

To perform vision tracking, configuring I/O settings on a controller is necessary. The operation procedure is different between "[Circular Tracking](003055.html)" and "[Conveyor Tracking](002219.html)". For detailed operation procedures, refer to the following.

* For the circle tracking, refer to "[I/O Setting](002884.html)".
* For the conveyor tracking, refer to "[I/O Setting](005358.html)".

# MC\_ChangeScene

To change the current scene to a sub scene.

| Graphic expression | FB number | FB category |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | FB2048 | Motion |

## Input Variable

| Parameter name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | Integer | 1 or larger | 1 | No |
| Robot number  Specify an element number for the variable "Robots[n]" (variable in the data block "DB\_DENSO\_ROBOTS (DB2990)") mapped to the controlled robot (robot controller).  If a specified value exceeds the valid range, the CPU (PLC) stops. The maximum valid range value is the maximum element number of the variable "Robots[n]". The default maximum element number is 10 but can be increased or decreased by the user. | | | |
| Execute | Boolean | * True : Start * False : - | False | No |
| Execution start  When the parameter is changed from False to True, this FB is executed. | | | |
| SceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 | 0 | Yes |
| Scene number  Specify a scene number. | | | |
| SubSceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 | 0 | Yes |
| Sub scene number  Specify a sub scene number. | | | |

(\*) : For some parameters, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Parameter name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  True : This FB execution is completed.  False : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  True : Being executed.  False : Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  True : This FB ended abnormally.  False : This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Word |
| Error location  2800 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DWord |
| Error Code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](002999.html)". |

## Function Description

Changes the current scene to a sub scene.

Before executing the command, move the TCP to the SafetyP position or area where you have specified by the scene parameter [Scene switching condition (Position) SafetyP type number].

During the command execution, robot motion differs depending on the following scene parameter setting of the specified scene. For details of the scene parameters, refer to "Scene Parameter Setting" in the description of each function.

### Scene switching condition (Stop monitoring)

0: Disable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the command value. Therefore, the scene could be changed even if the robot is in motion.

1: Enable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the encoder value. Therefore, the scene will be changed after confirming that the robot is completely stopped.

## Attention

To execute this FB, FB with the FB category "Motion" needs to be made executable.  
 To make FB with the FB category "Motion" executable, use the FB "[MC\_Power](002990.html)".

If any scene number set to [0: Disable] is specified in the scene parameter [Scene enable/disable setting] of the specified scene during the command execution, an error will occur.  
 If a program executing this command encountered a reset stop, the scene will be switched to the default scene in Auto mode and to the manual mode scene in Manual mode.

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# MC\_SetSlowSpdChk

To enable the Auto mode slow-speed check.

| Graphic expression | FB number | FB category |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | FB2049 | Motion |

## Input Variable

| Parameter name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | Integer | 1 or larger | 1 | No |
| Robot number  Specify an element number for the variable "Robots[n]" (variable in the data block "DB\_DENSO\_ROBOTS (DB2990)") mapped to the controlled robot (robot controller).  If a specified value exceeds the valid range, the CPU (PLC) stops. The maximum valid range value is the maximum element number of the variable "Robots[n]". The default maximum element number is 10 but can be increased or decreased by the user. | | | |
| Execute | Boolean | * True : Start * False : - | False | No |
| Execution start  When the parameter is changed from False to True, this FB is executed. | | | |

(\*) : For some parameters, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Parameter name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  True : This FB execution is completed.  False : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  True : Being executed.  False : Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  True : This FB ended abnormally.  False : This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Word |
| Error location  2800 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DWord |
| Error Code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](002999.html)". |

## Function Description

Enables the Auto mode slow-speed check.

When this function is enabled, the speed of a monitored point on the robot is reduced to ensure that it does not exceed the value specified in the "Auto mode slow check speed" of the scene parameter. Be sure to check the robot motion at low speed using this function before operating at high speed.

## Attention

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

## Input Variable

| Parameter name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | Integer | 1 or larger | 1 | No |
| Robot number  Specify an element number for the variable "Robots[n]" (variable in the data block "DB\_DENSO\_ROBOTS (DB2990)") mapped to the controlled robot (robot controller).  If a specified value exceeds the valid range, the CPU (PLC) stops. The maximum valid range value is the maximum element number of the variable "Robots[n]". The default maximum element number is 10 but can be increased or decreased by the user. | | | |
| Execute | Boolean | * True : Start * False : - | False | No |
| Execution start  When the parameter is changed from False to True, this FB is executed. | | | |

(\*) : For some parameters, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Parameter name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  True : This FB execution is completed.  False : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |

## Function Description

Executes Manual Reset.

When the robot controller is in the Manual Reset–Ready state, Manual Reset will be executed.  
 When the robot controller is in the Safety state, an error will occur.  
 When the robot controller is in neither the Manual Reset–Ready state nor the Safety state, no action will be executed.

 For example, ensure that this FB is executed when an operator presses a button on the control panel.

# MC\_ChangeScene

To change the current scene to a sub scene.

| Graphic expression | AOI category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Conditions for Input and Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007523.html) | | - |
| Robot group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data: eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE: Start * FALSE: - |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this AOI is executed. | |
| SceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 |
| Scene number  Specify a scene number. | |
| SubSceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 |
| Sub scene number  Specify a sub scene number. | |

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE: This AOI execution is completed.  FALSE: This AOI execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this AOI  TRUE: Being executed.  FALSE: Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE: This AOI ended abnormally.  FALSE: This AOI ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Integer |
| Error location  2800: The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801: The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DInt |
| Error code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007495.html)". |

## Function Description

Changes the current scene to a sub scene.

Before executing the command, move the TCP to the SafetyP position or area where you have specified by the scene parameter [Scene switching condition (Position) SafetyP type number].

During the command execution, robot motion differs depending on the following scene parameter setting of the specified scene. For details of the scene parameters, refer to "Scene Parameter Setting" in the description of each function.

### Scene switching condition (Stop monitoring)

0: Disable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the command value. Therefore, the scene could be changed even if the robot is in motion.

1: Enable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the encoder value. Therefore, the scene will be changed after confirming that the robot is completely stopped.

## Attention

To execute this AOI, AOI with the AOI category "Motion" needs to be made executable.  
 To make AOI with the AOI category "Motion" executable, use the AOI "[MC\_Power](007342.html)".

If any scene number set to [0: Disable] is specified in the scene parameter [Scene enable/disable setting] of the specified scene during the command execution, an error will occur.  
 If a program executing this command encountered a reset stop, the scene will be switched to the default scene in Auto mode and to the manual mode scene in Manual mode.

This AOI is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# MC\_SetSlowSpdChk

To enable the Auto mode slow-speed check.

| Graphic expression | AOI category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Conditions for Input and Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007523.html) | | - |
| Robot group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data: eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE: Start * FALSE: - |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this AOI is executed. | |

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE: This AOI execution is completed.  FALSE: This AOI execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this AOI  TRUE: Being executed.  FALSE: Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE: This AOI ended abnormally.  FALSE: This AOI ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Integer |
| Error location  2800: The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801: The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DInt |
| Error code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007495.html)". |

## Function Description

Enables the Auto mode slow-speed check.

When this function is enabled, the speed of a monitored point on the robot is reduced to ensure that it does not exceed the value specified in the "Auto mode slow check speed" of the scene parameter. Be sure to check the robot motion at low speed using this function before operating at high speed.

## Attention

This AOI is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

## Input Variable

| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this AOI is executed. | |

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE: This AOI execution is completed.  FALSE: This AOI execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this AOI  TRUE: Being executed.  FALSE: Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE: This AOI ended abnormally.  FALSE: This AOI ended successfully. |

## Function Description

Executes Manual Reset.

When the robot controller is in the Manual Reset–Ready state, Manual Reset will be executed.  
 When the robot controller is in the Safety state, an error will occur.  
 When the robot controller is in neither the Manual Reset–Ready state nor the Safety state, no action will be executed.

## Attention

To execute this AOI, be sure to have an operator execute the operation.  
 For example, ensure that this AOI is executed when an operator presses a button on the control panel.

This function is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# Using a Hypersen Force Sensor

This page describes the devices necessary for the force sensor-based force control function when a force sensor manufactured by Hypersen is used.

## Available Force Sensor

The HPS-FT series force sensor manufactured by Hypersen can be used.

For details of the force sensor, refer to the instruction manual of "HPS-FT Series". The instruction manual can be downloaded from [the website of Hypersen Technologies Co.](https://en.hypersen.com).

## Available Robot Controllers

The Hypersen force sensors can be used with robot controllers that meet all of the following conditions.

* The engine board in the [Controller Type](001314.html) is Type "E" or Type "C".
* The robot controller software version is 2.22.\* or higher.

# System Configuration

This page describes the devices necessary for the force control function when a force sensor manufactured by Hypersen is used.

## System Configuration

The following figure shows the system configuration.

You need to prepare the components 1 to 4.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001232_1.png)

| No. | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Force Sensor (HPS-FT series) | A force sensor manufactured by Hypersen. |
| 2 | Ethernet adapter (HPS-FT-EN2000-IO) | An Ethernet adapter manufactured by Hypersen. A communication device that connects the robot controller and the force sensor. |
| 3 | Power supply (24V DC) | A device that supplies power to an Ethernet adapter. |
| 4 | LAN cable | A cable that connects the robot controller and an Ethernet adaptor. |
| 5 | Software license | Licenses for expanding the functions of the robot controller.  The force sensor–based force control function is classified into two types: "Force Sensor Compliance Control" and "Force Sensor Robust Compliance Control".   Select a license for the type of function that you intend to use. |

## Software License

If you select "Built-in with License", a robot set will be shipped with the force control function enabled. When ordering a robot set, inform us whether you select "Built-in with License" or only "License".

If you intend to use the force control function with a robot set you have already purchased, select only "License". If you select only "License", you need to register a license and activate the function using your robot controller.

For instructions on how to activate the function, refer to "[Activating the Function](005932.html)".

| Item / Specifications | Part No. |

# MC\_ChangeScene

To change the current scene to a sub scene.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Conditions for Input and Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007871.html) | | - |
| Robot group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data: eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE: Start * FALSE: - |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | |
| SceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 |
| Scene number  Specify a scene number. | |
| SubSceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 |
| Sub scene number  Specify a sub scene number. | |

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE: This FB execution is completed.  FALSE: This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE: Being executed.  FALSE: Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE: This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE: This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Integer |
| Error location  2800: The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801: The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DInt |
| Error code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007870.html)". |

## Function Description

Changes the current scene to a sub scene.

Before executing the command, move the TCP to the SafetyP position or area where you have specified by the scene parameter [Scene switching condition (Position) SafetyP type number].

During the command execution, robot motion differs depending on the following scene parameter setting of the specified scene. For details of the scene parameters, refer to "Scene Parameter Setting" in the description of each function.

### Scene switching condition (Stop monitoring)

0: Disable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the command value. Therefore, the scene could be changed even if the robot is in motion.

1: Enable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the encoder value. Therefore, the scene will be changed after confirming that the robot is completely stopped.

## Attention

To execute this FB, FB with the FB category "Motion" needs to be made executable.  
 To make FB with the FB category "Motion" executable, use the FB "[MC\_Power](007717.html)".

If any scene number set to [0: Disable] is specified in the scene parameter [Scene enable/disable setting] of the specified scene during the command execution, an error will occur.  
 If a program executing this command encountered a reset stop, the scene will be switched to the default scene in Auto mode and to the manual mode scene in Manual mode.

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.
