# MC\_SetSlowSpdChk

To enable the Auto mode slow-speed check.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Conditions for Input and Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007871.html) | | - |
| Robot group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data: eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE: Start * FALSE: - |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | |

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE: This FB execution is completed.  FALSE: This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE: Being executed.  FALSE: Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE: This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE: This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Integer |
| Error location  2800: The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801: The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DInt |
| Error code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007870.html)". |

## Function Description

Enables the Auto mode slow-speed check.

When this function is enabled, the speed of a monitored point on the robot is reduced to ensure that it does not exceed the value specified in the "Auto mode slow check speed" of the scene parameter. Be sure to check the robot motion at low speed using this function before operating at high speed.

## Attention

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# MC\_ManualReset

To execute Manual Reset.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Non motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Conditions for Input and Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007871.html) | | - |
| Robot group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data: eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE: Start * FALSE: - |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | |

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE: This FB execution is completed.  FALSE: This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE: Being executed.  FALSE: Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE: This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE: This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Integer |
| Error location  2800: The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801: The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DInt |
| Error code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007870.html)". |

## Function Description

Executes Manual Reset.

When the robot controller is in the Manual Reset–Ready state, Manual Reset will be executed.  
 When the robot controller is in the Safety state, an error will occur.  
 When the robot controller is in neither the Manual Reset–Ready state nor the Safety state, no action will be executed.

## Attention

To execute this FB, be sure to have an operator execute the operation.  
 For example, ensure that this FB is executed when an operator presses a button on the control panel.

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

ID : 1266

# MC\_ChangeScene

To change the current scene to a sub scene.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007708.html) | | | No |
| Robot Group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data : eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE : Start * FALSE : - | FALSE | No |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | | | |
| SceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 | 0 | No |
| Scene number  Specify a scene number. | | | |
| SubSceneNum | Integer | 0 to 9 | 0 | No |
| Sub scene number  Specify a sub scene number. | | | |

(\*) : For some Variable, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE : This FB execution is completed.  FALSE : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE : Being executed.  FALSE : Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE : This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE : This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Word |
| Error location  2800 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DWord |
| Error Code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007684.html)". |

## Function Description

Changes the current scene to a sub scene.

Before executing the command, move the TCP to the SafetyP position or area where you have specified by the scene parameter [Scene switching condition (Position) SafetyP type number].

During the command execution, robot motion differs depending on the following scene parameter setting of the specified scene. For details of the scene parameters, refer to "Scene Parameter Setting" in the description of each function.

### Scene switching condition (Stop monitoring)

0: Disable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the command value. Therefore, the scene could be changed even if the robot is in motion.

1: Enable
:   Selecting this option judges the robot stop by the encoder value. Therefore, the scene will be changed after confirming that the robot is completely stopped.

## Attention

To execute this FB, FB with the FB category "Motion" needs to be made executable.  
To make FB with the FB category "Motion" executable, use the FB ["MC\_Power"](007531.html).

If any scene number set to [0: Disable] is specified in the scene parameter [Scene enable/disable setting] of the specified scene during the command execution, an error will occur.  
If a program executing this command encountered a reset stop, the scene will be switched to the default scene in Auto mode and to the manual mode scene in Manual mode.

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# MC\_SetSlowSpdChk

To enable the Auto mode slow-speed check.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Non Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007708.html) | | | No |
| Robot Group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data : eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE : Start * FALSE : - | FALSE | No |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | | | |

(\*) : For some Variable, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE : This FB execution is completed.  FALSE : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE : Being executed.  FALSE : Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE : This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE : This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Word |
| Error location  2800 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DWord |
| Error Code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007684.html)". |

## Function Description

Enables the Auto mode slow-speed check.

When this function is enabled, the speed of a monitored point on the robot is reduced to ensure that it does not exceed the value specified in the "Auto mode slow check speed" of the scene parameter. Be sure to check the robot motion at low speed using this function before operating at high speed.

## Attention

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# MC\_ManualReset

To execute Manual Reset.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007708.html) | | | No |
| Robot Group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data : eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE : Start * FALSE : - | FALSE | No |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | | | |

(\*) : For some Variable, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE : This FB execution is completed.  FALSE : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE : Being executed.  FALSE : Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE : This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE : This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Word |
| Error location  2800 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DWord |
| Error Code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007684.html)". |

## Function Description

Executes Manual Reset.

When the robot controller is in the Manual Reset–Ready state, Manual Reset will be executed.  
When the robot controller is in the Safety state, an error will occur.  
When the robot controller is in neither the Manual Reset–Ready state nor the Safety state, no action will be executed.

## Attention

To execute this FB, be sure to have an operator execute the operation.  
For example, ensure that this FB is executed when an operator presses a button on the control panel.

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# MC\_ReadSafePosVar

To call a SafetyP-type variable stored in the robot controller.

| Graphic expression | FB category |
| --- | --- |
|  | Non Motion |

## Input and Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AxesGroup | [eRC\_AxesGroup](007708.html) | | | No |
| Robot Group  Specify a robot variable (structured type data : eRC\_AxesGroup) of user-defined type. | | | |

## Input Variable

| Variable name | Data type | Valid range | Default | Omission (\*) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Execute | Boolean | * TRUE : Start * FALSE : - | FALSE | No |
| Execution start  When the variable is changed from FALSE to TRUE, this FB is executed. | | | |
| PositionVarNo | Integer | 0 or larger | 0 | No |
| SafetyP-type variable number  Select a number to store the variable. | | | |

(\*) : For some Variable, entries can be omitted.

* Yes : Entry can be omitted.
* No : Entry required always.

## Output Variable

| Variable name | Data type / Description |
| --- | --- |
| Done | Boolean |
| Execution completion confirmation  TRUE : This FB execution is completed.  FALSE : This FB execution is not completed. |
| Busy | Boolean |
| Processing status of this FB  TRUE : Being executed.  FALSE : Not being executed. |
| Error | Boolean |
| Error presence  TRUE : This FB ended abnormally.  FALSE : This FB ended successfully. |
| ErrorID | Word |
| Error location  2800 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the PLC program.  2801 (hexadecimal) : The error occurred in the robot controller. |
| ErrorIDEx | DWord |
| Error Code  This is a number to identify the error description.  For details, refer to "[Error code list](007684.html)". |
| PositionVarData | [eRC\_Position](007683.html#ID002998_erc_position) |
| SafetyP-type variable data |

## Function Description

-

## Attention

This FB is exclusive to COBOTTA PRO and is available when the robot controller software version for COBOTTA PRO is 1.9.\* or later.

# RC8 SERIES ROBOT CONTROLLER MANUAL

This manual describes RC8A and RC8 robot controllers. It also covers interface required when you integrate your robot system into your facilities, as well as providing the maintenance & inspection procedures.

Before use, read this manual carefully together with related manuals to safely get the maximum benefit from your robot in your assembling operations.

The following table shows the correspondence between the Standard and the Safety I/O-less specifications.

| Controller | Standard (including UL specification) | Safety I/O-less  (For details, refer to [Appendix](001359.html).) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RC8A | VM-6083 / VM-60B1  VS-6556 / VS-6577  VS050 / VS060 / VS068 / VS087  VP-6242 / VP-5243  HM series / HS series  XR series / SC series  HSR series / HSA1 series | VM-6083 / VM-60B1  VS-6556 / VS-6577  VS050 / VS060 / VS068 / VS087  VP-6242 / VP-5243  HM series / HS series  XR series / SC series  HSR series / HSA1 series |
| RC8 | VM-6083 / VM-60B1  VS-6556 / VS-6577  VS050 / VS060 / VS068 / VS087  VP-6242/ VP-5243  HM series / HS series  XR series / SC series | VM-6083 / VM-60B1  VS-6556 / VS-6577  VS050 / VS060 / VS068 / VS087  VP-6242/ VP-5243  HM series / HS series  XR series / SC series |

To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html) ".

Both robots and controllers imported into South Korea on or after 1st March 2013 are required to have KCs marks.

| RC8 | RC8 series |

| VSA4 | VS-068, VS-087 |  |
| VMA0 | VM-6083, VM-60B1 |  |
| VPA0 | VP-5243, VP-6242 |  |
| HSA0 | HS-4535\*, HS-4545\*, HS-4555\* |  |
| HSA1 | HS035A1\* , HS045A1\*, HS055A1\* | \*1 |
| HSB1 | HSR048\*, HSR055\*, HSR065\* | \*1 |
| HMA0 | HM-4060\*, HM-4A60\*, HM-4070\*, HM-4A70\*, HM-4085\*, HM-4A85\*, HM-40A0\*, HM-4AA0\* |  |
| XRA0 | XR-43\*\*\* |  |
| MC81 | MC8 |  |
| S1A1 | SCR: 1st to 2nd axes |  |
| S2A1 | SCR: 3rd to 4th axes |  |
| C | Supplied power | N | Standard | |
| D | Drive power | N | Standard | |
| E | Engine board | N | Standard | |
| E | Standard (since June 2020) \*2 | |
| 7 | High-performance CPU | |
| C | High-performance CPU (since January 2024) | |
| F | I/O | M | Minus common (NPN) | |
| P | Plus common (PNP) | |
| G | Standards | NN | - | |
| NI | Standards: CE   * Safety function: Safety I/O * Safety performance    Structure: Category 4, Performance level: e | |
| UI | Standards: UL   * Safety function: Safety I/O * Safety performance    Structure: Category 4, Performance level: e | |

# Parts Names of RC8 Controller

## Models Except UL-Listed Ones

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001315_1.png)

| Number | Label | Name | Purpose | | | Remarks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | - | Safety I/O |  | | |  |
| 2 | - | Expansion board slot (2 slots) | Install expansion board.  PCI board is installed to upper slot and PCI Express board to lower slot. | | |  |
| 3 | MINI I/O | Mini I/O conector |  | | | \*1 |
| 4 | HAND I/O | Hand I/O connector |  | | | \*1 |
| 5 | PENDANT | Pendant connector | Install teach pendant and mini-pendant. | | | \*2 |
| 6 | POWER | Power switch | Used for power ON and OFF of controller. | | |  |
| 7 | - | Intake filter | Prevent invasion of dust to inside controller. 3 locations. | | |  |
| 8 | INPUT AC | Power connector | Connect power cable. | | | \*1 |
| 9 | LAN | Ethernet connector | Use for communication with outside device through Ethernet circuit. | | |  |
| 10 | USB | USB connector (2 lines) | Connect with USB memories or USB devices. | | |  |
| 11 | RS-232C | Serial communication connector | Use for serial communication with outside devices. | | |  |
| 12 | VGA | VGA connector | Use for output images.  (Option) | | |  |
| 13 | P (POWER)  R (RUN)  E (ERR) | Status display LED | Check status of controller. | | |  |
| POWER | Controller power ON | Green lamp turns ON. |  |
| Power OFF | Turn OFF. |  |
| RUN | Program is running in Auto mode | Green lamp turns ON. |  |
| Other | Turn OFF. |  |
| ERROR | Robot errors and warnings  （See [Error Levels](000494.html)） | Red lamp turns ON. |  |
| Other | Turn OFF. |  |
| 14 | ENC | Encoder connector | Connect encoder cable. | | | \*1 |
| 15 | SLOT1, SLOT2, SLOT3, SLOT4 | Motor connector | Connect motor cable. | | | \*1 |
| 16 |  | Earth terminal (protective earth) | Protect from electric shock. | | | \*1 |

\*1 DO NOT connect or disconnect connectors to/from the controller when the AC power or the 24 VDC power for I/O is being supplied. Doing so may cause electric shock or controller failure. Do not unplug connector within 6 seconds of the shut down.

\*2 Before connecting the teach pendant connector, be sure to shut-off the robot controller. If the connector is connected without shut-off the robot controller, the teach pendant and robot controller may fail.  
Before disconnecting the teach pendant connector, perform the disconnection procedure. For information about the disconnection procedure, please refer to "[Displaying Setting Menu for Pendant and Panel](001776.html)".

ID : 1316

# Warning and Caution Labels

The robot unit has warning and caution labels pasted as shown below. They alert the user to the dangers of the areas on which they are pasted. Be sure to observe the instructions printed on those labels.

## Models Except UL-Listed Ones

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001316_1.png)

| Warning and caution labels on the controller | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Warning label 1 | (For maintenance of the controller)  DO NOT OPEN UNDER LOAD.  Do not touch inside within 6 minutes of turning off power and disconnecting cable.  Risk of electrical shock. |
| Warning label 2 | (For controller power switch)  Risk of injury.  Be sure to perform lockout/tagout before starting servicing.  Turning the power ON may move the arm, causing injuries if a person is inside the safety fence. |
| Caution label 1 | The controller is not designed to be dust-, splash-, or explosion-proof. Before installation, be sure to read the user's manual.  Do not put anything on the controller or apply any impact or shock to it. |
| Caution label 2 | DO NOT insert fingers or foreign objects into openings. Doing so may cause bodily injury.  When using an external power source, never apply the voltage not specified. Doing so can result in a controller failure. |
| Caution label 3 | After turning the power switch OFF, do not turn it ON for at least six seconds. |

## UL-Listed Model

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001316_7.png)

| Warning and caution labels on the controller | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| Warning label 1 | (For maintenance of the controller)  DO NOT OPEN UNDER LOAD.  Do not touch inside within 6 minutes of turning off power and disconnecting cable.  Risk of electrical shock. |
| Warning label 2 | (For controller power switch)  Risk of injury.  Be sure to perform lockout/tagout before starting servicing.  Turning the power ON may move the arm, causing injuries if a person is inside the safety fence. |
| Caution label 1 | The controller is not designed to be dust-, splash-, or explosion-proof. Before installation, be sure to read the user's manual.  Do not put anything on the controller or apply any impact or shock to it. |
| Caution label 2 | DO NOT insert fingers or foreign objects into openings. Doing so may cause bodily injury.  When using an external power source, never apply the voltage not specified. Doing so can result in a controller failure. |
| Caution label 3 | After turning the power switch OFF, do not turn it ON for at least six seconds. |
| Caution label 4 | DO NOT attach or detach this connector while power switch is on.  lmproper operation may cause electric shock and controller failure. |

# Specification of RC8 Controller

| Term | | Specification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applicable robot | | VM-6083 / VM-60B1 VS-6556 / VS-6577  VS050 / VS060 / VS068 / VS087  VP-6242 / VP-5243  HM series / HS series  XR series / SC series |
| Type | | RC8-\*\*\*\*-\*\*\*\*-\*\*-\*\*\* |
| Number of axes controlled | | Robot : 4 to 6 axes  Extended-joint : 2 to 4 axes (optional) |
| Control method | | PTP, CP 3-dimensional linear, 3-dimensional arc  (For SC series and Extended-joints, available PTP control only.) |
| Drive method | | All axes all digital AC servo |
| Language in use | | DENSO Robotics language (PacScript) |
| Memory capacity | | User area Variable area : 1.75 Mbyte (32,766 points equivalent), file area : 400 Mbyte (5,000 steps x 256 files) |
| Teaching method | | 1. Direct teaching...Horizontal articulated model only 2. Remote teaching 3. Numerical entry (MDI) |
| External signal  (I/O, etc.) | Mini I/O | Input : User open 8 points + System fix 14 points  Output : User open 8 points + System fix 16 points |
| Hand I/O | Input : 8 points  Output : 8 points |
| Safety I/O | Input and output signals are integrated into Mini I/O connector. |
| Parallel I/O board  (optional) (\*1) | Expansion slot : PCI  Input : 40 points  Output : 48 points |
| CC-Link remote device board  (optional) (\*1) | Expansion slot : PCI Express Input : Up to 8192 points  Output : Up to 8192 points  Remote register  Input : Up to 2048 words  Output : Up to 2048 words |
| DeviceNet slave board  (optional) (\*1) | Expansion slot : PCI Express Input : Up to 256 points  Output : Up to 256 points |
| DeviceNet master board  (optional) (\*1) | Expansion slot : PCI Express Input : 1024 points  Output : 1024 points |
| EtherNet/IP Adapter board  (optional) (\*1) | Expansion slot : PCI Express  Input : Up to 4032 points  Output : Up to 4032 points |
| PROFIBUS slave board  (optional) (\*1) | Expansion slot : PCI Express Input : Up to 256 points  Output : Up to 256 points |
| PROFINET IO Device board  (optional) | Expansion slot : PCI Express Input : Up to 8192 points  Output : Up to 8192 points |
| EtherCAT slave board  (optional) | Expansion slot : PCI Express  Input : Up to 2048 points  Output : Up to 2048 points |
| RS232C expansion board  (optional, not supplied) | DENSO supplies software only and board is not supplied. |
| External communication | RS232C | 1 line |
| Ethernet | 1 line (GbE : Gigabit Ethernet) |
| USB | 2 lines |
| VGA optional | 1 line |
| Electric gripper control board  (optional) ( \*1) | | Expansion slot : PCI |
| Expansion slot | | * PCI 1 slot * PCI Express 1 slot |
| Self diagnosis function | | Overrun, servo error, memory error, input error, short circuit detection (user wiring part), etc. |
| Timer function | | 0.02 to 10 sec. (1/60 sec. step) |
| Error display | | * External error output * Display error code on mini-pendant (optional) * Display error message, resume method on teach pendant (optional) |
| Cable | Motor & encoder cable for RC8series  (optional) | 2m, 4m, 6m, 12m, 20m Note) Motor connector x 3, encoder connector x 1  Note) VM, HS, HM are standard / splash-proof version  Note) VS is dedicated version  Note) SC is only for 4m, 6m and 12m Motor cable (connector x 1), encoder cable (connector x 1)  Note) The 20m cable is not available for the UL-listed robot unit. |
| I/O cable  (optional) | 8m, 15m  (for Mini I/O, for Hand I/O, for expansion parallel I/O) |
| RC8 series power cable | 5m |
| For RC8 series Extended-joint  motor cable  (optional) | 2m, 4m, 6m, 12m  (standard version) |
| For RC8 series Extended-joint  encoder cable  (optional) | 1m, 2m, 4m, 6m, 12m  (standard version) |
| External operation device | Teach pendant  (optional) | 4m, 8m, 12m |
| Mini-pendant  (optional) | 4m, 8m, 12m |
| Emergency stop switch box  (optional) | 4m |
| Pendant extension cable  (optional) | 4m, 8m  (Available for Emergency stop switch box as well) |
| Environmental condition (in motion) | | Temperature 0 to 40 degree C, humidity 20 to 90% RH (No dew condensation allowed.) |
| Defacement (pollution) degree | | 2 (\*2) |
| Power supply | | VM  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, +3.3 kVA |
| VS-6556/6577  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.8 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.8 kVA |
| VS-050/060  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.15 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.15 kVA |
| VS-068/087  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 2.78 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 2.78 kVA |
| VP  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.0 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.0 kVA 100V version AC100 V -5 % to AC110 V +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.0 kVA (\*2)  \* Extended-joint specification does not support 100V input. |
| HM series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 2.45 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 2.45 kVA |
| HS series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.8 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.8 kVA |
| XR series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.85 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.85 kVA |
| SC series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC + 10% 47 to 63Hz,1.5 ｋVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC + 10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.5 kVA |
| I/O power supply | Use external power supply | Supply 24VDC +/-10% from outside |
| Use internal power supply | Supply 24VDC +/-10% from inside controller |
| SCCR | | Other than UL-listed model: 5KA  UL-listed model: 10KA |
| Safety performance (\*4) | | Structure : Category 4 Performance Level : e  MTTFd : 100 years  DCavg : 99 %  PFHd : 7.42×10-8  Please note that the safety function of the enable (deadman) operation is 9.89×10-8.  \* Please specify the safety-I/O-less version in the case that safety I/O mounted on the standard version is not necessary |
| Stop category | | Category1 (except Safety-I/O-less type.)  (See IEC60204-1 for details of stop category) |
| IP code | | IP20  IP54 when using protective box (optional) |
| Stand for vertical setup | | Note) Set right side (power connector side) down |
| External dimension | | Standard : W 440.5 x D 299.6 x H 96.6 [mm] 12.8 L  UL : W 440.5 x D 400 x H 130 [mm] 17.8 L  \* Except for the projection part. |
| Weight | | Standard : approximately 12 kg  UL : approximately 18 kg |

\*1 : Expansion boards used in the RC7 robot controller cannot be used.

\*2 : Pollution degree 2 is equivalent to household and office environment.

When using in a factory, take either of the following measures.

・ Put it into the control panel corresponding to pollution degree 3.

・ Use [the controller protective box](005495.html) (optional).

\*3 : If the power supply can be dropped 95 V or less, such as in the heavily loaded facilities, using a transformer describes below is recommended. However, operation with 85 V or lower voltage is not guaranteed.

Transformer specification
:   Input voltage : 1Ph 100 V

    Output voltage : 1Ph 200 V

    Capacity : 1 kVA

\*4 : This safety performance is determined for the robot stop functions; such as an emergency stop, enable auto, protective stop and deadman switch.  
 However, customer-prepared input devices, which connect to signals for emergency stop, Enable Auto, and protective stop, are not included in the safety performance calculation.

Calculation conditions
:   · This calculation is based on ISO 13849-1:2006.

    · Expected operation counts a year (Nop) are as follows.

    | Operation | Mission time (year) | |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | 10 | 20 |
    | Start/Stop (Motor ON/OFF) | 136,986 | 68,493 |
    | Enable (Deadman) switch | 10,000 | 5,000 |

# Controller Handling Notes

* DO NOT insert fingers or foreign objects into openings. Doing so may cause bodily injury.
* Before opening the controller cover and accessing the inside of the controller for maintenance, be sure to turn off the power switch, disconnect the power cable, and wait 6 minutes or more. This is for protecting you from electric shock.
* After turning the power switch OFF, do not turn it ON for at least six seconds.
* DO NOT connect or disconnect connectors to/from the controller when the AC power or the 24 VDC power for I/O is being supplied. Doing so may cause electric shock or controller failure. For details, refer to "[Name of Each Section of Controller](001315.html)".

* This controller is not designed to be dust-, splash-, or explosion-proof.
* Read operation manuals before installation.
* Do not place anything on the controller or apply an impact or shock to the controller.
* Avoid mounting the controller in an environment where excessive vibration is applied to the controller.

* The robot controller connectors are of a screw-lock type or ring-lock type. Lock the connectors securely. If even one of the connectors is not locked, weak contact may result thereby causing an error.  
  Be sure to turn the robot controller OFF before connecting/ disconnecting the power connector or motor connector or encorder connector. Otherwise, the internal circuits of the robot controller may be damaged.
* When you turn on the controller power supply, do not turn it off until the software startup have been completed.  
  It may damage the internal data of the robot controller.

* If errors occur during robot operation (such as, overload, excessive position error and BUS under voltage), adjust the following items, or follow the instructions of the [error code list](001075.html).  
  - Increase waiting time before and after robot motion.  
  - Reduce speed or acceleration.

# General Information about the Interface

This section describes the I/O signals on the robot controller.

The I/O signals are grouped into two--user I/O signals and system I/O ones.

If no optional I/O extension board is mounted, the controller handles I/O signals in the mini I/O dedicated mode via the mini I/O connector and the hand I/O connector.

# Types of System I/O Signals

It issues PROGRAM START commands as I/O commands by using seven command execution inputs.

The table below lists the types of system I/O signals.

## Fixed by System

| Type | | No. of points | Function |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System input | | 7 | External Emergency Stop 1, External Emergency Stop 2, Enable Auto 1, Enable Auto 2, Step Stop (All tasks), Protective Stop 1, Protective Stop 2 |
| System output | RC8A | 18 (Note1) | Auto Mode, Robot Initialized, Robot Running, CPU Normal, Robot Error, Operation Preparation Completed, Battery Warning, Pendant Emergency Stop 1, Pendant Emergency Stop 2, Deadman SW 1 [Enable SW 1], Deadman SW 2 [Enable SW 2], STO Monitor 1a, STO Monitor 2a, STO Monitor 1b, STO Monitor 2b, Continue Start Permission (selectable by I/O parameter) (Note1), Auto Mode 1 (safety output) (Note2), Auto Mode 2 (safety output) (Note2) |
| RC8 | 16 (Note1) | Auto Mode, Robot Initialized, Robot Running, CPU Normal, Robot Error, Operation Preparation Completed, Battery Warning, Pendant Emergency Stop 1, Pendant Emergency Stop 2, Deadman SW 1 [Enable SW 1], Deadman SW 2 [Enable SW 2], Contactor Contact Monitor 1a, Contactor Contact Monitor 2a, Contactor Contact Monitor 1b, Contactor Contact Monitor 2b, Continue Start Permission (selectable by I/O parameter) (Note1) |
| Input for command execution | | 7 | Command (3 bits), data area (3 bits), and Strobe Signal |
| Output for command execution | | 1 | Command Processing Completed |

Note1 : The terminal number 53 (port number 24) on Mini I/O is assigned to a user output at the factory default.  
You can assign this terminal to a system output (Continue Start Permission output signal) by setting the [I/O parameter](005825.html) of "23 : User or System output setting" to "1".

Note2 : Except for RC8A Safety I/O-less specification.

## Controlled by User Program

| Type | No. of points | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User input | 8 | Inputs to read the external I/O status with an IN command or IO [ ] variable. Used for analysis condition identification, condition satisfaction wait, data input from the external equipment, etc. |
| User output | 7 (Note1) | Outputs to issue a signal to the external equipment during program execution with SET and RESET commands, etc. |
| HAND input | 8 | Inputs to read the external I/O status with an IN command or IO [ ] variable. Used for checking the hand status. |
| HAND output | 8 | Outputs to issue signals to the external equipment with SET and RESET commands, etc.  Used for controlling the hand to open or close. |

Note1 : The terminal number 53 (port number 24) on Mini I/O is assigned to a user output at the factory default.  
You can assign this terminal to a system output (Continue Start Permission output signal) by setting the [I/O parameter](005825.html) of "23 : User or System output setting" to "1".

# Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode

The total of up to 2 boards (one PCI board and one PIC Express board) can be mounted on the I/O expansion board.

The table below lists the permitted combination of I/O extension boards and selectable allocation mode.　PCIe bord stands for PIC Express board.

| No. | I/O extension boards | | Allocation modes \*2 | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PIC Express board　\*3 | PIC board | Mini I/O dedicated | RC3 Compatible | Standard | All user I/O |
| 0 | － | － | O |  |  |  |
| 1 | － | Parallel I/O board \*3 | O | O | O |  |
| 2 | DeviceNet slave board | － |  | O | O |  |
| 3 | DeviceNet slave board | Parallel I/O board |  | O | O |  |
| 4 | CC-Link remote device board | － |  | O | O |  |
| 5 | CC-Link remote device board | Parallel I/O board |  | O | O |  |
| 6 | PROFIBUS slave board | － |  | O | O |  |
| 7 | PROFIBUS slave board | Parallel I/O board |  | O | O |  |
| 8 | EtherNet/IP Adapter board | － |  | O | O |  |
| 9 | EtherNet/IP Adapter board | Parallel I/O board |  | O | O |  |
| 10 | PROFINET IO Device board | － |  | O | O |  |
| 11 | PROFINET IO Device board | Parallel I/O board |  | O | O |  |
| 12 | DeviceNet master board | － |  |  |  | O |
| 13 | DeviceNet master board | Parallel I/O board |  |  |  | O |
| 14 | EtherCAT slave board | － |  | O | O |  |
| 15 | EtherCAT slave board | Parallel I/O board |  | O | O |  |

\*1 A cell with "O" stands for the allocation mode is selectable, and empty cell stands for the allocation mode is not selectable.

\*2 Only one mode can be selected from among check-marked modes in the "Application modes" column.

\*3 PCI Express board has precedence over PCI board for System I/O allocation. If an I/O extension board is equipped with a parallel I/O board only, system I/Os are allocated to the parallel I/O board.

# Functions in Individual Allocation Modes

Functions of I/O signals differ depending on the allocation modes, as shown in the table below.

| Allocation mode | General description |
| --- | --- |
| Mini I/O dedicated | Combination of bits commands operations. Some functions are deleted from the ones provided in Standard allocation.  Mini I/O system allocation is allocated to the Mini I/O area. When an I/O option board is attached, only the user signal is allocated to the I/O option board area. |
| RC3 compatible | Functions, such as program activation, are specified by each bit. Operations are directed by the bit being set.  "Compatible" system allocation is allocated to the I/O extension board area.  Only the user signal (excluding CPU Normal) is allocated to all ports of the Mini I/O area. |
| Standard | Directs program activation, etc. with a combination of bits (I/O command.)  This allocation has the greatest number of functions.  "Standard" system allocation is allocated to the I/O extension board area. Only the user signal (excluding CPU Normal) is allocated to all ports of the Mini I/O area. |
| All user I/O | Only the user signal is allocated to the I/O extension board area. Only the user signal (excluding CPU Normal) is allocated to all ports of the Mini I/O area. |

# Mini I/O Functions for other than Mini I/O Dedicated mode

When any of the I/O allocation modes (compatible, standard, or all user I/O) except the mini I/O dedicated mode is selected, all of the ports (except *CPU Normal*) occupied by the system I/O signals in the mini I/O dedicated mode will be released and used as user I/O ports as shown below. (Refer to "[RC8 I/O Allocation](005533.html)" of the MINI I/O MANUAL).

* System input ports #0 to #7 (Terminals #11 to #18 on CN5) will be used as user input ports.
* System output ports #17 to #23 (Terminals #46 to #52 on CN5) will be used as user output ports.

The system output signal *CPU Normal* remains assigned to port #16 (Terminal #45 on CN5) even in the compatible, standard, or all user I/O mode.

# I/O Port Map and Allocation

When an I/O extension board is not used, I/O port numbers (the number specified when I/O is processed with PAC program or I/O command) go up to 511. However, when an I/O extension board (option)is used, I/O port numbers beyond 511 are added.

| I/O port number | Allocation | Area |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 ～ 15 | Mini I/O input ([RC8A](002627.html), [RC8](005533.html)) | Standard area |
| 16 ～ 31 | Mini I/O output ([RC8A](002627.html), [RC8](005533.html)) |
| 32 ～ 47 | Not used. |
| 48 ～ 55 | [Input by hand](005534.html) |
| 56 ～ 63 | Not used. |
| 64 ～ 71 | [Output by hand](005534.html) |
| 72 ～ 127 | Not used. |
| 128 ～ 511 | [Internal I/O](002157.html) |
| 512 ～ 767 | [CC-Link remote device input](001477.html)  [DeviceNet slave input](001457.html)  [EtherNet/IP Adapter input](005184.html)  [PROFIBUS slave input](001060.html)  [PROFINET IO Device input](005512.html)  [EtherCAT slave input](005789.html) | I/O extension board area |
| 768 ～ 1023 | [CC-Link remote device output](001477.html)  [DeviceNet slave output](001457.html)  [EtherNet/IP Adapter output](005184.html)  [PROFIBUS slave output](001060.html)  [PROFINET IO Device output](005512.html)  [EtherCAT slave output](005789.html) |
| 1024 ～ 2047 | [DeviceNet master input](005551.html) |
| 2048 ～ 3071 | [DeviceNet master output](005551.html) |
| 3072 ～ 3327 | Not used. |
| 3328 ～ 3583 | Not used. |
| 3584 ～ 3623 | [Parallel I/O board input](001441.html) |
| 3624 ～ 3839 | Not used. |
| 3840 ～ 3887 | [Parallel I/O board output](001441.html) |
| 3888 ～ 4095 | Not used. |
| 4096 ～ 7871 | [CC-Link remote device](001477.html)   * CC-Link Ver.1.10   4096 ～ 4351 : CC-Link remote device input  4352 ～ 4607 : Not used.  4608 ～ 4863 : CC-Link remote device output  4864 ～ 7871 : Not used.   * CC-Link Ver.2.00   4096 ～ 6783 : CC-Link remote device input  6784 ～ 7871 : Not used.  [EtherNet/IP Adapter input](005184.html)  [PROFINET IO Device input](005512.html)  [EtherCAT slave](005789.html)  4096 ～ 5887 : EtherCAT slave input  5888 ～ 7871 : Not used. |
| 7872 ～ 11647 | [CC-Link remote device](001477.html)   * CC-Link Ver.2.00   7872 ～ 10559 : CC-Link remote device output  10560 ～ 11647 : Not used.  [EtherNet/IP Adapter output](005184.html)  [PROFINET IO Device output](005512.html)  [EtherCAT slave](005789.html)  7872 ～ 9663 : EtherCAT slave output  9664 ～ 11647 : Not used. |
| 11648 ～ 15807 | [PROFINET IO Device input](005512.html) |
| 15808 ～ 19903 | Not used. |
| 19904 ～ 24063 | [PROFINET IO Device output](005512.html) |

# Installation Requirements for the Controller

The table below lists the installation requirements for the RC8 controller.

| Item | Environmental Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Installation type | Stand-alone and Wall-mount |
| Ambient temperature | In operation: 0 to 40℃  In storage or during transportation: -10 to 60℃ |
| Humidity | In operation: 20 to 90% RH (No dew condensation is allowed.)  In storage or during transportation: 40 to 75% RH (No dew condensation allowed.) |
| Altitude | In operation : 1,000 m or lower. |
| Safe installation environment | Refer to the SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, "[Insuring the Proper Installation Environment](001928.html)". |
| Working space | Sufficient service space must be available for inspection and disassembly. |
| Grounding conditions | Grounding resistance (protective ground): 100Ω or less |

# Mounting the Robot Controller

Install robot controller as shown below.

## Installation Caution

1. When using the robot controller in any environment where there is mist, put the controller in an optional robot controller protective box. The robot controller is not dust-proof, splash-proof, or explosion-proof.  
   Note that the controller protective box is not mounted on a UL-listed robot controller.
2. Set up the controller at the place where it is easy to replace air filters.
3. The installation jobs should be handled by at least two persons.
4. Do not place anything within 200 mm from the air inlet and outlet of the robot controller.
5. The robot controller has no air filter on the air outlet side. In wall-mounted installation, therefore, to prevent free-fall dust or dirt from getting into the controller, set up the controller with the air outlet side not facing upward.
6. System software installation, such as upgrade, is done by USB memory. When setting the controller, be sure to keep enough space in the vicinity of USB connector to connect USB memory.

## Stand-alone Installation

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001331_1.png)

## Installation by Fixing, Installation on Wall

It can be mounted on the frame or installed on the wall by using the stay set for wall-mount of the robot controller option.

Wall-mounting installations (see figure below) are available.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001331_2.png)

Fix each stays on the both side of the controller by using existing screws (three portion) of the controller.

The stay set (option part) comprises a long stay and a short stay. Fix each stay as follows;

* Long stay : Fix on the left, viewed from the front of the controller.
* Short stay : Fix on the right, viewed from the front of the controller. (power cable's side)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001331_3.png)

Mount stays on the frame or wall.

## Upright Setting

When placing the controller in the upright position, it is recommended to use customer-prepared parts to fix the controller to the wall and floor.

For details, refer to the following links.

* [Installation Guide for Upright Setting of RC8A Controller](002640.html)
* [Installation Guide for Upright Setting of RC8 Controller (Standard)](001110.html)

# Power Supply Circuit Breaker for RC8 (Recommendation)

When inserting a circuit breaker between the robot and the AC input power supply, select the circuit breaker with breaking capacity higher than the following specification. Use a high frequency-proof leakage breaker for inverters.

* Recommended circuit breaker example : CP33V/20 (Fuji Electric FA Components & Systems Co., Ltd.)

Using a circuit breaker with breaking capacity lower than the following specification may cause the circuit breaker to be shut down due to robot operation.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001334_1.png)

Take preventive measures against any electrical hazards, such as electric shock, caused by leakage current or grounding fault.

For countermeasures, refer to the following points.

* Use an earth leakage circuit breaker.
* Refer to EN 60204-1 (European Norm).

# Wiring of Primary Power Source

Observe the following precautions when wiring the primary power source of the robot controller:

## About Primary Power Source

* Use the correct power source (200 VAC or 100 VAC) for the controller specification.
* Be careful not to confuse AC 100V with AC 200V (or AC 230V), and also three-phase with single-phase.
* Connect the robot power cable to a power source separate from the welder power source.
* To cut off the controller power supply, use customer-prepared-breaker.

## Protective Grounding

Before connecting the power cable, make sure to connect 2.5mm＾2 or higher level of wire (yellow/green) to the [earth terminal (protective grounding)](001315.html) of the front metal panel. When disconnecting the bonding wire connected to the [earth terminal (protective grounding)](001315.html) of the front metal panel, make sure to disconnect the power cable beforehand.

## Additional Precautions

* Do not bundle the teach pendant cable, I/O cables or motor & encoder cable together with high power lines such as power cables and peripheral device cables, or route the motor cables near high power devices (motor, welder, parts feeder, etc.).
* Do not route any additional cables or air tubes of end-effectors through the robot unit. Doing so will result in broken cables or tubes.
* When you connect the controller's functional grounding, ground a wire with 1.25mm2 or larger.

# Connecting Power Cable

## Models Except UL-Listed Ones

###### 1

Confirm that the breaker of the power supply is turned off.

Insert connector of power cable to power supply connector of the controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001336_1.png)

###### 2

Insert until it is locked with a clicking sound.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001336_2.png)

* Pull the power cable straight out pushing down clicks on top and bottom of the connector when removing the power cable.
* Fix the power cable to the equipment.

## UL-Listed Model

###### 1

Confirm that the breaker of the power supply is turned off.

Insert connector of power cable to power supply connector of the controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001336_3.png)

###### 2

Screw up the connector ring clockwise until the connector is fastened.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001336_4.png)

* To remove the power cable, loosen the ring anti-clockwise, and then pull off the cable straightway.
* Fix the power cable to the equipment.

# Disconnecting the Robot from the Power Source

If you need to cut off the power supply from the robot unit for maintenance or transportation purpose, follow the steps below for safety.

###### 1

Turn OFF the power switch of the robot controller.

###### 2

Check that the motor ON lamp is OFF.

###### 3

Disconnect the power cable from the power connector on the robot controller.

# Connecting Robot

Controller and robot are connected by the motor & encoder cable.

For partnumber and outer dimensions of motor & encoder cable, please refer to "[Options for Robot Unit](001970.html)".

## Connection in Controller Side

### Models Except UL-Listed Ones

###### 1

Verify that the power of controller is OFF.

###### 2

Check positional relationship of three connectors of motor cable. Each connector has a tag. Connect each cable according to tags.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_1.png)

###### 3

Connect the connector with SLOT3 tag to SLOT3.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_2.png)

Insert it straight into the connector of the controller until it is locked with a clicking sound.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_3.png)

Check that the connector is locked firmly.

###### 4

Follow the same manner of SLOT3 to connect SLOT2 and then SLOT1.

Connect the connector of encoder cable to the encoder connector (ENC).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_4.png)

###### 5

Fix the ground wire with a screw.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_5.png)

Fix the motor and encoder cable to the equipment.

Since the part shown in red circle becomes very hot, do NOT touch while the power ON.

### UL-Listed Model

###### 1

Verify that the power of controller is OFF.

###### 2

Insert the cable to the controller's connector straightway.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_6.png)

###### 3

Lock the cable with the lever.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001339_7.png)

* Check that the connector is locked firmly.
* Fix the motor and encoder cable to the equipment.

## Connection in Robot Side

Refer to handling manual of each robot for connection in the robot side.

ID : 1340

# Connecting the Teach Pendant

Connect the teach pendant to the PENDANT connector on the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001340_1.png)

## Cautions in Connecting the Pendant Cable to the Controller

* Before connecting the cable, be sure to shut-off the robot controller.  
  If the cable is connected without shut-off the robot controller, the teach pendant and robot controller may fail.
* After connecting the pendant cable, do not apply pressure on the connector in either direction. Such pressure may cause a communications error.
* Before disconnecting the cable, be sure to perform disconnection procedure, unlock the connector, and pull out the cable straight without twisting it. For information about the disconnection procedure, please refer to "[Displaying Setting Menu for Pendant and Panel](001776.html)".

## Use Robot Controller without Teach Pendant

Install a dummy connector in the PENDANT connector; otherwise, you cannot release emergency stop.

ID : 1341

# Connecting LAN

Connect LAN cable to LAN connector.

Use shielded LAN cable with length shorter than 30 cm.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001341_1.png)

Perform communication setting with teach pendant when communicate with LAN port. Refer to the "[Displaying and Changing Communication Settings Screen](001783.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

When connecting USB of the controller, Ethernet, RS-232C connector to the commercial devices, additional measures against noise, such as ferrite core and others, could be required depending on the condition. Please check your operation environment. We do not guarantee performance and maintenance of the connection with commercial devices.

## For HSR/ HSA1 Series Robots

For HSR and HSA1 series robots (except UL-listed models), the motor & encoder cable is available in two types: the new type and the old type. Whether the cable will be shipped with a ferrite core depends on the cable length you choose. The new type cable 4 m or longer and the old type cable 12 m or longer will be shipped with a ferrite core.

If you choose a new type motor & encoder cable 4 m or longer, place the provided ferrite core on two turns of the LAN cable.

If you choose an old type motor & encoder cable 12 m or longer, place the provided ferrite core on two turns of the LAN cable.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001341_2.png)

# Connecting USB

Connect USB terminal of device to USB connector of the controller.

1. Length of cable for connecting USB device should be 3 m or shorter.
2. When connecting USB of the controller, Ethernet, RS-232C connector to the commercial devices, additional measures against noise, such as ferrite core and others, could be required depending on the condition. Please check your operation environment. We do not guarantee performance and maintenance of the connection with commercial devices.
3. Make sure not to affected noise when using USB. Noise can cause improper operation.
4. The width of USB devices which can connect to the controller without interference is 16.6mm or less.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001342_1.png)

# Connecting RS-232C

Connect to RS-232C terminal of the controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001343_1.png)

When connecting USB of the controller, Ethernet, RS-232C connector to the commercial devices, additional measures against noise, such as ferrite core and others, could be required depending on the condition. Please check your operation environment. We do not guarantee performance and maintenance of the connection with commercial devices.

RS-232C cable consists of a straight cable and a cross cable.  
Use cross cable for connecting controller and PC.

## RS-232C Connector Pin Assignment

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| View from the cable side | | | |
| Terminal No. | Name | Terminal No. | Name |
| 1 | - | 6 | DSR |
| 2 | RXD | 7 | RTS |
| 3 | TXD | 8 | CTS |
| 4 | DTR | 9 | - |
| 5 | SG |  |  |

# Setting Method for Mini I/O Power Supply

Mini I/O power supply (+24 V DC) can be selected to be obtained either from external power or from internal power by teach pendant. Factory setting is set to external power supply.

Refer to the "[Displaying and Changing I/O Parameters](001769.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

* When using external power supply, make sure that Mini I/O power supply is turned ON before supplying the power to the controller.
* Changing setting of Mini I/O power supply from external power to internal power changes terminal No. 32 to 34 and terminal No. 66 to 68 to the internal DC power source output from the external DC power input.

# Setting up Parallel I/O Board Power Source

The power source (+24 VDC) for the parallel I/O board can be switched between internal and external power supplies. The factory default is an external power supply.

For details, refer to the following "[Setting](#set)".

## Names of Components on the Parallel I/O Board

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001346_1.png)

Fuse F3 is not mounted on the NPN type.

## Setting

Check that the controller's power is turned off before setting.

| I/O power supply settings | P1 and JP2 settings | Setting method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External power supply | JP1, JP2 (Open) | Use the board under the factory default settings (both JP1 and JP2 are open). |
| Internal power supply | JP1, JP2 (Short-circuit) | 1. Short-circuit pin 1 to 2 on each of JP1 and JP2 using a short socket. 2. Disconnect the I/O power switching harness from CN2 on the parallel I/O board and connect it to 24 V connector (CNP101) on the controller's printed circuit board. |

# Installing Expansion Board

Methods to install expansion boards such as DeviceNet slave board or CC-Link to expansion slot of RC8 series controller is described here.

###### 1

Turn OFF the power switch of the controller, and then disconnect the power cable.

###### 2

Remove seven screws to remove top cover of the controller.

6 minutes or more must be elapsed after turning OFF the power switch before accessing inside the controller by removing cover for maintenance or other purpose. Failure to do so may be subject to risk of electrical shock.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_1.png)

###### 3

Remove four screws on the front of the controller and two screws on the top of the controller, and then remove the expansion board mounting case.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_2.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_3.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_4.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_5.png)

###### 4

Place the expansion board mounting case on surface.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_6.png)

###### 5

Remove screws to remove cover.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_7.png)

###### 6

Insert the expansion board in the expansion board connector securely all the way to end.

The expansion board must be inserted vertically to the connector (referring to the following figure, “Good/Bad
examples”). If fail to insert, the expansion board might not work properly (the robot controller might not recognize
the expansion board: Error code "8150202C").

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_8.png)

* Good/Bad examples

| View from A |
| --- |
|  |
|  |
|  |

| View from B | |
| --- | --- |
|  | |
|  |  |

| View from C | |
| --- | --- |
|  | |
|  |  |

###### 7

Fix expansion board stay with screws.

At this time, keep the connector vertical to the expansion board (referring to Good/Bad examples above).  
If fail to positioning, the expansion board might not work properly (the robot controller might not recognize the
expansion board: Error code "8150202C").

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_9.png)

###### 8

Re-assemble the expansion board mounting unit.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001347_10.png)

###### 9

Re-assemble the top cover of the controller.

# Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Motion I/O Wiring

## I/O Cable (Option)

Multi-core cables with connectors to be used for the I/O wiring of the Robot Controller are options. Select an appropriate cable from the table given below if necessary.

Refer to the "[OPTIONAL COMPONENTS](001971.html)".

| No. | Name | Remarks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Standard I/O cable set (8m) | Including Nos. 1-1 and 1-2 |
| 1-1 | Mini I/O cable set (8m) |  |
| 1-2 | Hand I/O cable set (8m) |  |
| 1-3 | Motion Input cable (8m) | For Safety Motion specification exclusive use |
| 1-4 | Motion Output cable (8m) | For Safety Motion specification exclusive use |
| 2 | Standard I/O cable set (15m) | Including Nos. 2-1 and 2-2 |
| 2-1 | Mini I/O cable set (15m) |  |
| 2-2 | Hand I/O cable set (15m) |  |
| 2-3 | Motion Input cable (15m) | For Safety Motion specification exclusive use |
| 2-4 | Motion Output cable (15m) | For Safety Motion specification exclusive use |

## Recommended Connector and Cable

If you do not use optional cables listed above, use the recommended connectors and cables listed below.

| Connector name | Connector model/manufacturer | Cable Standards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mini I/O | PCR-E68FS+ connector  PCS-E68LPA-1E cover OR PCS-E68LKPB-1E+R cover  (HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO Co., LTD) | UL2789 - With shield  Equivalent to AWG28x34P |
| HAND I/O | PCR-E20FS+ connector  PCS-E20LA cover  (HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO Co., LTD) | UL2789 - With shield  Equivalent to AWG28x10P |
| Motion I/F IN | PCR-E68FS+ connector  PCS-E68LKPB-2D+R cover  (HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO Co., LTD) | UL2789 - With shield  Equivalent to AWG28x34P |
| Motion I/F OUT | PCR-E68FS+ connector  PCS-E68LKPB-4B+R cover  (HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO Co., LTD) | UL2789 - With shield  Equivalent to AWG28x34P |

Be sure to modify the shielding wire at the end of the cable to be used, as shown below. Without this modification, the robot may malfunction due to noise.

### Modifying the Shielding Wire (Example)

###### 1

Prepare I/O cables.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001348_1.png)

###### 2

Stripe the cable jacket from the I/O cable end.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001348_2.png)

###### 3

Fold back the braided shield, and then cut it to the proper length.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001348_3.png)

###### 4

Wrap copper tape around the braided shield.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001348_4.png)

###### 5

Position the portion of wrapped copper tape with cable clamp, so as to be tightened, and then fix it with screws.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001348_5.png)

# Wiring Notes for Controller I/O Connectors

After the wiring of the controller's I/O connectors is completed, check the following before turning ON the power:

## **Check Point (1)**

Using a circuit tester, check across the **"+24V terminal"** and **"0V terminal"** of each connector and across the **"E24V terminal"** and the **"E0V terminal"** to see that there is no continuity.

If the connector wiring between the Robot Controller's "+24V terminal" and "0V terminal" and between the "E24V terminal" and the "E0V terminal" is shorted, damage to the power circuit of the Robot Controller will result.

## **Check Point (2)**

Using a circuit tester, check across **"each signal output terminal"** and **"+24V terminal"** or **"E24V terminal"** of each connector to see that there is no continuity.

1. If the wiring between "each signal output terminal" and "+24V terminal" or "E24V terminal" of each connector is shorted, damage to the output circuit and power circuit of the Robot Controller will result.
2. Wind adhesive vinyl tape around all ends of the unconnected wiring of each connector to prevent them from contacting other wiring and parts, which results in shorting.

# Configuring the I/O Allocation Mode Parameter

To switch between the mini I/O dedicated, RC3 compatible, standard, and all user I/O modes, you need to change the I/O allocation mode parameter using the WINCAPSIII. Regarding to operation procedures, please refer to "[I/O Mode Setting from WINCAPSIII](005271.html)" of START UP MANUAL.

If the controller has an I/O extension board that can be used in the RC3 compatible or standard mode as a factory option, the default is the standard mode.

# Wire Connection Required in Starting Up the Robot

This section shows the minimum wire connection required for the stand-alone robot unit to turn the motor power ON or run in Auto or Manual mode during adjustment in starting up the robot system.

## Configuration of Safety Circuit

Input signals to the safety circuit are important for safety. Be sure to configure their circuits with contacts as shown below, observing the notes given below.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

For the overall configuration of safety circuits, refer to Mini I/O MANUAL for respective controllers.

RC8A : [[NPN type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002347.html), [[PNP type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002348.html)

RC8 : [[NPN type] Safety Circuit of RC8](001374.html), [[PNP type] Safety Circuit of RC8](001381.html)

## Wire Connection Required for Motor ON

Short-circuiting both the Emergency Stop input circuits (dual line) only enables the motor to turn ON.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| External Emergency Stop 1 | #2 and #36 on Mini I/O connector |
| External Emergency Stop 2 | #3 and #37 on Mini I/O connector |

Two External Emergency Stop input signals must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the emergency stop state cannot be reset.

## Wire Connection Required for Automatic Operation

Turning this signal ON (shorting) enables switching to Auto mode.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| Enable Auto 1 | #1 and #35 on Mini I/O connector |
| Enable Auto 2 | #31 and #65 on Mini I/O connector |
| Protective Stop 1 | #4 and #38 on Mini I/O connector |
| Protective Stop 2 | #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector |

1. Two Enable Auto and two Protective Stop input signals must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the circuit will not operate.
2. If no Protective Stop input signals are needed, their circuits can be always short-circuited by terminal connection with jumpers between #4 and #38 and between terminals #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector.

# Cleaning Intake Port Filter

Intake port filters are located at intake side of the controller.

Clogging the filters may be subject to insufficient cooling of inside robot controller which may result in malfunction of internal electronics components due to heat.

Clog of filter may be one of the causes when power module error is displayed. Inspect and clean the filter.

Follow the procedure described below to clean the filters.

###### 1

Turn OFF the power switch (POWER switch) of the robot controller.

###### 2

Loosen each of a knurling screw to remove filter covers in locations of front panel.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/01355_1.png)

###### 3

Clean the filter with blowing air. Blow the air in the direction opposite to normal air flow.

Cleaning air must be de-humidified and de-oiled clean one.

Heavy stain of filter should be washed by water or lukewarm water (40 degree C or lower). Using neutral detergent may help further clean wash.

1. Thoroughly dry the filter before assembling it.
2. Replace the filter with new one when it does not become clean with air blow and water wash.

###### 4

Re-assemble the filter.

Reattach the filter cover that you removed in STEP 2 to where it was.   
 Secure the filter cover by tightening the knurling screws.

Any clearance between the front panel and the filter cover may cause the controller to break down. To prevent this, ensure that the cover is secured without clearance.

# Regarding RC8 Safety-I/O-less Version

Safety-I/O-less version of manufacturer option is described here.

Only the parts that differ from the standard controller are described here so that please refer to description for the standard controller as well.

Some of the controllers of safety-I/O-less version are not able to be used or sold as they are, depending on national or regional laws or regulations regarding safe.   
In such case, safety system should be additionally installed in the system side or use the standard controller with safety I/O in order to meet such laws or regulations.

# Wire Connection Required to Prepare a Robot and RC8 (Safety-I/O-Less)

This section shows the minimum wire connection required for the stand-alone robot unit to turn the motor power ON or run in Auto or Manual mode during adjustment in starting up the robot system.

## Configuration of Emergency Stop Circuitry

The *External Emergency Stop* and *Enable Auto* input signals are important for safety. Be sure to configure their circuits with contacts as shown below.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Wire Connection Required for Motor ON

Short-circuiting both the *Emergency Stop* input circuits (dual line) only enables the motor to turn ON.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| *External Emergency Stop 1* | #2 and #36 on connector CN5 |
| *External Emergency Stop 2* | #3 and #37 on connector CN5 |

The different status between two emergency stop circuits, if kept for at least approx. one second, will be interpreted as an occurrence of trouble, triggering an error "One of the external emergency stop  
line is disconnected."

## Wire Connection Required for Automatic Operation

1. Turning this signal ON (shorting) enables switching to Auto mode.
2. Turning this signal OFF (opening) enables switching to Manual or Teach check mode.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| *Enable Auto* | #1 and #35 on connector CN5 |
| *Protective Stop 1* | #4 and #38 on Mini I/O connector |
| *Protective Stop 2* | #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector |

If no *Protective Stop* input signals are needed, their circuits can be always short-circuited by terminal connection with jumpers between #4 and #38 and between terminals #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector.

# [NPN type] HAND I/O

The table below lists the pin assignment of Hand I/O(NPN type).

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| View from the cable side | | | | |
| Terminal No. | Name | Port No. | Wire color | |
| Standard | Reinforced |
| 1 | Hand output | 64 | Black | Blue |
| 2 | Hand output | 65 | Brown | Yellow |
| 3 | Hand output | 66 | Black | Green |
| 4 | Hand output | 67 | Brown | Red |
| 5 | Hand output | 68 | Red | Violet |
| 6 | Hand output | 69 | Orange | Blue |
| 7 | Hand output | 70 | Yellow | Yellow |
| 8 | Hand output | 71 | Green | Green |
| 9 | Hand input | 48 | Blue | Red |
| 10 | Hand input | 49 | Violet | Violet |
| 11 | Hand input | 50 | Pink | White |
| 12 | Hand input | 51 | Pink | White |
| 13 | Hand input | 52 | White | White |
| 14 | Hand input | 53 | White | White |
| 15 | Hand input | 54 | White | White |
| 16 | Hand input | 55 | White | Brown |

| 18 | Power output  (+0 VDC)  (External/internal source) | - | White | Brown |
| 19 | NC | - | White | Brown |
| 20 | NC | - | White | Brown |

# [NPN type] User-Input, System-Input and Hand-Input Circuits for RC8

The figure below shows examples of the user-input, system-input and hand-input circuit configurations and connections of the robot controller.

1. In addition to PLCs, proximity switches and relay contacts can be directly connected to the input terminals of the robot controller.
2. Note that the leakage current from the proximity switches should be 1 mA or below.
3. Use multi-core shielding cables for protecting the controller from external noise and ground them at the controller side.
4. The maximum allowable capacity for the total of Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Parallel I/O of the internal source is 1.3A. Use the internal source within this allowable range.

# [NPN type] User-Output, System-Output, and Hand-Output Circuits for RC8

The figure below shows examples of the configuration and connection of the robot controller's user-output, system-output and hand-output circuits.

1. The User-Output, System-Output and Hand-Output Circuits are open collector output circuits.
2. The maximum allowable source current is 70 mA.  
   Keep the current consumption of a device to be connected to the Robot Controller, such as a PLC and a relay coil, below the allowable current.
3. Select an induction load, such as a relay coil, which has a built-in diode (for absorbing inverse electromotive force).  
   To use an induction load without a built-in diode, add a diode equivalent to the 1S1888 (Toshiba) in close vicinity to the coil.  

   When externally attaching a diode, connect it with correct polarity. Incorrect polarity may damage the Output circuit.
4. Connecting a lamp requires a circuit through which dark current flows and use a lamp whose rating is 0.5W or less.  

   Since the initial resistance of a lamp is small, the output circuit may be damaged by rush current that flows when the lamp lights. To reduce rush current, select and connect a resistor R that allows dark current 1/3 or less of the rated current to flow when the lamp goes OFF.  
   Refer to the figureabelow.
5. Use a multi-core shielding cable for the purpose of protecting the devices from external noise. Ground it to the robot controller.
6. The maximum allowable capacity for the total of Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Parallel I/O of the internal source is 1.3A. Use the internal source within this allowable range.
7. +24V internal power source of the robot controller must not be grounded.  

   If the output terminal +24V of internal power source is grounded, there may be a case where the controller is damaged.
8. After the controller power supply is turned ON, the outputs perform with full-load until software start-up has finished. Do not use the outputs as signals before the start-up has finished.

# [NPN type] Configuration of Safety Circuit for RC8

Input signals to the safety circuit are important for safety. Be sure to configure their circuits with contacts as shown below, observing the notes given below.

For the entire scheme of safety circuit, see the followings.

RC8 : [[NPN type] Safety Circuit for RC8](001374.html)

## Precautions on Connecting the Safety I/O

1. Two External Emergency Stop input signals must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the emergency stop state cannot be reset.
2. Two Protective Stop input signals and two Enable Auto input signals each must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the circuitry will not operate.
3. If an inconsistency between the External Emergency Stop signal and the Enable Auto input signals, or between the Protective Stop signal and the Enable Auto input signals continues over a certain period of time(about 0.5sec), an error occurs.

## Input Circuits to the Safety Circuits

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Precautions for Multiple Controllers are Used

If you use two or more controllers, the External emergency stop input of each controller must be controlled at the separate points. If these are connected to the same line, it may damage the controllers. Please refer to the following connection diagrams.  
Each connection point of the enable Auto input and the Protective stop input must be controlled at the separate points as well.

# [NPN type] Safety Circuit for RC8

The figure below shows an internal connection equivalent circuit for the safety circuit in the controller. The actual safety circuit is configured with safety relays and others.

## Safety Circuit

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001374_1.png)

Please refer to this if the figure is not clear.[(PDF:293KB)](Img/001374/001374_1.pdf)

## Different Stop States Resulting from Emergency Stop input, Protective Stop, and Enable Auto (OFF)

1. The emergency stop input (External Emergency Stop or teach pendant/mini-pendant input) shuts down the power to the motor and resets the program, provided that the Continue parameter is set to the default (0: Disable) in Continue setting.
2. The Protective Stop or Enable Auto (OFF) input signal shuts down the power to the motor and places the robot in the Continue Stop state.

# [PNP type] User-Input, System-Input and Hand-Input Circuits for RC8

The figure below shows examples of the user-input, system-input and hand-input circuit configurations and connections of the robot controller.

1. In addition to PLCs, proximity switches and relay contacts can be directly connected to the input terminals of the robot controller.
2. Note that the leakage current from the proximity switches should be 1 mA or below.
3. Use multi-core shielding cables for protecting the controller from external noise and ground them at the controller side.
4. The maximum allowable capacity for the total of Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Parallel I/O of the internal source is 1.3A. Use the internal source within this allowable range.

# [PNP type] User-Output, System-Output, and Hand-Output Circuits for RC8

The figure below shows examples of the configuration and connection of the robot controller's user-output, system-output and hand-output circuits.

1. The User-Output, System-Output and Hand-Output Circuits are open collector output circuits.
2. The maximum allowable source current is 70 mA.  
   Keep the current consumption of a device to be connected to the Robot Controller, such as a PLC and a relay coil, below the allowable current.
3. Select an induction load, such as a relay coil, which has a built-in diode (for absorbing inverse electromotive force).  
   To use an induction load without a built-in diode, add a diode equivalent to the 1S1888 (Toshiba) in close vicinity to the coil.  

   When externally attaching a diode, connect it with correct polarity. Incorrect polarity may damage the Output circuit.
4. Connecting a lamp requires a circuit through which dark current flows and use a lamp whose rating is 0.5W or less.  

   Since the initial resistance of a lamp is small, the output circuit may be damaged by rush current that flows when the lamp lights. To reduce rush current, select and connect a resistor R that allows dark current 1/3 or less of the rated current to flow when the lamp goes OFF.  
   Refer to the figureabelow.
5. Use a multi-core shielding cable for the purpose of protecting the devices from external noise. Ground it to the robot controller.
6. The maximum allowable capacity for the total of Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Parallel I/O of the internal source is 1.3A. Use the internal source within this allowable range.
7. +24V internal power source of the robot controller must not be grounded.  

   If the output terminal +24V of internal power source is grounded, there may be a case where the controller is damaged.
8. After the controller power supply is turned ON, the outputs perform with full-load until software start-up has finished. Do not use the outputs as signals before the start-up has finished.

# [PNP type] Configuration of Safety Circuit for RC8

Input signals to the safety circuit are important for safety. Be sure to configure their circuits with contacts as shown below, observing the notes given below.

For the entire scheme of safety circuit, see the followings.

RC8 : [[PNP type] Safety Circuit for RC8](001381.html)

## Precautions on Connecting the Safety I/O

1. Two External Emergency Stop input signals must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the emergency stop state cannot be reset.
2. Two Protective Stop input signals and two Enable Auto input signals each must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the circuitry will not operate.
3. If an inconsistency between the External Emergency Stop signal and the Enable Auto input signals, or between the Protective Stop signal and the Enable Auto input signals continues over a certain period of time(about 0.5sec), an error occurs.

|  |

## Precautions for Multiple Controllers are Used

If you use two or more controllers, the External emergency stop input of each controller must be controlled at the separate points. If these are connected to the same line, it may damage the controllers. Please refer to the following connection diagrams.  
Each connection point of the enable Auto input and the Protective stop input must be controlled at the separate points as well.

# [PNP type] Safety Circuit for RC8

The figure below shows an internal connection equivalent circuit for the safety circuit in the controller. The actual safety circuit is configured with safety relays and others.

## Safety Circuit

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001381_1.png)

Please refer to this if the figure is not clear. [(PDF:293KB)](Img/001381/001381_1.pdf)

## Different Stop States Resulting from Emergency Stop Input, Protective Stop, and Enable Auto (OFF)

1. The emergency stop input (External Emergency Stop or teach pendant/mini-pendant input) shuts down the power to the motor and resets the program, provided that the Continue parameter is set to the default (0: Disable) in Continue setting.
2. The Protective Stop or Enable Auto (OFF) input signal shuts down the power to the motor and places the robot in the Continue Stop state.

# For RC8 Safety-I/O-less Version

The differences in the controller of safety-I/O-less version compared to the standard controller are described here.

The following points are different:

* Pin alignment of Mini I/O
* Emergency stop circuit architecture

Some of the controllers of safety-I/O-less version are not able to be used or sold as they are, depending on national or regional laws or regulations regarding safe. In such case, safety system should be additionally installed in the system side or use the standard controller with safety I/O in order to meet such laws or regulations.

| 12 | Strobe Signal (System input) | 1 | Blue | 46 | Robot Running (System output) | 17 | White | |
| 13 | Data area bit 0 (System input) | 2 | Violet | 47 | Robot Error (System output) | 18 | White | |
