ID : 1632

# Escaping from the Interference Check Area

## When Entering the Interference Check Area

If the [interference check setting](001631.html) is 1 or 2, an error will be issued once a robot enters the interference check area. (Error code: 0x83201281 to 0x832012A0, Message:TCP is interfering with Area\*)   
If the interference check setting is 2, the robot may escape from the interference check area with a teach pendant or mini pendant. In this case, you can use operations marked with "Available" in the table below only.

| Mode | Operation | | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Motor ON | Manual key | Variable shift | Motor lock | Direct |
| Manual | Available | Available | N/A | Available | N/A |
| Teach check | N/A |  | N/A | N/A |  |
| Auto | N/A |  |  | N/A |  |

### Escaping Procedure

###### 1

Error will occur when the robot enters the interference area.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001632_1.png)

###### 2

Switch off AutoEnable to change the operation mode to Manual.

###### 3

Move the robot outside the interference area.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001632_2.png)

1. Since the robot can move to the direction where an interference point exists,  
   make sure to move the robot in the direction away from the interference point.
2. Error will be issued once a robot enters the interference check area again. (Error code: 0x83201281 to 0x832012A0, Message:TCP is interfering with Area\*)
3. If the areas of interference overlap, as shown in the figure below, error occurs first upon the robot end starting within the area 1 enters in the area 2. However, this can be avoided by aid of the method given above.  
    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001632_3.png)

## When Leaving the Interference Check Area

The measures of this case is the same as that of "When entering the interference check area" mentioned above.  
If the [interference check setting](001631.html) is 4 or 5, an error will be issued once a robot leaves the interference check area. (Error code: 0x83201281 to 0x832012A0, Message:TCP is interfering with Area\*)  
If the interference check setting is "5", the robot may escape from the interference area. The way of this operation is the same as setting "2" to "When entering the interference check area".  
For about the way of escape from the interference check, refer to the description above. Note that the motion directions (inner/outer) are reversed.

# Machine Lock

Lock the machine to perform simulations with the robot controller without running the robot practically.

## Lock the Machine When

1. Testing programs without running the robot practically.
2. Checking the cycle time.

The cycle time calculated may be shorter than the actual one since End motion (@0 option) will apply when the machine is locked.

Also, the robot trajectory may deviate from the actual motion. In order to check the accurate cycle time and robot motion, use actual machine.

## Operation Procedure

This setting can be made by the button operations of the teach pendant.  
For details, refer to "[Simulating a Program Operation with Teach Pendant](005245.html)" in the Teach Pendant Operation Guide.

# Inching

Inching refers to moving robot slightly by a specified distance or angle each time any of the arm traverse keys is pressed in Manual mode. It is used for fine positioning. Once inching is set, it takes effect until the robot controller is turned off or it is cancelled.

When the robot controller is turned on, the default is normal speed running.

In Auto mode or Teach check mode, inching will not take effect. Even if inching is selected, switching from Manual mode to any other mode will automatically cancel inching. Switching back to Manual mode will cause the robot to switch back to inching.

## Operating Procedure

This mode can be selected using the teach pendant or mini-pendant.

For the operating procedures, refer to "[Displaying and Changing External Speed Setting Screen (Inching Mode)](001804.html)" of the TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE, or "[Changing the Inching Angle and Distance](001830.html)" of the MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Continue Function

Continue function is the function that restarts multiple suspended programs due to errors or other reasons during [multitasking](001593.html) from the latest process.  
To restart multiple tasks simultaneously is called "Continue start".  
The condition that able to execute "Continue start" is called "Continue-stopped (condition)".  
If the robot is moved by some cause after it is stopped, "Continue start" cannot be executed.

## Conditions to Enable "Continue-stopped(condition)"

"Continue-stopped(condition)" is executed when at least one of the following conditions is satisfied.

* Halt or Step stop for all tasks
* Motor power OFF
* Level 1 or Level 2 errors
* The emergency button on the teach pendant is pressed, or [Emergency Stop] caused by releasing the external emergency stop input (system input signal).  

  This condition is effective when [Suspend all tasks] is selected from [Program after Robot Stop] in the teach pendant settings.  
  For more details, refer to "[Settings Associated with Program Stop](001725.html)" of the teach pendant operation guide.

## Resume Operations

When "Continue start" is executed, all the programs being stopped by "Continue-stopped(condition)" resume operation.

### "Continue Start" Operating Procedure

"Continue start" is available only when there are "Continue-stopped" programs.  
To execute "[Continue Start Permitted (Output)](001000.html)" from I/O, be sure to check Continue start permission output signal is issued beforehand.

Regarding to operation procedures, please refer to "System I/O signal guide"

* "[Continue Start (011)](001421.html)" and "[Continue Start Permission (output): Selectable by I/O hardware setting](001402.html)" of Mini I/O" of the Mini I/O dedicated mode
* "[Program Operation Command(0001)](001012.html)" and "[Continue Start Permitted (Output)](001000.html)"of the Standard mode.
* "[Continue Start (Input)](001046.html)" and "[Continue Start Permitted (Output)](001035.html)"of the Compatible mode.

### Enabling Continue Start Permission Signal (in Mini I/O Dedicated Mode)

The continue start permission signal is disabled by factory default in mini I/O dedicated mode. One of the user outputs can be configured to be used as a continue start permission signal.

"[Continue Start Permission (output): Selectable by I/O hardware setting](001402.html)" of "System I/O signal guide".  
Regarding to the operation procedure, please refer to "[Displaying and Changing I/O Parameters](001769.html)" of "Teach pendant operation guide".

## Resetting Programs

Reset a "Continue-stopped" program to restart it from the beginning.

Regarding to operation procedures, please refer to the following links.

### From Teach Pendant

"[Displaying Program List Window (Automatic Mode)](001719.html)" of the Teach Pendant Operation Guide

### From Mini Pendant

"[Resetting Programs](001837.html)" of Mini Pendant Operation Guide.

### From System I/O Input Signals

* System I/O Signals Guide
* "[Specified Program Reset (100)](001422.html)" and "[All Programs Reset (101)](001423.html)" of Mini I/O Dedicated mode
* "[Program Operation Command(0001)](001012.html)" of Standard mode
* "[Program Reset (Input)](001041.html)" of Compatible mode

## Position Gap Detection Function

If the position or figure of the robot is changed after robot operation completes, "Continue start" execution may cause an error.  
This error occurs when the positional gap between current position and the robot stopped originally goes beyond the allowable level.  
Allowable level is set in "Allowance for Position gap detection(J1-J8)" of "[Configuration List](001551.html)".

# Parameters for the Continue Function

The Continue function enables "Automatic position restoration" and "Continue start." The user can access those Continue parameters listed in the table below.

## Parameters for the Continue Function

| Parameter | Setting | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Program stop state of emergency stop | 0: Reset Stop (Factory default) | "Continue stop" is effective in any of the following: (1) "Halt (Stop)" or "Step Stop," (2) Motor OFF, (3) Error at Level 2 |
| 1: Continue Stop | "Continue stop" is effective in any of the following: (1) to (3) above, (4) When the emergency stop button on the teach pendant is pressed, (5) When an external emergency stop input signal (system input signal) is released. |
| Allowance for position restoration arm | J1 to J6 (10 degrees.) | This parameter shows the valid area for performing Auto Position Correction. The valid area is expressed in degrees. |

The parameter "Program stop state of emergency stop" is in [Program](005824.html) parameter.

The parameter "Allowance for position restoration arm" is in [User](005818.html) parameter.

# Resetting Programs

Reset a "Continue-stopped" program to restart it from the beginning. Reset a program using the following methods:

## Using the Teach Pendant or Mini-Pendant

### Teach Pendant

Select a program in the program list screen and press [RESET] button.  
For details, refer to the "[Displaying Program List Window (Automatic Mode)](001719.html)", "[Displaying Program List Window (Teach Check Mode)](001729.html)" and "[Displaying Program List Window (Manual Mode)](001721.html)" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

### Mini-Pendant

To reset a program with Mini-pendant, use "Reset" screen.  
For details, refer to the "[Resetting Programs](001837.html)" of MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

## Using System Input Signals of I/O

### Mini I/O Dedicated Mode

Use an IO command dedicated to the program reset.  
For details, refer to the "[SPECIFIED PROGRAM RESET (100)](001422.html)" and "[ALL PROGRAMS RESET (101)](001423.html)" of SYSTEM I/O SIGNALS GUIDE.

### Standard Mode

Use an IO command dedicated to the program reset.  
For details, refer to the "[Program Operation Command(0001)](001012.html)" of SYSTEM I/O SIGNALS GUIDE.

### Compatible Mode

Use the program reset input.  
For details, refer to the "[Program Reset (Input)](001041.html)" of SYSTEM I/O SIGNALS GUIDE.

# Break Point Function

A break point may be set at any program step in programs. If a program is running and encounters a break point, it will immediately stop.

The step where a break point is set cannot be executed.

A break point can be set regardless of the operation mode.  
 Furthermore, a break point can be set in normal tasks, supervisory tasks, and operation panel tasks.

## Break Point Stop Mode

When a program encounters a break point step, either of the following two stop modes may be selected:

1. Immediate halt of that program in which the break point is set  
    If the program stops due to this setting, the program is Hold-stopped.
2. Immediate halt of all running programs  
    If the programs stop due to this setting, the programs are Continue-stopped.

## Clearing the Break Point

The break points to be cleared can be selected using the following methods.

* Clearing all the break points in a specified PacScript file or operation panel file
* Clearing all the break points in all the PacScript files and operation panel files

Further, turning off the robot controller power clears the break points in all the PacScript files and operation panel files.

## Operation Procedure

This setting can be made by the button operations when the teach pendant displays the program content.  
For details, refer to "[Displaying Folder or Contents of the File](001720.html)" in the Teach Pendant Operation Guide.

# Logging

Various types of logs can be recorded for robot operations and viewed or saved.

This data can be put to use to search out the causes of errors and remedy them to shorten cycle time.

Recording times, saving fields and acquisition methods differ according to the type of log.

The number of logs recordable is decided by log types.

The two types of memory fields for recording log data are as follows.

* [Working memory](005076.html)  
   Data will be lost in this field when the controller's power is switched off.
* [Data storage memory](005076.html)  
   Data is retained even when the power of the controller is switched off.

The types of logs usable are as follows.

| Log name | Acquisition timing | Acquisition interval | No. saved | Data record memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Error log | Regularly saved | When errors occur | 1,000 | Data storage memory |
| Operation log | Regularly saved | When operational event occurs | 1,000 | Data storage memory |
| Control log | Manual/program | Select from 8/16/24/32 ms | 30,000 | Working memory (\*1) |
| Trace logging | Manual/program | Command execution | 10,000 | Working memory |
| Servo log | Program | Select from 1-8 ms | 60,000 | Working memory |

(\*1) Control log data can be manually copied to Data storage memory.

# Log Record Timing

Logs are recorded at four different times as follows.

* Regular recording  
   Error logs and operational logs are regularly recorded. 1,000 logs can be recorded for each, with the latest 1,000 being retained.
* [Manual recording](002179.html) by WINCAPSIII or the teach pendant  
  Recording can be started and stopped manually using WINCAPSIII or the teach pendant.
* [Recording by program commands](001660.html)  
   Settings are available to start/stop log records or clear them in programs. This is used to record a particular operation in a program.  
   It is also possible to determine the range of logging by specifying program lines.

# Recording by Program Commands

The logs for which you can control the logging timing using program commands, a teach pendant, or WINCAPSIII are control log, trace log, and servo log. These logs use a memory field called a ring buffer. The ring buffer has a fixed capacity and overwrites its oldest data with the latest.

| When recording starts | When the log exceeds buffer size |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

## Command Types

By using the following three command logs can be retained for program-specified areas.

### CLEARLOG command

Deletes data retained in the ring buffer and starts logging.  
To obtain the logged data, you need to execute the STARTLOG or STOPLOG command below.

The CLEARLOG commands for each log are as follows:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Control log | [SysLog.Ctrl.Clear](000393.html) |
| Trace log | [SysLog.Trace.Clear](000396.html) |
| Servo log | [SysLog.Servo.Clear](000399.html) |

### STARTLOG command

Starts obtaining log data.

Executing this command starts obtaining log data from the logging initiated by the CLEARLOG command.

If the CLEARLOG command has not been executed before the STARTLOG command is executed, the data stored in the ring buffer will be deleted and then log data acquisition will start. In this case, when the STARTLOG command is executed, logging and log data acquisition start simultaneously.

The STARTLOG commands for each log are as follows:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Control log | [SysLog.Ctrl.Start](000391.html) |
| Trace log | [SysLog.Trace.Start](000394.html) |
| Servo log | [SysLog.Servo.Start](000397.html) |

### STOPLOG command

This command stops recording the log. Logging to the ring buffer stops at this command position.

The STOPLOG commands for each log are as follows:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Control log | [SysLog.Ctrl.Stop](000392.html) |
| Trace log | [SysLog.Trace.Stop](000395.html) |
| Servo log | [SysLog.Servo.Stop](000398.html) |

## Target Log Data to be Obtained

Logging is started with the CLEARLOG command; however, log data will not be obtained. The log data that can be obtained varies depending on the stop timing specified by the parameter, the STARTLOG command, or the STOPLOG command.

The differences in the timing of the start and end of log data acquisition are described below, along with the images.

In the image below, the light blue line indicates logging, and the red line indicates the log data that can be obtained.

### (1) Log Data from the STARTLOG Command to the Stop Timing Specified in Advance by the Parameter

Logging start: When the CLEARLOG command is executed.

Start of log data acquisition: When the STARTLOG command is executed.

End of log data acquisition: When the stop timing specified by the parameter [Control log mode] has elapsed.

After starting logging with a command such as the CLEARLOG command, executing the STARTLOG command starts log data acquisition. If the stop timing specified by the parameter has elapsed before the STOPLOG command is executed, you can obtain log data from the STARTLOG command to that point.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001660_3.png)

### (2) Log Data from the STARTLOG Command to the STOPLOG Command

Logging start: When the CLEARLOG command is executed.

Start of log data acquisition: When the STARTLOG command is executed.

End of log data acquisition: When the STOPLOG command is executed.

After starting logging with a command such as the CLEARLOG command, executing the STARTLOG command starts log data acquisition. If the STOPLOG command is executed before the stop timing specified by the parameter elapses, you can obtain log data from the STARTLOG command to that point.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001660_4.png)

If the STOPLOG command is enabled after the stop timing specified by the parameter, the log data you can obtain is from the STARTLOG command to the stop timing specified by the parameter.

### (3) Log Data Traced Back from the Execution of the STOPLOG Command or an Error Occurrence to the Stop Timing Specified by the Parameter

Logging start: When the CLEARLOG command is executed.

Start of log data acquisition: None

End of log data acquisition: When the STOPLOG command is executed, or an error occurs.

If the STARTLOG command has not been executed after starting logging with a command such as the CLEARLOG command, you can obtain log data by tracing back the logged data for the duration specified by the parameter, starting from the time the STOPLOG command was executed or an error occurred.

Even if logging stops due to an error, you can obtain log data by tracing back the logged data right before the error occurred, since the ring buffer retains the log data.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001660_5.png)

However, if the time from the start of logging to the end of log data acquisition is shorter than the stop timing specified by the parameter, you can only trace back to the point when the logging started.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001660_6.png)

## Logging Stop Timing

The logging to the ring buffer will stop at the following timings.

* When the stop timing specified in advance by the parameter elapsed from the STARTLOG command.
* When the STOPLOG command is executed.
* When an error occurred.

A robot controller with the software version 2.16.\* or higher and the home position guidance license registered will also stop logging under the following conditions, in addition to the conditions above.

* When it goes into the emergency stop state (e.g., when the emergency stop button is pressed)
* When an operation to reset all programs is executed (e.g., reset all programs by I/O command)

# Acquisition of Log Data

Log data saved in the controller can be exported by the following methods.

| Way | | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Export to WINCAPSIII | Data transfer to WINCAPSIII | Log data checked in the robot controller is exported into WINCAPSIII in the data transfer window.  For details, refer to the "[Acquisition of Log Data](004490.html)" of WINCAPSIII GUIDE. |
| Data transfer using the WINCAPSIII log window | Log data is received and displayed by pressing the Receive button in the log windows displayed by WINCAPSIII (Not for servo logs).  For details, refer to the "[Acquisition of Log Data](004490.html)" of WINCAPSIII GUIDE. |
| Export to USB memory | | Log data can be exported from the controller to USB memory.  For details, refer to the "[Displaying and Reading Project List](001788.html)" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE. |
| Export using the provider | | Log data can be exported from the controller by using the provider. For details, refer to each command of the [RC8 Provider User's Guide](001511.html#ID001511_RC8guide) of RC8 series user’s manual.  * Error log    GetErrorLogCount : count of error log    GetErrorLog : data of the error * Operation log    GetOprLogCount : count of operation log    GetOprLog : data of the operation * Control log    GetLogCount : count of control log    GetLogRecord : data of control log |

# Log Acquisition Settings

Some logs contain multiple fields for saving log data. Choices are available to select from which field log data will be acquired with WINCAPSIII.

Under default (standard) settings the error and operation logs are acquired from SRAM, and other logs from DRAM.

Selecting the log data on the data transfer screen makes the Select log data source button active.

# Detailed Description of Log Types

## Error Log

Records errors occurring in the controller. The most recent 1,000 errors are recorded.

The error log is regularly updated.

* Date/time
* Module  
  Invoker
* Code  
   Error code
* Message
* Level  
   Error level
* Filename, LineNumber  
  Name of the file and the line number in which error occurred.
* Uptime

## Operation Log

This is a record of controller operations. The most recent 1,000 items are recorded.

The operation log is regularly updated.

* Date/time
* Client  
  The device that was operated is recorded. (Pendant: Teach pendant. PC: WINCAPSIII, etc. PC. I/O: I/O. System: System)
* Code
* Operation
* Uptime

## Control Log

A record of the robot's control, including movement of axes, current values, load ratios, etc.

This is useful in the following cases.

* Checking robot behavior within a specified range.
* Checking the age deterioration of the robot.
* Approximating the minimal load on the motor by predicting load ratios.

The recording interval and recording time can be set for control log.  
Recording can be made manually from the teach pendant or WINCAPSIII or through program operations.

The following items are recorded for the log data.

* Axis command values [deg or mm]  
   Axis angles commanded by the controller in the specified recording interval
* Axis encoder value [deg or mm]  
   Current axis angle values (actual values)
* Axis current values [%]  
   Current values in the motors of the axes (compared with the rated value)

  In RC7M, the displayed value was a value compared with the overcurrent error detection level.
* Axis load ratios [%]  
   Load ratios in the axes

## Trace Logging

Trace logging records the program execution flow and timing.

The data recorded is as follows.

* PRO Name, Line Number
* Code  
   Program code
* Logtime [ms]
* Uptime [ms]

## Servo Log

More detailed recording of motor control.

The recording interval can be set from 1-8 ms.

The recording time can be set from 10-60 s.

The data recorded in the log can be selected with the teach pendant.

* Motor speed [r/min]
* Real speed [r/min]
* Torque [% of rating]
* Deviation [deg]
* Current [%]
* Instruction [deg or mm]
* Encoder [deg or mm]

The recording range can be specified with the program and [the teach pendant](001735.html).

# Setting the Control Log Recording Interval and Duration

"Control log mode" and "Control log sampling time" for recording control logs can be configured in the ring buffer.

"Control log mode" is set in the range from 10 to 240 seconds in one second unit.

"Control log sampling time" can be selected from 8 to 32 milliseconds. Note that the setting value is expressed in multiples of 8. For example, if 16 milliseconds is specified, the recording interval will be 9 to 16 milliseconds. If 24 milliseconds is specified, the recording interval will be 17 to 24 milliseconds.

For information about setting procedure, refer to "[Displaying and Changing the Control Log Setting](001734.html)"of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# CALSET

CALSET refers to calibrating the relation between the actual robot position and the positional information of the controller.

CALSET is required when the motor is replaced or the positional data in the encoder is lost due to exhaustion of the encoder backup battery.

When CALSET is executed, the calibration data of the robot is recorded to the controller. This data is called CALSET data. The CALSET data is different for each robot.

Back up the CALSET data at regular intervals using WINCAPSIII.

# Method for Executing CALSET

## Execution Method

Record the position by manually pressing each of the axes of the robot against the mechanical end.

On an axis without a mechanical end, install a CALSET jig to temporarily provide a mechanical end for CALSET and press the axis against this mechanical end to record the position.

## Precautions for Executing CALSET

1. When executing CALSET, sufficient space is required to press the robot axes against the mechanical ends.
2. When executing CALSET, move the target axis near the mechanical stopper and release the brake to press it against the mechanical stopper.
3. Be careful when executing the CALSET command because it releases the motor brake and the robot starts moving under its own weight.
4. After completing CALSET, check that the axes stop at the software limits before they hit the mechanical ends in Manual mode.
5. In Auto mode, first run the robot at a low speed and gradually increase the speed while paying attention to safety. Adjustment is easier if the speed is gradually increased from a low value.
6. In a program created before execution of CALSET, the positions may be a little different after it.
7. When rotating axes after releasing the brake, be careful that the range of rotation does not exceed the allowable motion range (default software limit). If the axes are rotated beyond the software limit, a brake lock (motor power OFF) occurs even while the brake is released.  
    Be careful of the arm since it may rotate under its own weight after the brake is released depending on the robot posture and end-effector position.
8. If the RANG value remains unchanged after the mechanical end is changed, remove the part with the changed mechanical end before executing CALSET.

## Record of CALSET Position

Because of the installation conditions, if the robot cannot reach to the mechanical end, move the robot to any position and store each axis angle value on the position in J-type variables. Doing so, you can perform CALSET by using them as reference values. (This function is available in Ver.2.8.\* or higher.)

If you perform CALSET in other than mechanical end position, place a marking so that users could find CALSET position even if the internal position information is lost.

# Releasing Brakes

Release brakes to move axes while the motor is OFF during an emergency stop. Release brakes using either of the following two methods:

## Releasing Brake Using a Teach Pendant

Turn on the controller power and select axes with brakes to be released in the Release Brakes screen and press [OK].

For details, refer to [SETTING-UP MANUAL](001750.html).

## Releasing Brakes Using a Brake Release Unit

Use the axis selector switch to select axes with brakes to be released.

Press the brake release button.

# Setting the Next Robot Replacement Date

Sets the next replacement date of the encoder backup battery of the robot controller.

When the replacement day comes, a system message will appear in the menu bar of the teach pendant.

After replacing the battery, use this function to set the next battery replacement date.

For details, refer to [SETTING-UP MANUAL](001793.html).

# Anticipated Overload

By means of [Control Log](001664.html) results, you can display the predictive load ratio for a series of operations in the log range of process through the Teach pendant or the WINCAPSIII.  
If the predictive load ratio exceeds 80%, an overload error is likely to occur.  
For further details, refer to the "[Displaying the Estimated Load Factor](001737.html)" of Teach pendant operation guide, or "[Control Log](004495.html)" of the WINCAPSIII guide.

# Overview of Device

Teach pendant is an input and operating device for creating programs and teaching. All operations except the external automatic robot run can be performed on the teach pendant.

## Function

The functions of tech pendant are described below.

### Programming and teaching function

Function to input command and store memory of robot arm position. Specify program and input command step by step.

Also change, delete and copy the command and robot arm position.

Execute and confirm the program. (Teaching mode)

### Operating and controlling functions

Functions to turn on/off motor, start and stop automatic robot run, and perform manual operation.

### Display function

Display program contents, program execution status, execution step number, the current position of robot, and error message if there is an error.

# Specification

The specification of tech pendant is shown in the table below.

| Term | | Specification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type | | TP-RC7/8 |
| Power supply | | DC24V (supplied by the controller) |
| Display | LCD | Liquid crystal display with back light  7.5" TFT Color LCD, 640x480 pixels |
| LED | 3 LEDs (POWER, MOTOR, LOCK) |
| Operation | Switch & Key | Emergency stop button, deadman switch, jog dial, operating mode switch, motor key, lock key, robot selection key, motion mode key, speed key, cursor key, stop key, OK key, cancel key, moving direction key, shift key function key |
| Touch Panel | Use LCD screen as touch panel. |
| Emergency stop button | | 4B contact point, 4-circuit output (forced separation type) |
| Deadman switch  (Enable switch) | | 3-position type (OFF-ON-OFF), 2-circuit output |
| Operating mode switch | | 3-position switching with keys (AUTO, MANUAL, and TEACHCHECK)  Note: Mode can be switched only with keys. |
| Ambient temperature | | 0 to 40 ℃ |
| Humidity | | In operation: 20 to 90% RH (No dew condensation is allowed.)  In storage or during transportation: 40 to 75% RH (No dew condensation is allowed.) |
| Protect grade | | IP65 |
| Weight | | 1.6kg or less (Cable is not included) |
| Cable length | | 4m, 8m, 12m |

## Precautions for Handling

1. Since LCD is made of glass, please do not drop or apply any strong impact to it.
2. Since the surface of touch panel is easily scratched, please use fingers to operate it. Do not use a pen or any other sharp object.

# Connecting Teach Pendant

Controller is in "pendantless" for factory setting. Connect teach pendant to PENDANT connector of robot controller as shown in the figure below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001679_1.png)

## Precautions for Connecting Pendant Cable to Controller

1. Before connecting the cable, be sure to shut-off the robot controller.  
   If the cable is connected without shut-off the robot controller, the teach pendant and robot controller may fail.
2. Do not apply external force in the transverse or longitudinal directions to connector area (○ section of the above below) after connecting the cable. It may cause communication error due to the damaged connector.
3. Before disconnecting the cable, be sure to perform disconnection procedure, unlock the connector, and pull out the cable straight without twisting it. For information about the disconnection procedure, please refer to "[Displaying Setting Menu for Pendant and Panel](001776.html)".

# Pendantless

## About pendantless

Pendantless is defined as the state in which both teach pendant and mini-pendant are not connected to the robot controller.

## Precautions for pendantless

Since teach pendant and mini-pendant are absent in pendantless, the mode of robot will not be manual nor teach check mode.

Because of this, the mode will be automatic mode in open state of automatic robot run enabled input. (Unable to switch external mode, and unable to start program.)

Make sure to execute the following when using in pendantless.

1. It cannot start in open state of automatic robot run enabled input.
2. When it is in open state of automatic robot run enable input and automatic mode output AND sate, emergency stop is applied on the equipment.

Please add 1 or 2 items in external sequence circuit.

# Method to Replace Pendant Cable

Tech pendant has waterproof construction (IP65). Replace the cable with caution by following the procedure given below when replacing the cable. Pay attention when replacing cable; otherwise, it may deteriorate waterproof performance.

Please make sure to replace the attached O-ring for sealing when you replace the pendant cable.

###### 1

Loosen 5 screws to remove rear cover.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_1.png)

###### 2

Loosen Nut A for the cable clamp.

###### 3

Then loosen Nut B.

###### 4

Remove three connectors (A, B, and C) of pendant cable using long nose pliers or similar.

Make sure not to damage the wires, connectors, and the groove for O-ring when removing the connector.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_2.png)

###### 5

Remove cable from pendant.

Please pull out Connector A in the direction shown in the figure on the right.

###### 6

Remove old O-ring.

Be careful not to damage the groove for O-ring to remove using adhesive tape.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_3.png)

###### 7

Insert "replacement pendant cable" into ^ pendant, and tighten Nut B.

<Tightening torque>

Nut B: 1.69 to 1.85 Nm

###### 8

Pull the cable in the direction of arrow shown until the banding band on the cable comes to contact with inside the bush.

Make sure that the banding band stays in the cable bush when pulling cable.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_4.png)

###### 9

Tighten Nut A. Connect three connectors (A, B, and C) of pendant cable.

<Tightening torque> Nut A: 1.69 to 1.85 Nm

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_5.png)

###### 10

Install new O-ring in the groove.

Please install O-ring in the groove without twisting.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_6.png)

###### 11

Install rear cover and tighten 5 screws.

1. Make sure not to pinch O-ring when you install rear cover.
2. Tighten screws in the order 1 to 5 as shown in the figure on the below.

<Tightening torque>

Screw for rear cover: 0.54 to 0.66 Nm

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001681_7.png)

# How to Hold Teach Pendant and the Deadman Switch

Hold tech pendant with both hands to operate.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001684_1.png)

The function of deadman switch is to stop the robot automatically and safely when operator cannot perform normal operation due to the unexpected fainting or death during the manual operation of robot using teach pendant. When the operator falls into this situation, the strength of pressing this switch is going to be either very week or strong. Deadman switch is a 3-position switch that is designed to recognize the following three operation state.

1. If switch is not pressed or pressed lightly → Switch is OFF.
2. If switch is pressed with medium pressure → Switch is ON.
3. If switch is pressed too hard → Switch is OFF.

Robot stops and is not operable unless switch is ON.   
To ensure your safety, the teach pendant is designed so that the robot does not move unless both moving direction key and deadman switch are pressed at the same time when in manual mode.

Deadman switch is also called Enable switch.

Never keep the deadman switch (es) held down with adhesive tape or the like. Doing so may fail to stop the robot when running it in the Manual mode. It is extremely DANGEROUS.

If you switch the operation mode from Manual to Teach check, or from Teach check to Manual with the deadman switch pressed, motor power does not turn OFF. (Ver.1.13.\* or higher)

# Error Display

Display error code and error contents shown in "[Error code list](001075.html)" on the screen of teach pendant when there is an error in controller during operation of robot.  
Only error code will be displayed on the mini-pendant screen.  
Reset the error by pressing OK button on the error message window after processing the error.  
The reset of all programs can be also processed on the error message window.  
The display example of error message window is shown in the figure below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001689_1.png)

Press "Show detail" shown in blue on the error message window to check the detail information on error and the method to recover error.  
"Show detail" shown in blue will be changed to "Hide detail" if pressed. Conversely, press "Hide detail" to hide the detail information.  
The display example of detailed contents is shown in the figure below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001689_2.png)

# Error Log

Record error logs for the errors that are occurred in the controller.  
The error history that was recorded in the logs in the past can be checked on the teach pendant screen.

###### 1

Press [F6 Setting].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001690_1.png)

###### 2

Press [Operation and Error Log] button.  
It can be selected by the following procedure.

* Press [Operation and Error Log] button under function menu.
* Press [F4] on pendant.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001690_2.png)

Error Log screen opens.  
Press up and down cursor keys on the teach pendant to move the cursor keys on the screen up and down, and check the log history.  
The cursor on the screen can be scrolled by the following procedure.

* Turn jog dial on the tech pendant.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001690_3.png)

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [F1 Prev] | Display the previous page of the currently displayed log information. |
| [F2 Next] | Display the next page of the currently displayed log information. |
| [F3 Jump To] | Displays numeric keypad.  Enter the list No. of logs with numeric keypad, and press [OK] to display the log of the target list No. |
| [F6 Setting] | Display [Record error level setting] window.  Select error level to record as a log. Once pressed [OK], error log will be recorded at this set error level.  Record logs for all error levels when [Error level 0] is selected. |
| [F7 ClearLog] | Delete the registered log information.  Select the log information to delete, and press [OK] to delete the log. |

# Basic Screen and Icons

## Command for Teach Pendant

Various screens can be displayed on the liquid crystal screen by using keys, buttons and switches on the teach pendant.  
Each screen has its own command menu.In the command menu, press function keys to select command.

## Basic Screen

Display the basic screen.Commands in the command menu can be sequentially reached from this basic screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001692_1.png)

The language selection screen is displayed when turning on the controller for the first time.   
For details about the way of setting, refer to "[Turning ON Robot Controller](001695.html)".

ID : 1695

# Turning ON Robot Controller

It allows robot operation from teach pendant and mini-pendant, or automatic robot run by turning on the robot controller.

## Turning ON Robot Controller

To operate the robot, it is necessary to turn on the robot controller.

The robot controller controls and supplies all power needed for the operation of robot.

## Operation Procedures

###### 1

Press "-" display side of power switch of the controller shown in the figure below until it clicks.

Power lamp (the leftmost of three pilot lamps) turns on. The other two pilot lamps, "Automatic mode" and "Error", briefly flash immediately after turning on.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001695_1.png)

Once the controller is powered-ON, do not turn off the controller until the initialization has completed.  
Otherwise, data you have created may be damaged.

### Completion of the Initialization

You can check the completion of the initialization with the following messages or signals.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP | | When "Initializing" is disappeared. |
| I/O | Mini IO-dedicated allocation | When "Robot Initialized" or "Robot Error" (both of them are Mini IO-dedicated allocations) is output. |
| Standard assignment mode | When "Robot Initialized", "Robot Error" or "Robot Warning" (both of them are Standard assignment mode) is output. |
| RC3 compatible assignment mode | When "Robot Power ON Complete", "Robot Error" or "Robot Warning" (RC3 compatible assignment mode) is output. |

## Language Settings

The screen to select the appropriate language is displayed when turning on the controller. Select your language and press [OK].

###### 1

Teach pendant displays the screen to select the appropriate language when turning on the controller.

###### 2

Select your language and press [OK].

###### 3

Select "Do not display", and press [OK] to not display language selection screen from next time.

###### 4

A system message appears on the teaching pendant that indicates the controller shutdown for the language setting change. In this state, without pressing [OK], restart the controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001695_3.png)

If you press [OK] in the above state, the controller is automatically shutdown.

After that, you can change the language at the controller restart, however, do not power off the controller during the system shutdown process.

Depending on the controller type, the system shutdown completed state is different.

For information about controller type, refer to "[Controller Type](001314.html) ".

* Engine board is not indicated as "E"

  The system shutdown has been completed once the following window appears.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003317_7.png)

* Engine board is indicated as "E"

  Once the teaching pendant displays white-and-black noise pattern and emits loud fan noise, the system shutdown has been completed.

###### 5

Display the basic screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001695_2.png)

If the engine board is expressed as E in the controller type, when you restart the controller after the language setting change, it will take about three minutes to complete the start-up because the system automatically restart three times.

For information about controller type, refer to "[Controller Type](001314.html)".

ID : 1696

# Turning OFF Robot Controller

Turn OFF robot controller if any of the following is applicable.

1. Operation of robot is all completed.
2. Maintenance work on the robot unit is performed.
3. Maintenance work on the robot controller itself is performed.
4. Visual device and/or expansion board are installed to or removed from the robot controller.
5. The cable that connects the controller with robot unit is installed or removed.

Make sure that controller is completely turned off before installing or removing the cable that connects the controller with robot unit. If the controller is not turned off completely and these cables are installed and removed, the joint rotational angle encoder interface circuit may be damaged. This damage cannot be recovered unless the hardware is changed.

## Operation Procedures

###### 1

If MOTOR lamp is flashing, press MOTOR key to turn off motor. MOTOR lamp is embedded in MOTOR key.

MOTOR lamp turns off.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001696_1.png)

###### 2

Press down the power switch of the robot controller.

Power lamp (the leftmost of three pilot lamps) turns off.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001696_2.png)

# Initial Settings for Robot

Set the basic parameters such as "mass of payload" of the tip of robot arm (total mass of tool and payload if too is used), "payload center of gravity", and "optimal speed control function" to set proper speed and acceleration of robot under these load conditions.

## Set Mass of Payload, Payload Center of Gravity, and Optimal Speed Control Function.

Follow the procedures described below to set the mass of payload (total mass of tool and the payload) and the center of gravity if they are understood for the operating conditions of the robot.

## Operation Procedures

This setting cannot be performed from the mini-pendant. Perform the setting by using teach pendant or WINCAPSIII.

For specific robots, this initial setting is available with Easy Setting function. For details, refer to [Easy Setting (Teach pendant)](002505.html). (Ver.2.0.\* or higher)

###### 1

Press [F2 Arm] on the basic screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_1.png)

Robot current position screen shown in STEP 2 will be displayed.

###### 2

Press [F6 Aux].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_2.png)

(Note 1) The displayed screen may be different depending on the settings of display contents.  
 Arm auxiliary functions screen shown in STEP 3 will be displayed.

###### 3

Press [F1 Config].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_3.png)

Config screen shown in STEP 4 will be displayed.

###### 4

Select [1: Mass of payload [g] ].  
 The selected line will be highlighted.

Now, press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_4.png)

Numeric keypad as shown in STEP 5 will be displayed.

###### 5

Use numeric keypad to enter the required value.  
 Press [CLR] or [BS] key to cancel the entered value.  
 Check the entered value, and press [OK] if it is correct.  
 Press [Cancel] key to cancel the entire operation of this STEP and go back to the original settings.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_5.png)

The system message appears on the screen.  
 Check the entered value, and press [OK] if it is correct.  
 To discard the new choice, press [Cancel].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_6.png)

Numeric keypad is disappeared, and [1: Mass of payload [g] ] is updated with the newly entered value as shown below.  
 Press [OK] to confirm this value. Press [Cancel] key to cancel. Screen will be back to normal.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_7.png)

###### 6

Press [2: Payload center of gravity X [mm] ] to select.  
 The selected line will be highlighted.  
 Selection can be done by using jog dial or [F3 Jump To].

Now, press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_8.png)

Numeric keypad as shown in STEP 7 will be displayed.

###### 7

Use numeric keypad to enter the required value.  
 Press [CLR] or [BS] key to cancel the entered value.  
 Check the entered value, and press [OK] if it is correct.  
 Press [Cancel] key to cancel the entire operation of this STEP and go back to the original settings.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001698_9.png)

Numeric keypad is disappeared, and [2: Payload center of gravity X [mm] ] is updated with the newly entered value as shown below.

In the Safety motion specification, if [Mass of payload] of [Setting condition (User parameter)](005818.html) is smaller than [Max payload setting] of [Safety-related parameters](002614.html), an error message appears when [OK] is pressed. （Ver.2.5.\* or higher） Clear the error and then enter appropriate value.

 The selected line will be highlighted.

# Turning ON Motor

Robot can be operated by turning on motor.

Before turning on the motor, make sure that no persons including operator are not in the motion space of the robot.

To perform the following operation, it is necessary to turn on motor.

* Operate robot in manual mode, teach check mode, or automatic mode.

## Operation Procedures

To turn ON the motor, do the following procedure.

| Mode | Interlock between the deadman switch and motor power ON (\*1) | Operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manual mode ⁄ Teach check mode | Interlocked. (factory default setting) | Press the dead man switches. |
| Not interlocked. | Press MOTOR key while pressing the deadman switch. |
| Automatic mode | - | Press the MOTOR key. |

(\*1) For details about the interlock between the deadman switch and motor power ON, refer to "[The Setting of the Deadman Switch Linkage Function](001079.html)".

Motor lamp lights when power supply turns on. MOTOR lamp is embedded in MOTOR key.  
Under the manual mode, motor power turns on only when the deadman switch is pressed. Motor power turns off once the deadman switch is released.

Safety I/O less specification can be set so that the motor power being ON even if the deadman switch is released. For details, refer to the "[The Setting of the Deadman Switch Linkage Function](001079.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001699_1.png)

1. If "Error 8150101A; Command is not executable while emergency stop is ON" is displayed when motor is turned on, that the circuit of "External emergency stop input" pin for robot controller connector Mini I/O is not closed.
   The controller judges as in "emergency stop" for this condition. Close "External emergency stop" pin.
2. Motor cannot be turned on in the "machine lock" state.
3. If turn off the motor immediately after turning the motor on, "MotorBUS-FET failure" might occur. If an error occurs, reboot the controller power supply.

# Turning OFF Motor

Some robot types may not have brake function in their joints.   
If joints do not have brake function, retention torque will be dissipated when motor is turned off; hence, robot may move unexpectedly due to the gravity or other external forces. Note that this is very dangerous.

It is necessary to turn off motor if any of the following is applicable.

1. Enter to the motion space of robot.
2. Turn off the controller.
3. Move robot with hands.
4. Modify parameters.
5. Load task (user) program.
6. Execute CALSET (Select joint to be calibrated, or cancel the selection).
7. Cancel any of joint brakes.

## Operation procedures

Release the deadman switch to turn off motor when in manual mode.

Motor can be turned off while the deadman switch is pressed.   
In that case, press MOTOR key. MOTOR lamp turns off. MOTOR lamp is embedded in MOTOR key.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001700_1.png)

# External Speed Settings

The speed of robot is determined by internal speed and external speed.

The internal speed is the speed determined by the commands in the program.

External speed is the speed to be set using teach pendant or mini-pendant for teaching or test run, and the unit is expressed in percentage (%) of the maximum speed (internal speed).

## Note on Speed Setting

1. The initial value of the external speed is 1% when power is turned on.
2. Once the external speed is set, it is valid until the controller is turned off or the setting is updated.
3. Actual robot moves at [internal speed x external speed (%)] when in Auto mode. For example, if the external speed is set at 80%, the robot moves at internal speed x 80%.  
   It moves at 10% of the internal speed in manual mode and teach check mode. For example, if the external speed is set at 80%, it moves at 10% x 80% (i.e. 8%). The example of actual operating speed is given in the figure below.
4. When speed is set, acceleration and deceleration will be automatically calculated by the following equation.  
   Acceleration (%) = ((Speed) /100)2 x 100  
   Deceleration (%) = ((Speed) /100)2 x 100  
   (Calculation example) Assuming that speed is 20% :  
   Acceleration (Deceleration) = (20 / 100)2 x 100 = 4 %  
   These automatically calculated values can be modified using teach pendant or mini-pendant. In that case, the latest modified value will be valid.
5. The minimum tolerance for the setting is 0.1%, and the respective external acceleration and external deceleration are 0.0001%. If external speed of 1% or less is set, the displayed speed of bar graph on the status bar of teach pendant or mini-pendant will be 1%.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_1.png)

## Operation Procedures

Set the external speed at 20% or less for starting robot operation. If you manually operate the robot at high speed when you are not familiar with the operation, robot may collide with the surrounding structures.

The external speed, acceleration, and deceleration can be set while robot is operated by the program. However, this change in the setting becomes effective immediately, and robot also changes the speed immediately. Please note that this is dangerous.

###### 1

Press SPEED key on the basic screen. External speed settings screen shown in STEP 2 will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_2.png)

This screen can be also displayed by pressing around Speed bar on the screen.

###### 2

Check if SPEED line is selected on the external speed settings screen, and press [F5 Change]. Numeric keypad shown in STEP 3 will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_3.png)

* The value displayed in function key can be directly entered by using any of F1 to F4 keys instead of [F5 Change].
* This value can be increased/decreased with an increment of 5% by using right and left cursor keys. The value can be also increased/decreased with an increment of 2% by using jog dial.

###### 3

Use numeric keypad displayed on the screen to enter any value. Press [CLR] or [BS] key to cancel the entered value. Check the entered value, and press [OK] key if it is correct.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_4.png)

Numeric keypad is disappeared, and the external speed is updated with the entered value as shown below. Press [Cancel] key to cancel updating. Screen will be back to normal.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_5.png)

###### 4

Check the automatically calculated acceleration that is displayed on the external speed settings screen.

1. If this value is correct, skip the following procedures to go to STEP 6.
2. To change these values manually, select ACCEL line by using down cursor key, and press [F5 Change]. Numeric keypad shown in STEP 5 will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_6.png)

The value displayed in function key can be directly entered by using any of F1 to F4 keys instead of [F5 Change]. Note: This value can be increased/decreased with an increment of 5% by using right and left cursor keys. The value can be also increased/decreased with an increment of 2% by using jog dial.

###### 5

Use numeric keypad displayed on the screen to enter any value. Press [CLR] or [BS] key to cancel the entered value. Check the entered value, and press [OK] key if it is correct.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_7.png)

Numeric keypad is disappeared, and the acceleration is updated with the entered value as shown below. Press [Cancel] key to cancel updating. Screen will be back to normal. If [Cancel] is pressed here, then the updated external speed will be also back to the original state.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_8.png)

###### 6

Check the automatically calculated deceleration that is displayed on the external speed settings screen.

1. Press [OK] button to confirm this value if it is correct. Then, skip the following procedures to go to STEP 8.
2. To change these values manually, select ACCEL line by using down cursor key, and press [F5 Change]. Numeric keypad shown in STEP 7 will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_9.png)

The value displayed in function key can be directly entered by using any of F1 to F4 keys instead of [F5 Change].  
This value can be increased/decreased with an increment of 5% by using right and left cursor keys. The value can be also increased/decreased with an increment of 2% by using jog dial.

###### 7

Use numeric keypad displayed on the screen to enter any value. Press [CLR] or [BS] key to cancel the entered value. Check the entered value, and press [OK] key if it is correct.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_10.png)

Numeric keypad is disappeared, and the deceleration is updated with the entered value as shown below. Press [OK] to confirm this value.

Press [Cancel] key to cancel. Screen will be back to normal. If [Cancel] is pressed here, then the updated external speed and acceleration will be also back to the original state.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_11.png)

###### 8

The screen of teach pendant is back to the basic screen. Please make sure that the displayed speed of the right side of status bar is updated to the speed that is set by following the above procedures.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001701_12.png)

# Teaching

This section describes the method to teach robot the position variables P1 and P2 in manual mode.

Please be sure to backup your data when you edit programs or teach robot.

## Teaching Robot Position (P1)

Press [F2 Arm] on the teach pendant to display information on each axis of the arm.

Press moving direction keys as required while pressing the deadman switch to move robot to the position to be set as P1.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_1.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_2.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_3.png)

## Saving the Teaching Value in Variable P1.

Follow the procedure below to save the teaching value in [VarName P1].

###### 1

Press [F4 Variable].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_4.png)

Display the screen as shown in the next procedure.

###### 2

Select variable type in the variable window.  
This procedure is for saving position in P variable; hence, press [P variable tab] on the screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_5.png)

If robot arm information is displayed on the right side of screen when variable window opens, the information can be deleted by pressing [Robot] button.

###### 3

Select the field of [VarName P1] by using cursor key or jog dial.  
This can be also selected by directly pressing any of data field for variable name P1 on the screen.

12 types of data per one variable will be displayed in P variable screen as shown in the figure.  
If one of 12 types of data is highlighted when selecting [VarName P1], this means that [VarName P1] is selected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_6.png)

###### 4

Confirm that [VarName P1] is selected.

###### 5

Press [F6 Get Position].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_7.png)

###### 6

Check the system message. If you agree the message, select a checkbox of "Write the coordinate system information to Usage." and then press [OK]. (This function is available in Ver.1.8.\* or higher.)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_8.png)

The current position is loaded as variable P1. Coordinate system information is written in Usage (Use/Macro/Smart) cell.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_9.png)

* If any data is already written in the Usage cell, a new coordinate system information will overwrite it.
* When a controller is rebooted, the check box of "Write the coordinate system information to Usage" remains selected. (Ver.1.13.\* or higher)
* To clear a coordinate system information in a Usage cell, select desired Usage cell, and press [F5 Edit].

## Teaching Robot Position (P2) and Saving it to [VarName P2]

###### 1

Press [Cancel] button once to go back to [Current Robot Position] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_10.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_11.png)

###### 2

Press moving direction keys as required while pressing the deadman switch to move robot to the position to be set as P2.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_1.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_2.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001704_12.png)

###### 3

Follow the procedure described in STEP 2 "Saving the teaching value in [VarName P1]" to save the value of P2 in [VarName P2].

Now, teaching of P1 and P2 is completed.

For information about how to move to the specified positions, refer to "[Move to the Position Specified by Variable (only for J type, T type, and P type)](001762.html)" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Teach Check Mode

Teach check mode allows to operate automatic robot run with speed control, and checks if there are any mistakes in the program after teaching by using teach pendant or mini-pendant. The restrictions are described in the following.

* The maximum speed in teach check mode is regulated at 10% or less of the maximum speed set for the automatic mode.

The maximum speed of the robot in manual operation or teach check is regulated at 250 mm/s or less in flange (mechanical interface) and TCP points.

* Keep pressing both deadman switch and [OK] for program execution; otherwise, robot does not move.

Teach check includes two types of checks: single-cycle check and feed check.  
The selected program is executed only once from the current execution line to the end in the single-cycle check. The selected program is executed for only one step from the current execution line in the feed check.

Robot moves automatically by executing this operation. Operator must be out of the motion space of robot before starting the operation.

Multiple programs cannot be executed simultaneously in teach check mode. Therefore, all motion commands for specifying the simultaneous execution of another program will be ignored.

## When this operation is necessary

This operation is performed when you want to safely check or modify points and trajectories specified by teaching while performing automatic robot run besides the robot using the program.

# Single-Cycle Check

Press [Display] at the bottom of [Program list] window to check program contents during single-cycle check.

## Operation procedures

###### 1

Set operating mode switch to [TEACHCHECK].

Teach check icon will be displayed on the leftmost of the status bar.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001706_1.png)

###### 2

Press [F1 Program].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001706_2.png)

The following [Program list] window will be displayed.

###### 3

Select the program to check by using cursor key or jog dial, or by directly touching the screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001706_3.png)

The selected program will be highlighted.

###### 4

Press [OK] while pressing the deadman switch on teach pendant to turn on the motor.  
The [MOTOR] lamp turns on.

Motor cannot be turned on when the deadman switch is not pressed.   
Release the deadman switch to turn off motor.

###### 5

Set external speed, acceleration, and deceleration of robot by using [SPEED] button of teach pendant or by directly touching speed bar on the screen.

###### 6

Press [F4 CycleStart] on the program list screen in STEP 3.  
The following system message will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001706_4.png)

###### 7

Press [OK] while pressing the deadman switch. Keep pressing both deadman switch and [OK] until the execution of program is completed.  
Robot stops immediately if either of them is released before completing the execution.

# Run From

This is specifying the line to perform teach check from the given line during the teach check.

* Both single-cycle check and step forward check can be performed.

## When this Operation is Necessary

This is performed when you want to check or modify the operation or calculation of the given line and after during the teach check.

## Considerations for Execution by Specifying Line

* If the specified line is comment line or blank line that does not require any execution, the first executable line after the specified line will be executed.
* To specify the line, select appropriate program from the program list and specify the line.
* Error may occur if local variables are used without executing the commands for declare statement of the local variable, initialization of variable, and acquisition of axis control, or the calculation and motor operation are performed.

* Local variables will be save on the memory if the domain on the memory is released and the commands to declare local variables such as DIM and DEFINT are executed when user program is forwarded from WINCAPSIII and compiled on the teach pendant. Once local variable domain is saved, it will be maintained until it is released. Hence, local variables can be used without executing variable declare command after executing it once. However, even if the local variable domain is saved, contents of the variable will be indeterminate when it is used without initializing the local variable (assigning value).
* Multiple programs cannot be executed simultaneously in teach check mode. Therefore, all motion commands for specifying the simultaneous execution of another program will be ignored.
* Line cannot be specified for teach check on the mini-pendant. Operation procedures: the following operation procedures are common to single-cycle check and step forward check.

## Operation Procedures

###### 1

Proceed from STEP 1 to STEP 3 of the respective teach check ("[Single-cycle check](001706.html)" or "[Step forward check](001707.html)").

###### 2

Press [Display] on the screen. Program contents will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001708_1.png)

###### 3

Press [Run From] on the screen. Input numeric keypad will be displayed on the screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001708_2.png)

###### 4

Enter any line number and press [OK]. Input numeric keypad closes, and cursor moves.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001708_3.png)

###### 5

Continue to proceed from STEP 4 of the respective teach check ("[Single-cycle check](001706.html)" or "[Step forward check](001707.html)").

# Automatic Mode

Perform automatic robot run by executing the program selected from teach pendant or mini-pendant. Automatic robot run has three types: single-cycle start, continuous start, and step-start.

|  | Types of start | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Single-cycle Start | Execute the selected program from the beginning to the end only once. |
| 2 | Continuous Start | Execute the selected program repeatedly. |
| 3 | Step Start | Execute the selected program in only one step. |

Note: Robot moves when automatic robot run starts. Please read "Precautions for automatic robot run" before operation.

## When this operation is necessary

This operation is necessary when you check the motion of robot, or when you operate the robot alone without using external device such as PLC.

## Change of key switch

The protective stop function is activated when changing to the auto mode.

# Single-Cycle Start

Set the speed, acceleration and deceleration before executing single-cycle start operation.

Set the speed at less than 20% for starting operation. If robot is operated at high speed in the beginning, it may collide with the surrounding structures.

## Operation Procedures

###### 1

Set the operating mode switch to [AUTO].

###### 2

Press [F1 Program].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001710_1.png)

Display [Programs] window shown in the next step.

###### 3

Select the program to start by using cursor key or jog dial, or by directly touching the screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001710_2.png)

The selected program will be highlighted.

###### 4

Press [MOTOR] of the teach pendant to turn on the motor.   
 The [MOTOR] lamp turns on.

###### 5

Make sure that the selected program is highlighted, and tap [F4 Start].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001710_3.png)

The system message as shown in the next step will be displayed.

###### 6

Select [Single-cycle] in the [Run Program] dialog box, and press [OK].

Single-cycle start will be started.

During program running, always keep one hand free and ready to press the STOP key.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001710_4.png)

To restart the program after completing single-cycle start, go back to STEP 3 and repeat the operation.

The displayed run time shows time from the start of program to the end, which includes suspended time due to the step stop or halt.

Press [F1 Program].

# Emergency Stop

Pressing the emergency stop button halts currently running all programs and the robot stops. The motor power turns OFF at this timing.

## Operation Procedures

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001716_1.png)

Press [Emergency stop] button on the tech pendant.

Restarting the robot after an emergency stop executes the selected program from the first line.

To restart the robot, first turn the motor power ON, then execute any of the "step start," "cycle start," or "continuous start."

* Motor will be turned off at the emergency stop; however, robot may unexpectedly move by inertia.
* Make sure that there is no danger such as collision or accident in advance when restarting robot after emergency stop.If the robot is restarted as it is after emergency stop, it will execute the selected program from beginning.

## Difference of Stop Process in the Controller's Version

### Version 2.1.\* or higher

All axes synchronize the motion and stop at the same time. The robot stops on the planned path.

* Speed  
  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001716_2.png)
* Path  
  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001716_3.png)

### Version 2.0.\* or before

Each axis stops with the maximum deceleration speed respectively.

When all axes immediately stop with the maximum deceleration during synchronous motion or cooperative motion, the relative position and synchronicity are not guaranteed.

* Speed  
  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001716_4.png)
* Path  
  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001716_5.png)

If your controller is version 2.1.\* or higher, you can select the stop process for the version 2.0.\* or before as well. To do so, set the VRC parameter [48 : Stop process of robots at the emergency stop] to [0 : Stop at the axis maximum deceleration]. Please set the user level to [Maintainer] before the change.  
Reboot the controller after you change the parameter.

# Setting Connection with WINCAPSIII

## For EtherNet Connection

### Setting Robot Controller

Set robot controller to enable the communication between PC (WINCAPSIII) and robot controller through the Ethernet.This setting is done by teach pendant.

Set communication permission and IP address.

###### 1

Press [F6 Setting] on the basic screen of tech pendant.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_1.png)

[Settings (main)] window will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_2.png)

###### 2

Press [F5 Communication and Token].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_3.png)

[Menu] window of Communication Settings will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_4.png)

###### 3

Press [F2 Network and Permission].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_5.png)

[Communication Settings] window will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_6.png)

###### 4

Select [Permission] by using cursor key or jog dial, or by directly touching the screen.  
This can be also selected by directly touching the screen.  
The selected section will be highlighted.

###### 5

Press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_7.png)

The following system message will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_8.png)

###### 6

Select [Read/Write].

Communication permission is defined as follows.  
To use Ethernet, it is necessary to select [Read/Write].

* Disabled : Communication port is not used.
* Read only : Data of robot controller can be read in PC.Data cannot be sent from PC to robot controller.
* Read/Write : Data can be bidirectionally exchangeable between PC and robot controller.

Select, and then press [OK].  
The display will be back to [Communication Settings] window.

###### 7

Select [IP Address] by using cursor key or jog dial, or by directly touching the screen.  
The selected section will be highlighted.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_9.png)

###### 8

Press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_10.png)

Numeric keypad as shown in the next step will be displayed.

###### 9

Enter address using numeric keypad.  
Press [OK] on the numeric keypad after finishing entering the address.  
 Press [OK] to go back to [Communication Settings] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_11.png)

If subnet mask is also required to be changed, follow the operation procedure (STEP 7 to STEP 9) to change it.

###### 10

Press [OK] on Communication Settings screen.  
Display will be back to [Menu] window of Communication Settings.

###### 11

Press [Cancel] button twice on the tech pendant.  
Display will be back to the basic screen.

You can use multiple Ethernet IP address by adding a LAN adopter listed in "[RECOMMENDED BOARD LIST](005079.html)".  
Note that communication may fail if IP addresses in the same network are used.

* Incorrect IP address assignment  
  LAN1：192.168.0.1  
  LAN2：192.168.0.2
* Revised IP address assignment  
  LAN1：192.168.0.1  
  LAN2：192.168.1.2

# Displaying Program List Window (Automatic Mode)

Press [F1 Program] on the basic screen of automatic mode to display the following program list window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001719_1.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001719_2.png)

| Keys other than function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| Robot | Display 3D image of the robot during the machine lock. For information about operation keys, refer to " [Displaying Current Position Information and 3D Image of Robot](001731.html) ".  Button turns blue while robot button is pressed. |
| [Var](005071.html) | Display a static variable monitoring window. |
| Error | Display syntax error log information. |
| Reset | Reset the selected program or reset all programs. |
| Root | Move to root of folder. |
| Up | Move to the folder hierarchy that is one higher than the current one. |
| Path | Enter the file path on the displayed file path input screen, and press [OK] to move to the specified file path. |
| Display | Display contents of the selected folder and file. |
| Prev | Move to the previous page of the currently displayed program list. |
| Next | Move to the next page of the currently displayed program list. |
| Search | Enter the file name on the displayed file name search screen, and press [OK] to search the entered file name. |
| Up | Move to the folder hierarchy that is one higher than the current one. |
| Display | Display contents of the selected folder and file. |

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [[F1 Halt]](001715.html) | Halt the program being executed. |
| [F2 StepStop] | Execute step stop of the program being executed. |
| [F3 CycleStop] | Execute cycle stop of the program being executed. |
| [F4 Start] | Execute [single-cycle start](001710.html) or [continuous start](001711.html) of the selected program. |
| [F6 StepStart] | Execute step feed start of the selected program.  Step In and Step Over are available.  What's Step In : Run into the procedure caｌled from current program.  What's Step Over : Run over the procedure called from current program. |
| [F7 Reset] | Reset the selected program or reset all programs. |
| [F9 Priority] | Set priority of program (low to high). |
| [F10 Continue Start] | Execute continue start of all programs that are under suspension. |
| [[F11 Display]](001720.html) | Display contents of the selected folder and file. |

# Displaying Folder or Contents of the File

Operation path : [F1 Program] - [F11 Display]

Display the folder selected from the program list or contents of file.  
Press [F11 Display] to display the folder selected from the program list or contents of file as shown below.

When [Shift] is not pressed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001720_1.png)

When [Shift] is pressed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001720_2.png)

| Keys other than function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| Robot | Display 3D image of the robot during the machine lock.  Button turns blue while robot button is pressed. |
| [Var](005078.html) | Monitor variables in the program. |
| [Trace](005661.html) | Display trace log to record the flow and timing of program execution. |
| MSG | Output message. |
| BP | Set breakpoint.  System message of [BreakPoint Setting] will be displayed. Select one of "BreakPoint Setting", "Clear all BreakPoint in a file", and "Clear all BreakPoint in the project" in the message, and press [OK] to set or cancel the break point.  If the breakpoint is set in null line, proess does not stop at the breakpoint. |
| Reset | [Program reset] window opens. Select either "Only this program" or "All programs", and press [OK] to reset the target program. |
| Auto | Switch the auto scroll settings ON and OFF. When this option is ON, the button lights blue.  This option is ON under normal state.In ON state, the cursor in the editor follows the currently running line. By that, user can check which line is executed on the screen.  If this option turns OFF, the cursor in the editor can move anywhere within the displayed file.By that, arbitrary line can be displayed.  Note 1: The displayed file is not switched during this option turns OFF  Note 2: This option turns ON when restarting the controller |
| [Call Stack](005898.html) | Display a history of program call.  This item is available in Auto mode and in Teach-check mode. |
| [Cmd Build](005899.html) | With this function, some commands are automatically entered. You can enter necessary parameters at a time. This item is available in Auto mode. |
| [Log](005661.html) | In this button, start, stop and clear of trace log, control log and servo log are available.  Choose one of the items below and click [OK], then setting window appears.   * Line No. of start logging   Setting/Clear * Line No. of stop logging   Setting/Clear * Line No. of clear log   Setting/Clear * Clear logging line No.   Setting/Clear |
| Prev | Display the previous page of the currently displayed program. |
| Next | Display the next page of the currently displayed program. |
| Jump To | Move to the specified line.  Numeric keypad will be displayed. Enter the line number with numeric keypad, and press [OK] to move to the specified line. |

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [F1 Halt] | Halt the program being executed. |
| [F2 StepStop] | Execute step stop of the program being executed. |
| [F3 CycleStop] | Execute cycle stop of the program being executed. |
| [F4 Start] | Execute "single-cycle start" or "continuous start" of the selected program. |
| [F6 StepStart] | Execute "single-step start" of the selected program. |
| [F7 Reset] | [Program reset] window opens. Select either "Only this program" or "All programs", and press [OK] to reset the target program. |
| [F9 Priority] | System message to set the priority will be displayed. Select either of lowest, low, normal, high, and highest, and press [OK] to change the priority of the selected program. |
| [F10 Continue start] | Execute continue start of all programs that are under suspension. |
