# Using Example of Command Content

To make programming more efficient and easy, you can copy programs written in Example on command content, and then paste it to WINCAPSIII.

Not all Example can be used as-is. Modify the programs according to your needs.

###### 1

On a project window on WINCAPSIII, create a new program. Place a cursor on a line where you want to paste Example.  
For details, please refer to "Creating a New Program" of WINCAPSIII GUIDE.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002337_1.png)

###### 2

From the Example of command content, select lines where you want to copy, and then press [Ctrl]+[C] keys.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002337_2.png)

###### 3

Place a cursor on the programming line of WINCAPSIII, and then press [Ctrl]+[V] keys to paste.  
Modify the pasted program depending on your needs.

###### 4

Perform Syntax check and Motion check to check the program works properly.  
For details, refer to "Syntax Check of the Program" and "Motion Check of the Program" of WINCAPSIII GUIDE.

# Robot Controller

* [General Info.](#General)
* [Installation/Maintenance](#Installation-Maintenance)
* [Operation/Function](#Function)
* [Robot Unit](#Body)
* [Electrical Circuit](#Electric-circuit)
* [Programming](#Programming)
* [Others](#Other)

## General Info.

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| What types of option boards are available? Are there boards listed in RC8 manual? | There are variety of boards. For details, please refer to ID [987](000987.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUAL. |
| Where can we buy DENSO robots? How much it? | You can purchase our robots from our dealers. For details, please contact our sales office. |
| How long is the warranty period of RC8? | Warranty period should be a period of 24 months from the shipment of the product. However, within the said period, the warranty is valid either; for a period of 18 months from the start of use, or up to 6,000 hours of operation (running) time.  For details, please refer to ID [6085](006085.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| Where should we contact in case of failure? | We will inform the contact addresses of service representatives.  Please contact the nearest support office.  Contact addresses are listed in ID [1078](001078.html) of DENSO ROBOT SERVICE MANUAL as well. |
| What is the safety category of RC8 standard type? | Safety category is 4. |
| Can we choose the length of Motor & Encoder cable that connects RC8 to a robot unit? | Yes. |
| Are there any types of Motor and Encoder cable other than the straight type? | Yes. We offer an angle type as well. |
| Does RC8 have global specification? | Yes. RC8 standard type is a global specification because it equips the safety IO box.  RC7M standard type is not a global specification because it does not equip the safety IO box. |
| For RC8, is it possible to use a teach pendant that we've used in RC7M? | Yes. |
| Are there any devices that we have to prepare for UL specification? | Prepare a teach pendant or a mini-pendant.  If your robot is VS-050, -060, -068, or -087, you also need to prepare a brake release unit. |
| How many extension boards can be installed in RC8? | Up to 2 boards (one PCI board and one PCIexpress board) can be added. |
| Are RC8 expansion boards common to RC8 and RC7M? | All expansion boards are designed to respective controllers.  (Expansion board for RC7M cannot be used for RC8.) |

## Installation/Maintenance

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| How long is the RC8 power cable? | Five meters |
| What is the purpose of Functional grounding that is mentioned in the installation condition of RC8? | The purpose of functional grounding is to prevent noise emission as well as to protect RC8 from noise. Whereas, the purpose of protective grounding is to prevent electric shock. |
| Please tell us the power supply specification of the RC8 controller protective box. | Power supply specifications are as follows;  Three-phase: 185 to 253VAC (200VAC-7% to 230VAC＋10%)  Single-phase : 207 to 253VAC (230VAC±10%)  For details, please refer to ID [5489](005489.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| What is the IP code of RC8? | IP20 |
| What is the power supply capacity? | Power supply capacity differs depending on the robot type (specifications).  For details, please refer to ID [1333](001333.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| What is the RC8 IO conversion box? | RC8 I/O conversion box allows you to use RC5 INPUT connector (CN8), OUTPUT connector (CN10), and I/O Power (CN7) as-is. To use RC8 I/O conversion box, you need to install a Parallel IO board (option board) into RC8 (Safety I/O less specification). |
| We would like to know the installation direction of RC8. | There are three types of setting ways; Stand-alone, Fixing- or Wall-mount, and Upright setting.  For details, please refer to ID [1331](001331.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| We would like to know the installation environment for RC8. | Please refer to ID [1330](001330.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| What is the weight of RC8 standard type? | Approximately 12 kilograms. |
| Are there any connectors and jumper pins that sets internal/external power supply of IO power supply? | In RC8, you can change the external/internal power supply with a teach pendant (Factory default setting is External power supply.).  \* RC5 does not have I/O power connectors. RC7M does not have jumper pins. |
| Do we have to lay wires after purchasing a robot? | At least, you need to prepare a power cable, Motor-and-Encoder cable, and Mini-I/O wiring.  Mini I/O requires wirings for Enable auto, External emergency stop, and Protective stop. |
| How often do we have to replace the internal batery of RC8? | RC8 includes a battery to maintain the time and date of clock. The lifetime of this battery is 10 years. After the the years has passed, please contact our service or sales representative for replacement. |
| Are the Motor and Encoder cable common to RC8 and RC7M? | No. This is RC8-dedicated cable.  (To save the connector wiring space.) |
| Are the power cable common to RC8 and RC7M? | No. This is RC8-dedicated cable. |
| Does RC8 equip a safety I/O-dedicated connector? | No. Safety I/O connector is integrated into Mini I/O connector. |
| Does RC8 equip a fuse for input circuit protection? | No. RC8 uses resettable fuses so that users will have no trouble of replacing them. |
| Is it possible to add extended joints after controller installation? | Please consult with the nearest sales office. |
| On RC8, where are the connection ports of encoder cable and motor cable? | On the right front side of RC8.  One connector of a motor cable consists of two motor axes. Four-axis robot has two connection ports and Six-axis robot has three connection ports.  From the leftmost side, SLOT1 for J1&J2, SLOT2 for J3&J4, and SLOT3 for J5&J6.  Encoder cable is located immediate below the controller power switch. Encoder cables of all axes are bundled in one connector. |
| We want to share a teach pendant another RC8. Is it possible to run RC8 in Auto mode without connecting a teach pendant? | Yes.  Automatic operation without teach pendant is achieved by mounting a pendantless dummy connector, which is shipped with an RC8 as a standard part. However, for the manual operation, you need to prepare a teach pendat or mini pendant, |

## Operation/Function

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| How can we check the version of RC8? | You can check the RC8 version with a teach pendant.  From the top screen, press [F6: Setting] - [F2: System Info]. |
| Please tell us passwords of Programmer and Maintainer. | For Programmer ; 5596045  For Maintainer ; 5596060  To change the login status, from the main menu, press [F6 : Setting] - [F1 : Login] |
| How can we configure the program expansion? | Use a teach pendant.  From the main menu, press [F6: Setting] - [F8 : Option] - [F1: Extension]. |
| When are we likely to use an RS-232C connector? | Use the connector when you connect to external devices, such as a camera. Please note that RS-232C is not available for RC8 to communicate with WINCAPSIII, although it is available in RC7M. |
| When are we likely to use a USB connector? | Use this connector to connect to a USB camera, to read/write data via USB memory (backup, log, etc.), and to upgrade RC8 software. |
| If we purchase an expansion board solely, does the RC8 controller recognizes it automatically as the RC7M does? | No.  You need to set an allocation mode by using WINCAPSIII, and then send IO parameters to RC8. |
| To add an expansion board, what do we have to prepare? | Prepare licenses for an expansion board and the function expansion. |
| Is it possible to back up data with USB memory? | Yes.  For details, please refer to ID [1787](001787.html) of DENSO ROBOT MANUAL. |
| Setting items written in the RC8 manual are not displayed in the teach pendant. | Some setting items are not displayed in the teach pendant depending on the user level. Logging in the teach pendant with higher user level may enable to display these items. For details, please refer to ID [1772](001772.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| Is it possible to connect RC8 to WINCAPSIII via RS232C? | No.  Only Ethernet connection is available. |
| Are error codes of RC8 and RC7M the same? | No.  Error codes of RC8 are 8-digit number. |
| Is it possible to output 8-digit error codes of RC8? | Yes.  From the I/O parameter, set User output start port.  To set a start port, with a teach pendant, from the top screen, press [F4:I/O] -[F6: Aux] - [F5 : I/O parameters] - [445 : 32bit Error Code Output IO No].  This occupies 32 ports (including the start port). |
| When we use RC8 in Auto mode, can we set the external speed with a teach pendant? | Yes.  RC7M has External/Internal mode. When External mode is selected, RC7M can stop operation only.  However, in RC8, because External and Internal modes are integrated, operations other than the program start are available. |
| What is the difference between a teach pendant and Mini pendant? | Mini pendant is an input and operation devices that executes robot manual operation, program start, and teaching.  This is not capable of programming. By combining WINCAPSIII or WINCAPSIII Light with a pendant, you can program efficiently. |
| How can we keep the TOOL number that is used immediately before the shutdown. | It is impossible to maintain the tool number after rebooting.  Specify Operation mode (Joint, XY, TOOL), TOOL number (0 to 63), WORK number (0 to 7) at the controller start-up. If not, Joint mode, TOOL0, and WORK0 are selected automatically. |
| To check the robot motion during machine-lock state, do we need a PC (WINCAPSIII)? | If you have a teach pendant, you can see the robot motion from [F2: Arm] window only when the machine-lock is selected. |
| What is an executable token? | Executable token is a control authority that is given to devices to allow execution of robot program and motor power-on.  There are four types of control.  - Any : All devices  - TP : Teach pendant or Mini pendant  - IO : Computer or PLC  - Ethernet : Computer or PLC  Factory default is [I/O]. |
| How can we change executable token? | With a teach pendant, select [F6: Setting] - [F5: Communication and Token] - [F1 : Executable Token] |
| Do we have to set motor power ON when obtaining robot position into a variable? | You can obtain the robot position even if the motor power is OFF. |
| How do we switch Motor ON/OFF? | When in manual mode or teach check mode, motor power turns ON when deadman switches is gripped.  In Auto mode, motor power turns on by pressing MOTOR directly. |
| In a teach pendant, is Smart display available for I/O? | Yes.  From the IO window, select Smart checkbox of desired IO number, and then select a checkbox of [F4 : Dummy / Smart]. Press [Smart] on the bottom left of the window to display the Smart view. |
| In a teach pendant, is Smart display available for variables? | Yes.  From the variable window, select Smart checkbox of desired variable number, and then select a checkbox of [F5 : Edit]. Press [Smart] on the bottom left of the window to display the Smart view. |
| Can we change the way of Motor ON/OFF to conventional way? | Yes.  From the teach pendant, press [F6 Setting] - [F3 Pendant and Panel] - [F7 DSW interlock] and then set the Deadman switch linkage function to OFF. |

## Robot Unit

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| If a robot is communication interface flange-A type, is it possible to supply electric power via PoE? | Yes.  Communication interface flange-A type equips 1000BASE-T (CAT5e) -standard cables. |
| What is the difference among VS-A1,VS-A2, VS-A3, and VS-A4? | These notations have different combinations of robot unit and robot controller.  VS-A1 : VS050/VS060 + RC7M controller  VS-A2 : VS068/VS087 + RC7M controller  VS-A3 : VS050/VS060 + RC8 controller  VS-A4 : VS068/VS087 + RC8 controller |

## Electrical Circuit

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| How can we "Continue-start" a robot that has been stopped by "Emergency stop"? | With a teach pendant, on the Program parameter list, change the setting of [13: Program stop state of emergency stop].  "Continue stop" means the program-stop state that occurs when (1) Emergency stop button on the teach pendant is pressed, or, (2) External emergency stop signal is issued.  For details, refer to ID [1639](001639.html) of DENSO ROBOT MANUAL. |
| How can we get an EDS file? | EDS file has been installed in RC8 beforehand. To obtain the file, connect the controller to a computer. For details, please refer to ID [1468](001468.html) of DENSO ROBOT MANUAL.  You can also download it from our website (field network-related). |
| When we try to control RC8 from PLC through an expansion board, an error occurs. How can we avoid that? | [Step stop] and [Instantaneous stop] signals of System input turn OFF in short-circuit state.  The robot stops when at least one of these signals opens.  For details, please refer to ID [1002](001002.html) and [1003](001003.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| What is odd parity? | Odd parity is a mechanism that prevents wrong detection of IO command. This mechanism adjusts the sum of command bits to odd number at any time. When the sum of command bits is even number, it is deemed as an error. |
| If we control RC8 from a PLC, do we have to use a command that selects external auto mode? | Not necessary.  In RC8, internal auto mode and external auto mode are integrated. |
| When we move a robot in Manual mode, do we need to set Enable auto signal OFF? | No you don't.  In RC8, you can move a robot in Manual mode or Teach check mode, even if Enable auto signal is ON. |
| Are the protective stop of RC8 and that of RC7M the same? | No.  In RC7M, protective stop and Enable auto are connected in series, whereas protective stop of RC8 is independent. In RC8, protective stop is effective only in the Auto mode. |
| What is Mini I/O? | Mini-IO is a parallel IO that is offered as a standard component. Number of IO is as follows;  <Standard controller (global specification)>  Input : User IO 8 ports + System IO 14 ports.  Output : User IO 8 ports + System IO 16 ports |
| What is Hand I/O? | Hand IO is a parallel IO that is offered as a standard component. This IO is mainly used to control the robot hand-embedded valve or the automatic switch.  Number of IO is as follows;  Input : User IO 8 ports + System IO 14 ports.  Output : User IO 8 ports + System IO 16 ports |
| How can we add I/O port? | We prepare many types of IO expansion boards as option. RC8 has two expansion slots. Up to two IO expansion boards can be mounted simultaneously. |
| What types of signals does Mini I/O equip? | The following signals are provided:   * System input (7 ports) : External emergency stop input 1 and 2, Enable Auto input 1 and 2, Step stop (all task), Protective stop input 1 and 2 * System output (11 ports) : Auto Mode, Robot Initialized, Robot Running, CPU Normal, Robot Error, Operation Preparation Completed, Battery Warning, Pendant Emergency Stop 1and 2, Deadman SW 1and 2 * Input for command execution (7 ports) : Command and data area, Strobe signal * Output for command execution (1 port) : Command processing completed * User input (8 ports) * User output (8 ports) |
| What is the difference between Standard mode and Compatible mode? | If an expansion board is mounted, the following four modes are available.   * Mini-IO dedicated mode : Robot motion is specified by the combination of bits. Compare to the standard allocation, functions are limited. * Compatible mode: Functions (such as program execution) are allocated to respective bits. Raising a bit issues a designated motion. * Standard mode : Use a combination of bits (IO command) to execute a program. This allocation has the functions most. * All User IO mode : All ports in IO expansion board are user ports. |

## Programming

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| Can we use RC7M program for RC8? | No.  \* Programs for RC7M are "\*.pac" format, and programs for RC8 are "\*.pcs" format. |
| Can RC8 call other programs? | Yes.  In the setting area, you need to invoke a Call-program by writing "Include". |
| Are the local variables of RC7M and that of RC8 the same? | No.  RC7M keeps setting values after power-off (values are initialized by compiling).  RC8 deletes (invalidate) local variables when programs end. |
| Is RC8 capable of saving local variables? | Yes.  You can keep values after power-off by using Static variables. |
| Does RC8 have folder variables? | No.  To refer variables from other tasks, use Public variables. |
| Are robot languages of RC8 and that of RC7M the same? | No.  RC8 uses PacScript which is VBA-compliance (some robot motion commands are SLIM-compliance).  \* RC7M uses PAC which is SLIM-compliance language. |
| Regarding commands, is there any compatibility between RC8 and RC7M? | Most of motion commands have compatibility.  Programming and conditional branching are changed due to VBA-compliance.  For details, please refer to ID [513](000513.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| Does RC8 have ProgramLibrary? | No. In RC8, programs in RC7M ProgramLibrary are converted to commands. For details, please refer to ID [513](000513.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |
| Can RC8 use RC7M ProgramLibrary? | No. In RC8, programs in RC7M ProgramLibrary are converted to commands. For details, please refer to ID [513](000513.html) of DENSO ROBOT USER MANUALS. |

## Others

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| In what format is the RC8 manual offered? | HTML format.  The manual DVD is shipped with the product when you purchase an RC8. You can also download the RC8 CONTROLLER MANUAL from DENSO WAVE homepage after logon. |

# WINCAPSIII

* [General Info.](#General)
* [Function](#Function)
* [Safety](#Safty)

## General Info.

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| What is WINCAPSIII? | WINCAPSIII is a software that enables users to program (PacScript, PAC) and/or simulate DENSO robot on a computer. |
| Are there any function restrictions on WINCAPSIII Trial version? | In addition to the restrictions of WINCAPSIII Light, user cannot use any other program than PRO1. |
| Are there any function restrictions on WINCAPSIII Light? | It has same restrictions as WINCAPSII Light has.   * Not printable * The minimum monitoring interval is 1 second. * Available libraries are limited. |
| Is it possible to coexist WINCAPSIII and WINCAPSII in one computer? | Yes. |
| What is the supported Windows OS? | Windows XP, Vista, 7, and 8. |
| How can we obtain WINCAPSIII Trial version? | Please consult with DENSO robot dealer or sales representatives. You can directly download from our website as well. Please register our website for that. |
| We install WINCAPSIII in computers which OS are Windows Vista or higher. When we enter a license, administration authority is required. How to deal with that? | Once installing WINCAPSIII, click Start button, right-click on WINCAPSIII, and then select "Run as administrator". You will be able to enter a license. |

## Function

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| What format is used when obtaining 3D data? | VRML (extension: .wrl) and DirectX (extension: .x).  \* VRML 1.0 is not supported. |
| If we need to obtain any data other than VRML or DirectX format, how can we do? | \*If you use 3D-CAD software, in some case, data can be output with VRML 2.0 (or VRML97) format.  Example of Converter   * XVLstudio : Because it converts data into XVL format temporary, data size significantly decreases, so the created data will run smoothly even in laptop PC. * DeepExploration : This supports variety of file formats. |
| Is it possible to check I/O log and variable log with a teach pendant? | Only WINCAPSIII can display these logs.  The following two expansions are required for teach pendant.   * Display program name and line number on error log. * Expand the number of error log and operation log to 1000. |
| On which WINCAPSIII version can we use Online debug mode? | RC7: Debug function is available for controllers which ROM version is 2.7 or higher. |
| What is a NODE? | A "NODE" is an assembly of objects to handle these object as a block.  \* Since users can handle several objects at once, this is helpful tool for operation, such as setting coordinates per NODE. |
| What is the "unit" of Detection level of Collision detection? How is an object expanded if we change the number of Detection level? | A target object is enclosed by rectangles. The number of Detection level denotes how many rectangles enclose the detection target object.  The number varies depending on the size of the object.  Once rectangles collide a target object, the rectangles are divided into smaller rectangles, and then repeats it until rectangles cannot be divided anymore. When it is impossible to further division, it is regarded as collision. If you set the number larger, the accuracy becomes higher. However, setting larger number for the complicated 3D data will lower the processing speed. |
| Is it possible to display multiple robots in Arm 3D view? | No. |
| We use RC7M ver.2.6. Are there any unavailable functions? | Online debug mode is not available. All functions same as WINCAPSII are available. |
| How has WINCAPSIII been changed from WINCAPSII? | WINCAPSIII has the window structure just like other Windows-based application. |
| Is it possible to open RC5 programs from WINCAPSIII? | You cannot directly open RC5 projects of WINCAPSII. (It is possible to import programs.) |
| Does WINCAPSIII have any functions that enables users to check path under offline-mode or to examine cycle time, just like Arm Player does? | WINCAPSIII equips simulation function as a standard function. Also, collision check is available. For details, refer to [WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html). |
| Is it possible to copy IO data or variable data of WINCAPSIII and then to paste the data to Excel? | You can paste copied data to Excel sheet. |
| Can WINCAPSIII import 3D data of VRML1.0 file? | VRML1.0 is not supported.  \*VRML2.0 (or VRML97) file and Directx file are supported. |
| Can WINCAPSIII use (import) programs created by WINCAPSII? | Programs can be used as-is.   (There is no change of robot language and instruction. Since the differences between WINCAPSIII and II are the window layout and available functions, instruction language is not changed at all. Therefore, programs can be used as-is. )  Also, WINCAPSIII can import RC7J project and RC7M project directly. |
| When using Arm Player Plus, if we set the maximum payload for a VP robot, is the setting really reflected to the robot motion? | No.  Please use the simulation function of WINCAPSIII instead of Arm Player Plus. (Ver.3.20 or higher) |
| We controls VP by using WINCAPSIII and a mini pendant. How can we release errors in compatible mode? | RC7 : Turn ON the "Clear Robot Error" signal, and then turn ON the "Operation Preparation"signal. Please turn OFF the "Clear Robot Error" signal once the "Robot Error" output signal turns OFF, |

## Safety

| Q | A |
| --- | --- |
| If a computer shuts down or Ethernet cable disconnects while running in On-line mode (debug mode), what will happen to the robot? | Robot stops.  The safety is assured by the following two measures.  1) Program stops on the controller side if controller does receive data within 300 milliseconds from the previous data reception.  2) Even if the operation of WINCAPSIII becomes slow, robot can stop by pressing a Stop button that is running on another process. |
| Is the red button displayed in Online mode (debug mode) the emergency stop button? | No. From the viewpoint of standard, we cannot call it as an emergency stop. This is [Motor power OFF] + [All task stop].  For emergency, place a teach pendant nearby so that users can press the emergency stop button at any time. |
| When a teach pendant-less connector is inserted, is it possible to start a program in Online (debug) mode? | Yes.  \*For the safety reason, operate nearby the emergency stop button of equipment. |

# [NPN type] Safety Circuit for RC8A

The figure below shows an internal connection equivalent circuit for the safety circuit in the controller. The actual safety circuit is configured with safety relays and others.

## Safety Circuit

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002347_1.png)

Please refer to this if the figure is not clear. [(PDF:194KB)](img/002347/002347_1.pdf)

## Different Stop States Resulting from Emergency Stop input, Protective Stop, and Enable Auto (OFF)

1. The emergency stop input (External Emergency Stop or teach pendant/mini-pendant input) shuts down the power to the motor and resets the program, provided that the Continue parameter is set to the default (0: Disable) in Continue setting.
2. The Protective Stop or Enable Auto (OFF) input signal shuts down the power to the motor and places the robot in the Continue Stop state.

1. The optional I/O cable for the above connector consists of twisted pair wires--pairs of #1 and #35, #2 and #36, #34 and #68.
2. If no Protective Stop input signals are needed, short-circuit by terminal connection with jumpers between #4 and #38 and between terminals #5 and #39.
3. For Compatible Mode/Standard Mode/All User I/O mode,   
   terminals #11 to #18 are user input, termilals #46 to #53 are user output.

The reserved pins and output pins should be prevented from direct contact with other pins or conductive part.
Direct contact could result in a controller failure or damage.

| 2 | MOTION I/F IN | Safety motion input connector | Connect an input cable for Safety Motion. | | | \*1, \*2 |

| 10 | INPUT AC | Power connector | Connect power cable. | | | \*2 |
| 11 | LAN | Ethernet connector | Use for communication with outside device through Ethernet circuit. | | |  |

| 13 | RS-232C | Serial communication connector | Use for serial communication with outside devices. | | |  |

| Other | Turn OFF. |  |

| HSA1 series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.69 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.69 kVA |
| HSR series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.8 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.8 kVA |
| XR series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.85 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.85 kVA |
| SC series  3-phase 200 VAC -15% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.5 kVA  Single phase 230 VAC -10% to 240 VAC +10% 47 to 63 Hz, 1.5 kVA |
| I/O power supply | Use external power supply | Supply 24VDC +/-10% from outside |
| Use internal power supply | Supply 24VDC +/-10% from inside controller |
| Short Circuit Current Rating（SCCR) | | Other than UL-listed model: 5 kA  UL-listed model: 10 kA |
| Safety performance (\*5) | | Structure : Category 4 Performance Level : e  MTTFD : 163.2 years  DCavg : 99%  PFHD : 1.50×10^-8/h  \* Please specify the safety-I/O-less version in the case that safety I/O mounted on the standard version is not necessary |
| Stop category | | Category 1 (except Safety-I/O-less type.)  (See IEC 60204-1 for details of stop category) |
| [Safety Functions](002479.html) | | Comply with IEC 61508 (except Safety-I/O-less type.)  For a third-party certifier, refer to [this(PDF:692KB)](img/001204/968_FSP_1371_05_23_en_el.pdf). |
| IP code | | Top plate : IP3X  Other surfaces : IP20  IP54 when using protective box (optional) |
| Stand for vertical setup | | Note) Set right side (power connector side) down |
| External dimension | | 【Models except UL-Listed ones】  Standard, Safety I/O–less: W 356.5 x D 319.6 x H 96.8 [mm] 11.1 L  Safety motion : W 410.3 x D 319.6 x H 96.8 [mm] 12.7 L  【UL-Listed models】  Standard, Safety motion : W 410.3 x D 420 x H 130 [mm] 19.8L  \* Except for the projection part. |
| Weight | | 【Models except UL-Listed ones】  Standard, Safety I/O–less : approximately 10 kg  Safety motion : approximately 11 kg  【UL-Listed models】  Standard, Safety motion : approximately 16 kg |

To ensure safety functions, reboot the robot controller once in every 24 hours.

\*1 : Expansion boards used in the RC7 robot controller cannot be used.

\*2 : Pollution degree 2 is equivalent to household and office environment.

When using in a factory, take either of the following measures.

・ Put it into the control panel corresponding to pollution degree 3.

・ Use [the controller protective box](005495.html) (optional).

\*3 : Corresponding power distribution systems are as follows.

　TT, TN, IT

\*4 : If the power supply can be dropped 95 V or less, such as in the heavily loaded facilities, using a transformer describes below is recommended. However, operation with 85 V or lower voltage is not guaranteed.

Transformer specification
:   Input voltage : 1Ph 100 V

    Output voltage : 1Ph 200 V

    Capacity : 1 kVA

\*5 : This safety performance is determined for the robot stop functions; such as an emergency stop, enable auto, protective stop and deadman switch.  
 However, customer-prepared input devices, which connect to signals for emergency stop, Enable Auto, and protective stop, are not included in the safety performance calculation.

Calculation conditions
:   · This calculation is based on ISO 13849-1:2015.

    · Expected operation counts a year (Nop) are as follows.

    | Operation | Mission time (year) | |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | 10 | 20 |
    | Start/Stop (Motor ON/OFF) | 38,933 | 19,466 |
    | Enable (Deadman) switch | 10,000 | 5,000 |

# RC8A (Standard/ Safety I/O-less / Standard UL)

Definition of the specification of the robot controller described here is as shown below.

* Standard specification : Code showing the compliant standards of the controller type is "NI".
* Safety I/O-less specification : Code showing the compliant standards of the controller type is "NN".
* Standard UL specification : Code showing the compliant standards of the controller type is "UI".

For details of the code, refer to the category “G” written in "[Controller Type](001314.html)" of "RC8 Series Robot Controller Manual".

# Auto Mode Mutual Monitoring (output)

## Function

This signal notifies the external device that the robot is in Auto mode. (dual line) (RC8A only) (Except for Safety I/O less)

## Terminal Number

| Signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| Auto Mode Mutual Monitoring 1 | #30 on Mini I/O connector |
| Auto Mode Mutual Monitoring 2 | #64 on Mini I/O connector |

## Usage

When you execute "OPERATION PREPARATION" or "PROGRAM START", this signal must be on-state. Refer to RC8A MINI I/O MANUAL, "[[NPN type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002347.html)" or "[[PNP type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002348.html)".

When using the external power source to Mini I/O power supply, if you turn on the power to the robot controller without supplying the external power, or supply the external power after that of the robot, an error may occur and fail to operate the robot as a result.

Be sure to supply the external power before the robot controller will be powered on.

## ON Condition

This signal will be turned on when the robot controller enters Auto mode by turning the mode selector switch on the teach pendant or mini-pendant to "AUTO" with the Enable Auto input signal being on.

## OFF Conditions

This signal will be turned off when one of the following condition is satisfied.

1. The operation mode is switched to the Manual or Teach check mode by using the teach pendant or mini-pendant.
2. The Enable Auto input signal is off. The Enable Auto input signal will not be turned off in the pendantless state described in the OPTIONS MANUAL.

The Auto Mode output signal will not be turned off with "INSTANTANEOUS STOP", "STEP STOP" or "CYCLE STOP" commands.

ID : 2358

# STO Monitor (output)

## Function

This signal outputs the STO status. (RC8A only) (Except for Safety I/O less)

[STO](002500.html) (Safe Torque Off) is a function that turns OFF the motor power of the robot.  
 The 1a and 2a dry contacts CLOSE when the motor is ON and OPEN when the motor is OFF.   
 The 1b and 2b dry contacts OPEN when the motor is ON and CLOSE when the motor is OFF.

## Terminal Number

| Signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| STO monitor output 1b | #6 and #40 on Mini I/O connector |
| STO monitor output 2b | #7 and #41 on Mini I/O connector |
| STO monitor output 1a | #10 and #44 on Mini I/O connector |
| STO monitor output 2a | #27 and #61 on Mini I/O connector |

## Usage

This signal is used to confirm the Motor ON/OFF state.

Refer to RC8A MINI I/O MANUAL, "[[NPN type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002347.html)"or"[[PNP type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002348.html)".

* It takes 40 milliseconds from the turning-ON of the Monitor output 1 to the turning-ON of the Monitor output 2.

* Apply at least 10 milliamperes through the contacts.
* When using the STO Monitor output signal for the Drive Power Indicator, install the Drive Power Indicator in a visible location near the safety door outside the robot cell.

# Overview

Emergency stop switch box is a switchbox that extracts only an emergency stop function from a teach pendant.

When an emergency stop switch box is used, the operation mode will be Auto mode, just like when a pendantless dummy connector is used.

If you need a UL-listed robot, be sure to purchase either of the following options in addition to a UL-listed robot set.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Either of the following options   * Teach pendant * Mini-pendant * Emergency stop switch box   However, if you use the controller as a slave for the cooperative control function, these options are not necessary. Instead, you need to purchase the pendantless connector (dummy connector). |
| 2 | Only for the VS robot: Brake release unit (option) |

# Specification

The specification of emergency stop switch box is shown in the table below.

| Weight | Approx. 0.5 kg |

# How to Use an Electric Gripper in Cooperative Control Function

Electric grippers connected to each robot controller can be operated and/or configured from the master controller-connected teach pendant.  
In programming, a robot name is used to specify an electric gripper to move.

The function mentioned above is available to a robot controller which software version is 1.13.\* or higher.

When an electric gripper is used in the cooperative control function, in some cases, an electric gripper which is wired to the robot controller of Robot1 may be attached to the tool end of Robot0.  
In this case, the electric gripper-attached robot name and the robot name of the electric gripper-wired robot controller will be inconsistent.  
For such application, it is not intuitive from the viewpoint of operation/configuration though, a robot controller has a feature that realizes intuitive operation/setting (robot name-electric gripper linkage function).

The function mentioned above is available to the robot controller which software version is 2.5.\* or higher.

## Operaiton and Configuration

Basically, electric grippers can be controlled and configured from the master controller. However, only the license registration needs to be done with slave controllers.

### License Registration

When using electric grippers in cooperative control function, you need to register licenses for each controller that use an electric gripper.

Connect a teach pendant or mini pendant to a slave controller, and then register a license.

### Designate a Setting-Target Robot as Leader Robot

Basically, any operation and configuration with the master controller-connected teach pendant works on the robot which is assigned as a leader.  
Therefore, to control or configure a slave controller-connected electric gripper, assign a robot connected to the slave controller as a leader.  
The following is a sample window image when two robots are linked for cooperation.

To set Robot1 as a leader robot, from the [Robot selection] button on the top of the window, select [R1] and then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_2.png)

From the top menu, press [F9:Hand] to display Hand window of the leader robot. On the top of the window, you will see the robot number of the leader robot.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_3.png)

### Linkage between Robot Names and Electric Grippers

This function is available to the robot controller which software version is 2.5.\* or higher.

When an electric gripper is used in the cooperative control function, in some cases, an electric gripper which is wired to the robot controller of Robot1 may be attached to the tool end of Robot0, as the following figure shows.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_6.png)

In this case, the electric gripper control board is installed in the robot controller of Robot1. Therefore, to control/configure an electric gripper of Robot0, assign Robot1 as a leader.  
Above-mentioned application is not intuitive from the viewpoint of operation/configuration though, a robot controller has a "SelectHand" function that realizes intuitive operation.  
SelectHand is a command written in PacScript to control an electric gripper. There are necessary configuration before use.  
Setting parameters are located in VRC setting.  
Before operation, set the user level to "Maintainer".

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path : [F6 Setting]-[F2 System info]-[F6 VRC Setting] |

By following the above operation path, VRC Setting window will appear.  
No.390 to 397 are the setting parameters of SelectHand. Select one of them and then press [F5: Edit] to display the following window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_7.png)

SelectHand has array structure. For the meaning of each element, see the figure above.  
The figure above shows how to specify the control-target electric gripper when SelectHand[0,0] is used.  
Suppose that you create the following system structure.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_8.png)

When parameters in VRC setting are entered as the following image shows, if "SelectHand[0,0]" is used, an electric gripper attached to Robot0 is controlled.  
Also, if "SelectHand[1,0]" is used, an electric gripper attached to Robot1 is controlled. This realizes the intuitive programming.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_9.png)

This logic is applied not only to PacScript-used programming but also teach pendant-used robot operation/configuration (For example, an electric gripper attached to Robot0 can be operated/controlled by setting Robot0 as a leader robot).  
Except for the robot name and electric gripper link function, functions of SelectHand command and Hand command are the same. For details, refer to "Command" in the following content.

### Setting of the Electric Gripper

Perform STEP 3 to 8 of [Settings of the Electric Gripper](001796.html).

## Command

Electric grippers can be used by SelectHand command or by specifying a robot name.

### Using SelectHand Command

This function is available to the robot controller which software version is 2.5.\* or higher.

SelectHand command controls an electric gripper which has been linked with a robot name (For information about the electric gripper-robot name link, refer to "[Linkage between robot names and electric grippers](#Robot)").

Except for the robot name and electric gripper link function, functions of SelectHand command and Hand command are the same.  
Also, the syntax is the same as the string which is followed by the "Hand[n]" of Hand command (Refer to the following image).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002368_10.png)

For example, to turn on the motor of electric gripper which is linked with SelectHand[0,0], write as follows.

```
  SelectHand[0,0].Motor On
```

### Using a Robot Name

Write the robot name of an electric gripper control board-installed robot controller in front of the Hand command.  
Note that the setting of "SelectHand" is not reflected.  
The following is a sample program that uses robot names for Hand command.

#### Example

```
'!TITLE "Motion of the Electric gripper"
Sub Main   

  TakeArm Keep = 0
  Motor On   

  If Robot0.Hand[0].MotorState = False Then
    Robot0.Hand[0].Motor On
  End If  

  If Robot1.Hand[0].MotorState = False Then
    Robot1.Hand[0].Motor On
  End If  

  If Robot0.Hand[0].OrgState = False Then
    Robot0.Hand[0].Org
  End If  

  If Robot1.Hand[0].OrgState = False Then
    Robot1.Hand[0].Org
  End If   

  'Gripping motion of Robot0
  Robot0.Move P, @0 P0
  Robot0.Depart L, @E -50, S = 20
  Robot0.Hand[0].Chuck 0
  Wait Robot0.Hand[0].HoldState = -1
  Robot0.Depart L, @E 20, S = 20
  Robot0.Depart L, @E -20, S = 20
  Robot0.Hand[0].Unchuck 1
  Robot0.Depart L, @E 50, S = 20
  Move P, @0 P1  

  'Gripping motion of Robot1
  Robot1.Move P, @0 P2
  Robot1.Depart L, @E -50, S = 20
  Robot1.Hand[0].Chuck 0
  Wait Robot1.Hand[0].HoldState = -1
  Robot1.Depart L, @E 20, S = 20
  Robot1.Depart L, @E -20, S = 20
  Robot1.Hand[0].Unchuck 1
  Robot1.Depart L, @E 50, S = 20
  Robot1.Move P, @0 P1  

  'Simultaneous gripping motion of Robot0 and Robot1
  Robot0.Hand[0].MoveH 50, 80, Next
  Robot1.Hand[0].MoveH 50, 80
  Delay( 500 )
  Move P, @0 P1,SyncTime = Robot1
  Robot0.Hand[0].MoveA 0, 80, Next
  Robot1.Hand[0].MoveA 0, 80
  Robot0.Move P, @0 P0, SyncTime = Robot1  

End Sub
```

# Delete All Variables

Operation path : [F3 Variable] - [F12 Aux] - [F2 Delete all variables]

Delete all Variable value, Usage, Macro at once.

Press [F2 Delete all variables] to display [Select items to delete] panel.

From the [Select items to delete] panel, select an item to delete, and then press [OK].

All contents of the selected item are deleted. You can select several items at once.

Pressing [SelectAll] will select all items and [Selection release] will release all selected items.

# Connection with OMRON PLC

Connecting OMRON PLC with controller through EtherCAT may require additional settings on PLC side by using Sysmac Studio.

## Setting for the Sysmac Studio

###### 1

On the setting item of OMRON EtherCAT Master, you will find "Wait Time for Slave Startup".  
The default value is 30 seconds. Change this value to 45 seconds or higher.  
Depending on the EtherCAT Slave device to connect, a longer waiting time may be required. Please set a suitable value according to the operation environment you use.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002370_1.png)

###### 2

Check if the error "8350200B: Preparing for the field network communication" is not displayed at the startup of controller.

This completes the setting process.

# HSR SERIES USER'S MANUAL

This HSR series are the high-speed, high-accuracy assembly robots developed by the comprehensive technology of DENSO WAVE.

Before operating your robot, read this manual carefully to safely get the maximum benefit from your robot in your assembling operations.

## Robot Series and/or Models Covered by this Manual

| Series | Model | | Overall arm length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Floor-mount | Overhead-mount |
| HSR  (Horizontal articulated) | HSR048A1-N\* | HSR048A1-S\* | 480 mm |
| HSR055A1-N\* | HSR055A1-S\* | 550 mm |
| HSR065A1-N\* | HSR065A1-S\* | 650 mm |

To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html) ".

Both robots and controllers imported into South Korea on or after 1st March 2013 are required to have KCs marks.

# Standard Components

The components listed below are contained in the product package.

| Group | Item | Q'ty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Robot & Accessories | Robot unit | 1 |
| Motor & encoder cable (option) | 1 |
| Sheet of direction indicator labels | 1 |
| Connector set for hand control signals (for CN20 and CN21) | 1set |
| Dowel pin (Internally-threaded positioning pin & diamond shaped pin) | 1set |
| Controller & Accessories | Robot controller | 1 |
| Power cable (5 m) | 1 |
| Pendantless connector (Dummy connector) (not contained in UL-Listed robot systems) | 1 |
| Cable clamp | 1 |
| Software etc | Reference guide for user manuals | 1 |
| Warning label | 1 |

If you need a UL-listed robot, be sure to purchase either of the following options in addition to a UL-listed robot set.

* Teach pendant
* Mini-pendant
* Emergency stop switch box

However, if you use the controller as a slave for the cooperative control function, these options are not necessary. Instead, you need to purchase the pendantless connector (dummy connector).

# Components 1

## Robot Unit

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002415_1.png)

Robot units

## Motor & Encoder Cable (option)

| Standard type | UL-Listed model |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

Cable that connects the robot unit to the robot controller, consisting of a motor cable and an encoder cable.

When placing an order for a robot system, select a motor & encoder cable from the list given below.

For partnumber and outer dimensions, please refer to "[Options for Robot Unit](001970.html)".

| Type | Item / Specifications | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Models except UL-Listed ones | Motor and encoder cable  (for HSR robot) | Straight | 2 m |
| 4 m |
| 6 m |
| 12 m |
| 20 m |
| Angle | 2 m |
| 4 m |
| 6 m |
| 12 m |
| 20 m |
| UL-Listed models | Straight | 2 m |
| 4 m |
| 6 m |
| 12 m |
| Angle | 2 m |
| 4 m |
| 6 m |
| 12 m |

* The bending radius (internal) of a motor & encoder cable should be at least 33.8 mm when the cable is stationary, and at least 225 mm when it is movable. Excessively bending will result in broken lead wires.
* If the length of the motor and encoder cable is 20 m, the leakage current of power supply exceeds 3.5 mA. To reduce the touch current on the controller surface to 3.5 mA or less, take any measures, for example, connecting additional protective earthing conductor which cross section is 2.5mmˆ2 or larger to the controller.

### Connector to Join the Cable to the Robot Unit

| Standard type |  |  |

Cable that supplies power to the robot controller. It is 5 m long.

| Model except UL-Listed ones | UL-Listed model |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

## Pendantless Connector (Dummy Connector) (Models Except UL-Listed Ones)

Connector to be plugged in the controller when neither the teach pendant (TP) nor the mini-pendant (MP) is connected

For details, refer to the "[Pendantless State](001540.html)" of FUNCTION GUIDE.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000004_5_1.png)

If you need a UL-listed robot, be sure to purchase either of the following options in addition to a UL-listed robot set.

* Teach pendant
* Mini-pendant
* Emergency stop switch box

However, if you use the controller as a slave for the cooperative control function, these options are not necessary. Instead, you need to purchase the pendantless connector (dummy connector).

## Cable Clamp

Cable clamps are used to fasten LAN cables and USB cables.

# Factory Option

## Ethernet Specification

This option provides a signal wiring and a connector for Ethernet (1000BASE-T) on the second arm.  
For information about connectors used, please refer to "[Options for Robot Unit](001970.html)".  
For information about how to assemble cable and connector, refer to "[Connector for the Ethernet (Option)](002644.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002417_1.png)

## External Battery Specification

This connector allows to connect to an encoder backup battery which is incorporated in the robot unit from the outside of the robot.

For details, refer to "[External Battery Unit (Option)](002653.html)".

# Coding Information of Robot Model

The robot model is coded as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002419_1.png)

## Model No.

### Robot Name

HSR : Horizontal articulated robot

### Arm Length

048 : 480 mm

055 : 550 mm

065 : 650 mm

## Detail

### Installation Type

N : Floor-mount type

S : Overhead-mount type

### Z-axis stroke

#### Standard Type

10 : 100 mm

20 : 200 mm

32 : 320 mm

51 : 510 mm

#### Bellows Type, Dust- & Splash-proof Type, Cleanroom Type, H1 Grease Type

17 : 170 mm

29 : 290 mm

45 : 450 mm（Except cleanroom type）

#### Metal-detectable bellows type, Metal-detectable bellows + dust- & splash-proof (IP65) type

12 : 120mm

24 : 240mm

### Ingress Protection

NN : Standard type (IP20)

W5 : Dust- & splash-proof type (IP65)

C3 : Cleanroom type (ISO3)

JN : Bellows type (IP20)

KJ : Metal-detectable bellows type

KW : Metal-detectable bellows + dust- & splash-proof (IP65) type

### Safety Standard Compliance

N : Standard

U : UL-Listed model

### Signal Lines & Ethernet

N : Standard

A : Ethernet specification

### Grease

N : Standard

H : H1 grease type

The ingress protection level of the H1 grease type is IP65 (Dust- & Splash-proof type).

### External Battery Specification

N : Without External battery

A : With External battery

# Robot Unit Components and Motion Direction

The figure below shows the names of the components of the robot unit and the rotation direction of each axis.

* UL-listed models have Motor-ON lamps on the back.
* Be sure not to hold the part of Motor-ON lamps at the time of transporting, installation, and/or adjusting. That may cause a breakage.
* In the bellow type, dust- & splash-proof type, cleanroom type, H1 grease type ,there are some areas where the base interferes with the bellows. Be sure there is no interference between them before the use. If interfered, the paint of the base will be removed and the bellows may break.
* Bellows type is not a leak-proof structure.
* If any axes do not move, or move but only a little, the oil coating on the bearing of axes may not be formed sufficiently, it could leading to the early wear off.  
  To prevent early wear-off of bearings, move the target axes in sufficiently large angle for more than a few times a day.
* If any customer-prepared parts (end effector, air piping for the end effector) are installed in the robot unit, depending on the installation, it might hit the robot body when you fold the robot arm up. Pay attention when you perform teaching.

# Name Plate

The name plate is affixed in the base part, which includes serial number of the robot, robot model, and day of manufacturer, etc.

The serial number is the figure which identifies the robot of each customer and it is paired with the figure of the controller.

* Robot unit model name
* Robot unit Part number
* Serial number
* Manufacture date

# Warning and Caution Labels

The robot unit has warning and caution labels pasted as shown below. They alert the user to the dangers of the areas on which they are pasted. Be sure to observe the instructions printed on those labels.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Location of labels | |
| Warning and caution labels on the robot unit | Additional description |
| Label 1 | Contact with the robot unit which is in motion can cause serious injuries. Observe the following:   1. Never enter the safeguarded space when the robot is in motion or the motor power is on. 2. When you need to enter the safeguarded space for recovery from robot failures, be sure to cut the power to the robot motors by activating an emergency stop device or the like. |
| Label 2 | There is a high voltage part.  This label alerts the user to the dangers of electrical shocks. |
| Label 3 | The figure shows how to hoist a robot. |
| Label 4 | Do not apply strong force on the external cable unit. NEVER do the following operations. Doing so will damage the external cable unit.   * Carry the robot with gripping the external cable unit. * Move the robot with pushing the external cable unit.   This label does not prohibit users from touching the external cable unit. It simply prohibits users from applying strong force on the unit. Therefore, you may touch the unit when you lay cables or pipes on it. |
| Label 5 | If the brake release switch is pressed while the controller is on, the Z-axis will drop.   1. Do not press the brake release switch except in an emergency. 2. Before pressing the brake release switch, ensure that there is no risk of injury or damage to equipment.   This label is attached only to the new HSR model. Although this label is not attached to the old HSR model, be sure to follow the precautions above. |

# Air Piping and Signal Wiring for Standard Type/ Bellows Type

The following image shows the Ethernet- and the External battery unit-equipped robot unit.

|  |
| --- |
| Please refer to this if the figure is not clear. [(PDF:812KB)](img/002430/002430_1.pdf) |
| Note 1: Pins #1 to #19 on CN21 and those on CN20 are connected with each other. The maximum rated current per line is 1A.  Note 2: Use the attached connector set for CN20 and CN21. |

Supply dry air filtered through an air filter (Recommended filtration rating: 5 µm or below).  
Before piping, blow the air tube out with dry air to clean out the inside (flushing); otherwise, any chips, cutting oil, dust or dirt remaining in the air tube may result in a damaged valve.

| Connector set part No. | Part No. | Model and name | Appearance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 410889-007\* | 410877-017\*  (for CN20) | SRCN6A25-24S (Round connector)  (Japan Aviation Electronics Industry Ltd.) |  |
| 410877-042\*  (for CN21) | JMSP2119M (Straight plug)  (DDK Electronics, Inc.) |  |
| - | 410877-098\*  (for Ethernet) | SACC-MS-8QO SH ETH SCO  (Phoenix) |  |

# Engineering-design Notes for Robot Hands

Design a hand (end-effector) so that it will satisfy conditions (1) and (2) described below.

Strictly observe these engineering-design notes. Otherwise, the clamped sections of the robot unit will become loose, rattle or be out of position. In the worst case, the mechanical parts of the robot unit and the robot controller may be damaged.

## Mass of Hand

The total mass of a hand or tool (including work-piece) should be less than the maximum allowable payload of the robot.

Be sure to include the mass of wirings and piping used for a hand or tool.

|  |
| --- |
| Total mass of hand or tool ≦ Max. allowable payload (incl.work-piece). (Mass of payload that you have preset) |

## Hand Center of Gravity

The center of gravity of a hand or tool (including work-piece) should be located within the range specified in Figure below.

|  |
| --- |
| Unit: mm |

For each center of gravity position, figure out the speed based on the following graph.

For acceleration, use the value calculated by the formula below.

Acceleration (%) = (Speed/100)2 x 100

(The above setting is not required if you set the payload center of gravity and payload moment of inertia, and select Control set 3 of the Optimal speed control function.)

|  |
| --- |
| <Application sample>   * To run the robot at 100% of the programmed speed and acceleration: Design so that the center of gravity of hand/tool is zero. * When the mass of hand/tool is 8 kg and the position of center of gravity is 85 mm, set the speed to 49% (acceleration: 24%) or less. |
|  |

## Moment of Inertia Around the T Axis

The moment of inertia of a hand or tool (including work-piece) around the T axis should be less than the maximum allowable moment of inertia around the T axis of the robot.

|  |
| --- |
| Hand's or Tool's moment of inertia around the T axis ≦ Max. allowable moment of inertia (incl.work-piece). (refer to the graph below). |

Calculate the moment of inertia around the T axis according to the graph given below.

You may program the reduced ratio of the speed and acceleration individually within the range specified below. If you set the reduced ratio of the programmed speed only, the controller automatically calculates that of the acceleration according to the formula below.

Acceleration (%) = (Speed/100)2 x 100

(The above setting is not required if you set the payload center of gravity and payload moment of inertia, and select Control set 3 of the Optimal speed control function.)

|  |
| --- |
| <Application sample>   * To run the robot at 100% of the programmed speed and acceleration: The moment of inertia around the T axis should be 0.01 kgm2 or less. * If the moment of inertia around the T axis is 0.12 kgm2: Run the robot at 29% or less of the programmed speed and at 8% or less of the programmed acceleration. |
|  |

# Notes for Setting the Positioning Speed

1. To horizontally traverse the robot arm at high speeds, teach the robot so that Z axis comes to be as close as possible to its upper end.
2. To stabilize positioning of Z axis near its lower end, the following maximum speed limiting control is automatically provided for J1 and J2 axes depending on the Z-axis coordinate value, only when the robot is moved under PTP control.  
   The positioning time of J1 and J2 axes becomes longer according to the maximum speed limit shown below.  

   |  |
   | --- |
   |  |

   For example, in case of the HSR series robot(floor-mount type), when the robot arm moves by SP100 from the start point (Z-axis coordinate 220 mm) to the target point (Z-axis coordinated -100 mm), the maximum speed limits are as follows:  
   100% when Z-axis coordinate is 220 mm, 60% when Z-axis coordinate is -100 mm.  
   At this time, the maximum speed is the smaller value (at the lowest end) of 60%.

# Installation Environment of the Robot Unit

Before installing the robot unit and robot controller, confirm that the operating environment is in conformity with each item of "SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, [Installation Precautions](001928.html)". Also, take proper measures to protect the components from vibration.

In an inappropriate environment, the robot will not operate to its full capacity or performance, components may not last long, and unexpected failure may result.

## Vibration

Do not install the robot in an environment where it will be exposed to excessive vibration or impact.  
To prevent damage of the installed robot from excessive impact or vibration during transportation, place the robot so that all axes contact with mechanical stoppers. Be sure to take measures to protect each axis such as wrapping up axis with cushions.

When the robot unit with the power off has undergone an excessive vibration during transportation, the ERROR 0x8320411\* (Encoder reference position error) may occur.

If the ERROR 0x8320411\* occurs when the robot power is first turned ON after purchase, refer to the "ERROR CODE TABLES" or contact the [DENSO service representative](001078.html).

## Connecting the Robot Unit and Robot Controller

Before delivery, the robot unit and the robot controller are adjusted to each other as a set. When two or more robots are to be used, use the robots and robot controllers that have been adjusted to each other as a set.

A robot set, which consists of a robot unit and a robot controller, have a common same serial number.

## Installation Environment of the Robot Unit

The table below lists the installation requirements for the robot unit.

* Do not electric-weld the equipment including the robot. A large current may flow through the motor encoder or robot controller resulting in a failure. If electric welding is required, remove the robot unit and the robot controller from the equipment beforehand.
* In operation, do not apply any direct jet flow into the bellows.

| Item | Environments and Conditions |
| --- | --- |
| Flatness of the mount | 0.1/500 mm (See the figure below.) |
| Rigidity of the mount | Use steel materials. (See the figure below.) |
| Installation type | Floor-mount or overhead-mount \*(Do not install a robot horizontally.) |
| Ambient temperature | During operation: 0 to 40℃  During storage and transportation: -10 to 60℃ |
| Humidity | During operation: 20 to 90% RH (No dew condensation allowed.)  During storage and transportation: 40 to 75% RH (No dew condensation allowed.) |
| Vibration | During operation: 4.9 m/s2 (0.5G) or less  During storage and transportation: 29.4 m/s2 (3G) or less |
| Altitude | During operation: 1,000 m or less |
| Safe installation environment | Refer to the SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, "[Insuring the Proper Installation Environment](001928.html)". |
| Working space, etc. | • Sufficient service space must be available for inspection and disassembly.  • Keep wiring space behind the robot, and fasten the wiring to the mounting face or beam so that the weight of the cables will not be directly applied to the connectors.  Wiring space for motor and encoder cable must be at least   * 190 mm for a straight connector, * 160 mm for an angle connector. |
| Grounding conditions | See "[Grounding the Robot Unit](002444.html)". |

### Robot Mount Sample for Floor-mount Type

|  |
| --- |
|  |

1. When the robot operates at high speed, the robot mount undergoes large reaction forces. The mount must be rigid enough so that it will not vibrate or be displaced due to reaction forces. It is also advisable to mechanically join the robot mount with heavy equipment.
2. Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling). If this sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or slightly modify the robot speed.

### Robot Mount Sample for Overhead-mount Type

|  |
| --- |
|  |

1. When the robot operates at high speed, the top plate structure undergoes large reaction forces. The robot mount must be vibration-proof so that the top plate will not vibrate due to reaction forces. Also it must be designed to be separated from other top plate structures in the equipment.
2. Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling). If this sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or slightly modify the robot speed.

# Robot Mount

The robot mount should be rigid enough. It is also advisable to mechanically join the robot mount with heavy equipment.

Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling). If the sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or slightly modify the robot speed.

## Maximum Reaction Force Applied to the Robot Mount

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002440_1.png)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Overturning moment Ml: | 703 Nm |
| Torsional moment Mt: | 762 Nm |
| Horizontal translational force Fh: | 2136 N |
| Vertical translational force Fv: | 1273 N |

Design the top plate structure so that it is independent from other top plate structures in the equipment.

# Transporting the Floor-Mount Type

This section gives the typical installation procedure assuming that you have set up the robot mount bed and prepared robot mounting bolt holes in it. If you have not done it yet, first read "[Securing the Robot Unit](004629.html)".

1. The installation jobs should be handled by at least two persons. Robot unit weight: approximately 32 kg (70.6 lbs)
2. Be sure to put on a helmet, safety shoes, and gloves.

1. Les travaux d'installation doivent être réalisés par deux personnes au moins.  
   Poids du robot: environ 32 kg (70.6 lbs)
2. Porter un casque, des chaussures de sécurité et des gants.

###### **1**

Turn the 2nd axis until it comes into contact with the mechanical end in order to keep the safe position. Then remove the four bolts and release the robot unit from the pallet.

When worker A is removing those bolts, worker B should support the 1st-axis arm to prevent the robot unit from overturning.

Lorsque le travailleur A retire les boulons, le travailleur B doit soutenir le premier bras à axe pour éviter que le robot ne se retourne.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002441_1.png)

###### 2

Transport the robot unit to the mounting position using the crane and eyebolts.

1. Since the robot unit weighs approximately 32 kg (70.6 lbs), prepare a crane and forklift with a hoisting load of 0.2 ton or more.
2. Be sure to put on a helmet, safety shoes, and gloves.

1. Étant donné que le robot pèse environ 32 kg (70.6 lbs), préparer une grue et un chariot élévateur à fourche pour une charge de 0,2 tonne minimum.
2. Porter un casque, des chaussures de sécurité et des gants.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002441_2.png)

###### 3

Put the robot unit on the mount bed and secure it with four bolts temporarily.

###### 4

Fix the robot unit, referring to"[Securing the Robot Unit](004629.html)".

Tightening torque: 70±14 Nm

# Securing the Robot Unit

###### 1

According to the dimensions specified in the figure below, drill four robot fixing holes and two dowel pin holes in the robot mount where the robot unit is to be anchored.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Four robot fixing holes | | M10 bolt holes, a minimum of 20 mm deep |
| Two holes for dowel pins | For diamond-shaped pin | φ4H7 dia. hole a minimum of 10 mm deep |
| For internally-threaded positioning pin | φ6H7 dia. hole, a minimum of 10 mm deep |

###### 2

Drive a diamond-shaped pin into the hole (φ4H7 dia.) so that the pin becomes oriented as shown below.

###### 3

Drive an internally-threaded positioning pin into the hole (φ6H7 dia.).

Never skip this step. These dowel pins can minimize the risk of misalignment that could be caused by replacement of the robot unit during maintenance or due to vibration.

###### 4

Put the robot unit on the robot mount.

###### 5

Secure the robot unit with four bolts and plain washers.

* Fixing bolts: M10 x 30 mm, JIS strength class: 12.9 (For HSR series)
* Tightening torque: 70±4 Nm (For HSR series)

## Bolt Positions for Securing the Robot Unit

# Grounding the Robot Unit

Ground the grounding terminal of the robot unit using a wire of 5.5 mm2 or more and no longer than 2 m.

Use a dedicated grounding wire and grounding electrode. Do not share them with other power facilities or welding machines.

## Precautions for Using the Old Type Motor & Encoder Cable

For the HSR series robot, the motor & encoder cable is available in two types: the new type and the old type.

An old type motor & encoder cable 6 m in length is shipped with a grounding wire and ferrite core.

If you choose the 6-meter old type motor & encoder cable, perform the following.

* Connect the provided wire to the A part of the controller for grounding.
* Install the provided ferrite core to the earth cable that connects to the B part of the controller.
* Install the provided ferrite core to the earth cable that connects to the Part C of the robot.  
  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002444_2.png)

# Notes for Wiring and Piping Through a Hollow in the Z-axis Shaft

The Z-axis shaft has a hollow through which you may make wiring and piping from the hand control signal connector or air piping joints on the top of the 2nd arm.

In this wiring and piping, check that:

1. Be sure to mount a stopper with wiring protection (option) and a wiring protection kit (option of the bellows type, dust- & splash-proof type, cleanroom type, H1 grease type) as the following shows.
2. When the robot is in motion, the wiring and piping do not become taut or interfere with other sections.
3. During up- or down-movement of the Z-axis, the wiring and piping inside the hollow do not become taut or interfere with other sections.
4. Making the wiring and piping able to be pulled out through the hollow makes maintenance easy.

For information about the part number of the stopper with wiring protection and the wiring protection kit, please refer to "[Options for Robot Unit](001970.html)".

## Installation of Stoppers

###### 1

Remove a stopper bolt (M5 x 16) mounted on the top of the Z-axis shaft.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002447_1.png)

###### 2

Insert the stopper with wiring protection into the shaft end, and then tighten it with a bolt (M5 x 16).

(Tightening torque: 5.9±0.59Nm)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002447_2.png)

## Installation of Wiring Protection Kit (Bellows Type, Dust- & Splash-proof Type, Cleanroom Type, H1 Grease Type)

###### 1

Mount the wiring protection kit on the top of Z-axis shaft and fix it with bolts (M3 x 8).  
(Tightening torque:1.6±0.16Nm)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002447_3.png)

# Prohibition of Removing Mechanical Stoppers

Do not leave the 3rd-axis mechanical stopper removed.  
Doing so, the CALSET initial position may deviate when CALSET is performed, resulting in the following problems;

* Software limits will become invalid.
* The robot will fail to run as programmed.
* The robot will interfere with its peripheral devices.

# Installing the Flange Kit (Option)

The flange kit consists of a flange, fixing bolt (M6x16), and setscrew (M5x8). Install the flange to the T-axis shaft according to the procedure below.

1. Wipe off oil from the circumference of the T-axis shaft which the flange should be fitted on.
2. Loosen the set screw of the flange so that the flange can be fitted on the T axis.
3. Push the flange until it comes into contact with nut end "A," and then rotate the flange so that the set screw becomes aligned with the flat section of the T-axis shaft.
4. Gradually tighten the set screw until it comes into contact with the flat section of the T-axis shaft and the flange can be rotated without looseness. Then torque the set screw to 3.6±0.6 Nm.
5. Tighten the set screw 2 just the same way as the set screw 1. (You can tighten the set screw 1 and 2 in any order.)
6. Tighten the fixing bolt (M6x16) to 14.7±2.94 Nm for securing the flange.

# Setting the Control Set of Motion Optimization

The optimum speed or acceleration will vary depending upon the payload and center of gravity of an end-effector or workpiece that is to be set at the end of the robot flange. Set the payload and center of gravity position of the end-effector or workpiece and the control set of motion optimization according to the payload and robot posture.

For details, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Optimal Speed Control Function](001542.html)
".

For the operating procedure, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Setting the Load Conditions](001547.html)
".

The mass of payload is a total mass of an end-effector and workpiece, expressed in grams.

Define the payload center of gravity in the TOOL0 coordinates in units of mm.

## 6Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 6axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 6th axis.

The Y component is defined on the orientation vector directed from the center of the flange to the center of the datum hole. The Z component is defined on the approach vector directed from the center of the flange to the normal line of the flange center. The X component is defined on the normal vector directed along the X axis (+) in the right-hand coordinates whose Y axis is an orientation vector and whose Z axis is an approach vector.

Datum hole is a pin hole which exists on the flange surface.

The size of datum hole differs depending on the robot types; φ6H7 for VM series, φ5H7 for other robots.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_1_1.png)

### Right Hand Coordinate System

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_2_1.png)

## 4-Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 4axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 4th axis.

# Moving Each Axis with Motor Power OFF in an Emergency Stop or When a Worker Trapped by the Robot

This section describes how to move each axis with the motor power being OFF at the time of an emergency stop or when a worker is trapped by the robot. Note that moving the 3rd (Z) and 4th (T) axes requires releasing their brakes beforehand.

Performing the brake release operation drops the Z axis. Make sure beforehand that the release operation will not cause bodily injuries or equipment damages.

Le desserrement du frein provoque la chute de l'axe Z. Vérifier au préalable que le desserrement du frein ne risque pas de provoquer des blessures ou d'endommager l'équipement.

## Moving the Axes in an Emergency Stop

| Axis | How to move the axes |
| --- | --- |
| 1st axis | Move the robot arm by hand. |
| 2nd axis |
| 3rd axis (Z-axis) | None of these axes can be moved by hand.  To move these axes, clear the emergency stop and release the brake. After that, move the target axis by hand.  To release the brake as shown below.   * Press the brake release switch. Only while being pressed, the brake can be released. * Brake can be released with teach pendant or mini-pendant (UL-Listed robot units are not available). For the detailed operation, refer to the following links.  |  |  |  | | --- | --- | --- | | Teach pendant | | Refer to "[Brake Setting](001750.html)" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE. | | Mini-pendant | 6Axis Robots | Refer to "[Releasing and Locking Brakes(6-axis)](001841.html)" of MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE. | | 4Axis Robots | Refer to "[Releasing and Locking Brakes(4-axis)](001842.html)" of MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE. | |
| 4th axis (T-axis) |
|  | |

When moving the robot by hand, hold by a part other than the plastic cover.

# Changing the Mechanical End

Adding mechanical stops to change mechanical ends is called "Mechanical end change."

For HSR series, you may change mechanical ends on the 1st through 3rd axes(Z).

Regarding to the additional mechanical stopper installation, you may need to prepare and install the stopper on your own.

## Cautions at Changing The Mechanical Ends

1. To change the mechanical ends, design and produce the mechanical stoppers suited for the usage conditions, referring to this manual.
2. After changing the mechanical ends using the mechanical stoppers, be sure to change also the software motion limits to prevent the robot arm from coming into contact with the mechanical stoppers when the robot runs.
3. If the robot arm collides against any mechanical stopper, it may be damaged. Before use, contact the Denso service representative for inspection and repair. The mechanical stopper designed and produced by the customer may also be damaged. Do not use it again and replace it.
4. A mass increase due to the mounted mechanical stoppers may influence the payload capacity of the robot unit.
5. The robot failures resulting from the mechanical stoppers shall not be covered by the warranty even if the robot is under warranty.

This manual does not include reference diagram of mechanical stoppers. Please contact your [DENSO representative](001077.html) for more details.

# Changing the Software Motion Limits

To avoid damages that could be caused by collision or contact with mechanical stoppers, configure the motion space by setting the software motion limits on individual axes.

By default, the software motion limits are configured slightly inside the mechanical ends.

If the robot arm reaches a software motion limit during manual or automatic operation, the robot displays an error message and comes to a stop. If the robot is in automatic operation, it also cuts off the power to the motors.

This function becomes valid after the robot arm enters the motion space configured by the software motion limits.

Software motion limits are not functions in accordance with safety standards.

## Precautions When Changing the Software Motion Limits

Confirm the robot motion range in actual working environment. Set the software motion limits using the correct unit of measurement.

If the robot arm lies in the position overriding the software motion limits, e.g., immediately after change of the software motion limits, only a manual operation that moves the robot arm towards the motion space is possible. Move the robot arm in Joint mode.

## Software Motion Limits Changing Procedure

In order to change the setting, change the value on the display of the software motion limit on the teach pendant, then, restart the controller.

For details of operation, refer to the "[Displaying and Setting the Software Motion Limit](001758.html)"of TEACH PENDANT GUIDE.

Newly programmed software motion limit will be valid after restart of the controller.
