# Base Coordinate Setting

To set an exclusive area on the World coordinate system, set the base definition with WINCAPSIII.

###### 1

Set a user parameter, [190: BASE number setting] [1: Enable].

If that is NOT enable, the change of base coordinates cannot be reflected to the arm 3D view when setting the exclusive area.

###### 2

Set the base definition.

Operation path : [Menu] – [View] – [Arm coordinate] – [Base]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002845_1.png)

You are able to create an exclusive area without performing the base definition in this step though, in this case, you need to change the coordinate values of the created exclusive area by using ConvertPosBase command later. For details, refer to Example of [ConvertPosBase](002283.html).

Even if you change the base definition on the controller, it cannot be reflected to the monitoring model.  
When you change the base definition with the teach pendant, receive the base definition of controller with WINCAPSIII. Then, perform [Export exclusive control data] and send that definition to the controller.

Since WINCAPSIII cannot receive the base definition changed by Base command, it cannot be reflected to the monitoring model.

# Kinematics Configuration

Kinematics Configuration enables to operate the robot, which is prepared by user, with MC8 series.

Although the normal use of MC8 series allows to control a linear motion robot only, this function enables "Arm-robot", such as SCARA robot, Parallel link robot, etc., to operate by pointing the position of the edge of the robot's arm.

This function is available for only MC8 series. (Ver.2.2.\* or higher)

Kinematics configuration of the robot type X, XY, XYZ, XYZT is equipped as standard function of MC8 series. Therefore, this function is available without a license. Existence or non-existence of license does not influence the behavior.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002846_1.png)

This function enables exclusively the robot which is prepared by user, by pointing the position of the edge of its robot's arm to operating; it is NOT the same capabilities as DENSO robot's. Some capability, such as Repeat positioning accuracy, is according to the configuration of the robot which is prepared by user.

## System Configuration

This function requires a robot other than MC8 series to operating. That robot shall be prepared by user.

For details about System Configuration of MC8 series, refer to "[System Configuration](005304.html)" of MC8 series (Motion Controller) in manual.

# Robot Type

Kinds of robots which are available with this function are below.

## List of Linear Motion Robot

| X | All axis is extra joints | XY | 2 axis XY robot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MC8 series standard function (available without license). | | MC8 series standard function (available without license). | |
| XYZ | 3 axis XYZ robot | XYZT | 4 axis XYZT robot |
| MC8 series standard function (available without license). | | MC8 series standard function (available without license).  For XYZT robot's coordinate on the edge of its arm, Z direction points downward. | |
| XYMZT | 4 axis XYMZT robot | LZ | 2 axis LZ robot |
| For XYMZT robot's coordinate on the edge of its arm, Z direction points upward. | |  | |
| LZZ | 3 axis LZZ robot | LYZZ | 4 axis LYZZ robot |
|  | |  | |
| LYY | 3 axis LYY robot | LZY | 3 axis LZY robot |
|  | |  | |
| LZYY | 4 axis LZYY robot |  | |
|  | |

| DLT3 | 3 axis parallel link robot | DLT4 | 4 axis parallel link robot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | | A telescopic bar transmitting power to the edge of the robot's arm is attached in the center of the arm. | |
| XR | 4 axis XR robot | H | 4 axis scalar robot |
|  | |  | |
| 6 axis TypeA | 6 axis TypeA robot | 6 axis TypeB | 6 axis TypeB robot |
|  | |  | |

# Setup Procedure

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002848_1.png)

It is possible to do "(4) Setting Each Axis" before doing "(2) Creating a Project".

In that case, after "Setting Each Axis", select "Editing an Existing Project" at the step of Kinematics Configuration Tool.

## (1) Registering License

This function requires a license key for each controller since this is an option function.

To enter a license key, use a teach pendant.

For how to enter it, refer to “[Registering License](002685.html)” in OPTION.

Kinematics configuration of the robot type X, XY, XYZ, XYZT is equipped as standard function of MC8 series. Therefore, this function is available without a license.  
 If you don't have the license, Kinematics configuration of X, XY, XYZ, XYZT is automatically set according to the number of robot joints selected in [Configuring Robot Joints](005318.html) (For example, if you select 4 joints as the robot axis range, Kinematics configuration of XYZT is internally set).

## (2) [Creating a Project](002849.html) (Kinematics Configuration Tool)

Create a project with Kinematics Configuration Tool.

## (3) [Sending a Project](002851.html) (WINCAPSIII)

Send a project to a controller with WINCAPSIII.

## (4) Setting Each Axis

Set each axis respectively to operate a robot.

Complete all the steps of "[Start-up procedure of the extended-joint (ball screw)](004933.html)" in "EXTENDED-JOINT MANUAL".

In addition, if you use a parallel link robot, you need to set parameters for some items. For details, refer to the "[Additional Setting Parameters of Parallel Link Robot](002973.html)".  
 For setting the arm parameters, refer to "[Arm Parameter Settings](005316.html)" in "MC8 SERIES (MOTION CONTROLLER) MANUAL".

When setting the gain parameter in the control system, if the conditions of conduct on auto gain tuning are not met, perform manual gain tuning.

For derails, refer to "[Auto Gain Tuning Procedure](005092.html)", "[Manual Gain Tuning](004927.html)" in EXTENDED-JOINT MANUAL.

# Creating a Project

There are two ways of performing if a user operates the robot prepared by him/herself with Kinematics configuration; one is to make a new project of WINCAPSIII with Kinematics configuration tool, and the other is to edit an existing project.

Kinematics configuration tool is automatically installed when WINCAPSIII is installed.

## Procedure

###### 1

Start up Kinematics configuration tool.

Operation path: PC [Start ] button - [All Programs] - [DENSO ROBOTICS] - [WINCAPSIII] - [Tools] - [Kinematics Configuration Tool].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_1.png)

###### 2

For creating a project newly, choose [Create a new project], set [Name] and [Save in] and then press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_2.png)

If you use Kinematics configuration tool after [Setting Each Axis], receive the controller project to WINCAPSIII, and save it; then, choose [Edit an existing project data] at the step of Kinematics Configuration Tool.

###### 3

Select the controller type and press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_3.png)

If you have selected [Edit an existing project data], this window will be skipped.

###### 4

Select the robot type which you want to operate and press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_4.png)

For more information about the robot types available, see "[Robot Type](002847.html)".

###### 5

Set arm length depending on the robot type you selected, and press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_5.png)

* The values of arm length to be set are limited. About every particular item of arm length, refer to "[Arm Parameter Settings](002850.html)".
* When Ball Screw Spline is used to the linear motion axis on 4-axis robot, or when the 5th-axis motion interferes with the 6th-axis motion under 6-axis robot use, additional parameter settings are required. For details, refer to "[Additional Setting of 4-axis or 6-axis Robot](003045.html)".

###### 6

Confirm your settings on the screen and press [Next].

If the setting is incorrect, the robot may operate unintentionally.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_6.png)

###### 7

Press [Complete] to finish creating the project.

If you check on "Open the project with WINCAPSIII", after pressing [Complete], WINCAPSIII will boot.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002849_7.png)

# Arm Length Setting

## 3 Axis Parallel Link Robot

Set the lengths from L1 to L6 shown by the figure. (Unit: mm)

| Arm No. | Description | Arm Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Length: from base coordinate origin to center of robot arm joint | 0 mm or more |
| L2 | Length: from center of robot arm joint to portion of its elbow | 0 mm or more |
| L3 | Length: from portion of elbow to side of flange | 0 mm or more |
| L4 | Length: from side of flange to center of flange | 0 mm or more |
| L5 | Offset in Z axis direction: from base coordinate origin to the center of robot arm joint | 0 mm or more |
| L6 | Length in Z axis direction: from flange surface to its edge | 0 mm or more |
|  | | |

## 4 Axis Parallel Link Robot

Set the lengths of L7 and L8 adding to the dimension mentioned above for 3 Axis Parallel Link Robot (Unit: mm)

| Arm No. | Description | Arm Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L7 | Length of the attachment part on the 4th-axis telescoping bar to be transmitted power (upper) | 0 mm or more |
| L8 | Length of the attachment part on the 4th-axis telescoping bar to be transmitted power (lower) | 0 mm or more |
|  | | |

## 4 Axis XR Robot

Set the length of L1 shown by the figure. (Unit: mm)

| Arm No. | Description | Arm Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Length: from the 2nd-axis rotation center to the 4th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
|  | | |

## 4 Axis Scalar Robot

Set the length of L1 and L2 shown by the figure. (Unit: mm)

| Arm No. | Description | Arm Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Length: from the 1st-axis rotation center to the 2nd-axis rotation center | More than 0 mm |
| L2 | Length: from the 2nd-axis rotation center to the 4th-axis rotation center | More than 0mm |
|  | | |

## 6 Axis TypeA Robot

Set the lengths from L1 to L6 shown by the figure. (Unit: mm)

| Arm No. | Description | Arm Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Length in Z axis direction: from base coordinate origin to the 2nd-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L2 | Offset in X axis direction: from base coordinate origin to the 2nd-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L3 | Length in Z axis direction: from the 2nd-axis rotation center to the 3rd-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L4 | Offset in X axis direction: from the 3rd-axis rotation center to the 4th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L5 | Length in Z axis direction: from the 3rd-axis rotation center to the 5th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L6 | Length in Z axis direction: from the 5th-axis rotation center to the flange surface | 0 mm or more |
|  | | |

## 6 Axis TypeB Robot

Set the lengths from L1 to L6 shown by the figure. (Unit: mm)

| Arm No. | Description | Arm Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | Length in Z axis direction: from base coordinate origin to the 2nd-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L2 | Length in Z axis direction: from the 2nd-axis rotation center to the 3rd-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L3 | Length in Z axis direction: from the 3rd-axis rotation center to the 4th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L4 | Offset in Y axis direction: from base coordinate origin to the 5th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L5 | Offset in X axis direction: from base coordinate origin to the 6th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
| L6 | Length in Z axis direction: from the 4th-axis rotation center to the 6th-axis rotation center | 0 mm or more |
|  | | |

# Sending a Project

After creating a project, open it with WINCAPSIII and send its parameter to the controller.

After sending, confirm if the parameter have been sent correctly by using a teach pendant.

###### 1

Send the data to the controller.

Make sure that [Parameter] has been verified with a check mark; and press [Send].

For details, please refer to "[Communications Settings](004409.html)" and "[Data Transfers](004410.html)" in WINCAPSIII GUIDE.

Reboot the robot controller after sending the data.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002851_1.png)

To perform this step, the robot controller and WINCAPSIII must be connected with a cable.

For information on how to connect, please refer to [Link with Robot Controller](004408.html) in "WINCAPSIII GUIDE".

###### 2

Open the Arm window with a teach pendant.

The robot type you selected will be displayed after clicking the button, which is on the upper window displaying MC8 series as an example.

If that selected robot type is not shown, configure again with Kinematics Configuration Tool.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002851_2.png)

Robot types are able to be shown only if the controller is MC8 series and the license is valid.

# Precautions for Use

## Unavailable Functions

The following functions and commands cannot be used.

| Function Name | Command Name | Remarks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Optimal speed control function | SpeedMode | - |
| Arch motion | ArchMove | - |
| High precision control | HighPathAccuracy | - |
| Current limiting function | CurLmt, Zforce | CurLmt Command is available to any robots other than parallel link robot and 6 axis robot. The other robots can use CurLmt Command.  Zforce Command is unable to use to all robots. |
| Force control function | ForceCtrl | - |
| Ambient temperature settings on the robot operation | - | - |
| Temperature drift offset function | - | - |
| Path accuracy enhancement option at high speed operation | - | - |
| Gravity compensation function | GrvOffset, GrvCtrl | GrvOffset Command is available to any robots other than parallel link robot and 6 axis robot. The other robots can use GrvOffset Command.  GrvCtrl Command is unable to use to all robots. |
| Deflection compensation function | - | - |
| Singularity avoidance function | SingularAvoid | - |
| Virtual fence | - | - |
| Exclusive control | - | - |
| Cooperative control function | - | - |

## 3D Models

3D Models are not available. It is not available to simulate 3D models on the screen with teach pendant or WINCAPSIII.

## Robot Motion

The following robot types are only able to do Motion of each axis.

* LZZ
* LYZZ
* LYY
* LZYY

## Configuring Functions of Existing Robot Joints

If Kinematics Configuration Tool is enabled, "[Configuring Robot Joints](005318.html)" will be disabled.

If you want to change the robot type after its license has been enabled, change it with Kinematics Configuration Tool.

## Programming

This is not a dedicated command to using with only Kinematics Configuration Tool.

For details on programming, refer to "[PROGRMMAR'S MANUAL](001301.html)".

# CIRCULAR TRACKING MANUAL

This manual describes the circular tracking system. This function is available in Ver.2.3.\* or higher.

To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html)."

This expanded the function of conveyor tracking for Turntable, some words could be used as the same as the words for conveyor tracking.  
e.g. Conveyor number, Conveyor reference position, and Conveyor calibration

# Overview

## Brief Description of the Circular Tracking

Circular tracking is a robot function that allows robots to keep track of workpieces carried by the turntable without stopping the turntable.  
There are two types of circular tracking.

Sensor tracking
:   The sensor tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed in the same arc with arbitrary interval on the moving turntable.  
    In this system, a signal is generated when a workpiece traverses in front of a photoelectric sensor.  
    Once this signal is generated, position data of the workpiece is registered in the controller. Based on that, the controller calculates the expected workpiece position on the turntable and instructs the robot to follow the workpiece. This process is performed whenever a workpiece passes in front of the photoelectric sensor.
:   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_1.png)

Vision tracking
:   The vision tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed on arbitrary position and attitude on the moving turntable.  
    In this system, a signal is generated when an image recognition unit of the vision sensor detects a workpiece.  
    Once this signal is generated, position and the angle of the workpiece are registered in the controller. Based on that, the controller calculates the expected workpiece position and instructs the robot to follow the workpiece. This process is performed whenever the signal is generated.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_2.png)

The sensor tracking and the vision tracking function cannot be used with the cooperative control function and the force control function.

The combination use with the exclusive control is available in version 2.8.\* or higher.

## Enabling Circular Tracking Function

The operation status of the circular tracking are defined by the following terms.

Tracking mode
:   "Tracking mode" means a state that the circular tracking is enabled.  
    Calling circular tracking-dedicated commands ("[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)", "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)", "[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)" and "[TrackDraw](003049.html)")  
    while the circular tracking is enabled will allow robots to follow the target position according to the turntabler's motion.

Non-tracking mode (Normal operation mode)
:   "Non-tracking mode" means a state that the circular tracking is disabled. This is the default setting at the controller startup.  
    To move a robot arm to a static target position, use motion commands ("[Approach](000161.html)", ["Depart](000186.html)" and "[Move](000207.html)") in this mode.

To change the [tracking mode](#trackingMode), use dedicated commands for tracking mode change ([TrackStart](005377.html) and [TrackStop](005378.html)).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_3.png)

## Robot Motion during Tracking Mode

While tracking mode is enabled, robot motion is controlled by the tracking mode-dedicated commands ("[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)", "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)", "[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)" and "[TrackDraw](003049.html)").  
Please note that if a tracking mode-dedicated command is used during [tracking mode](#trackingMode) even once, robot starts automatically moving in parallel with the turntable in order to track with the turntable motion.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_4.png)

The robot motion status during the [tracking mode](#trackingMode) are defined by the following terms.

Catch-up motion
:   Catch-up motion indicates a robot motion that catches up to the target workpiece on the turntable.  
    The robot accelerates its speed until it catches up to the workpiece, and then moves in parallel to the turntable once the robot reaches the workpiece.  
    When the conveyor is running at high speed, the robot may move at a speed faster than the specified external speed to catch up with the conveyor.

Robot task motion
:   Robot task motion is a robot motion that performs actual robot tasks along with the [catch-up motion](#tracking).

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_5.png)

Robot motion during the [tracking mode](#trackingMode) is the synthesized motion of the [catch-up motion](#tracking) and the [robot task motion](#operation).  
For example, a [TrackApproach](005346.html) motion is a synthesized motion of the [catch-up motion](#tracking) and [Approach](000161.html) motion. In this context, Approach motion corresponds to the robot task motion.

### Types of the tool-end posture control

In the circular tracking, there are two types of end-effector posture control during the tracking mode.

#### To rotate the tool-end posture along with the turntable rotation.

As the following figure shows, a robot moves with turning the tool-end posture along with the turntable rotation.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_8.png)

The reference posture at the rotation differs depending on the motion command.

* Motion command is "[TrackApproach](005346.html)” or "[TrackMove](005356.html)"

  The reference posture is the posture of [Calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos).

  [Calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos) is a position that is taught by customers to configure [Upstream limit of the tracking range](002856.html#trackURange).

  In the actual motion, by the angle between the [Upstream limit of the tracking range](002856.html#trackURange) to the position where a robot catches up a workpiece, the robot rotates the said reference posture.

  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_9.png)
* Motion command is "[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)", "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)"

  The reference posture in the "[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)" is the posture in the position which is specified in the second argument "Reference position".

  The reference posture in "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)" is the posture in the position which is specified in the second argument of "Target position".

  In the actual motion, by the rotation angle of the turntable from the start timing of a motion command (either "[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)" or "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)") to the timing when a robot catches up a workpiece, the robot moves with rotating the said reference posture.

  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_11.png)
* Motion command is "[TrackDepart](005350.html)" or "[TrackDraw](003049.html)"

  The reference posture is the posture in the position when the motion command ("[TrackDepart](005350.html)"or "[TrackDraw](003049.html)") starts.

  In the actual motion, by the rotation angle of the turntable from the start timing of a motion command (either "[TrackDepart](005350.html)" or "[TrackDraw](003049.html)") to the timing when a robot catches up a workpiece, the robot moves with rotating the said reference posture.

  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_12.png)

#### To keep the tool-end posture stable

As the following figure shows, regardless of the rotation angle of turntable, a robot moves with keeping a given tool-end posture.

However, this control method is only available in the robot controller software version 2.8.\* or higher.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_10.png)

The posture of the tool end to be taken as a stable posture differs depending on the motion command. Refer to the following table.

| Commands | The posture of the tool end to be taken as a stable posture |
| --- | --- |
| [TrackAbsApproach](003133.html) | The posture taken in the position specified by the guaranteed entry "Reference position". |
| [TrackApproach](005346.html) |
| [TrackAbsMove](003134.html) | The posture taken in the position specified by the guaranteed entry "Target position". |
| [TrackMove](005356.html) |
| [TrackDepart](005350.html) | Posture in the current position |
| [TrackDraw](003049.html) |

### How to specify the tool-end posture control

To specify the tool-end posture control, use [TrackStart](005377.html) command. For details, refer to [TrackStart](005377.html) command.

## Range of the [Catch-up motion](005346.html)

If a tracking mode-dedicated command ("[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)", "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)", "[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)", "[TrackDraw](003049.html)") is used during [tracking mode](#trackingMode) even once, robot starts automatically moving in parallel with the turntable in order to keep tracking with the turntable motion.  
In RC8 series, to define the area of circular tracking according to the operation, following terms are defined.

Tracking range
:   This is an area on the turntable where the robot can perform the [catch-up motion](#tracking).  
    Tracking range is delimited by the upstream limit and the downstream limit. The upstream limit is set to the direction where a workpiece comes from, whereas the downstream limit is set to the direction where a workpiece goes to. To use multiple robots, set a tracking range for respective robots.

Upstream limit of the tracking range (Upstream limit)
:   This is the tracking limit on the upstream of the turntable. Once a workpiece passes this limit, a robot starts the [catch-up motion](#tracking).  
    This must be set within the motion range of the robot arm.

Downstream limit of the tracking range (Downstream limit)
:   This is the tracking limit on the downstream of the turntable. Once a workpiece reaches this limit, robot stops the [catch-up motion](#tracking) and starts deceleration.  
    This must be set within the motion range of the robot arm.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_6.png)

## Circular Tracking with Multiple Robots

By using RC8 series, multiple robots can perform circular tracking on one turntable.  
This operation is practical when multiple robots perform each task in different area on the turntable, provided that the circular tracking area is divided into two parts; upstream and downstream.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002855_7.png)

When circular tracking is performed by multiple robots, each robot controller is assigned to one of the following.

Master Controller
:   Master controller receives a signal that is generated when a sensor or vision sensor detects a workpiece in order to obtain the position information of the workpiece.  
    Among multiple controllers, only one controller is assigned to the master controller. This controller performs circular tracking itself and also is entitled to instruct other controllers which workpiece to track.

Slave Controller
:   All controllers except master controller will be the slave controller.  
    A slave controller receives tracking target workpiece data via Ethernet communication, and then performs circular tracking.

# Terminology and Definitions

Tracking mode
:   "Tracking mode" means a state that the circular tracking is enabled.  
     Calling circular tracking-dedicated commands ("[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)", "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)", "[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)", and "[TrackDraw](003049.html)") while the circular tracking is enabled will allow robots to follow the target position according to the turntable's motion.
:   During tracking mode, any deceleration caused by the exclusive control, SS2, RSM are not available.  
     Doing so, the robot will stop with an error.  
     The combination use of the exclusive control and circular tracking is available in version 2.8.\* or higher.

Non-tracking mode (Normal operation mode)
:   "Non-tracking mode" means a state that the circular tracking is disabled. This is the default setting at the controller startup.  
     To move a robot arm to a static target position, use motion commands ("[Approach](000161.html)", "[Depart](000186.html)", and "[Move](000207.html)") in this mode.  
     Executing tracking-dedicated commands ("[TrackAbsApproach](003133.html)", "[TrackAbsMove](003134.html)", "[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)", and "[TrackDraw](003049.html)") in this mode will cause an error.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_1.png)

Catch-up motion
:   Catch-up motion indicates a robot motion that catches up to the target workpiece on the turntable.  
     The robot accelerates its speed until it catches up to the workpiece, and then moves in parallel to the turntable once the robot reaches the workpiece.  
    When the conveyor is running at high speed, the robot may move at a speed faster than the specified external speed to catch up with the conveyor.

Robot task motion
:   Robot task motion is a robot motion that performs actual robot tasks along with the turntable [catch-up motion](#tracking).  
     For example, a [TrackApproach](005346.html) motion is a synthesized motion of the [catch-up motion](#tracking) and [Approach](000161.html) motion. In this context, Approach motion corresponds to the robot task motion.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_2.png)

Tracking buffer
:   This indicates the memory storage area that is used to store data with regard to workpieces detected by a sensor or vision sensors.  
     The following data is stored when a workpiece is registered.

|  | Stored values |
| --- | --- |
| (1) | Index value in the tracking buffer ([integer type](000451.html) data) |
| (2) | Turntable encoder value at workpiece detection ([integer type](000451.html) data) |
| (3) | [Vision sensor detection coordinates](#visionCoordinate) ([variant type](005067.html) data array) |
| [Sensor detection position](#sensorPos) ([position type](000456.html) data) |
| (4) | User data ([integer type](000451.html) data) |
| (5) | Attribute data ([integer type](000451.html) data) |

Conveyor vector
:   A conveyor vector is a three-dimensional vector whose length is one. This shows the motion direction of a turntable. This is a direction vector viewed from the base coordinate system.

Tracking-target work
:   A tracking-target work indicates a workpiece data that has just been taken out of the [tracking buffer](#trackBuf) and is about to be used for the tracking motion.  
     This will be the processing object of some commands, such as [TrackInRange](005355.html) and [TrackArrivalTime](005351.html).

Tracking range
:   This is an area on the turntable where the robot can perform the [catch-up motion](#tracking).  
     Tracking range is delimited by the upstream limit and the downstream limit. The upstream limit is set to the direction where a workpiece comes from, whereas the downstream limit is set to the direction where a workpiece goes to.  
     To use multiple robots, set a tracking range for respective robots.

Upstream limit of the tracking range (Upstream limit)
:   This is the tracking limit on the upstream of the turntable. Once a workpiece passes this limit, a robot starts the  [catch-up motion.](#tracking)  
     This must be set within the motion range of the robot arm.

Downstream limit of the tracking range (Downstream limit)
:   This is the tracking limit on the downstream of the turntable. Once a workpiece reaches this limit, a robot stops the [catch-up motion](#tracking) and starts deceleration.  
     This must be set within the motion range of the robot arm.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_3.png)

Calibration point on upstream limit
:   This is a point registered at the conveyor calibration to delimit the [upstream limit of the tracking range](#trackURange).  
     This is a center position of a robot flange viewed from the base coordinate system.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_4.png)

Calibration point on downstream limit
:   This is a point registered at the conveyor calibration to delimit the [downstream limit of the tracking range](#trackLRange).  
     This is a center position of a robot flange viewed from the base coordinate system.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_5.png)

Conveyor reference position
:   This is a midpoint (X, Y, Z) between the [calibration point on upstream limit](#trackURangePos) and the  [calibration point on downstream limit](#trackLRangePos).  
     As the calibration point on [upstream](#trackURange) and/or [downstream](#trackLRange) limit changes, this position changes together.  
     This is a center position of a robot flange viewed from the base coordinate system.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_6.png)

Default posture of holding the work
:   This is the posture of [position type](000456.html) (Rx, Ry, Rz) that goes and holds a workpiece when operating the circular tracking.  
     This is the posture that those position and posture registered, when teaching of [calibration point on upstream limit](#trackURangePos), have been rotated to the conveyor reference coordinate around the conveyor axis.  
     When [upstream limit of the tracking range](#trackURange) and/or [downstream limit of the tracking range](#trackLRange) changes, the posture changes together.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_7.png)

Conveyor reference coordinate
:   This consists of the [conveyor reference position](#conveyorBase) and the [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture). It is [position type](000456.html) data.

Calibration
:   In the circular tracking of RC8 series, calibration means measuring the exact positional relationship between the turntable, sensor (vision sensor), and robot. Specifically, it refers to executing the [conveyor calibration](#convCalibration), [sensor calibration](#sensCalibration) (at the time of sensor tracking), and [camera calibration](#camCalibration) (at the time of vision tracking).

Conveyor calibration
:   In the circular tracking of RC8 series, conveyor calibration means measuring the exact positional relationship between the turntable and robot. Specifically, it means the measurement of the following parameters.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor CALDATA (X, Y) | Rotating angle around the Z axis of the base coordinate that shows the direction of rotary axis of the turntable [rad] |
| Conveyor CALDATA (Z) | Inclination seen from the XY plane of the base coordinate that shows the direction of rotary axis of the turntable [rad] |
| Conveyor feed rate | Amount of turntable movement per one rotation of encoder [deg/rev] |
| Encoder rotation direction | Rotational direction of encoder when the turntable is moved from upstream to the downstream (1: Normal, -1: Reverse) |

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Upstream limit of the tracking range | Once a workpiece passes this limit, a robot starts the [catch-up motion](#tracking). [mm] |
| Downstream limit of the tracking range | Once a workpiece reaches this limit, a robot stops the [catch-up motion](#tracking) and starts deceleration. [mm] |

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate X | Midpoint X between the [calibration point on upstream limit](#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](#trackLRangePos) [mm] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Y | Midpoint Y between the [calibration point on upstream limit](#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](#trackLRangePos) [mm] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Z | Midpoint Z between the [calibration point on upstream limit](#trackURangePos)  and the [calibration point on downstream limit](#trackLRangePos) [mm] |

Sensor calibration
:   In the circular tracking of RC8 series, sensor calibration means measuring the exact positional relationship between the sensor and robot. Concretely to say, it means the measurement of the following parameters.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CALDATA (00) | Nx for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (01) | Ox for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (02) | Ax for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (03) | [Sensor detection position](#sensorPos) X [mm] |
| CALDATA (10) | Ny for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (11) | Oy for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (12) | Ay for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (13) | [Sensor detection position](#sensorPos) Y [mm] |
| CALDATA (20) | Nz for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (21) | Oz for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (22) | Az for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [homogeneous translation type](#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA (23) | [Sensor detection position](#sensorPos) Z [mm] |

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate RX | RX of [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate RY | RY of [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate RZ | RZ of [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture) [deg] |

Camera parameter
:   In the circular tracking of RC8 series, camera parameter means the parameter which converts the image coordinates of vision sensor to the position seen from the base coordinates of the robot. Concretely to say, it means the following parameters.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CALDATA (00) | Nx for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (01) | Ox for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (02) | Ax for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (03) | [Vision sensor detection position](#visionPos) X [mm] |
| CALDATA (10) | Ny for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (11) | Oy for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (12) | Ay for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (13) | [Vision sensor detection position](#visionPos) Y [mm] |
| CALDATA (20) | Nz for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (21) | Oz for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (22) | Az for the [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA (23) | [Vision sensor detection position](#visionPos) Z [mm] |

Camera calibration
:   In the circular tracking of RC8 series, camera calibration means measuring the exact positional relationship between the vision sensor and robot. Concretely to say, it means the measurement of the [camera parameter](#camParam) and the following parameters.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate RX | RX of [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate RY | RY of [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate RZ | RZ of [default posture of holding the work](#gripBasePosture) [deg] |

Sensor detection position
:   This is a workpiece position (X, Y, Z) when it is detected by the line sensor, viewed from the robot coordinate system. This position is as follows. In the [sensor calibration](#sensCalibration), teaching of the position of [calibration point on upstream limit](#trackURangePos) is executed and moved back in the opposite of the [conveyor vector](#conveyorVec) direction.  
     This is a center position of a robot flange viewed from the base coordinate system.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_8.png)

Coordinate of zero point
:   Reference point on the image coordinate which is used to define the [vision sensor detection position](#visionPos). The image coordinate of the first point among three reference points taught at the [camera calibration](#CamCalibration) is specified.

Vision sensor detection position
:   This is a workpiece position (X, Y, Z) on the [coordinate of zero point](#ZeroPoint) when it is detected by the vision sensor, viewed from the robot coordinate system. This is a center position of a robot flange viewed from the base coordinate system.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_9.png)

Vision sensor detection coordinates
:   Vision sensor detection coordinates consist of the image coordinates (x- and y-coordinates expressed in pixel) and the workpiece's attitude angle θ (expressed in degree) when the vision sensor detects a workpiece.  
     This is expressed by a [variant type](005067.html) data array with three elements that stores x, y, and θ in this order. Each element is expressed by single precision real type data.

Amount of movement from the vision sensor detection position to the workpiece imaging position
:   In circular conveyor tracking, it refers to the amount of movement Δθ (expressed in degree) of the target workpiece on the turntable from the "[vision sensor detection position](#visionPos)" to the "workpiece’s position where the camera captures an image".![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_11.png)

Tracking start range
:   Tracking start range is a position that the [upstream limit of the tracking range](#trackLRange) is offset to the upstream direction in specified distance.  
     In the [tracking buffer](#trackBuf), work data that locates downstream than this range is counted as possible [tracking-target work](#targetWork).  
     By setting the tracking start range, the system enables to recognize a workpiece that is moved into the [tracking range](#trackRange) while the robot moves from the waiting position to the [upstream limit of the tracking range](#trackURange), as a tracking target work.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002856_10.png)

# System Configuration

This chapter describes the system configuration of the circular tracking.

* For safety reason and to prevent damage to the devices, disconnect the power cable of the controller or shut down the power supply to the controller from the facilities before disconnecting or connecting cables.
* A robot controller that the circular tracking license is enabled restricts communication speed for other operations. This is because the controller places a priority on ensuring the communication for the tracking motion.  
  If time-out occurs before other operations are not completed, take any prevention measures, such as setting longer time-out period.

# System Configuration of the Sensor Tracking

Configuration of the sensor tracking is illustrated below.

The sensor tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed in the same arc with arbitrary interval on the moving conveyor.  
The system executes two different programs simultaneously; one is a program to recognize the position of a workpiece and the other is a program to pick it up.

In a program which recognizes workpieces, the sensor activates trigger on once a workpiece passes through the sensor, and then the controller receives the encoder data and stores it at that moment.  
In a picking up program, based on the stored data, the robot picks up a workpiece by adjusting the robot arm in response to the workpiece's motion.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002858_1.png)

## Wiring diagram

Wiring diagram is illustrated below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002858_2.png)

### Encoder Hub

For encoder hub, there are old model and new model.

If you use a new model, connect the encoder line of the motor & encoder cable to the encoder hub's connector port indicated as "ROBOT-0" (on the left side viewed from the front).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003322_2.png)

For details about the external diagram and the precaution on installation, refer to ["Encoder HUB"](018093.html).

# System Configuration of the Vision Tracking

Configuration of the vision tracking is illustrated below.

The vision tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed on arbitrary position on the moving turntable.  
The system executes two different programs simultaneously; one is a program to recognize coordinates of a workpiece and the other is a program to pick it up.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002859_1.png)

A program which recognizes coordinates of workpieces operates as shown below.

Visual device starts recording once receiving an instruction from the controller. If workpiece exists, the visual device sends position data of workpiece to the controller.  
Once the visual device starts recording, it transmits trigger signal to the controller, then the controller immediately obtains position data from the encoder.  
The controller stores workpiece's position data transmitted from the visual device and position data obtained from encoder per workpiece.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002859_2.png)

In a picking up program, the controller reads the stored position data of workpiece, then the robot picks up a workpiece by adjusting the robot arm in response to the workpiece's motion.

## Wiring Diagram

Wiring diagram is illustrated below.

To connect to the encoder HUB, connect to the port according to the joint number of the encoder.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002859_3.png)

### Encoder Hub

For encoder hub, there are old model and new model.

If you use a new model, connect the encoder line of the motor & encoder cable to the encoder hub's connector port indicated as "ROBOT-0" (on the left side viewed from the front).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003322_2.png)

For details about the external diagram and the precaution on installation, refer to ["Encoder HUB"](018093.html).

# Configuration of the Circular Tracking System with One Turntable and Two or more Robots

The example of the vision tracking system is illustrated below.  
This system configuration is effective in the case where the turntable moves so fast that one robot is not enough to pick up all workpieces. Up to three slave controllers are available.

In this application, one controller is designated as a master controller, and the remaining controllers are designated as slave controllers.  
The master controller is connected to the visual device and the encoder. This controller obtains position data of workpieces and then executes picking up operation by robot.  
The slave controller connects to the master controller with Ethernet cable. This controller executes program to pickup workpieces based on the position data obtained by the master controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002860_1.png)

* When you install two or more robots in one system, arrange these robots so as not to interfere each other.
* The specifications for the master controller and slave controllers must be the same. All of them must have the circular tracking licenses, and must be set to Extended-joint-supported, and the same software version.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002860_2.png)

If you use a new model, connect the encoder line of the motor & encoder cable to the encoder hub's connector port indicated as "ROBOT-0" (on the left side viewed from the front).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003322_2.png)

For details about the external diagram and the precaution on installation, refer to ["Encoder HUB"](018093.html).

# Encoder Specification

The below table shows the specifications of the encoder.  
Be sure to read the INSTRUCTION Sheet enclosed in the package.

## Specification

| Item | Specifications |
| --- | --- |
| Part No. | 410010-752\* |
| Model | E6B2-CWZ1X （OMRON） |
| Type | Incremental |
| Supply voltage | 5 VDC(±5 %) |
| Current consumption | 160 mA max. |
| Output circuit configuration | Line driver output |
| Output phase |  |
| Maximum response frequency | 100 kHz |
| Slewing speed | 6000 r/min |
| Resolution | 1000 pulses/revolution (Note 1) |
| Starting torque | 9980 µNｍ max. |
| Moment of inertia | 1×10-6 kgm2 max. |
| Shaft loading | Radial：30 N, Axial：20 N |
| Dust & splash proof | IP50 |
| Ambient temperature | -10 ℃ to +70 ℃ |
| Ambient humidity | 35 % to 85 % RH |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002864_2.png)

Note 1: The number of pulses is multiplied by 4, so the count value is 4000 pulses/revolution.  
Note 2: Since this equipment is neither dust-proof nor drip-proof, protect it with a cover or something if used in an adverse environment.  
Note 3: Protect the encoder connectors by putting covers on them after installation.

## Appearance Diagram and Dimensional Outline Drawing

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002864_3.png)

For information about how to install the encoder, see OMRON's website.

If an error message "Execute CALSET" is displayed at the start-up of the controller, perform CALSET.  
For information about the CALSET procedure, see ["Executing CALSET"](005090.html) in the "EXTENDED-JOINT MANUAL".

## Encoder Cable

To connect the encoder with the encoder hub, use a dedicated encoder cable (cable for RC8-OMRON encoder).  
The length of cables are 1 m, 2 m, 3 m, 4 m, 6 m and 12 m. The encoder junction cable is the same as the one used for the extended-joint support controller. For details, see ["Options for Robot Controller"](001971.html) of "OPTIONAL COMPONENTS".

* Incorrect connection of the extended-joint or encoder may cause malfunction.
* The total length of an encoder cable for each axis between a connection port of the encoder hub and a connection port of the motor shall be 16 m or less.
* The bending radius for the encoder cable and encoder relay cable should be 12.5 mm or more for the fixed cable, and 83 mm or more for the movable cable. Excessive bending will damage the cable.

# Restrictions on the Application of Encoder

## Precautions for Safe Use

1. Avoid wiring the prduct's cables parallel to power lines or high-voltage lines. Doing so may cause the product to malfunction due to induction or may cause the damage the product.
2. Minimize the wiring length to prevent the product from being affected by noise,etc.
3. Since improper pulses may occur when the power is turned on or off, use the devices connected to this product at least 1.0 seconds before or after the power is turned on or off.
4. Be careful when wiring, such as being careful with the polarities of the power supply. Incorrect wiring may break or burn the product.
5. Do not short-circuit the load. Doing so may break or burn the product.
6. Do not use the encorder under the environment with explosive or ignition gas.
7. Never disassemble, repair nor tamper with the product.

## Precautions for Correct Use

1. Since the product consists of high-precision components, handle it with utmost care.
2. Be careful not to expose the product to water or oil.
3. Be sure to turn off the power supply before wiring. If the output line contacts the power supply line while the power is being supplied, the outout circuit may be damaged.
4. If the product is mounted and wired with a cord, do not pull the cord with force greater then 29.4N.
5. Be careful not to apply excessive load to the shaft. Excessive load may cause the product break. Especially when linking with a chain, timing belt, or gears, connect a separate bearing before the couping to the product.
6. If an installation error such as misalignment is too large,(in case using the coupling or without coupling) the shaft will be subjected to an excessive load which will damage it or shorten its service life. Be careful when installing.
7. When inserting the shaft in the coupling, do not use excessive force (by striking it with hammer, for example).
8. When installing or removing the coupling, do not apply an excessive being, compressing, or tensile force.
9. Be careful not to connect the cable incorrectly. Doing so, incorrect encoder value will be read.

## Agreement for Use

1. To ensure the operator's safety, do not use this product for the purpose of the direct or indirect human body detection.
2. If use in the application is acceptable, use the product with extra allowance in ratings and specifications, and provide safety measures to minimize hazards in the event of failure (such as using safety circuits).

* Outdoor use, use involving potential chemical contamination or electrical interference, or use in conditions or environments not described in product catalogs or manuals.
* Nuclear energy control systems, combustion systems, railroad systems, aviation systems, vehicle systems, medical equipment, amusement machines, and installations subject to separate industry or government regulations.
* Systems, machines, and equipment that may present a risk to life or property.
* Systems that require a high degree of reliability, such as systems that supply gas, water, or electricity, or systems that operate continuously 24 hours a day.
* Other systems that require a similar high degree of safety.

# Setting Procedure of the Circular Tracking

## Outline

This section describes the outline of how to set up the circular tracking.

### (1) Selecting a Hardware

In this step, execute various settings of hardware.  
- Selecting the conveyors and devices  
- Setting of the encoder joint number  
- I/O setting

### (2) Hardware Connection Confirmation

In this step, execute Joint and I/O setting confirmation.

### (3) Calibration

Calibration measures the exact positional relationship between the turntable, sensor (vision sensor), and robot.

## Detailed Procedure

Detailed setting procedures are different for sensor tracking and for vision tracking.   
For details about the sensor tracking, refer to "[Setup of the Sensor Tracking](002868.html)".  
For details about the vision tracking, refer to "[Setup of the Vision Tracking System](002880.html)".

## Adding the Circular Tracking Function to the Existing Robot Controller

When adding the circular tracking function to the existing robot controller, the license of the circular tracking function and the encoder hub are necessary.

Please contact your [DENSO representative](001077.html) for more details.

When adding the circular tracking function to the robot controller, customers need to change the project data of the robot controller to the project for extended-joint.

In that case, please perform the procedure below.

### Procedure to Change to the Project Data for Extended-joint

With WINCAPSIII, after getting data from the robot controller and changing to the project for extended-joint, send data to the robot controller.

###### 1

Use WINCAPSIII.

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path：[File] - [New Project] |

Select "Get information from the controller for creating a new project.", create data.

For details, refer to "[Creating a New Project](004403.html)".

###### 2

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path：[Project] - [Property] |

Change to "Use" by [Change] button of "Robot info." tab.

For details, refer to "[Robot](004406.html#ID004406_Robot)" of "Robot info." tab.

###### 3

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path：[Connect] - [Transfer data] |

Select "Local data" of WINCAPSIII and click [Send].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002867_1.png)

When sending is complete, please restart the controller.

# Selecting the Conveyors and Devices

Choose a conveyor number and type of device to be configured.

## Selection Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Tracking Setting Window

Choose [F10 Tracking] from the top window.

To use [F10 Tracking], the license of the circular tracking is required.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002870_1.png)

"Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002870_2.png)

To set the conveyor or to edit the items of the [F12 Detail], the log-in level needs to be the Maintainer or the higher.

###### 2 Displaying the Conveyor Setting Window

Press [Settings].

* Before pressing [Setting], set the "Enabled" on the left side of [Setting] to OFF state. You cannot press [Setting] when the "Enabled" is set to ON state.
* Setting the conveyor to OFF state after executing one of the following commands, the value set by each command is written into the parameter.  
  [TrackStartArea](005490.html), [TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html), [TrackTargetOffset](005493.html), [TrackMinimumIntervalLength](005794.html)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002870_3.png)

###### 3 Setting the Conveyor

Choose [Circular] and press [Next].  
Turntable is selected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002870_4.png)

###### 4 Setting the Device

Choose [Sensor] and press [Next].  
[Sensor] is selected.  
Once pressing [Stop] - [OK], the calibration is canceled, and then the "Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002870_5.png)

This continues to "[Setting of the Encoder Joint Number](002871.html)".

# Calibration

## Outline

Calibration measures the exact positional relationship between the turntable, sensor, and robot.  
The calibration result is stored as the parameter shown below and used when performing the tracking motion.

Each turntable needs to be calibrated respectively.

## Parameters Related to the Positional Relation between Robot and Conveyor

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor CALDATA(X, Y) | Rotating angle around the Z axis of the base coordinate that shows the direction of rotary axis of the turntable [rad] |
| Conveyor CALDATA(Z) | Inclination seen from the XY plane of the base coordinate that shows the direction of rotary axis of the turntable [rad] |
| Conveyor Feed Rate | Amount of turntable movement per one rotation of encoder [deg/rev] |
| Encoder Rotation Direction | Rotational direction of encoder when the turntable is moved from upstream to the downstream (1: Normal, -1: Reverse) |

## Parameters Related to the Positional Relation between Robot and Sensor

Homogeneous transform matrix of [sensor detection position](002856.html#sensorPos) and [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) are stored.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CALDATA（00） | Nx for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（01） | Ox for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（02） | Ax for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（03） | [Sensor detection position](002856.html#sensorPos) X [mm] |
| CALDATA（10） | Ny for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（11） | Oy for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（12） | Ay for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（13） | [Sensor detection position](002856.html#sensorPos) Y [mm] |
| CALDATA（20） | Nz for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（21） | Oz for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（22） | Az for the [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](000458.html) |
| CALDATA（23） | [Sensor detection position](002856.html#sensorPos) Z [mm] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002874_1.png)

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Rx | RX of [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Ry | RY of [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Rz | RZ of [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) [deg] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002874_2.png)

## Parameters Related to the Tracking Range

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Upstream limit of the Tracking range | Once a workpiece passes this limit, a robot starts the [catch-up motion](002856.html#tracking). [mm] |
| Downstream limit of the Tracking range | Once a workpiece reaches this limit, robot stops the [catch-up motion](002856.html#tracking) and starts deceleration. [mm] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002874_3.png)

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate X | Midpoint X between the [calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](002856.html#trackLRangePos) [mm] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Y | Midpoint Y between the [calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](002856.html#trackLRangePos) [mm] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Z | Midpoint Z between the [calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](002856.html#trackLRangePos) [mm] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002874_4.png)

# Calibration Procedure

The following shows a calibration procedure.

###### 1 Confirmation of the Calibration Procedure

After confirming the calibration procedure, press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_1.png)

###### 2 Confirmation of Passing Sensor

Pass through the object to the sensor.  
Check that the encoder value of the [tracking buffer](002856.html#trackBuf) is increased when the workpiece passes through the sensor.  
Once the value is increased, press [Next].

The encoder value at the trigger signal input timing is stored in the [tracking buffer](002856.html#trackBuf).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_2.png)

###### 3 Executing Teaching of Upstream Limit of the Tracking Range

Stop the workpiece at the upper end limit of the tracking range.  
Then move the robot to the workpiece and press
[Get of the upstream limit] to get the robot position.  
Checks the obtained value, and press [Next] if everything is satisfactory.

1. When retrying to get the robot position, a system message is displayed to confirm whether to get the position.
2. The [default posture of holding the work](002856.html#gripBasePosture) can be calculated based on the posture obtained at the time of upstream limit.
3. The height of gripping at the tracking motion is determined by the midpoint of positions obtained at the upstream limit and the downstream limit.

The obtained coordinate values can be changed. To do so, press the edit button on the bottom of the screen. Ten keys are displayed. By the ten keys, change each coordinates values.

The obtained coordinates and encoder values on both of the upstream limit and the downstream limit are used to determine the turntable feed rate and the direction. If you change the coordinate values by the method shown above, keep in mind that the change may affect the turntable feed rate and the direction.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_3.png)

###### 4 Executing Teaching of Passing Point of the Tracking Range

Stop the workpiece on the way to passing point in the tracking range.  
Then move the robot to the workpiece and press [Get position of the passing point] to get the robot position.  
Checks the obtained value, and press [Next] if everything is satisfactory.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_4.png)

###### 5 Executing Teaching of Downstream Limit of the Tracking Range

Stop the workpiece at the lower end limit of the tracking range.  
Then move the robot to the workpiece and press [Get position of the downstream limit] to get the robot position.  
Checks the obtained value, and press [Next] if everything is satisfactory.

The midpoint between the upstream limit position and downstream limit position is the [conveyor reference position](002856.html#conveyorBase).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_5.png)

###### 6 Confirmation of the Calibration Result

Check the calculated parameters, and press [Finish] if everything is satisfactory.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_6.png)

###### 7 Applying the Calibration Result

A system message is displayed to confirm whether to set the calculated data to the controller. Press [OK] if everything is satisfactory.  
Calculated data is set to the controller.  
The setting change is not confirmed if [Cancel] is pressed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_7.png)

The setting change is confirmed and returns to the "Tracking" window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002875_8.png)

For the installation for one turntable and one robot, this is the end of the setup.

# Confirmation of the Calibration Result

This section describes how to check the calibration result; obtain the current position of a work-piece by TrackCurPos command, move the robot manually by variables, check that the robot arm moves to the teaching position above the work-piece at the calibration.

## Procedure of the Calibration Result

The sample program below confirms that the robot arm moves above the workpiece; execute the program to provide workpieces from the upstream of the sensor, stop the workpieces between the upstream limit and the downstream limit of the tracking, turn on IO[128] to stop the program, move to P[13] by variables

###### 1

Execute the program below.

```
'TITLE "Get and evaluate the current position by conveyor tracking commands"

Sub Main

	Takearm Keep = 0
    
	Trackinitialize 1,0	
    
	Wait IO[48] = OFF		'Move the turntable to pass 
					'the workpiece through the sensor.
	Wait IO[48]			'IO[48]:Number of the sensor IO   
    
	TrackSetSensor 1,1,2
    
	P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1)
    	
	'Move the turntable to stop the workpiece between 
	'the upstream limit and the downstream limit.
    
	Wait IO[128] = OFF		'Get the current position of 
	Wait IO[128]			'the workpiece at the timing of 
					'turning on the dummy IO[128]
			
	
	P[13] = TrackCurPos(1)		'The current position of 
					'the workpiece is stored in P[13].  
    
End sub
```

###### 2

Turn on the dummy IO[128].

###### 3

Move to P[13] by variables. Check that the robot arm moves above the work-piece.

# Parameter Setting

This section describes the parameter setting procedure.

## Parameter Setting Procedure

###### 1 Displaying Detail Setting Window

Press [F12 Detail] on the "Tracking" window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002877_1.png)

Conveyor Tracking window is displayed.

###### 2 Selecting Setting Item

Select an item to set, then press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002877_2.png)

###### 3 Changing Setting Value

Input parameters with the numeric keypad, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002877_3.png)

## Parameter List

The parameters described in the table below are not configured automatically in the Detail window.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Tracking Start Range | Refer to the corresponding item of "[Terminology and Definitions](002856.html#ofstMargin)".   Enter a negative value to offset to the upstream direction. |
| Minimum Interval between workpieces (sensor) | This is a threshold value which prevents duplicate data of the work that already exits in the [tracking buffer](002856.html#trackBuf) from being registered by TrackSetSensor command. |
| Low pass filter TC for conveyor pulse | This controls a sudden fluctuation of value by filtering the input value form the encoder.  Setting a value too high lowers the responsiveness to the fluctuation of input value. |
| speed proportional gain | Use this parameter when catch up accuracy of robot deteriorates when the speed of turntable is increased.   When the robot cannot catch up the workpiece, set this value higher than 1.   When the robot overpasses the workpiece, set this value lower than 1. |
| Stationary deviation compensation | Use this parameter when the robot catches up the workpiece always with a certain amount of shift.   Specify the value with a positive value [mm] when the robot cannot catch up the workpiece.   Specify the value with a negative value [mm] when the robot overpasses the workpiece.  If the stationary deviation compensation is set to a large positive value, the robot may move at a speed faster than the specified external speed to catch up with the conveyor. |

# Setup Procedure when Operating with N Turntables

If you operate with N (2 to 16) turntable, setup the second and following turntables in the same way as with the first turntable.

Depending on the number of slave controllers and turntables, sufficient performance may not be obtained because of the performance of the master controller's CPU.
In that case, reduce the number of slave controllers and turntables and split the system to lower the load on the master controller's CPU.
Alternatively, consider to use a controller with a higher specification CPU as the master controller.

###### 1　Selecting the Conveyor Number

On the "Tracking" window, select the tab, where the used conveyor number is displayed, from the conveyor number tabs display at the top of the screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002878_1.png)

###### 2　Setting Up the Conveyor

Press [Setting] button of the "Conveyor N".  
Setup the "Conveyor 2" with same procedure as the "Conveyor 1".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002878_2.png)

The following steps are the same as the installation for one turntable and one robot.  
See "[Selecting a Hardware](002869.html)", "[Hardware Connection Confirmation](002873.html)", "[Calibration](002874.html)".

# Setup Procedure when Operating with Two or More Robots

If you operate with two or more robots, you need to setup both a master controller and a slave controller, respectively.

* For the calibration of the circular tracking, perform in order of the master controller, the slave controller.
* Check that [the joint setting](004936.html) of the slave controller is set to "Disable". If not, change the setting.
* Depending on the number of slave controllers and turntables, sufficient performance may not be obtained because of the performance of the master controller's CPU.
  In that case, reduce the number of slave controllers and turntables and split the system to lower the load on the master controller's CPU.
  Alternatively, consider to use a controller with a higher specification CPU as the master controller.

## Setting Procedure for Using an Additional LAN Board

To use an additional LAN board for communication between the master-slave controllers, you need to change the "Multicast. I/F [IP Address]" parameter from the default value. For details, refer to ["Communication between Master and Slave by Using Additional LAN Board"](018028.html).

## Setting Procedure for the Master Controller

###### 1 Displaying the [Master/Slave] window

On the "Tracking" window, press "Master/Slave" for the turntable which should be set as a slave.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_1.png)

[Master/Slave] window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_2.png)

###### 2 Setting the Slave Count

Press [Slave Count].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_3.png)

[Slave Count] window is displayed.

Enter the number of slave, and then press [OK].

This example assumes that three slaves are used.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_4.png)

###### 3 Setting the IP Address of Slaves

From the "Slave IP address" selection, press [Slave1].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_5.png)

To select different slave address, use up and down allow keys.

[Slave IP address] is displayed.

Enter the I/P address of the slave controller using numeric keypad, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_6.png)

Enter all slave controller's IP addresses by repeating Step 3.

###### 4 Applying the Setting

Once master controller's settings are complete, press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_7.png)

When system message is displayed, press [OK] if everything is satisfactory.  
To discard the new settings, press [Cancel].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_8.png)

The setting change is confirmed and "Tracking" window is displayed.

###### 5 Setting Up the Turntable

Press [Setting] button of the "Conveyor 1" to setup.  
The following steps are the same as the installation for one turntable and one robot.

See "[Selecting a Hardware](002869.html)", "[Hardware Connection Confirmation](002873.html)", "[Calibration](002874.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_9.png)

## Setting Procedure for the Slave Controller

###### 1 Displaying the [Master/Slave] window

On the "Tracking" window, press "Master/Slave" for the turntable which should be set as master.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_1.png)

[Master/Slave] window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_11.png)

###### 2 Setting the IP Address of Master

Press [Slave].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_12.png)

[Slave setting] window is displayed.

Press [Master IP address].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_13.png)

[Master IP address] is displayed.

Enter the I/P address of the master controller using numeric keypad, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_14.png)

###### 3 Set the Master Robot Number

Specify the robot number. This operation is available in Ver.2.7.\* or higher.

When you use the dual arm control function, to set a dual arm-controlled robot as a master, enter the robot number that you want to run as a master of the conveyor tracking operation. If the dual arm control function is not used, leave this entry as 0.

To change the entry, touch the number on the right of the [Master Robot Number] on the window.

The conveyor tracking operation for the dual arm control function is supported from Ver.2.8.\*.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_21.png)

Once the [Master Robot Number] window appears, enter a number and press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_22.png)

###### 4 Applying the Setting

Once all item's settings are complete, press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_15.png)

When system message is displayed, press [OK] if everything is satisfactory.  
To discard the new settings, press [Cancel].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_16.png)

The setting change is confirmed and "Tracking" window is displayed.

Check the system message then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_17.png)

###### 5 Switching to CAL the Slave (Run mode)

This operation is required if your robot controller version is lower than 2.7.\*.

Start the [CAL the Slave (Run mode)] in the master controller.  
Operation route: Top screen- [F10 Tracking] - [F4 CAL the Slave (Run mode)].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_20.png)

Do not operate the master controller during slave controller calibration.

###### 6 Checking Connection with Master Controller

Press [Setting] on "Tracking" window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_18.png)

Conveyor setting window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_19.png)

Start the turntable then check whether the value of [Current encoder value], [Data buffer]changes properly. If the value changes, the setting is normal.

The "data buffer" in this context represents a "tracking buffer".

###### 7 Setting Up the Turntable

The following steps are the same as the installation for one turntable and one robot.  
See "[Selecting a Hardware](002869.html)", "[Hardware Connection Confirmation](002873.html)", "[Calibration](002874.html)".

###### 8 Terminating the CAL the Slave (Run Mode)

This operation is required if your robot controller version is lower than 2.7.\*.

After calibration is complete, press [Exit Mode] of the master controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002879_20.png)

## If You Use a Robot which was Used as Slave for a Master Robot.

You need to change the following items if you use a robot which was used as slave for a master robot.

* Connecting to the encoder for circular tracking
* Connecting to the I/O connector of the trigger signal
* Because the encoder of the circular tracking is not in use, select [Enable encoder only] to use the encoder.
* Because the robot is set as a slave, change it to a master.

## If You do not Use a Slave Robot

If the system includes multiple robots but some of these robots are unused, delete unused robots from the slave list which has set by the master robot.  
If robots fail to chuck a workpiece on the turntable, the data of the workpiece is stored in the memory in the master robot. As stored data accumulates, the speed of calculation to assign robots to workpieces will be longer. As a result, the chuck start timing of the robot will be delayed.

This section describes the setup procedure for a system which includes one robot and one turntable.

# Selecting the Conveyors and Devices

Choose a conveyor number and type of device to be configured.

## Selection Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Tracking Setting Window

Choose [F10 Tracking] from the top window.

To use [F10 Tracking], the license of the circular tracking is required.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002882_1.png)

"Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002882_2.png)

To set the conveyor or to edit the items of the [F12 Detail], the log-in level needs to be the Maintainer or the higher.

###### 2 Displaying the Conveyor Setting Window

Press [Settings].

* Before pressing [Setting], set the "Enabled" on the left side of [Setting] to OFF state. You cannot press [Setting] when the "Enabled" is set to ON state.
* Setting the conveyor to OFF state after executing one of the following commands, the value set by each command is written into the parameter.  
  [TrackStartArea](005490.html), [TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html), [TrackTargetOffset](005493.html), [TrackMinimumIntervalLength](005794.html)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002882_3.png)

###### 3 Setting the Conveyor

Choose [circular] and press [Next].  
Turntable is selected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002882_4.png)

###### 4 Setting the Device

Choose [Vision] and press [Next].  
[Vision] is selected.  
Once pressing [Stop] - [OK], the calibration is canceled, and then the "Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002882_5.png)

This continues to "[Setting of the Encoder Joint Number](002883.html)".

# I/O Setting

This section describes how to set the I/O port number that is connected to the sensor detecting workpiece, and the edge type.

###### 1 Displaying the Number Selection Window

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Rising edge | To detect a workpiece at the rising edge |
| Falling edge | To detect a workpiece at the falling edge |
| Rising and Falling | To detect a workpiece at the rising edge and falling edge |

# Hardware Connection Confirmation

This section describes the hardware connection confirmation methods of the vision tracking system.

## Joint and I/O Setting Confirmation

This section describes how to confirm the encoder connection and the trigger detection.

###### 1 Checking Encoder Connection

Press [Check connected] button to enable the conveyor.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002885_1.png)

Operate the turntable then check whether the value of [Current encoder value] changes properly.

Press [Next].

The "data buffer" in this context represents a "[tracking buffer](002856.html#trackBuf)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002885_3.png)

If [Data buffer] does not change, press [F1 Start trigger detection].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002885_4.png)
