# Programming for the Dual Arm Control Function-Used Operation

The following describes the programming information in three sections.

* [Programming Examples of the Sensor Tracking](#ID003414_SensorTracking)
* [Programming Examples of the Vision Tracking](#ID003414_VisionTracking)
* [Other Programming Example](#ID003414_Others)

## Programming Examples of the Sensor Tracking

Now we will explain the program for the following system. The size of workpiece shall be less than the tracking range.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003414_1.png)

The following figure shows the overall configuration of the expected system.

(File names used in the following image are samples. You can give any names.)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003414_2.png)

The following table contains the sample program file and description of each program.

There are two prerequisites.

* Conveyor number should be 1.
* Trigger signal from the sensor is connected to the I/O port #48 and the signal is detected at the rising edge.

| Program name  (Sample program) | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [SensorTracking.pcs (PCS:338B)](img/003414/SensorTracking.pcs) | This program initializes the conveyor tracking system and executes three other programs.  Initialization is done for both Robot0 and Robot1.  There are two ways to specify a robot name (Robot0 / Robot1) for a command. In the sample program, "Robot0." or "Robot1." are entered in front of the initialization command "TrackInitialize". |
| [Sensor.pcs (PCS:2KB)](img/003414/Sensor.pcs) | This program detects workpiece positions and registers the obtained data into tracking buffer.  In this example, Robot0 is a master. Workpiece registration into the tracking buffer must be done for the master (in this case, Robot0). Therefore, this program is written as Robot0 program.  In the sample program, the following line is added in front of the program to specify that the program is written for Robot0. ```` ```   #Pragma Optimize ("DefaultRobot", 0) ``` ```` |
| [TrackingRob0.pcs (PCS:2KB)](img/003414/TrackingRob0.pcs) | This program reads positional data of the workpiece from the tracking buffer area, and orders Robot0 to execute tracking and picking up operation by use of obtained positional data.  In the sample program, the following line is added in front of the program to specify that the program is written for Robot0. ```` ```   #Pragma Optimize ("DefaultRobot", 0) ``` ```` |
| [TrackingRob1.pcs (PCS:2KB)](img/003414/TrackingRob1.pcs) | This program reads positional data of the workpiece from the tracking buffer area, and orders Robot1 to execute tracking and picking up operation by use of obtained positional data.  In the sample program, the following line is added in front of the program to specify that the program is written for Robot1. ```` ```   #Pragma Optimize ("DefaultRobot", 1) ``` ```` |

For information about how to specify the robot name (Robot0 / Robot1), refer to ["Data Registration to the Tracking Buffer" in "Basic Knowledge (The Concept of Master and Slave)"](003410.html#ID003410_RegisterInBuffer).

## Programming Examples of the Vision Tracking

Now we will explain the program for the following system. The size of workpiece shall be less than the tracking range.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003414_3.png)

The following figure shows the overall configuration of the expected system.

(File names used in the following image are samples. You can give any names.)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003414_4.png)

The following table contains the sample program file and description of each program.

There are two prerequisites.

* Conveyor number should be 1.

| Program name  (Sample program) | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [VisionTracking.pcs (PCS:337B)](img/003414/VisionTracking.pcs) | This program initializes the conveyor tracking system and executes three other programs.  Initialization is done for both Robot0 and Robot1.  There are two ways to specify a robot name (Robot0 / Robot1) for a command. In the sample program, "Robot0." or "Robot1." are entered in front of the initialization command "TrackInitialize". |
| [Vision.pcs (PCS:4KB)](img/003414/Vision.pcs) | This program detects workpiece positions and registers the obtained data into tracking buffer.  Workpiece registration into the tracking buffer must be done for the master. In this example, Robot0 is a master. Workpiece registration into the tracking buffer must be done for the master (in this case, Robot0). Therefore, this program is written as Robot0 program.  In the sample program, the following line is added in front of the program to specify that the program is written for Robot0. ```` ```   #Pragma Optimize ("DefaultRobot", 0) ``` ```` |
| [TrackingRob0.pcs (PCS:2KB)](img/003414/TrackingRob0.pcs) | This program reads positional data of the workpiece from the tracking buffer area, and orders Robot0 to execute tracking and picking up operation by use of obtained positional data.  In the sample program, the following line is added in front of the program to specify that the program is written for Robot0. ```` ```   #Pragma Optimize ("DefaultRobot", 0) ``` ```` |
| [TrackingRob1.pcs (PCS:2KB)](img/003414/TrackingRob1.pcs) | This program reads positional data of the workpiece from the tracking buffer area, and orders Robot1 to execute tracking and picking up operation by use of obtained positional data.  In the sample program, the following line is added in front of the program to specify that the program is written for Robot1. ```` ```   #Pragma Optimize ("DefaultRobot", 1) ``` ```` |

For information about how to specify the robot name (Robot0 / Robot1), refer to ["Data Registration to the Tracking Buffer" in "Basic Knowledge (The Concept of Master and Slave)"](018026.html#ID003410_RegisterInBuffer).

## Other Programming Example

As programming example of conveyor tracking operation, we offer ["Sample Program for a Workpiece whose Length is Over the Tracking Range"](002223.html) and ["Programming Examples of Free Curve Interpolation during Tracking"](002980.html). These sample programs are created for operations with one robot. However, you can partly reuse them by specifying Robot0 and/or Robot1. Refer to other content stored in the lower layer of ["Programming"](005364.html).

# Overview

The robot protective jacket set for food processing is optional equipment that consists of a sanitary-minded jacket ("robot jacket" hereinafter) designed for food factory robots and accessories for putting the robot jacket on the robot.

Just installing the robot protective jacket for food processing on the robot prevents liquid from attaching to the robot unit.

Cleaning and sterilizing the robot jacket before starting the robot also allows hygienic robot operation.

## Supported Robot Types

The robot protective jacket set for food processing can be used for the following robots:

* VS-068
* VS-087

However, it cannot be used for the following specifications and type:

* Communication flange-A
* UL specification
* Clean type

## Installing the Set on the Robot

The robot protective jacket set for food processing needs to be installed on the robot by the customer. For how to install the set, refer to the corresponding section in this manual.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003417_1.png)

## How to Put the Robot Jacket On

There are the following two methods to put the robot jacket on near the robot installation surface.

|  |
| --- |
| Prioritizing the Easiness of Putting On/Taking Off   This method prioritizes the easiness of putting the robot jacket on or taking it off.  The mount is not included in the robot protective jacket set for food processing. |
| Prioritizing the Protectiveness   This method prioritizes the protectiveness against contaminants near the robot installation surface.  To use this method, a dedicated plate needs to be created separately. For details, refer to "[Bottom-raising Plate for the Robot](003422.html#ID003422_cradle)".  The mount is not included in the robot protective jacket set for food processing. |

For how to clean and sterilize the robot jacket, refer to "[Cleaning/Sterilization and Maintenance](003427.html)".

The robot specifications (Example: Robot workable space) are different between before and after putting the robot jacket on. Check the following appropriate reference before use:

* VS-068: "[Specifications of VS-068 with the Robot Jacket On](003419.html)"
* VS-087: "[Specifications of VS-087 the with the Robot Jacket On](003449.html)"

# Specifications of VS-068 with the Robot Jacket On

Check the following specifications of the robot with the robot jacket on and use the robot within the allowable ranges.

| Item | Specification |
| --- | --- |
| With robot jacket on |
| Overall arm length  (to end-effector mounting face) | 340 (first arm) + 340 (second arm) + 150 (to end-effector mounting face) = 830 mm |
| Operation angle | J1: +/-120° (\*1)  J2: +90°, -70°  J3: +140°, -20°  J4: +/-90°  J5: +110, -100°  J6: +/-240° |
| Outer dimensions and workable space | Refer to [this link (PDF:653KB)](img/003419/003419_1.pdf). |
| Maximum payload | 6 kg |
| Maximum allowable inertia   (inertia moment) | Around J4 and J5: 0.440 kgm2  Around J6: 0.100 kgm2 |
| Maximum allowable moment | Around J4 and J5: 14.4 Nm  Around J6: 6.69 Nm |
| Number of available signal line and air piping solenoid valves for 2nd arm | Signal line: 10 (CN21) (no single line allowed, one cable with the outer jacket diameter: φ6.5 to 8 mm)   Air pipe: Up to 6 (\*2) |
| Installation direction | Placed on floor |
| Weight | Approx. 50 kg (Approx. 110 lb) |

Specifications other than the above are the same as before putting the jacket on.

(\*1) This is the workable space for an all-axis-combined operation. Meanwhile, a single axis operation runs within the standard workable space, except for J5.

(\*2) The total number of signal lines and air pipes that can be guided outside the robot jacket is six.

* In a combined operation, the robot may not run due to interference from the robot jacket.
* When the robot jacket is put on the robot, the temperature of the robot unit is more likely to rise than usual.

# Precautions for Use

This section describes the precautions for use according to the following categories.

Note the following when using the robot protective jacket set for food processing:

* [Precautions When Using the Robot Jacket](#ID003420_usagenotes)
* [Conditions for Designing the End-effectors](#ID003420_deconditions)
* [Cleaning and Sterilizing the Robot Protective Jacket When the End-effector Is Removed](#ID003420_removal)

## Precautions When Using the Robot Jacket

| Precaution | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Guide for replacement | The robot jacket is expendable. It is recommended that it should be replaced after about one year of use. Also, check the robot jacket periodically and replace it if any scratch, tear, or fraying is found.  \* The robot jacket is warranted only during a period from taking it out of the package to putting it on the robot. |
| Notes on putting on/taking off | * Be sure to turn off the robot controller before putting the jacket on or taking it off. * Do not expose the robot jacket to any strong impact or friction. Otherwise, it may be damaged sooner. * Be careful when taking the robot jacket off because the robot unit surface may be extremely hot right after stopping. Wait for a certain period of time before taking the robot jacket off after the robot stops. * Wipe grease off the outer surface with alcohol before installing the flange. |
| Precautions for use | * Avoid using the robot in a way that intentionally brings food into contact with the robot jacket. * When the robot jacket is put on the robot, the temperature of the robot unit is more likely to rise, causing an overload error. In such a case, change the operation, such as slowing down the robot. * Do not apply external force of 5 kgf directly to the robot jacket. Otherwise, the service life of the jacket may be shortened. * Do not put the robot jacket on any other robot than those supported by DENSO. * With the robot jacket on, the shape of the robot is difficult to see. Check the posture of the robot with TP before teaching. |
| Storage | * Store the robot jacket in a cold, dark place without high temperature and humidity. |
| Others | * Take the robot jacket off before performing the following operations:     |  |   | --- |   | - Moving the robot |   | - Replacing the encoder backup battery |   | - Changing the mechanical end | * Take the robot jacket off and remove the robot jacket mounting flange from the robot before performing CALSET |

## Conditions for Designing the End-effectors

Note the following when designing the end-effectors:

* Maximum payload, maximum allowable inertia (inertia moment)

  The following table shows the specifications of each robot with the protective jacket on.

  | Item | VS-068 | VS-087 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Maximum payload | 6 kg | |
  | Maximum allowable inertia (inertia moment) | Around J4 and J5: 0.440 kgm2  Around J6: 0.100 kgm2 | |

  Make sure to stay within the allowable ranges indicated above.

  In calculation for an end-effector design, take into account not only an end-effector but also all loads to be applied to the flange such as workpieces, wiring, and piping. Design an end-effector (including workpieces) so that it does not vibrate.

  When calculating the mass of the loads to be applied to the flange such as the end-effector and workpieces, add the mass (0.7 kg) of the robot mounting flange to the value.

  For example, when the mass of the end-effector is 3.0 kg and the mass of any other object than the end-effector, such as workpieces, is 0.2 kg, the total mass of the load to be applied to the flange will be as follows:

  |  |
  | --- |
  | 3.0 kg + 0.2 kg + 0.7 kg = 3.9 kg |

  If the end-effector design requirements are not met, the clamped sections of the robot unit may become loose, rattle or get out of position. In the worst case, the mechanical parts of the robot and the controller may become damaged.

  The graph below shows the distribution of the center of gravity position of an end-effector (including workpieces) whose volume is relatively small.

  Referring to the graph, design an end-effector.

  ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003420_1.png)
* Position of the tool

  Installing the robot jacket mounting flange moves the end-effector mounting face by 70 mm in the approach vector direction.

  When setting the tool, add 70 mm to the approach vector direction.
* Conditions for the end-effector mounting face (in an environment where water drops may fall near the end-effector)

  The outer dimensions of the mounting face on the end-effector must have a diameter of 59 mm or more so that the circumference of the O-ring for the robot jacket mounting flange-A can be crushed.

  Set the roughness of the contact surface with the O-ring on the end-effector to Rz 6.3 (Ra 1.6). Make sure that feed machining is not performed for the contact finish. If the conditions are not met, water drops may enter the robot jacket, causing damage to the robot unit.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003420_2.png)

* If the diameter of the end-effector is larger than 70mm, when you lay the user wiring and piping through the cable gland, pay attention to the bending radius. In this case, because the end-effector is large, passing the user wiring and piping straight through the cable gland will hit the end effector. To by-pass the end-effector, the wiring and piping need to be bent.

  If the bending radius of the wiring and piping are too small, it may be damaged or lead to loss of performance. To avoid that, ensure buffer space between the end-effector and the cable ground to provide sufficient bending radius to the user wiring and piping.

  For details, refer to "[Notes on End-effector Dimensions (PDF:215KB)](img/003420/003420_5.pdf)".

## Cleaning and Sterilizing the Robot Protective Jacket When the End-effector Is Removed

When washing and sterilizing the removed end-effector, be sure to attach the washing protective cover as shown in the figure below because liquid may enter the inside without the cover.

Make sure that the O-ring is installed on the robot jacket mounting flange-A before attaching the washing protective cover.

The washing protective cover is sold as an option (Part number: 410389-317\*).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003420_3.png)

There are positioning holes for the washing protective cover on the contact surface with the robot jacket mounting flange-A. Attach the washing protective cover while aligning with the positioning holes on the robot jacket mounting flange-A.

* To wash the robot jacket when it is put on the robot, be sure to clean it with wiping.
* Do not use the washing protective cover for any other purpose than washing.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003420_4.png)

# Installing Procedures for the Robot Jacket, Signal Lines, and Air Pipes

Before transporting or installing the robot, be sure to read "[Installation Precautions](001928.html)" in "SAFETY PRECAUTIONS", as well as this section.

## Preparing for Installation

Before installing this robot protective jacket for food processing, check "[Items Contained in the Robot Jacket Set](003421.html)" and place necessary parts within reach of your hand.

The installing procedures for the robot jacket are described in the order shown in the following table:

| Workflow  (Reference) | Overview |
| --- | --- |
| [Installing the Flange](003423.html) | Install the flange for the robot protective jacket for food processing on the robot unit. |
| [Signal Lines, Guides, and Wires](003424.html) | Attach the cover and guides to protect the end-effector signal lines and air pipes.  Fix the end-effector signal lines and air pipes to the jacket flange through the cable ground. |
| [Putting the Jacket On](003425.html) | Put the robot protective jacket for food processing on the robot unit. |
| [Tightening near the Robot Base](003426.html) | Use the accompanied band to tighten the jacket near the robot base or install a bottom-raising plate according to the purpose. |

## Bottom-raising Plate for the Robot

To prevent dust from entering from the robot base, a bottom-raising plate needs to be installed between the robot and the mount (prepared by the customer) as shown in the figure below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003422_1.png)

A bottom-raising plate requires robot mounting bolt holes and a dowel pin hole.

Machine the plate in the correct size according to the following bottom-raising plate drawing and robot jacket fixing plate drawing:

* [Bottom-raising Plate Drawing (PDF:324KB)](img/003422/003422_2.pdf)
* [Robot Jacket Fixing Plate Drawing (PDF:1,332KB)](img/003422/003422_3.pdf)

# Installing the Flange

###### 1

Install the flange for the robot protective jacket for food processing on the robot unit.

Setting the posture with the following axis angles makes it easier to install the flange.

| Axis | Angle | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| J1 | 0° |  |
| J2 | 0° |
| J3 | 90° |
| J4 | 0° |
| J5 | -90° |
| J6 | 0° |

###### 2

For the standard type robot, fix the 6th-axis cross roller protective cover to the 6th-axis.

This step is unnecessary for the splash-proof type robot.

Use the accompanied cross screws (M3x10) to attach the cover.

* Mounting screw size: M3x10
* Screw tightening torque: 0.59 Nm +/-20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003423_2.png)

Without the protective cover, the jacket or wiring may be damaged depending on the robot motion, resulting in a shorter service life.

###### 3

Fix the robot jacket mounting flange-B with the accompanied bolts and dowel pin.

The bolt size and tightening torque are as follows:

* Mounting bolt size: M5x40 mm
* Bolt tightening torque: 5.9 Nm +/-20%

Wipe grease off the outer surface with alcohol before installing the flange.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003423_3.png)

###### 4

Fix the robot jacket mounting flange-A with the accompanied bolts.

The bolt size and tightening torque are as follows:

* Mounting bolt size: M5x30 mm
* Bolt tightening torque: 5.2 Nm +/-20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003423_4.png)

There is a seal (rubber) attached on the back of the flange-A, which is used to bring the flange-A into full contact with the flange-B.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003423_5.png)

Install the flange-A straight onto the mounting face of the flange-B as shown in the above STEP 3 so that the seal (rubber) on the back of the flange-A is not crushed.

###### 5

Install the O-ring on the flange-A. (In case of an environment where water drops may fall near the end-effector)

Set the roughness of the contact surface with the O-ring to Rz 6.3 (Ra 1.6). Make sure that feed machining is not performed for the contact finish. If the conditions are not met, washing the robot jacket when it is put on the robot with liquid, such as detergent, may cause the liquid to penetrate the jacket.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003423_6.png)

# Signal Lines, Guides, and Wires

###### 1

Attach the cover to protect the end-effector signal lines and pipe connector to the robot's second arm.

When using the signal line connector CN21 or the robot's built-in valve on the second arm, install an air pipe joint or dedicated connector before attaching the protective cover to prevent the robot jacket from being rubbed against the protrusions.

For details on the signal lines and connectors, refer to "[Signal Lines & Air Piping·](000027.html)" in the robot manual.

The bolt size and tightening torque are as follows:

* Mounting bolt size: M3x8 mm
* Screw tightening torque: 1.6 Nm +/-20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003424_1.png)

Even when the connector CN21 or the robot's built-in valve is not used, attach the protective cover to prevent the robot jacket from being rubbed against the protrusions.

###### 2

Install the guides to protect wiring and piping on the second arm of the robot unit.

To install the guides, remove the cross screws fastened on the second arm cover.

After removing the screws, fix the end-effector signal line and air piping guides with the accompanied cross screws (M3x16 size) as shown in the figure below.

Install the guide engraved as "R" on the right side and the guide engraved as "L" on the left side viewed from the robot.

The bolt size and tightening torque are as follows:

* Mounting bolt size: M3x16 mm
* Screw tightening torque: 0.59 Nm +/-20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003424_2.png)

Even when wiring and piping are not used, be sure to install the guides to prevent the robot jacket from being rubbed against the bolt protrusions.

###### 3

Install the appropriate cable ground on the jacket flange according to the signal line and piping to be used as shown in the table below.

Fill an unused cable ground hole with a seal plug.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003424_3.png)

For the cable ground types and conditions, refer to the following table.

| Condition | Wiring and piping are used | | Wiring and piping are not used | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Type | Wiring and piping diameter  φ5 - φ8 mm | Wiring and piping diameter  φ3 - φ5 mm | Normal | Thin head (\*1) |
| Part number | Cable ground 1  410887-027\* | Cable ground 2  410887-026\* | Cable ground 1  410887-027\*＆  seal plug 1  410915-021\*  or  cable ground 2  410887-026\*＆  seal plug 2  410915-020\* | 410915-023\* |
| Seal inner diameter | φ8 | φ5 | - | - |
| Cable ground main unit  (tightening torque) | 1.0 - 1.5 Nm | | | 19.2 Nm +/-10% |
| Seal nut  (tightening torque) | 0.8 - 1.2 Nm | | | - |
| Appearance color | Black | | | Silver |

(\*1) To prevent interference from the end-effector caused by a normal seal plug, select a thin head seal plug instead.

* Select a cable ground with an inner diameter appropriate for the lines to be used. Check the inner diameter according to the seal inner part shown in the figure below.
* Wipe grease off fully before installing the cable ground.
* A nut is tightened on the washer of the cable ground, but remove it according to the image below as it is not used in this product. The nut can be removed by turning.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003424_5.png)

###### 4

Put the signal lines and pipes through the cable ground and fix them by tightening the seal nut of the cable ground.

Before attaching the end-effector signal line connector to the cables, put the cables through the cable ground.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003424_4.png)

* Adjust the length of the signal lines and pipes according to your workable space.
* To maximize the workable space, a wiring length of 350 mm or more is required between the connector (pipe joint) and the cable ground seal.

# Putting the Jacket On

###### 1

Put the jacket on the robot. The seams of the jacket must be on the front side of the robot.

Cover the robot from the tip of J6 to the base with the jacket and tighten the tip of the 6th-axis so that the soft fabric inside the jacket is around the flange.

Do not put the jacket on inside out. The side with the washing instruction tag is the inside as shown in the picture.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003425_1.png)

* Do not apply excessive force to the jacket when putting it on the robot.
* If parts prepared by the customer are installed on the robot, take appropriate actions, such as by attaching tape to sharp edges, to prevent damage to the jacket when putting it on. (Example: Wiring/piping plate guide, etc.)

###### 2

Tighten the jacket at the tip of the 6th-axis so that the soft fabric inside the jacket is around the flange.

Fold the hem of the jacket inside before tightening.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003425_2.png)

###### 3

Tighten the jacket at the tip of the axis with the hose clamp.

Set the hose clamp with the screw part at the top.

* Hose clamp tightening torque: 3 Nm +/-20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003425_3.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003425_4.png)

###### 4

The loosen part of the jacket may get in the way depending on the robot motion set by the customer. In such a case, adjust the looseness by tightening the jacket at the robot arm using the accompanied 90-cm band.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003425_5.png)

After putting the jacket on the robot, make sure that it is not torn or damaged before starting the robot.

# Tightening near the Robot Base

Tighten the jacket near the robot base with the accompanied bands.

Be sure to tighten the jacket near the robot base.

There are the following two methods to tighten the jacket, and the robot needs to be fixed to the mount depending on the purpose.

* [When Prioritizing the Easiness of Putting On/Taking Off](#ID003426_simple)
* [When Prioritizing the Protectiveness](#ID003426_dripproof)

## When Prioritizing the Easiness of Putting On/Taking Off

Use the accompanied 146cm band to tighten the jacket at the bottom through the loops on the jacket bottom.

This easy-tightening method saves time when the jacket needs to be put on or taken off easily such as for daily washing.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_1.png)

The following shows how to tighten the jacket at the bottom by fastening the tightening band (146 cm) through the loops on the jacket.

###### 1

Put the jacket bottom tightening band (146 cm) through the four loops on the jacket and fasten the band. The band should be fastened tightly because the jacket bottom moves if the band is loose.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_2.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_3.png)

###### 2

Put the accompanied 60cm jacket tightening band through the loops on the jacket and fasten the band to seal the opening for the motor & encoder cable.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_4.png)

## When Prioritizing the Protectiveness

To prevent dust from entering from the robot base, a bottom-raising plate needs to be installed between the robot and the mount (prepared by the customer), and then the jacket and the bottom-raising plate need to be fixed with the fixing plate.

For the bottom-raising plate and fixing plate, refer to "[Robot and Bottom-raising Plate](003422.html#ID003422_cradle)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_5.png)

The following shows how to fix the jacket by sandwiching the jacket and the bottom-raising plate with the fixing plate.

###### 1

Put the fixing plate through the four loops on the jacket.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_6.png)

###### 2

Fix the plate with bolts while aligning the jacket holes with the fixing plate holes.

The bolt size is as follows:

* Mounting bolt size: M5x30 mm (10 bolts)
* Bolt tightening torque (recommended)  
  - Bolt strength class A-20-70: 3.6 Nm +/-20%  
  - Bolt strength class 10.8: 5.2 Nm +/-20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_7.png)

###### 3

Place the right and left of the jacket on the back of the robot on top of each other by aligning with the bolt holes.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_8.png)

###### 4

Fix the fixing plate to the jacket with the bolts.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_9.png)

###### 5

Put the two accompanied 60cm jacket tightening bands through the loops on the jacket and fasten the band to seal the opening for the motor & encoder cable.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003426_10.png)

# Cleaning/Sterilization and Maintenance

## Cleaning and Sterilization

Note the following when cleaning and sterilizing the robot protective jacket for food processing:

* Use a designated chemical when cleaning or sterilizing the robot jacket according to the table below
* For safety, be sure to turn off the robot controller before cleaning.
* The robot may be extremely hot right after stopping. Wait for a certain period of time before cleaning.
* It is recommended that robot jacket should be first taken off of the robot and then soaked and washed to prevent any missing spots.
* If your environment does not allow the robot jacket to be taken off on a daily basis, clean the jacket with wiping. Cleaning by splashing water over the jacket may cause the water to enter the robot unit.
* It is recommended that sodium hypochlorite should be used for sterilization.  
  Sodium hypochlorite concentration: 200 ppm or less  
  Sodium hypochlorite diluted with acetic acid can be used.
* For sterilization with hot water of 60°C or more, take the robot jacket off of the robot and perform only on the jacket.
  At that time, make sure that hot water is kept off the robot unit.
* After washing or sterilization, be sure to wash the chemical off with water and dry the jacket well before use.
  If the jacket is used with any chemical remaining on, it will deteriorate sooner. Even using it without being dried up causes molds to form and germs to grow. Make sure that the jacket should be dried in the shade.
* If water or chemical liquid ends up penetrating the fabric, replace the jacket.

| Cleaning method | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Soaking and washing  (recommended) | It is recommended that the robot jacket should be soaked and washed for cleaning.  Perform the following steps to clean with soaking and washing:   1. Soaking  Use the following chemical to remove the metal-washable bellows with a full or immersion wash. (\*1)(\*3)   * ethanol (\*2)  2. Hand-washing, rinsing  * Wipe the dirt off with a sponge. * Do not use a washing machine. * Do not rub the jacket with a scrub brush because it may damage the fabric. Also, do not rub the jacket forcibly. * Be sure to wash the chemical off with water.  3. Drying  * Hang the jacket in the shade and dry it naturally. * Do not use a spin-dryer or dryer. * Dry the jacket well to prevent molds from forming. |
| Wiping | If your environment does not allow the robot jacket to be taken off on a daily basis, perform the following steps to wipe the jacket with a chemical for cleaning. Water may penetrate the seams of the jacket. Be careful when wiping with a chemical or wiping with water. Make sure that there are no missing spots left.   1. Prepare the following chemical:  * ethanol (\*2)  2. Wiping with a chemical  * Wipe the jacket with a sponge or dry cloth soaked in the chemical.  Alternatively, spray the chemical over the jacket and wipe it off. * Do not apply excessive force to the jacket when wiping off. * If liquid ends up penetrating the fabric, replace the jacket.  3. Wiping with water  * Wipe the chemical off with a wet cloth. * Do not rub the jacket with a scrub brush because it may damage the fabric. Do not also apply excessive force to the jacket when wiping off.  4. Wiping with a dry cloth, drying  * Wipe off with a dry cloth and dry the jacket. * Dry the jacket well to prevent molds from forming. |
| Sterilization | Periodic sterilization with the following chemical, as well as daily washing, keeps the jacket cleaner.   * Recommended: Sodium hypochlorite (\*2) (diluted with water or acetic acid)    Dilution concentration: 200 ppm or less  \* Do not soak the jacket for 15 minutes or more. |

(\*1) Be careful not to damage the jacket when taking the robot jacket off of the robot.

(\*2) If detergent or disinfectant is used, be sure to check its "SDS (Safety Data Sheet)" and "Precautions for Use".

(\*3) Do not use strong alkaline detergent (above ph11) to clean the flange.

Before use, examine that if the selected chemical do not deteriorate the jacket property, or select a detergent suitable for the following materials.

* Jacket material (synthesized fabric material)

+ Nylon
+ PET
+ Polyurethane

For the detergent and disinfectant, contact your "[DENSO representative](001077.html)".

1. When removing the end-effector and wiping it with detergent, be sure to clean it after installing the O-ring or washing protective cover on the robot jacket mounting flange according to "[Cleaning and Sterilizing the Robot Protective Jacket When the End-effector Is Removed](003420.html#ID003420_removal)". Otherwise, the liquid enters the inside, causing damage to the end-effector. The washing protective cover is sold as an option. (Part number: 410389-317\*)
2. Do not wash the jacket in a washing machine. Do not rub the jacket forcibly when washing with hands.
3. When using an iron, the temperature must be low (up to 100°C).

## Maintenance

### Daily Inspections

Add the following check items to the daily inspections in the robot manual.

| Check: | How to check: | Criterion | What to do: |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Robot jacket | Visually | No scratch, tear, or fraying | Repair or replacement |
| No dirt | Cleaning and sterilization |

Some repair and replacement jobs, shown in "What to do" column, may involve special work. Contact the [DENSO service representative](001078.html).

# Controller Protective Box Light

This manual describes the specifications and usage of the controller protective box Light.

The controller protective box Light is an optional part for the RC8 series robot controller. However, this product cannot be used for some controller models. If your robot system satisfies one of the following conditions, use the conventional ["Controller Protective Box"](003447.html) . Conditions: VM series robot is used; VS-068 robot and extended joint are used together; VS-087 and extended-joint are used together; MC series controller (total motor capacity of 2000 W or higher) is used.

# Specifications

The table below lists the specifications of the controller protective box Light.

| Item | | Specifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applicable controller | | RC8 series robot controller (The controller equipped with an I/O conversion box is also applicable.) \*2 |
| Environmental conditions (Temperature and humidity) | In operation | 0 to 40 ℃, RH 90 % or below  (dew condensation not allowed) |
| In storage or during transportation | -10 to 60 ℃, RH 75 % or below  (dew condensation not allowed) |
| Enclosure | | Equivalent to IP54 |
| Installation Type | | Stand-alone installation, upright installation \*3 |
| Weight (Mass) | | Approx. 18 kg (RC8 series robot controller is not included) |
| Power supply \*1 | Three-phase | AC185-253V (AC200V-7%～AC230V+10%) |
| Single-phase | AC207-253V (AC230V±10%) |
| Heat exchanger | Fans | Internal fan and external fan  External fan: 11938SB-B3N-LAU-0 (Manufactured by Minebea Co.,Ltd)  Internal fan : 11938SB-B3N-JP-00 (Manufactured by Minebea Co.,Ltd) |
| Cooling power | 25 W/K (temperature change 1 ℃ , calculated value) |
| Power supply | Supplied from the controller power and branched by the protective box Light-incorporated terminal.  Power supply capacity: 0.15 KVA |

\*1: The power supply of the controller protective box, unlike that of the controller.

\*2: Not contained in UL-Listed controller.

\*3: When placing the protective box Light in the upright position, please purchase a stand set (option). The stand set supports the protective box Light shipped after July, 2019. For details, refer to "[Upright Installation](003443.html)".

# Precautions for Use

1. The controller protective box Light is a dust- and splash-proof structure equivalent to IP54. However, it has not been designed to withstand explosions, so avoid installing the protective box Light in any environment where:  
   - there are any flammable gases or liquids,  
   - there are any acidic, alkaline or other corrosive gases,  
   - there are any large-sized inverters, high output/high frequency transmitters, large contactors, welders, or other sources of electrical noise,  
   - the ambient temperature is out of the range from 0°C to 40°C,  
   - the protective box Light is directly exposed to rains,  
   - the protective box Light is directly exposed to water, oil, grinding chips or shavings,  
   - there are any grinding or machining chips or shavings.
2. Clean the filter once for two weeks.
3. Sealing performance may degrade due to aging or other reasons. If the sealing performance degrades, tighten the screws on the top plate A and top plate B. In the event of water ingress into the controller protective box Light, remove the drain hall screws to drain water.
4. The controller protective box Light has no power switch, so externally turn the controller power on and off.
5. To reduce the risk of electric shock, observe the following precautions.  
   - Do not supply power from the facilities during wiring, controller connection, and controller disconnection.  
   - Do not open the top plate and the rear cover during energizing.  
   - Do not touch the inside parts within 6 minutes from the power OFF.  
   - Do not touch the power terminals (circled area in the image below) during other than wiring operation.  
   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003441_1.png)
6. Using voltage beyond the specified range may damage the controller protective box Light or reduce the lifetime.
7. If an abnormal temperature is detected, check that whether the internal fan and the external fan of the controller protective box Light works correctly.
8. Fans are installed on the top surface and the inside of the controller protective box Light.   
   To avoid injury, do not insert fingers or any objects into the fans.

# Installation

* Place the protective box Light indoors.
* Place the protective box Light on a horizontal plane.
* Keep a space of at least 150 mm at the top opening of the protective box Light.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003443_1.png)

## Upright Installation

When placing the protective box Light in the upright position, please purchase a stand set (option).

The stand set supports the protective box Light shipped after July, 2019. To check whether the protective box Light supports the stand set, check the part number of the protective box Light.

The part number of the protective box Light is "410181-020\*". Actually, the number is entered in asterisk "\*".

* "1" or larger in "\*" (e.g. Part No. : 410181-0201)  
  The protective box Light was shipped after July, 2019. This supports the stand set.
* "0" in "\*" (Part No. : 410181-0200)  
  The protective box Light was shipped before July, 2019. This does not support the stand set.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003443_5.png)

The protective box Light has screw holes to mount a stand set. There are four screw holes for each side, so customers can choose the side to mount a stand set by customers.

* Stand set (sold separately)

| Parts name | Parts number |
| --- | --- |
| Stand set (RC8 controller protective box Light) | 410349-296\* |

The external dimensions of the protective box Light when using a stand set are shown in the figure below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003443_2.png)

### Installation Procedure

###### 1

Remove four screws of the side to install the protective box Light.

Then, with the rubber washer and the hexagon socket head bolts that come with the stand set, fix the protective box Light and the stand. Put the rubber washer on both side of the stand (refer to the figure below), fix four screw holes (φ6.5) with the hexagon socket head bolts.

Recommended torque : 3N･m

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003443_3.png)

###### 2

Place the protective box Light fixed with the stand to the installation position. As same as the installation in horizontal position, keep a space of at least 150 mm at the top opening of the protective box Light.

Put M8 screws for fixing through the screw holes (φ10), fix with four screws to the floor.

Screws to fix to the floor are not provided. Please prepare the screws by customers.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003443_4.png)

# Preparation of the Power Cable

To connect the power cable shipped with the controller to the controller protective box Light, you need to process cables as shown below.

The power supply of the controller protective box Light, unlike that of the controller, does not support 100V and 240V.

###### 1

Cut the cable at a point about 330 mm from the connector end.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_1.png)

###### 2

Remove the 60 mm of the outer jacket. (2 parts)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_2.png)

###### 3

Remove the 6 mm of outer jackets of each line, then pass the cables through insulation tubes. (8 parts)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_3.png)

###### 4

Attach ring terminals to each end, then move the insulation tubes to the position shown below. (8 parts)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_4.png)

# Storing of the Controller

This section describes the process to store a controller in the controller protective box Light and to connect wires.

Before operation, make sure that there is no power supply from the facilities.

The following uses RC8 standard specification controller as an example.

Recommended torque : M3:0.6N･m, M4:1.5N･m, M5:3N･m

###### 1

To remove the top panel B, unscrew 10 of M4 screws on the top surface.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_1.png)

###### 2

To use 13 or more cables, remove the square plate enclosed in the red dotted circle.

Please purchase rubber packing set for extended-joint cables (option part) separately and install it.

* Rubber Packing Set for Extended-Joint Cables

| Parts name | Parts number |
| --- | --- |
| Rubber packing set for extended-joint cables  (RC8 controller protective box Light) | 410169-291\* |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_2.png)

###### 3

Remove the terminal board cover. Lay prepared power cable with M4 screws as shown below.

For the preparation of cables, see "[Preparation of the power cable](003444.html)".

Once the power cable is laid, put the terminal board cover back in place.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_3.png)

###### 4

As the following figure shows, install the controller support bracket L on the left side of the RC8, and the controller support bracket R on the right side of the RC8, respectively. (Controller support bracket L and R are temporarily installed inside of the controller protective box Light at the shipment.)

Tighten the brackets with M4 screws, marked by six of red circles on the image below.

| Left side of the RC8 | Right side of the RC8 |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

###### 5

Connect the FG harness to the earthing point, marked by red circles (solid line) in the image below.![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_8.png)

The image below shows the standard specification controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_6.png)

###### 6

Tighten four of mounting holes on the bracket with M5 screws.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_7.png)

The image below shows the safety I/O less specification controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_8.png)

###### 7

To use an encoder hub (option part), tighten the encoder hub with four of M4 screws marked by red circles in the image below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_9.png)

###### 8

Pass cables through the holes of multi-outlet plate EMS10 and EMS8M4 (accessory parts) and connect them to the RC8.

For information on how to attach the multi-outlet plates, see "[Clamping the Cables](003446.html)".

###### 9

With an accompanied M4 screw, connect the FG harness, which you have connect in STEP5, to the circle near the terminal board.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003445_10.png)

###### 10

Put the top plate back in place with 10 of M4 screws which was removed in the STEP1.

ID : 3446

# Clamp the Cables

This section describes the process to clamp cables with the multi-outlet plate.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003446_1.png)

###### 1

Install rubber packings in the ditches of the corner plate and the middle plate.

* Rubber Packing Set

| Model | Application cable dia | Application |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EMSP0 | - | To be used as a blind cover |
| EMSP4 | φ4-φ6 | Communication cable |
| EMSP6 | φ6-φ8 | Pendant cable, Hand I/O cable |
| EMSP8 | φ8-φ10 | Mini I/O cable |
| EMSP10 | φ10-φ12 | Extended parallel I/O cable |
| EM28P0 | - | To be used as a blind cover |
| EM28P10 | φ10-φ12 | Power cable |
| EM28P20 | φ20-φ22 | Motor and encoder cable |

* Rubber Packing Set for Extended-Joint Cables

| Parts name | Parts number |
| --- | --- |
| Rubber packing set for extended-joint cables  (RC8 controller protective box Light) | 410169-291\* |

Note the following points when installing the EMS packings on the plates.

* Install the EMS packings in the ditches in order starting from both ends of the ditches to the center. (Figure 1)
* Ensure that the ends of the packing seal strings mounted on the plates are neither lifted up by nor caught in the installed EMS packings. (Figure 2)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003446_2.png)![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003446_3.png)

###### 2

Pass the M5 bolts through the hex holes so that the head of bolts go under the hole.

###### 3

Pass the cables through the holes between the corner plate and the middle plate. Adjust both plates to the vertical direction.

###### 4

Attach the M5 nuts to the M5 bolts.

###### 5

Tighten the corner plate and the middle plate with a spanner until no space remains between the plates.

###### 6

Pass the cables through the holes between the middle plate and the corner plate. Adjust both plates to the vertical direction.

###### 7

Attach M5 nuts to the M5 bolts.

###### 8

Tighten the middle plate and the corner plates with a spanner until no space remains between the plates.

###### 9

Once you finish assembly, pass the cables through the square opening part of the controller protective box Light. Pass the M6 screws through the sealing washer holes. With the M6 screws, tighten the plates from the front side of the protective box.

# Specifications of the Robot Protective Jacket Set for Food Processing

This section describes the specifications according to the following categories.

## Robot Jacket Specifications

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Fabric | * Antibacterial material * Heat resistance: 100°C  (However, use the jacket within the allowable operating temperature range (0 to 40°C) when it is put on the robot.) * Chemical resistance: Sodium hypochlorite and alcohol can be used. |
| Recommended replacement timing | 1 year |
| Warranty | The jacket is warranted only during a period from taking it out of the package to putting it on the robot. |
| Structure | The jacket is designed to be integrated from the top to the base without any joint separation so that liquid runs easily down the surface for easy washing. |
| Washing and sterilization | DetergentDisinfectant The following disinfectant can be used:   * Sodium hypochlorite (with concentration of up to 200 ppm)  Method  * Soaking (recommended)  This requires the robot jacket to be taken off of the robot but allows secure washing and sterilization. * Wiping with chemical  This allows the washing and sterilization of the robot with the robot jacket on. |
| * For the detergent and disinfectant, contact your [DENSO representative](001077.html). * For details on the detergent and disinfectant, refer to "[Cleaning/Sterilization and Maintenance](003427.html)". |

## Accessories

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Packed item | * Robot jacket mounting flange * End-effector wiring guide   For details on the packed items, refer to "[Packed Items](003421.html)". |

## Supported Robots

# Specifications of VS-087 with the Robot Jacket On

Check the following specifications of the robot with the robot jacket on and use the robot within the allowable ranges.

| Item | Specifications |
| --- | --- |
| With robot jacket on |
| Overall arm length (to end-effector mounting face) | 445 (first arm) + 430 (second arm) + 150 (to end-effector mounting face) = 1025 mm |
| Operation angle | J1: +/-120° (\*1)  J2: +90°, -70°  J3: +140°, -20°  J4: +/-90°  J5: +110, -100°  J6: +/-240° |
| Outer dimensions and workable space | Refer to [this link (PDF:601KB)](img/003449/003449_1.pdf). |
| Maximum payload | 6 kg |
| Maximum allowable inertia (inertia moment) | Around J4 and J5: 0.440 kgm2  Around J6: 0.100 kgm2 |
| Maximum allowable moment | Around J4 and J5: 14.4 Nm  Around J6: 6.69 Nm |
| Number of available signal line and air piping solenoid valves for 2nd arm | Signal line: 10 (CN21) (no single line allowed, one cable with the outer jacket diameter: φ6.5 to 8 mm)  Air pipe: Up to 6 (\*2) |
| Installation direction | Placed on floor |
| Weight | Approx. 52 kg (Approx. 115 lb) |

Specifications other than the above are the same as before putting the jacket on.

(\*1) This is the workable space for an all-axis-combined operation. Meanwhile, a single axis operation runs within the standard workable space, except for J5.

(\*2) The total number of signal lines and air pipes that can be guided outside the robot jacket is six.

* In a combined operation, the robot may not run due to interference from the robot jacket.
* When the robot jacket is put on the robot, the temperature of the robot unit is more likely to rise than usual.

# Safety Rules for Robot Protective Jacket Set for Food Processing

Be sure to observe all of the following safety precautions for the robot protective jacket for food processing.

1. To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[Safety Precautions](001924.html)".
2. Be sure to turn off the robot controller before entering the robot workable space for putting the robot jacket on, taking it off, cleaning, or checking for any dirt.
3. Be careful when taking the jacket off of the robot because the robot unit surface may be extremely hot right after stopping. Wait for a certain period of time before taking the robot jacket off after the robot stops.

   To start working with the robot immediately after stopping, wear thick long gloves to prevent direct contact with the robot.
4. When moving the robot, if you hold the robot over the jacket to lift up, the jacket may slip, causing the robot to drop.

   Be sure to take the robot jacket off before moving the robot to another location.
5. Be sure to tighten the robot jacket at the base as well when putting the jacket on the robot to prevent from tumbling over by stepping on the loosed jacket around the robot base.
6. If detergent or disinfectant is used to wash or sterilize the robot jacket, be sure to check its "SDS (Safety Data Sheet)" and "Precautions for Use" for appropriate cleaning. Also, be careful not to be burnt when using hot water.

This section describes an example of a reversal assistance jig required to mount the robot overhead.

Make a reversal assistance jig as shown in the figure below to reverse the HSR series robot for overhead-mount.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003458_1.png)

###### 1

Assemble the part A to H as shown in the figure below. Make each part, referring to the reference drawings shown in the table below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003458_2.png)

| 番号 | 参考図 |
| --- | --- |
| Part A | PLATE （[Reference Drawing(PDF:678KB)](img/003458/003458_a.pdf)） |
| Part B | PLATE （[Reference Drawing(PDF:614KB)](img/003458/003458_b.pdf)） |
| Part C | PLATE （[Reference Drawing(PDF:132KB)](img/003458/003458_c.pdf)） |
| Part D | PLATE （[Reference Drawing(PDF:136KB)](img/003458/003458_d.pdf)） |

# Robot protective jacket set for food processing

The robot protective jacket set for food processing is optional equipment that consists of a sanitary-minded jacket ("robot jacket" hereinafter) designed for food factory robots and accessories for putting the robot jacket on the robot.

Just installing the robot protective jacket for food processing on the robot prevents liquid from attaching to the robot unit.

Cleaning and sterilizing the robot jacket before starting the robot also allows hygienic robot operation.

食Robot protective jacket set for food processing,"[ROBOT PROTECTIVE JACKET SET FOR FOOD PROCESSING USER'S MANUAL of OPTION](003415.html)".

# Executable Token

Executable token is a safety function to permit only one device to execute robot automatic operation. Only a device with the token can perform the following operations necessary for automatic operation.

* Activating the robot program
* Turning the motor ON
* Running the robot (e.g., execute motion commands by b-CAP)

Therefore, robot automatic operation requires the executable token. A device without the token cannot execute automatic operation.

| Setting | Devices supported for automatic operation |
| --- | --- |
| Any | Any device   * Device limitation is not in effect. See the caution below. |
| TP | Teach pendant and Mini Pendant |
| I/O | An external device (a PLC, a computer or others) that executes automatic operation through I/O |
| Ethernet | An external device (a PLC, a computer or others) that executes automatic operation through a LAN |

If an executable token is set to "Any", the control of automatic operation from any device is possible. Take necessary precautions for safety (e.g., let only one device execute automatic operation at one time) when using this setting.

* The factory default is "I/O". Thus, if you activate a robot program with a teach pendant, you need to set the executable token to "TP".
* The executable token setting can be adjusted with a teach pendant or Mini Pendant. For details, refer to "[Displaying and Changing Executable
  Token Setting Screen](001782.html)" (for teach pendant) and "[Executable Token Setting](005081.html)" (for Mini Pendant).
* The executable token setting can be changed only in Manual mode.

# WINCAPSIII Features

WINCAPSIII is software that provides total support for Denso robot operation from the facilities installation through maintenances.  
This software supports the robot operation from every aspect by providing various practical functions; such as creating robot programs, controller data backup, checking the robot posture in 3D display.

# Robot Controller and WINCAPSIII Versions

Use WINCAPSIII whose version is equal to or higher than the robot controller's software version.  
If the version of WINCAPSIII is lower than the robot controller's software version, connection may fail or functions available may be limited.

* If the robot controller's software version is higher than that of WINCAPSIII, upgrade the version of WINCAPSIII by using WINCAPSIII Trial version that is shipped with a new robot set. License will remain. For how to use, refer to [License Certificate (with User ID)](005251.html) in STARTUP MANUAL.
* Match the version of the output code selected in the Project Properties (select Property from the Project menu and use the Compile tab displayed in the dialog box) to that of the robot controller software connected to.

## Operating System

Microsoft Windows 10, 11

## PC

### Memory

4 gigabytes or more

### Hard Disk Drive

2.5 gigabytes or more free space

### Others

Using a graphics card is recommended for displaying 3D data.

# License Certificate and User Registration

## License

DENSO grants you a non-exclusive license to install the Software into one computer in your possession or under your control ("Computer"), and to use the Software for the sole purpose to execute WINCAPSIII ("Purpose").

## Retaining License for Service

The User ID on the license identifies your copy of this product. It is required for after-sales service, so file the license for future reference.

## User Registration

User registration holds the key to our efforts to provide the best possible after-sales service. Registration ensures timely arrival of notification of technical enhancements and upgrade availability. To register as a user, use the web address given on license.

# Types of WINCAPSIII

In addition to the Product version, WINCAPS III is available in two other versions: “WINCAPSIII Trial”, which is included in the robot set, and “WINCAPSIII Light”, which accompanies Mini Pendant.

The following table shows the differences between these versions.

| Function | Product | Light | Trial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create/Edit program | ● | ● | (\*1) |
| 3D data import | ● | - | - |
| 3D View teaching | ● | ● | ● |
| Simulation | ● | - | - |
| Debug | ● | - | - |
| Monitoring | ● | (\*2) | (\*2) |
| Movie saving | ● | ● | ● |
| Print | ● | - | - |
| Simple position correction | ● | ● | ● |

\*1: Available for 1 program (PRO1) only. Even if the project received from the robot controller contains a program other than 1 program (PRO1), it cannot be displayed or edited.

\*2: Sampling interval is one second. Local variables cannot be monitored.

* The Trial or Light version displays "Trial" or "Light" on the status bar at the bottom of the screen.
* Entering the license key of the Product version for the Trial or Light version makes it available as a Product version.

# Note on Languages

When you connect WINCAPSIII with the robot controller or when you use an existing project, use the same language for WINCAPSIII and the controller or the project.

Otherwise, different encodings can lead to the following problems when receiving data from the robot controller, when opening projects, etc.

* Editing and saving programs or string variables with garbled text can corrupt data.
* Project and file names can be garbled, making it impossible to open the project.

# Registering License

During installation a License Information dialog box will appear.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004348_1.png)

Enter the user ID printed on the license included with the product to the License Key field, and press the Add button.

Input the license key printed on the installation disc label for Light or Trial versions.

If the user ID appears under License Key, press the Close button.

* Skipping over this license registration process loads WINCAPSIII in test drive mode with limited functionality.
* To register at a later date, choose Help|License... to display the above dialog box.

The installer may take a while before starting installation of WINCAPSIII because it installs necessary components as shown below.

* ORiN2SDK : Components for communication
* VRC : Components for simulation

# Uninstalling

The following is the procedure for uninstalling this software.

###### 1

From the Start menu, choose Settings|Control panel and then Add or Remove programs.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004349_1.png)

###### 2

Choose WINCAPSIII and then press the Change/Remove button to display a confirmation dialog box.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004349_2.png)

###### 3

Press the OK button to proceed with the uninstall operation.

* If a dialog box appears warning of shared files, press the Leave all button.
* Installing WINCAPSIII also installs ORiN2 SDK and VRC. To uninstall ORiN2 SDK and VRC, first check that no other applications use these and then uninstall them using the same procedure as above.

# WINCAPSIII Basic Functions

The following describes the product's basic functions.

## Communications

Communicating with a robot controller over an Ethernet or serial link.

## Writing Programs

Program using an editor. For further details on programs, please refer to the programming manual.

The editor provides the following functions.

## Online Monitoring

WINCAPSIII monitors controller status, providing immediate access to variables, I/O values, and other quantities.

## Online Debugging

With connecting the robot controller with WINCAPSIII, an operator can control robot programs from WINCAPSIII.  
You can debug the program by using Breakpoint settings or Step start function, with checking the variables and I/O status during operation.

## Arm 3D View

This is for visualizing the robot motion and posture on the PC screen. Loading 3D data or creating simple objects enables the user to check interference with the equipment and movements of workpieces and tools without running the actual robot.

## Logging

The following functions for logging variables, I/O values, and error messages are available for efficient program debugging.

* Error log
* Operation log
* Control log
* Trace log
* servo log

The following functions are exclusive functions for the RC7M controller and not available for the RC8 series robot controller.

* Program bank \*exclusive to RC7M PAC language
* Logging  
  Variable log, I/O log

# Steps in Writing Robot Programs

The following shows the WINCAPSIII work flow for writing a program and validating its operation.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004353_1.png)

## Step 1: Load WINCAPSIII.

Launch WINCAPSIII.

For further details, refer to [Starting Up/Shutting Down](004355.html).

## Step 2: Create a Project.

This project contains all necessary data for the target robot.

For further details, refer to [Creating a Project](004400.html).

## Step 3: Write Robot Program.

Write the robot operation program using the built-in editor.

For further details, refer to [Writing Programs](004416.html).

## Step 4: Teach Operation Positions.

Specify operation positions by manipulating the virtual robot in the Arm 3D view window.

For further details, refer to [Arm 3D View Window](004454.html).

Using simple modeling and importing 3D data creates an on-screen simulation for specifying the robot's operation range and detecting collisions with surrounding equipment.

## Step 5: Checking Program Syntax.

This step runs syntax check on the created program.  
If errors are detected, the line number, and a brief note of the error appears on the output window.  
For further details, refer to [Syntax Check of the Program](004446.html).

## Step 6: Confirmation of robot motion

Check the motion of the program that you have created with the simulation function.  
To modify the program, do STEP3-5 again. Adjust the program until the robot moves as you expected.

## Step 7: Send Data to Robot Controller.

Connect to the robot controller and send it the data necessary for robot operation.

For further details, refer to [Link with Robot Controller](004408.html).

## Step 8: Test Program Operation (debug).

Actually run the robot program and check the program flow,the robot operation range, and collisions with surrounding equipment.

If any problems are found, correct the program and repeat this operation until it works properly.

## Step 9: Back Up Data.

Use WINCAPSIII to save the robot controller's internal data in projects.

For further details, refer to [Data Transfer](004410.html).

## Step 10: Exit WINCAPSIII.

For further details, refer to [Starting Up/Shutting Down](004355.html).

# User Levels and Access Rights

WINCAPSIII's two user access levels, operator and programmer, ensure data security by limiting access to advanced functionality and sensitive data.

The user specifies which on the log-in screen when WINCAPSIII first starts.

For further details on logging in, refer to [Loading WINCAPSIII](004356.html).

## Operator Level

Level enabling PAC program creation / editing and other basic operations.

It blocks changes to WINCAPSIII settings.

It does not require a password.

## Programmer Level

Level enabling changes in project settings and other higher operations.

It allows changes to WINCAPSIII settings.

It requires a password.

For further details on setting this password, refer to [Programmer Password](004358.html).

Differences in functions due to user levels are as follows.

| Function | Operator | Programmer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Creating a new project | Available | Available |
| Writing / editing programs | Available | Available |
| Data transfers | Available | Available |
| Online (monitoring/debugging functions) | Available | Available |
| Addition of controller function extension | Available | Available |
| Altering project properties | Conditionally available\* | Available |
| Altering parameters | Not available | Available |
| Reading / writing arm parameters | Not available | Available |

\*Only communications settings can be changed

To change the user level after starting WINCAPSIII, from the menu bar, click Tool, click Re-Login.

# WINCAPSIII Basic Settings

###### 1

From the menu bar, click Tool, click Option.

The [Option setting] dialog appears.

###### 2

Select a tab you want to set.

Option setting dialog consists of four tabs.

###### 3

When configuration is complete, click the [OK] button.

Click the [Cancel] button to discard the change.

If a different tab is selected during the setting, entries are not confirmed until you click the [OK] button. Be sure to click the [OK] button to confirm the change before moving to another tab.

## Option Setting Dialogue Box

### General Tab

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004357_1.png)

#### A: Project

Specify a folder to save a project. A folder specified here will be the default folder to save a new project.

#### B: When loading it, the last window arrangement is restored.

Open project with the program window and 3D view window in the same place as when last closed.

#### C: When loading, restore grid width of the last variable and arm coordinate.

Restore the grid width of the variable screen and arm coordinate screen to the state when last closed.

#### D: [Trace Log] display PAC Commands.

Selecting this check box will display source code on the Code column of the Trace log window.

Note that large logs can take considerable time to display.

#### E: Enable RC7 online-debug mode.

Enable the debug mode.  
\* You can set it only when using RC7M.

#### F: Values of global variable when Simulation mode end:

Switch the display of the dialog message that appears when exiting the simulation mode.

#### G: Show message when get current position.

A confirmation message is displayed when acquiring position. Turn this ON to avoid overwriting position data by mistake.

### Editor Tab

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004357_2.png)

#### A: Font

This area specifies the font type and size for Program edit windows.

#### B: Code color

This area specifies the colors for highlighting text in the Program edit window. Select the text type, then choose text color with Front color and surrounding color as Back color.

#### C: Tab

This area specifies the tabs for Program edit window.

#### D: Others

Automatic grammar check at window close
:   Selecting this check box automatically runs a syntax check on the selected program before closing the Program edit window.

Delete comment except for "REM"statement ,when "Add comment"
:   Select the check box to delete comments other than those in REM for Adding Comments.

Use programing input assistance.
:   Display forms by the tooltip at command input.

### Communication Tab

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004357_3.png)

#### A: Monitor sampling time

Specify intervals for robot controller monitoring.

#### B: Data send option

Specify data transfer option at data sending to the robot controller.

### Arm tab

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004357_4.png)

#### A: Moving Record

Set the point numbers on the robot operation trajectory displayed in the Arm 3D view window.

#### B: Back Color

Set the Arm 3D View window background color.

#### C:Omit rendering the surface does not display

If this box is checked, only visible surface of the 3D data is drawn. Check this box when you would like to accelerate the display speed of the [Arm 3D View].

#### D: Show message when collision is detected

Select to display the Collision dialog box when a collision is detected.

#### E: Type to display collision position

Choose the method of displaying the robot's position when a collision occurs.

# Screen Components

WINCAPSIII uses the following general screen layout.

WINCAPSIII offers the user considerable flexibility in rearranging screen elements to match the needs at hand.

The screen shots in this document use the default layout, so may not necessarily match what appears on your screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004362_1.png)

## A: Menus

This area displays the following ten menu items available in WINCAPSIII.

* [File](004364.html) menu
* [Edit](004365.html) menu
* [View](004366.html) menu
* [Project](004367.html) menu
* [Connect](004368.html) menu
* [Debug](004369.html) menu
* [Arm](004370.html) menu
* [Tool](004371.html) menu
* [Window](004372.html) menu
* [Help](004373.html) menu

For further details on menu items, refer to [Menu Items](004363.html).

## B: Toolbars

This area displays the following six toolbars that provide user alternate access to most menu items with button icons.

For further details on toolbars, refer to [Toolbar](004374.html).

## C: Docking View

Docking view displays various windows for information, such as the project list, variables and IO window.  
You can arrange the layout of windows depending on your needs.

## D: Client area

Client area displays various windows for information, such as Program edit window, Arm 3D window and log windows.  
You can arrange the layout of windows depending on your needs.  
For each window, refer to Client area.

## E: Status bar

Status bar displays detailed descriptions for each menu, WINCAPSIII login level, keyboard status and others.

# File Menu

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004364_1.png)

## Description of the Drop-down Menu

### [New Project](004400.html)

This is for creating a new project.

### [Open Project...](004404.html)

This is for opening an existing project.

### Close Project

This closes the currently open project. If the project has program edits or other unsaved modifications, a dialog box asks whether you wish to save them.

### [Save Project](004405.html)

This saves the currently open project.

### [Save As Project](004405.html)

This is for saving the currently open project under a new name. It creates a folder under a specified name and copies all current project data into the folder.

### Import

This is to import variables and log data that have been exported from other projects into current project.

You cannot import I/O allocation.

### Export...

This exports variables, log data and others of current project to CSV files.

### [Save](004419.html)

This saves the program or header file selected in the Program view area.

### [Save As...](004419.html)

This saves the program or header file selected in the Program view area under a different name.

It adds saved file into a project.

### [Print...](004415.html)

This is for printing programs, variables, and a list of I/Os.

### Recent Projects

This displays recently used projects.

Choosing one opens it.

### [Exit](004399.html)

This is for shutting down the program.

If the project has program edits or other unsaved modifications, a dialog box asks whether you wish to save them.

ID : 4365

# Edit Menu

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004365_1.png)

## Description of the Drop-down Menu

### Undo

This cancels the last operation, returning edits to the preceding state.

### Redo

This repeats the operation canceled with Undo.

### Cut

This moves to the Windows clipboard and deletes the contents selected in the Program edit window.

### Copy

This copies to the Windows clipboard the contents selected in the Program edit window.

It does not delete the original.

### Paste

This copies the clipboard contents to the selected portion of the Program edit window.

### Delete

This deletes the area selected in the Program edit window.

### Select All

This selects the entire contents of the Program edit window.

### [Find and Replace...](004421.html)

This searches for or replaces desired character strings in projects or files being edited.

### [Jump to...](004423.html)

This is for moving the cursor to a line, specified by number, in the Program edit window.

### [Comment Block](004424.html)

This submenu converts the lines selected in the Program edit window to and from comments.

### [Indent](004425.html)

This submenu controls indenting of the lines selected in the Program edit window

### [Bookmark](004426.html)

This is for working with bookmarks.

### [Insert Registered String](004433.html)

Previously registered character strings are placed in the program.

### [Register String](004434.html)

Character strings selected in the program edit window can be registered in advance and placed in program through shortcuts.

### [Add Comment](004436.html)

Selecting this automatically adds texts written in the application columns of variables and I/O lists to the source code as comments.

### [Format Code](005094.html)

The program code is shaped into a standard form. Line indents are inserted and blank spaces inside the code added or deleted automatically.

### Delete code for Simulation

Delete code which is automatically inserted the program (program code written between "#Ifdef\_VRC\_" and "#Endif") at the point of simulation execution.

The following functions are exclusive functions for the RC7M controller and not available for the RC8 series robot controller.

* Command List \*exclusive to RC7M PAC language
* Insert Command \*exclusive to RC7M PAC language

# Project Menu

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004367_1.png)

## Description of the Drop-down Menu

### [Add Program...](004417.html)

This is for creating a new program and adding it to the current project.

### [Add Existing File...](004418.html)

This submenu is for copying the selected program into the current project folder to add it in the project.

### Make on Boot Setting of Program Files

Execute PRE-CHECK of the selected program.

### [Program Encryption](005904.html)

Encrypt or decrypt the selected program.

Enable or disable the edit lock on the selected program.

### Create Macro Definition File

### Import Macro Definition File

This submenu is for reading the content of header files defining macro names to apply it to variables and I/O ports.

### Command Builder

This submenu is for displaying the Command builder dialog box to support PAC commands input.

### Program Template

### [Check Grammar](004446.html)

### [Parameter](004407.html)

This displays the dialog box for specifying project parameters.

### Joint Setting Table

This displays the dialog box for specifying joint settings. Axis settings are used in SMRT4G, MC2F and Added axes.

### [Property](004406.html)

This submenu displays the dialog box containing property sheets of communication, compile, variables, and I/O items for referring to them or configuring the project.

* Program bank

# Connect Menu

## Description of the Drop-down Menu

### [Transfer Data...](004410.html)

* Online(Debug): (This function is available in Ver.1.7.\* or higher.)  
  Selecting this command will allow a computer to control programs when robot controller runs in Auto mode. You can start a program and debug a program by changing variables and I/O values.

ID : 4369

# Debug Menu

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004369_1.png)

Debug menu is available in Ver.1.7.\* or higher.  
Some functions are disabled depending on the combination between the controller and the robot.

## Description of the Drop-down Menu

### Simulation Mode

Start the simulation function.

This enables checking of cycle time or operation posture.

### Start All Supervisor Tasks

This starts all supervisory tasks.

### Stop All Supervisor Tasks

This stops all supervisory tasks.

### Start a Task

This starts the selected program.

### Step in

This executes one program step.

If the step executed calls another program, the program will stop at the first line of the called program.

### Continue All Tasks

This resumes suspended tasks.

### Halt

This suspends program execution.

### Step-stop

Program execution runs through to the end of the current step.

### Cycle-stop

Program execution runs through to the end of the current cycle.

### Program Reset

This returns the current program to its starting point.

### Reset All Tasks

This returns all programs to their starting points.

### Show Quick Watch \*exclusive to RC7M PAC language

This displays the current values of all variables and I/O ports currently selected in the Program edit window.

\*This function is the exclusive function for the RC7M controller and not available for the RC8 series robot controller.

### Register to Watch \*exclusive to RC7M PAC language

Add the currently selected quick watch items to the watch list in the Watch window.

\*This function is the exclusive function for the RC7M controller and not available for the RC8 series robot controller.

### Delete Watch \*exclusive to RC7M PAC language

This deletes the watch items selected in the Watch window.

\*This function is the exclusive function for the RC7M controller and not available for the RC8 series robot controller.

### Set/Reset a Break Point

This specifies whether program execution breaks at the step currently under the cursor in the Program edit window.

### Reset All Break Points

This clears all breakpoints.

### Break Point Stop Setting

This specifies whether hitting a breakpoint pauses the current program only or all programs.

### Set Line to Start/Stop Log

Set the range of logging from Program edit window. Logging will start or stop from the cursor position on the program window.

### Get Single Trace Log

This displays the trace log for the specified program, a listing of the program steps executed and their execution times.

### Controller Settings

This submenu controls controller operation: turning motors and machine locks ON and OFF and specifying times for reading control logs.
