# Configuring Robot Joints

The MC8 series controller is capable of controlling a maximum of eight joints.  
The motors connected to the controller can be configured as robot joints or extended-joints.  
Any or all of joints 1 to 4 can be configured as robot joints.  
Robot joints can be driven by robot motion commands enabling CP motion (linear and circular).  
To enable those robot motion commands, however, joints J1 to J4 should be configured as predetermined.  
All joints except robot joints are used as extended-joints.  
For details about operations of robot joints and extended-joints, refer to the ["Extended-joint Manual"](004868.html) .

## Robot Joints

According to the number of robot joint used, configuring robot joints J1 to J4 in Cartesian coordinates will enable you to drive those joints with robot motion command with CP motion (linear and circular).  
The following images show available motion directions in different robot joints configuration.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Configuring with a single joint |  |
| Configuring with two joints |  |
| Configuring with three joints |  |
| Configuring with four joints |  |

To drive joints correctly in a CP motion (linear or circular), the joint configuration and the motion directions must match the Cartesian coordinates (coordinates for RIGHTY) shown above.  
In a different joint configuration, executing a CP motion command causes an unexpected motion. It is dangerous. Use a PTP motion instead of a CP motion.

## Extended-Joints

A single extended-joint is configured as shown below. It can execute only PTP motion. A MOVE command is not available for extended-joints, so use "DriveA" and "Drive commands" to drive extended-joints.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005318_5.png)

# Configuring Robot Joints

To configure the robot joint, use the teach pendant or in WINCAPSIII with the following procedures.

1. Joints not configured as robot joints are regarded as extended-joints.
2. Modifying the robot joint configuration initializes the arm group and link information settings.

## Configuring Using the Teach Pendant

###### 1

Access : Top screen- [F2 Arm] - [F2 Maintenance] - [F10 Joint Settings] - [F12 Robot Axis Range]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005319_1.png)

"Robot axis range screen" appears.

###### 2

Select axis range to set as a robot axis, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005319_2.png)

## Configuring Using WINCAPSIII

###### 1

Access : Project | Joint Setting Table (This display is the Joint Setting window)  
"Joint setting" window appears.  
Choose the Selecting Robot Joint tab.  
Select joints to be configured as robot joints and press OK.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005319_3.png)

###### 2

Choose Connect | Transfer data to display the Transfer data window.  
In the WINCAPSIII pane, select Parameters | Arm parameters and then press Send to transfer the data to the robot controller.

# CONVEYOR TRACKING MANUAL

This manual describes the conveyor tracking system and Extended-joint tracking system. Conveyor tracking system is available in Version.1.6.\* or higher. Extended-joint tracking system is available in Version 2.5.\* or higher.

To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html)".

Unless otherwise described, any of this manual written as "conveyor tracking" includes the extended-joint tracking.

# Overview

## Conveyor Tracking and Extended-Joint Tracking

### Brief Description of the Conveyor Tracking

Conveyor tracking is a robot function that allows robots to keep track of workpieces carried by the conveyor without stopping the conveyor.

There are two types of conveyor tracking.

Sensor tracking
:   The sensor tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed linearly (but with arbitrary interval) on the moving conveyor.   
    In this system, a signal is generated when a workpiece traverses in front of a photoelectric sensor.   
    Once this signal is generated, position data of the workpiece is registered in the controller. Based on that, the controller calculates the expected workpiece position on the conveyor and instructs the robot to follow the workpiece. This process is performed whenever a workpiece passes in front of the photoelectric sensor.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_1.png)

Vision tracking
:   The vision tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed on arbitrary position and attitude on the moving conveyor.   
    In this system, a signal is generated when an image recognition unit of the vision sensor detects a workpiece.   
    Once this signal is generated, position and the angle of the workpiece are registered in the controller. Based on that, the controller calculates the expected workpiece position and instructs the robot to follow the workpiece. This process is performed whenever the signal is generated.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_2.png)

The sensor tracking and the vision tracking function cannot be used with the cooperative control function and the force control function.

The combination use with the exclusive control is available in version 2.8.\* or higher.

### Extended-joint Tracking

The extended-joint tracking system enables to pick up a workpiece on the moving conveyor which is driven by the extended-joint without stopping the conveyor.   
The difference between the conveyor tracking system and this system is the drive mechanism of the conveyor. The conveyor in this system is driven by the extended-joint. Other functions are the same as the conveyor tracking.   
Just like the conveyor tracking, there are two types of extended-joint tracking: sensor tracking and vision tracking.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_8.png)

The sensor tracking and the vision tracking function cannot be used with the cooperative control function and the force control function.

The combination use with the exclusive control is available in version 2.8.\* or higher.

## Enabling Conveyor Tracking Function

The terms referring to whether the conveyor tracking function is enabled or disabled are defined as follows.

Tracking mode
:   "Tracking mode" means a state that the conveyor tracking is enabled.   
    Calling conveyor tracking-dedicated commands ("[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)", and "[TrackDraw](003049.html)") while the conveyor tracking is enabled will allow robots to follow the target position according to the conveyor's motion.

Non-tracking mode (Normal operation mode)
:   "Non-tracking mode" means a state that the conveyor tracking is disabled. This is the default setting at the controller startup.   
    Use motion commands, such as "[Approach](000161.html)", "[Depart](000186.html)", and "[Move](000207.html)", to move a robot arm to a static target position.

To change the [tracking mode](#trackingMode), use dedicated commands for tracking mode change ([TrackStart](005377.html) and [TrackStop](005378.html)).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_3.png)

## Robot Motion during Tracking Mode

While [tracking mode](#trackingMode) is enabled, robot motion is controlled by the tracking mode-dedicated commands, such as "[TrackApproach](005346.html)", "[TrackDepart](005350.html)", "[TrackMove](005356.html)", and "[TrackDraw](003049.html)".   
Please note that if a tracking mode-dedicated command is used during [tracking mode](#trackingMode) even once, a robot starts automatically moving in parallel with the conveyor in order to track with the conveyor motion.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_4.png)

The robot motion status during the [tracking mode](#trackingMode) are defined by the following terms.

Conveyor catch-up motion (Catch-up motion)
:   Conveyor catch-up motion indicates a robot motion that catches up to the target workpiece on the conveyor.   
    The robot accelerates its speed until it catches up to the workpiece, and then moves in parallel to the conveyor once the robot reaches the workpiece.   
    When the conveyor is running at high speed, the robot may move at a speed faster than the specified external speed to catch up with the conveyor.

Robot task motion
:   Robot task motion is a robot motion that performs actual robot tasks along with the conveyor [catch-up motion](#tracking).

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_5.png)

Robot motion during the [tracking mode](#trackingMode) is the synthesized motion of the [conveyor catch-up motion](#tracking) and the [robot task motion](#operation).   
For example, a [TrackApproach](005346.html) motion is a synthesized motion of the [conveyor catch-up motion](#tracking) and [Approach](000161.html) motion. In this context, Approach motion corresponds to the robot task motion.

## Range of the [Conveyor Catch-up motion](#tracking)

If a tracking mode-dedicated command ([TrackApproach](005346.html), [TrackDepart](005350.html), [TrackMove](005356.html), and [TrackDraw](003049.html)) is used during [tracking mode](#trackingMode) even once, a robot starts automatically moving in parallel with the conveyor in order to keep tracking with the conveyor motion.   
In RC8 series, to define the area of conveyor tracking according to the operation, the following terms are defined.

Tracking range
:   This is an area on the conveyor where the robot can perform the [conveyor catch-up motion](#tracking).   
    Tracking range is delimited by the upstream limit and the downstream limit. The upstream limit is set to the direction where a workpiece comes from, whereas the downstream limit is set to the direction where a workpiece goes to.   
    To use multiple robots, set a tracking range for respective robots.

Upstream limit of the tracking range (Upstream limit)
:   This is the tracking limit on the upstream of the conveyor. Once a workpiece passes this limit, a robot starts the [conveyor catch-up motion.](#tracking)   
    This must be set within the motion range of the robot arm.

Downstream limit of the tracking range (Downstream limit)
:   This is the tracking limit on the downstream of the conveyor. Once a workpiece reaches this limit, a robot stops the [conveyor catch-up motion](#tracking) and starts deceleration.   
    This must be set within the motion range of the robot arm.

    ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_6.png)

## Conveyor Tracking with Multiple Robots

For RC8 series, multiple robots can perform conveyor tracking on one conveyor.   
This operation is practical when multiple robots perform each task in different area on the conveyor, provided that the conveyor tracking area is divided into two parts: upstream and downstream.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005324_7.png)

When conveyor tracking is performed by multiple robots, each robot controller is assigned to one of the following.

Master controller
:   Master controller receives a signal that is generated when a sensor or vision sensor detects a workpiece in order to obtain the position information of the workpiece.   
    Among multiple controllers, only one controller is assigned to the master controller. While this controller performs conveyor tracking itself, it also has the role of instructing other controllers on which workpieces to track.

Slave controller
:   All controllers except master controller will be the slave controller.   
    A slave controller receives tracking target workpiece data via Ethernet communication, and then performs conveyor tracking.

# System Configuration

This chapter describes the system configuration of the conveyor tracking/extended-joint tracking.

* For safety reason and to prevent damage to the devices, disconnect the power cable of the controller or shut down the power supply to the controller from the facilities before disconnecting or connecting cables.
* A robot controller that the conveyor tracking license is enabled restricts communication speed for other operations. This is because the controller places a priority on ensuring the communication for the conveyor tracking operation or the extended-joint tracking.  
  If time-out occurs before other operations are not completed, take any prevention measures, such as setting longer time-out period.

# System Configuration of the Sensor Tracking

Configuration of the sensor tracking is illustrated below.

The sensor tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces which are placed linearly (but with arbitrary interval) on the moving conveyor.  
The system executes two different programs simultaneously; one is a program to recognize the position of a workpiece and the other is a program to pick it up.

In a program which recognizes workpieces, the sensor activates trigger on once a workpiece passes through the sensor, and then the controller receives the encoder data and stores it at that moment.  
In a picking up program, based on the stored data, the robot picks up a workpiece by adjusting the robot arm in response to the workpiece's motion.

# System Configuration of the Vision Tracking

Configuration of the vision tracking is illustrated below.

The vision tracking system is applied to pick up workpieces that are placed at arbitrary positions on the moving conveyor.  
 The system executes two different programs simultaneously: one to recognize the coordinates of a workpiece and the other for pickup.

## Conveyor Tracking

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005327_1.png)

A program that recognizes the coordinates of workpieces operates as shown below.

A visual device starts recording once receiving an instruction from the controller. If a workpiece exists, the visual device sends the workpiece’s position data to the controller.  
 Once the visual device starts recording, it transmits a trigger signal to the controller, and then the controller immediately obtains the position data from the encoder.  
 The controller stores the workpiece's position data transmitted from the visual device and the position data obtained from the encoder for each workpiece.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005327_2.png)

In a picking up program, the controller reads the stored position data of the workpiece, and then the robot picks up the workpiece by adjusting its arm in response to the workpiece's motion.

### Wiring Diagram

Wiring diagram is illustrated below.

When connecting to the encoder hub, connect to the port corresponding to the joint number of the encoder.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005327_3.png)

For information about the I/O cable wiring when performing vision tracking with a Basler camera, refer to "[Wiring an I/O cable to a GigE Camera](001214.html)".

### Encoder Hub

The encoder hub is available in old and new models.

If you use a new model, connect the encoder line of the motor & encoder cable to the encoder hub's connector port indicated as "ROBOT-0" (on the left side viewed from the front).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/003322_2_3.png)

For details about the external diagram and the installation precautions, refer to "[Encoder HUB](018092.html)".

# Encoder Specification

The below table shows the specifications of the encoder.  
Be sure to read the INSTRUCTION Sheet enclosed in the package.

## Specification

| Item | Specifications |
| --- | --- |
| Part No. | 410010-752\* |
| Model | E6B2-CWZ1X （OMRON） |
| Type | Incremental |
| Supply voltage | 5 VDC(±5 %) |
| Current consumption | 160 mA max. |
| Output circuit configuration | Line driver output |
| Output phase |  |
| Maximum response frequency | 100 kHz |
| Slewing speed | 6000 r/min |
| Resolution | 1000 pulses/revolution (Note 1) |
| Starting torque | 9980 µNｍ max. |
| Moment of inertia | 1×10-6 kgm2 max. |
| Shaft loading | Radial：30 N, Axial：20 N |
| Dust & splash proof | IP50 |
| Ambient temperature | -10 ℃ to +70 ℃ |
| Ambient humidity | 35 % to 85 % RH |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005329_2.png)

Note 1: The number of pulses is multiplied by 4, so the count value is 4000 pulses/revolution.  
Note 2: Since this equipment is neither dust-proof nor drip-proof, protect it with a cover or something if used in an adverse environment.  
Note 3: Protect the encoder connectors by putting covers on them after installation.

## Appearance Diagram and Dimensional Outline Drawing

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005329_3.png)

For information about how to install the encoder, see OMRON's website.

If an error message "Execute CALSET" is displayed at the start-up of the controller, perform CALSET.  
For information about the CALSET procedure, see ["Executing CALSET"](005090.html) in the "EXTENDED-JOINT MANUAL".

## Encoder Cable

To connect the encoder with the encoder hub, use a dedicated encoder cable (cable for RC8-OMRON encoder).  
The length of cables are 1 m, 2 m, 3 m, 4 m, 6 m and 12 m. The encoder junction cable is the same as the one used for the extended-joint support controller. For details, see ["Options for Robot Controller"](001971.html) of "OPTIONAL COMPONENTS".

* Incorrect connection of the extended-joint or encoder may cause malfunction.
* The total length of an encoder cable for each axis between a connection port of the encoder hub and a connection port of the motor shall be 16 m or less.
* The bending radius for the encoder cable and encoder relay cable should be 12.5 mm or more for the fixed cable, and 83 mm or more for the movable cable. Excessive bending will damage the cable.

# Setting Procedure of the Conveyor Tracking

## Outline

This section describes the outline of how to set up the conveyor tracking/extended-joint tracking.

### (1) Selecting a Hardware

In this step, execute various settings of hardware.  
- Selecting the conveyors and devices  
- Setting of the encoder joint number  
- I/O setting

### (2) Hardware Connection Confirmation

In this step, execute Joint and I/O setting confirmation.

### (3) Calibration

Calibration measures the exact positional relationship between the conveyor, sensor (vision sensor), and robot.

## Detailed Procedure

Detailed setting procedures are different for sensor tracking and for vision tracking.  
For details about the sensor tracking, refer to "[Setup of the Sensor Tracking](005332.html)".  
For details about the vision tracking, refer to "[Setup of the Vision Tracking System](005342.html)".

Extended-joint tracking requires extended-joint setup before the tracking-related setup described in this page. For details, refer to "[Start-up procedure of the extended-joint (ball screw)](004933.html)".

## Adding the Conveyor Tracking Function to the Existing Robot Controller

When adding the conveyor tracking function to the existing robot controller, the license of the conveyor tracking function and the encoder hub are necessary.

Please contact your [DENSO representative](001077.html) for more details.

When adding the conveyor tracking function to the robot controller, customers may need to change the project data of the robot controller to the project for extended-joint.

In that case, please perform the procedure below.

### Procedure to Change to the Project Data for Extended-joint

With WINCAPSIII, after getting data from the robot controller and changing to the project for extended-joint, send data to the robot controller.

###### 1

Use WINCAPSIII.

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path：[File] - [New Project] |

Select "Get information from the controller for creating a new project.", create data.

For details, refer to "[Creating a New Project](004403.html)".

###### 2

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path：[Project] - [Property] |

Change to "Use" by [Change] button of "Robot info." tab.

For details, refer to "[Robot](004406.html#ID004406_Robot)" of "Robot info." tab.

###### 3

|  |
| --- |
| Operation path：[Connect] - [Transfer data] |

Select "Local data" of WINCAPSIII and click [Send].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/002867_1.png)

When sending is complete, please restart the controller.

# Setup of the Sensor Tracking

This section describes how to setup the sensor tracking system.

[The joint setting](004936.html) is disabled at default setting. With the teach-pendant, set the joint setting to "Enable encoder only" for the conveyor tracking, or, "Enable" for the extended-joint tracking. For about the way of settings, see "[Enabling the extended-joint](004936.html)".

For the extended-joint tracking setup, if there are any needs of servo-related parameter change, the motor-off is required for the setup. For that reason, turn off all motors before the setup.

This section describes the setup procedure for a system which includes one robot and one conveyor.

# Selecting the Conveyors and Devices

Choose a conveyor number and type of device to be configured.

## Selection Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Tracking Setting Window

Choose [F10 Tracking] from the top window.

To use [F10 Tracking], the license of the conveyor tracking or the extended-joint tracking is required.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005334_1.png)

"Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005334_2.png)

To set the conveyor or to edit the items of the [F12 Detail], the log-in level needs to be the Maintainer or the higher.

###### 2 Displaying the Conveyor Setting Window

Press [Settings].

* Before pressing [Setting], set the "Enabled" on the left side of [Setting] to OFF state. You cannot press [Setting] when the "Enabled" is set to ON state.
* Setting the conveyor to OFF state after executing one of the following commands, the value set by each command is written into the parameter.  
  [TrackStartArea](005490.html), [TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html), [TrackTargetOffset](005493.html), [TrackMinimumIntervalLength](005794.html)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005334_3.png)

###### 3 Setting the Conveyor

Choose [Linear] and press [Next].

Linear conveyor is selected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005334_4.png)

###### 4 Setting the Device

Choose [Sensor] and press [Next].  
[Sensor] is selected.

Once [Stop] - [OK] pressed, the calibration is canceled and the "Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005334_5.png)

This continues to "[Setting of the Encoder Joint Number](005335.html)".

# Setting of the Encoder Joint Number

This section describes how to set the joint number of the encoder that is connected to the conveyor.

## Setting Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Joint Number Selection Window

Press [Joint No].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005335_1.png)

[Joint Number] setting window is displayed.

###### 2 Selecting the Joint Number and Applying the Selection

Choose a joint number then press [OK].

Items to be displayed in the [Joint Number] window are as follows. If an applicable license is not registered, Encoder or ExJoint on the [Joint number selection window] is not displayed.

* Joint that is set to [Enable encoder only]: Available to the conveyor tracking.
* Joint that is set to [Enabled]: Available to the extended-joint tracking.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005335_2.png)

Selective extended joint is not selectable.

###### 3 Confirmation of Setting Value

The joint number selected in STEP2 is displayed.  
Press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005335_3.png)

To change the joint number of the encoder which is assigned to the conveyor, set the [Conveyor joint number (Conveyor\*)] to "0" from [Tracking] - [F12 Detail] - [Conveyor tracking] beforehand.

This continues to the ["I/O Settings"](005336.html).

# I/O Setting

This section describes how to set the I/O port number that is connected to the sensor detecting workpiece, and the edge type.

## Setting Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Number Selection Window

Press [I/O Number].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005336_1.png)

I/O setting window is displayed.

###### 2 Setting Number

Enter the I/O number to use, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005336_2.png)

Available I/O numbers are listed below.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| User input | No.8 to 15 |
| Hand input | No.48 to 55 |

Once the connection confirmation button is pressed, parameter setting process will start. For the extended-joint tracking, this setting process will not be performed under the Motor-ON state. A system message that asks to turn off the motor is displayed.

###### 3 Setting the Edge Type

Choose desired [Edge type] then press [Next].  
Edge type is selected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005336_3.png)

For details about each edge type, see the table below.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Rising edge | To detect a workpiece at the rising edge. |
| Falling edge | To detect a workpiece at the falling edge. |
| Rising and Falling | To detect a workpiece at the rising edge and falling edge. |

This continues to ["Hardware Connection Confirmation"](005337.html).

# Hardware Connection Confirmation

This section describes the hardware connection confirmation methods of the sensor tracking system.

## Joint and I/O Setting Confirmation

This section describes how to confirm the encoder connection and the trigger detection.

###### 1 Checking Encoder Connection

Press [Check connected] button to enable the conveyor.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005337_1.png)

Operate the conveyor then check whether the value of [Current encoder value] changes properly.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005337_2.png)

###### 2 Checking Trigger Detection

Place a work piece on the conveyor to pass through the sensor, and then check whether the value of the [Data buffer] changes properly.  
Press [Next].

The "data buffer" in this context represents a "tracking buffer".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005337_3.png)

If [Data buffer] does not change, press [F1 Start trigger detection].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005337_4.png)

This continues to "[Calibration](005338.html)".

# Calibration

## Outline

Calibration measures the exact positional relationship between the conveyor, sensor, and robot.  
The calibration result is stored as the parameter shown below and used when performing the conveyor tracking operation.

Each conveyor needs to be calibrated respectively.

## Parameters Related to the Positional Relation between Robot and Conveyor

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor CALDATA(X, Y) | Rotating angle around the Z axis of the base coordinate that shows the motion direction of a conveyor [rad] |
| Conveyor CALDATA(Z) | Inclination seen from the XY plane of the base coordinate that shows the motion direction of a conveyor [rad] |
| Conveyor Feed Rate | Amount of conveyor movement per one rotation of encoder [mm/rev] |
| Encoder Rotation Direction | Rotational direction of encoder when the conveyor is moved from upstream to the downstream (1: Normal, -1: Reverse) |

## Parameters Related to the Positional Relation between Robot and Sensor

Homogeneous transform matrix of [sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) and [default posture of holding the work](002221.html#gripBasePosture) are stored.

Between Ver.1.11.\* or lower and Ver.1.12.\* or higher, different storage format is used when performing calibration.  
Also, in Ver.1.11.\* or lower, different storage format was used by sensor tracking and by vision tracking.  
The result of calibration performed by Ver.1.12.\* or higher cannot be used with a controller of Ver.1.11.\* or lower.

| Parameter name | Description (Ver.1.11.\* or lower) | Description (Ver.1.12.\* or higher) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CALDATA（00） | [Sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) X [mm] | Nx for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（01） | [Sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) Y [mm] | Ox for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（02） | [Sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) Z [mm] | Ax for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（03） | Ox for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) | [Sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) X [mm] |
| CALDATA（10） | Oy for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) | Ny for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（11） | Oz for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) | Oy for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（12） | Ax for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) | Ay for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（13） | Ay for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) | [Sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) Y [mm] |
| CALDATA（20） | Az for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) | Nz for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（21） | 0 | Oz for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（22） | 0 | Az for the [default posture of holding the work](000458.html) on the [Homogeneous Translation Type](002221.html#gripBasePosture) |
| CALDATA（23） | 0 | [Sensor detection position](002221.html#sensorPos) Z [mm] |

### Ver.1.11.\* or Lower

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005338_1.png)

### Ver.1.12.\* or Higher

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005338_2.png)

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Rx | RX of [default posture of holding the work](002221.html#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Ry | RY of [default posture of holding the work](002221.html#gripBasePosture) [deg] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Rz | RZ of [default posture of holding the work](002221.html#gripBasePosture) [deg] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005338_3.png)

## Parameters Related to the Tracking Range

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Upstream limit of the Tracking range | Once a workpiece passes this limit, a robot starts the [conveyor catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking). [mm] |
| Downstream limit of the Tracking range | Once a workpiece reaches this limit, robot stops the [conveyor catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking) and starts deceleration. [mm] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005338_4.png)

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Conveyor reference coordinate X | Midpoint X between the [calibration point on upstream limit](002221.html#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](002221.html#trackLRangePos) [mm] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Y | Midpoint Y between the [calibration point on upstream limit](002221.html#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](002221.html#trackLRangePos) [mm] |
| Conveyor reference coordinate Z | Midpoint Z between the [calibration point on upstream limit](002221.html#trackURangePos) and the [calibration point on downstream limit](002221.html#trackLRangePos) [mm] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005338_5.png)

ID : 5339

# Calibration Procedure

The following shows a calibration procedure.

###### 1 Confirmation of the Calibration Procedure

After confirming the calibration procedure, press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_1.png)

###### 2 Confirmation of Passing Sensor

Pass through the object to the sensor.  
Check that the encoder value of the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) is increased when the workpiece passes through the sensor.  
Once the value is increased, press [Next].

The encoder value at the trigger signal input timing is stored in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_2.png)

###### 3 Executing Teaching of Upstream Limit of the Tracking Range

Stop the workpiece at the upper end limit of the tracking range.  
Then move the robot to the teaching position.  
Execute robot teaching and press [Get position of the upstream limit] to get the robot position.  
Checks the obtained value, and press [Next] if everything is satisfactory.

1. When retrying to get the robot position, a system message is displayed to confirm whether to get the position.
2. The posture at the time of getting the upstream limit is set as the [default posture of holding the work](002221.html#gripBasePosture).
3. The height of gripping at the tracking motion is determined by the midpoint of positions obtained at the upstream limit and the downstream limit.

The obtained coordinate values can be changed. To do so, press the edit button on the bottom of the screen. Ten keys are displayed. By the ten keys, change each coordinates values.

The obtained coordinates and encoder values on both of the upstream limit and the downstream limit are used to determine the conveyor feed rate and the direction. If you change the coordinate values by the method shown above, keep in mind that the change may affect the conveyor feed rate and the direction.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_3.png)

###### 4 Executing Teaching of Downstream Limit of the Tracking Range

Stop the workpiece at the lower end limit of the tracking range.  
Then move the robot to the teaching position.  
Execute robot teaching and press [Get position of the downstream limit] to get the robot position.  
Checks the obtained value, and press [Next] if everything is satisfactory.

The midpoint between the upstream limit position and downstream limit position is the [conveyor reference position](002221.html#conveyorBase).

> > ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_4.png)

###### 5 Confirmation of the Calibration Result

Check the calculated parameters, and press [Finish] if everything is satisfactory.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_5.png)

Once the complete button is pressed, parameter setting process will start. For the extended-joint tracking, this setting process will not be performed under the Motor-ON state. A system message that asks to turn off the motor is displayed.

###### 6 Applying the Calibration Result

A system message is displayed to confirm whether to set the calculated data to the controller. Press [OK] if everything is satisfactory.  
Calculated data is set to the controller.  
The setting change is not confirmed if [Cancel] is pressed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_6.png)

The setting change is confirmed and returns to the "Tracking" window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005339_7.png)

For the installation for one conveyor and one robot, this is the end of the setup.

# Setup Procedure when Operating with N Conveyors

If you operate with N (2 to 16) conveyors, setup the second and following conveyors in the same way as with the first conveyor. (For Ver.1.11.\* or lower, up to two conveyors are available.)

Depending on the number of slave controllers and conveyors, sufficient performance may not be obtained because of the performance of the master controller's CPU.
In that case, reduce the number of slave controllers and conveyors and split the system to lower the load on the master controller's CPU.
Alternatively, consider to use a controller with a higher specification CPU as the master controller.

###### 1 Selecting the Conveyor Number

On the "Tracking" window, select the tab, where the used conveyor number is displayed, from the conveyor number tabs display at the top of the screen.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005340_1.png)

###### 2　Setting Up the Conveyor

Press [Setting] button of the "Conveyor N".  
Setup the "Conveyor 2" with same procedure as the "Conveyor 1".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005340_2.png)

The following steps are the same as the installation for one conveyor and one robot.  
See "[Selecting a Hardware](005333.html)", "[Hardware Connection Confirmation](005337.html)", "[Calibration](005338.html)".

# Setup Procedure when Operating with Two or More Robots

If you operate with two or more robots, you need to setup both a master controller and a slave controller, respectively.

* For the calibration of the conveyor tracking/extended-joint tracking, perform in order of the master controller, the slave controller.
* Check that [the joint setting](004936.html) of the slave controller is set to "Disable". If not, change the setting.
* Depending on the number of slave controllers and conveyors, sufficient performance may not be obtained because of the performance of the master controller's CPU.
  In that case, reduce the number of slave controllers and conveyors and split the system to lower the load on the master controller's CPU.
  Alternatively, consider to use a controller with a higher specification CPU as the master controller.

## Setting Procedure for Using an Additional LAN Board

To use an additional LAN board for communication between the master-slave controllers, you need to change the "Multicast. I/F [IP Address]" parameter from the default value. For details, refer to ["Communication between Master and Slave by Using Additional LAN Board"](003411.html).

## Setting Procedure for the Master Controller

###### 1 Displaying the [Master/Slave] window

On the "Tracking" window, press "Master/Slave" for the conveyor which should be set as a slave.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_1.png)

[Master/Slave] window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_2.png)

###### 2 Setting the Slave Count

Press [Slave Count].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_3.png)

[Slave Count] window is displayed.

Enter the number of slave, and then press [OK].

This example assumes that three slaves are used.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_4.png)

###### 3 Setting the IP Address of Slaves

From the "Slave IP address" selection, press [Slave1].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_5.png)

To select different slave address, use up and down allow keys.

[Slave IP address] is displayed.

Enter the I/P address of the slave controller using numeric keypad, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_6.png)

Enter all slave controller's IP addresses by repeating Step 3.

###### 4 Applying the Setting

Once master controller's settings are complete, press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_7.png)

When system message is displayed, press [OK] if everything is satisfactory.  
To discard the new settings, press [Cancel].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_8.png)

The setting change is confirmed and "Tracking" window is displayed.

###### 5 Setting Up the Conveyor

Press [Setting] button of the "Conveyor 1" to setup.  
The following steps are the same as the installation for one conveyor and one robot.  
See "[Selecting a Hardware](005333.html)", "[Hardware Connection Confirmation](005337.html)", "[Calibration](005338.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_9.png)

## Setting Procedure for the Slave Controller

###### 1 Displaying the [Master/Slave] window

On the "Tracking" window, press "Master/Slave" for the conveyor which should be set as master.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_10.png)

[Master/Slave] window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_11.png)

###### 2 Setting the IP Address of Master

Press [Slave].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_12.png)

[Slave setting] window is displayed.

Press [Master IP address].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_13.png)

[Master IP address] is displayed.

Enter the I/P address of the master controller using numeric keypad, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_14.png)

Once the [OK] button is pressed, parameter setting process will start. For the extended-joint tracking, this setting process will not be performed under the Motor-ON state. A system message that asks to turn off the motor is displayed.

###### 3 Set the Master Robot Number

Specify the robot number. This operation is available in Ver.2.8.\* or higher.

When you use the dual arm control function, to set a dual arm-controlled robot as a master, enter the robot number that you want to run as a master of the conveyor tracking operation. If the dual arm control function is not used, leave this entry as 0.

To change the entry, touch the number on the right of the [Master Robot Number] on the window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_22.png)

Once the [Master Robot Number] window appears, enter a number and press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_23.png)

###### 4 Applying the Setting

Once all item's settings are complete, press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_15.png)

When system message is displayed, press [OK] if everything is satisfactory.  
To discard the new settings, press [Cancel].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_16.png)

The setting change is confirmed and [Tracking] window is displayed.

Check the system message then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_17.png)

###### 5 Switching to CAL the Slave (Run mode)

This operation is required if your robot controller version is lower than 2.8.\*.

Start the [CAL the Slave (Run mode)] in the master controller.  
Operation route: Top screen- [F10 Tracking] - [F4 CAL the Slave (Run mode)].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_18.png)

Do not operate the master controller during slave controller calibration.

###### 6 Checking Connection with Master Controller

Press [Setting] on"Tracking" window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_19.png)

Conveyor setting window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_20.png)

Start the conveyor then check whether the value of [Current encoder value], [Data buffer]changes properly. If the value changes, the setting is normal.

The "data buffer" in this context represents a "tracking buffer".

###### 7 Setting Up the Conveyor

The following steps are the same as the installation for one conveyor and one robot.  
See "[Selecting a hardware](005333.html)", "[Hardware Connection Confirmation](005337.html)", "[Conveyor](005338.html)".

###### 8 Terminating the CAL the Slave (Run Mode)

This operation is required if your robot controller version is lower than 2.8.\*.

After calibration is complete, press [Exit Mode] of the master controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005341_21.png)

## If You Use a Robot which was Used as Slave for a Master Robot.

You need to change the following items if you use a robot which was used as slave for a master robot.

### Conveyor Tracking

* Connecting to the encoder for conveyor tracking
* Connecting to the I/O connector of the trigger signal
* Because the encoder of the conveyor tracking is not in use, select [Enable encoder only] to use the encoder.
* Because the robot is set as a slave, change it to a master.

### Extended-joint Tracking

* Connecting to the extended-joint motor
* Connecting to the I/O connector of the trigger signal
* Because the extended-joint motor for the extended-joint tracking is not used, set it to [Enable]
* Because the robot is set as a slave, change it to a master
* Perform necessary setup for the extended-joint use

## If You do not Use a Slave Robot

If the system includes multiple robots but some of these robots are unused, delete unused robots from the slave list which has set by the master robot.  
If robots fail to chuck a workpiece on the conveyor, the data of the workpiece is stored in the memory in the master robot. As stored data accumulates, the speed of calculation to assign robots to workpieces will be longer. As a result, the chuck start timing of the robot will be delayed.

# Setup of the Vision Tracking System

This section describes how to setup the vision tracking system.

[The joint setting](004936.html) is disabled at default setting. With the teach-pendant, set the joint setting to "Enable encoder only" for the conveyor tracking, or, "Enable" for the extended-joint tracking. For about the way of settings, see "[Enabling the extended-joint](004936.html)".

For the extended-joint tracking setup, if there are any needs of servo-related parameter change, the motor-off is required for the setup. For that reason, turn off all motors before the setup.

This section describes the setup procedure for a system which includes one robot and one conveyor.

# Selecting the Conveyors and Devices

Choose a conveyor number and type of device to be configured.

## Selection Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Tracking Setting Window

Choose [F10 Tracking] from the top window.

To use [F10 Tracking], the license of the conveyor tracking is required.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005344_1.png)

"Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005344_2.png)

To set the conveyor or to edit the items of the [F12 Detail], the log-in level needs to be the Maintainer or the higher.

###### 2 Displaying the Conveyor Setting Window

Press [Settings].

* Before pressing [Setting], set the "Enabled" on the left side of [Setting] to OFF state. You cannot press [Setting] when the "Enabled" is set to ON state.
* Setting the conveyor to OFF state after executing one of the following commands, the value set by each command is written into the parameter.  
  [TrackStartArea](005490.html), [TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html), [TrackTargetOffset](005493.html), [TrackMinimumIntervalLength](005794.html)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005344_3.png)

###### 3 Setting the Conveyor

Choose [Linear] and press [Next].

Linear conveyor is selected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005344_4.png)

###### 4 Setting the Device

Choose [Vision] and press [Next].  
[Vision] is selected.

Once [Stop] - [OK] pressed, the calibration is canceled and the "Tracking" window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005344_5.png)

This continues to "[Setting of the Encoder Joint Number](005345.html)".

# Setting of the Encoder Joint Number

This section describes how to set the joint number of the encoder that is connected to the conveyor.

## Setting Procedure

###### 1 Displaying the Joint Number Selection Window

Press [Joint No.]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005345_1.png)

[Joint Number] window is displayed.

###### 2 Selecting the Joint Number and Applying the Selection

Choose a joint number then press [OK].

Items to be displayed in the [Joint Number] window are as follows. If an applicable license is not registered, Encoder or ExJoint on the [Joint number selection window] is not displayed.

* Joint that is set to [Enable encoder only]: Available to the conveyor tracking.
* Joint that is set to [Enabled]: Available to the extended-joint tracking.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005345_2.png)

If you cannot select a joint number, please confirm the below.

1. Selective extended joint is not selectable.
2. Please check whether the target joint is "Enable" in the joint setting.  
   [The joint setting](004936.html) is disabled at default setting. With the teach-pendant, set the joint setting to "Enable encoder only" for the conveyor tracking, or, "Enable" for the extended-joint tracking.  
   For about the way of settings, see "[Enabling the extended-joint](004936.html)".
3. Please check the connection of the wiring.  
   For contents of check, refer to "[Encoder Hub](018092.html)".

###### 3 Confirmation of Setting Value

The joint number selected in STEP2 is displayed.  
Press [Next].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005345_3.png)

To change the joint number of the encoder which is assigned to the conveyor, set the [Conveyor joint number (Conveyor\*)] to "0" from [Tracking] - [F12 Detail] - [Conveyor tracking] beforehand.

This continues to the "[I/O Setting](005358.html)".

# TrackApproach

## Function

With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), move a robot arm to the approach position that is apart from the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) by specified distance.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackApproach motion interpolation, reference position, approach length
[, motion option]
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Motion interpolation
:   Designate a [motion interpolation method](001614.html): "P"/"PTP" for PTP interpolation motion, or "L" for CP interpolation motion.

Reference position
:   Specify [position type](000456.html) data that stands for a [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) obtained by "[TrackTargetPos](005353.html)".  
    For a reference position, it is possible to specify [position type](000456.html) data that is offset in specified position/attitude from position type data obtained by "[TrackTargetPos](005353.html)".

Approach length
:   Designate an approach length by [single precision real number type](000452.html) data. [Target position option](000536.html) can be added to the approach length.

Motion option
:   A [motion option](000521.html) can be specified.

## Description

With the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking), move a robot arm to the approach position that is apart from the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) by specified distance. To execute this command, the task must acquire robot [axis control](000511.html).  
If you enter the [position type](000456.html) data obtained by "[TrackTargetPos](005353.html)" in the second argument "[Reference position](#basePos)" as-is, the robot attitude will be the [Default posture of holding the work](002221.html#gripBasePosture).

However, this is different in the circular tracking operation.

In the circular tracking, the posture of the end-effector rotates by the rotation angle between the [Upstream limit of the tracking range](002856.html#trackURange) to the position where a robot catches up a workpiece.

The posture to be rotated is different depending on the posture in the position which is specified in the second argument "[Reference position](#basePos)".

If the [position type](000456.html) acquired by "[TrackTargetPos](005353.html)" is entered in the second argument "[Reference position](#basePos)" without any change, the posture of [Calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos) will be the posture to be rotated.

If you specify the value that is the sum of [position type](000456.html) data acquired by "[TrackTargetPos](005353.html)" and the correction values described in "To correct robot attitude” in the second argument "[Reference position](#basePos)", the posture to be rotated is the posture that is the correction value is added to the posture of [Calibration point on upstream limit](002856.html#trackURangePos).

Also, in the circular tracking, the robot posture can be kept as the posture in the position where the second argument "[Reference position](#basePos)" specifies.

In this case, change the control method of the tool-end with [TrackStart](005377.html#optonSet) command. For details, refer to [the guaranteed entry of TrackStart command, "Option setting"](005377.html#optonSet).

For details about the tool-end posture, refer to ["Types of tool-end posture control"](002855.html#ID002855_FigControl).

To correct robot attitude

To correct the robot attitude depending on the workpiece direction detected by the vision sensor, as the following sample code shows, obtain the workpiece's attitude angle detected by the vision sensor by [TrackBufferRead](005492.html) first, and then add correction values for each attitude element (Rx, Ry, and Rz) of the second argument [[Reference position](#basePos)].

[Lower than Ver.2.0.\*]

```
Retrieve workpiece data from the buffer, and set it as a tracking-target workpiece  
P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1, -1, -1, 1)
```

```
Retrieve the index number of tracking-target workpiece  
vIndex = TrackBufferIndexes(1, 1)
```

```
Add attitude and angle of workpiece to the attitude element  
LetRZ P10 = PosRZ(P10) + TrackBufferRead(1, vIndex(0), 10)
```

```
Delete the tracking-target workpiece data from the buffer  
TrackTargetRelease 1
```

[Ver.2.0.\* or higher]

```
Retrieve workpiece data from the buffer, and set it as a tracking-target workpiece  
P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1)
```

```
Add attitude and angle of workpiece to the attitude element  
LetRZ P10 = PosRZ(P10) + TrackBufferRead(1, -1, 10)
```

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005346_2.png)

## Related Terms

[Approach](000161.html),
[TrackBufferRead](005492.html),
[TrackDepart](005350.html),

[TrackTargetOffset](005493.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html),
[Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attentio

* This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.
* This command is available only when it is written between [TrackStart](005377.html) and [TrackStop](005378.html).
* Note that the external speed limit and internal speed limit only affect "[Approach](000161.html)" motion that is the [robot task motion](002221.html#operation).  
  These limits do not affect the [catch-up motion](002221.html#tracking).
* Unlike "[Approach](000161.html)" motion, this command does not move a robot arm to the static target position specified by arguments.
* Please note that the motion target position of the robot will differ depending on the positions where the tool definition and work definition are inserted.

1. If the definition change is written before the "TrackTargetPos".

```
ChangeTool 1
ChangeWork 1

P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1,-1,1)
TrackApproach P, P[10], 100
```

The motion target position of the robot is not affected by the changes of tool definition and work definition.

2. If the definition change is written after the "TrackTargetPos".

```
P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1,-1,1)

ChangeTool 1
ChangeWork 1

TrackApproach P, P[10], 100
```

The motion target position of the robot is affected by the changes of the tool definition and work definition.  
Since the tool and work definitions at the TrackTargetPos execution and at the TrackApproach execution are different, the robot motion target position will deviate by these differences.

# TrackCount

## Function

Return the number of data within the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackCount (Conveyor number [, userdata[, Count object]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1 to 16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Userdata
:   Specify userdata by [integer type](000451.html). User data is not judged when you enter a negative value.  
    This is an optional value. This should be "-1" if it is omitted.

Count object
:   Specify the count object by [integer type](000451.html). (See the table below.)  
    This is an optional value. This should be "-1" if it is omitted.  
    This entry is available in Ver.1.10.\* or higher.

    | Setting value | Data count condition |
    | --- | --- |
    | 1 | All data |
    | 2 | Data whose workpiece's current position is upper than the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange). |
    | 3 | Data whose workpiece's current position is lower than the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange). |
    | 4 | Data whose workpiece's current position is upper than the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange). |
    | 5 | Data whose workpiece's current position is lower than the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange). |
    | -1 | Data whose workpiece's current position is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange). |

### Return Value

The number of workpiece data that meets the specified conditions is returned by [integer type](000451.html) data.

## Description

This command returns the number of workpiece data within the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). The counting condition is determined by the user data and the count object.  
If the number of data in the tracking buffer is zero, "0" is returned.  
If the number of data in the tracking buffer is one or more, return values will be as follows.

| User data | Count object | Reurn value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pos. | None / -1 | Return the number of data in the tracking buffer that belongs to the specified user data. |
| Pos. | Pos. | Return the number of count object specified that belongs to the specified user data. |
| Neg. / No | None / -1 | Return the number of data within the tracking buffer. |
| Neg. / No | Pos. | Return the number of the specified count object regardless of the user data. |

Pos. : Positive value entry  
Neg. / No : Negative value entry or no entry.  
None / -1 : No value entry or "-1" is entered.

## Related Terms

[TrackCurStartArea](002225.html),
[TrackInRange](005355.html),
[TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html),
[TrackSetSensor](005375.html),
[TrackSetVision](005376.html),
[TrackStartArea](005490.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html),
[Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

* This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.
* If the ["Tracking Buffer Data" in the fourth argument](005353.html#Mode1) of [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) is "Enabled", the original data of the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) remains the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). Note that the remained data in this [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) is not the object of [TrackCount](005347.html) command.

ID : 5351

# TrackArrivalTime

## Function

Return the estimated execution time in which a [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) arrives at the specified limit of the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackArrivalTime (Conveyor number [, Specify upstream limit/downstream limit[, Offset value]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Specify upstream limit/downstream limit
:   Specify attribute by [integer type](000451.html). This is an optional value. This should be "0"([upstream limit](002221.html#trackURange)) if the value is omitted. This should be the [downstream limit](002221.html#trackLRange) if "-1" is specified.

Offset value
:   Specify the offset distance by [double-precision real number](000453.html). Unit is "mm".  
    Specifying positive values will offset in the [conveyor vector](002221.html#conveyorVec) direction, and specifying negative values will offset in the opposite of the [conveyor vector](002221.html#conveyorVec) direction.  
    Offset value is the distance from the datum point on the workpiece that have been determined at the conveyor calibration.  
    This value determines a point on the workpiece that is used to determine whether the workpiece exists within the tracking range.   
    If the offset value is "0", the workpiece is judged as "within the tracking range" when the said datum point is located in the tracking range.  
    This is omittable. This should be "0" if it is omitted. This entry is available in Ver.1.10.\* or higher.

### Return Value

Return the time in which a work piece arrives at the [upstream limit](002221.html#trackURange) and the [downstream limit](002221.html#trackLRange) of the tracking range with [double-precision real number](000453.html) data. Unit is millisecond.  
Return value will be "0" in one of the following conditions:  
- if the target workpiece has already passed through the [upstream limit](002221.html#trackURange) of the tracking start position when [upstream limit](002221.html#trackURange) is specified,  
- if the target workpiece has already passed through the [downstream limit](002221.html#trackLRange) of the tracking start position when upstream limit is specified.

## Description

This command returns the estimated execution time in which a [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) specified by [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) arrives at the specified [upstream](002221.html#trackURange)/[downstream](002221.html#trackLRange) limit of the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005351_1.png)

## Related Terms

[TrackCurPos](005348.html),
[TrackCurStartArea](002225.html),
[TrackInRange](005355.html),
[TrackStartArea](005490.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html),
[Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

This program will branch the processing according to the time of the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) of arriving at the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange).

```
Dim restTime As Double
restTime = TrackArrivalTime(1, -1)
If (restTime > 500) Then
  ' Tracking is available
  ' Continue the catch-up motion
  ' TrackMove P, P[10]
Else

  ' Tracking is not available
  ' End of tracking
  ' TrackStop 1
End If
```

# TrackStandByPos

## Function

Return the coordinates when a [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) piece arrives at the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackStandByPos (Conveyor number)
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specifies the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

### Return Value

Returns the coordinate of the tracking-target work piece at the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange) by [position type](000456.html) data.

## Description

Return the coordinates when a [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) piece arrives at the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005352_1.png)

## Related Terms

[TrackCurStartArea](002225.html), [TrackInRange](005355.html), [TrackStartArea](005490.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

```
-
```

# TrackTargetPos

## Function

Read out workpiece data from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) and then set them to the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackTargetPos (Conveyor number[, Time-out period[, UserData[, Data Processing type[, Remaining time]]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Time-out period
:   Specify a timeout period by [integer type](000451.html) data. Unit is [msec]. This should be "infinite waiting" if "-1" is set. If UserData is not set, this can be omitted. In that case, this should be "infinite waiting".  
    If time-out period passes, Level 1 error will occur. To continue processing without stopping the program when an error occurs, use "[On Error](000109.html)" command.

UserData
:   Specifying a UserData value allows to take out workpiece data with specified UserData value from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).  
    Specify userdata by [integer type](000451.html). This is an optional value. This does not judge the UserData if it is omitted. If minus value is set, it is treated same as when it is omitted.  
    UserData can be specified with "[TrackSetVision](005376.html)" and/or "[TrackSetSensor](005375.html)" per workpiece.

Data processing type
:   Specify the data retention by [integer type](000451.html) data. This is omittable. This should be "-1" if it is omitted.  
    Data processing type consists of three items: Tracking Buffer data, Picking order, and Downstream limit picking. As the following table shows, more than one items can be enabled at the same time.

    | Setting value | Tracking Buffer data | Picking order | Downstream limit picking |
    | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    | 1 | Enabled | - | - |
    | 2 | - | Enabled | - |
    | 3 | Enabled | Enabled | - |
    | 4 | - | - | Enabled |
    | 5 | Enabled | - | Enabled |
    | 6 | - | Enabled | Enabled |
    | 7 | Enabled | Enabled | Enabled |
    | -1 | - | - | - |

    The table below shows the functions of each item.

    | Mode | Setting | Description |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Tracking Buffer data | Enabled | Copied work data will be used. The original work data in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) remains. |
    | Disabled | Work data in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) will be deleted once the work data is taken out of the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
    | Picking order | Enabled | Retrieve the data within the tracking buffer in order from the beginning. |
    | Disabled | Retrieve the data within the tracking buffer in order from the end. |
    | Downstream limit picking | Enabled | Work data that has passed the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange) is included in the picking target.  This function is used to perform tracking operation with long object whose length is larger than the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange). |
    | Disabled | Work data that has passed the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange) is not included in the picking target. |

Remaining time
:   Specify the traveling time to the downstream limit by [integer type](000451.html) data. Unit is [msec].  
    The conveyor range calculated from this value and the current conveyor speed will be excluded from the search area.  
    If "-1" is entered, the whole tracking area will be the search area. This entry is omittable. If there is no entry, "-1" will be set automatically.  
    This function is available in Ver.2.3.\* or higher.

### Return Value

The conveyor reference position based on the currently selected work coordinate and tool coordinate is returned with [position type](000456.html) data.  
This data indicates the [conveyor reference position](002221.html#conveyorBase) that is perpetual position.  
This data is used as the target position of "[TrackMove](005356.html)" command and as the reference position of "[TrackApproach](005346.html)" command.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005353_1.png)

## Description

From the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), take out workdata which positions are within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).  
Obtained workdata is set as [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork). If specified workdata does not exist in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), program stops in the line until the [time-out time](#timeout) specified in the second argument elapses.  
If [time-out period](#timeout) passes, Level 1 error will occur.

## Related Terms

[TrackBufferDelete](005671.html),
[TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html),
[TrackBufferRead](005492.html),
[TrackCount](005347.html),
[TrackCurStartArea](002225.html),
[TrackInRange](005355.html),
[TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html),
[TrackSetSensor](005375.html),
[TrackSetVision](005376.html),
[TrackStartArea](005490.html),
[TrackTargetRelease](005567.html),
[Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

* This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.
* This command sorts the data in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), therefore storing too many data in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) will take longer time to return the value.
* If a workpiece is detected by the vision and is registered with [TrackSetVision](005376.html) after the same workpiece has already been selected from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) with TrackTargetPos, the workpiece will be registered as the different workpiece. Please take into consideration this point if the range of TrackTargetPos overlaps with the vision area.

## Example

```
P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1, -1, 1)
```

Wait indefinitely until workdata of userdata 1 on the Conveyor 1 is taken out from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

```
P[10] = TrackTargetPos(1, -1, -1, 1, 1000)
```

Workpiece which remaining time to the downstream limit is less than 1000 milliseconds is not selected as a target workpiece.

# TrackInitialize

## Function

Initializes the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), then starts trigger detection.  
Executing this command to a slave robot connects it to the master robot when you use the conveyor tracking system with coordinated multiple robots.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackInitialize Conveyor number,Initializing mode
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specifies the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
     (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Initializing mode
:   Specifies initializing mode by [integer type](000451.html) data.

    | Controller | Setting value | Description |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Master | 0 | Initializes the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) of the designated conveyor, then starts trigger detection. |
    | 1 | Starts the trigger detection of designated conveyor.  (This option is available in Ver.1.12.1 or higher.) |
    | -1 | Stops the trigger detection of designated conveyor. |
    | Slave | 0 | Disconnect the communication with the master controller, and then establish the connection again. |
    | -1 | This is not supported. An error will occur if it is executed. |

## Description

* Tracking with a single robot

  The function initializes the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) and starts *trigger detection*.
* Tracking with multiple robots

  The function operates differently in the master robot and a slave robot when the command is executed to them.

  + For the master robot, it initializes the tracking buffer and operates to start trigger detection.
  + For a slave robot, it connects the slave robot to the master controller.

Execute the command to all the robots intended to perform the tracking motion before starting the motion.

## Related Terms

[TrackEncoder](005494.html), [TrackSetSensor](005375.html), [TrackSetVision](005376.html), [TrackTargetPos](005353.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

* This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.
* The command is not executable while the robot is running.
* If the command is not executed, the following problems occur.
  + The master robot will experience the error [0x81201213: I/O state is not changed] when the TrackSetVision command or the TrackSetSensor command is executed.
  + A slave robot may experience delays in processing tracking commands, which affects the cycle time.

## Example

* Tracking with a single robot or the master controller

```
'!TITLE "Preparation for conveyor tracking"

  Sub Main 

    ' It initializes the buffer of the conveyor 1 and starts trigger detection of signals from the sensor.
    TrackInitialize 1, 0

  End Sub
```

* Tracking with two robots, using the dual arm control function

```
'!TITLE "Preparation for conveyor tracking"

  Sub Main 

    ' It initializes the buffer of the conveyor 1, and Robot 0 starts trigger detection of signals from the sensor.
    Robot0.TrackInitialize 1, 0
    ' The slave robot (Robot 1) connects to the master robot (Robot 0).
    Robot1.TrackInitialize 1, 0

  End Sub
```

# TrackInRange

## Function

Check whether the current position of the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackInRange (Conveyor number[, Offset value[, Downstream limit check]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Offset value
:   Specify the offset distance by [double-precision real number](000453.html).   
    Conveyor tracking is expressed in units of [mm]; circular tracking (Ver.2.3.\* or higher) is expressed in units of [deg].   
    Specifying positive values will offset in the [conveyor vector](002221.html#conveyorVec) direction, and specifying negative values will offset in the opposite of the [conveyor vector](002221.html#conveyorVec) direction.  
    Offset value is the distance from the datum point on the workpiece that have been determined at the conveyor calibration.  
    This value determines a point on the workpiece that is used to determine whether the workpiece exists within the tracking range.   
    If the offset value is "0", the workpiece is judged as "within the tracking range" when the said datum point is located in the tracking range.  
    This is omittable. This should be "0" if it is omitted. This entry is available in Ver.1.10.\* or higher.

Downstream limit check
:   Set the downstream limit check on the tracking range.  
    If this option is enabled, the workpieces that exist between the upstream and the downstream limits of the tracking range are tracked. To enable this option, specify VARIANT\_TRUE(-1).  
    If this option is disabled, all workpieces that exist on the downstream from the upstream limit of the tracking range are tracked. To disable this option, specify VARIANT\_FALSE(0).   
    This is omittable. This should be VARIANT\_FALSE(0) if it is omitted.  
    If this option is disabled, note that it is impossible to distinguish whether a workpiece exists between upstream and downstream limits or exists in the downstream of the downstream limit. This entry is available in Ver.1.12.1 or higher.

### Return Value

An [integer type](000451.html) data is returned.  
If the position specified by the offset value is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange), a value other than "0" (True) is returned. If the position is out of the tracking range, "0" (false) is returned.

## Description

Check if the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) specified by [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).  
Combining this command with "[Wait](000218.html)" command will suspend a task until a [tracking-target work piece](002221.html#targetWork) enters the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005355_1.png)

## Related Terms

[TrackStartArea](005490.html),
[TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html),
[TrackStandByPos](005352.html),
[TrackCurPos](005348.html),
[TrackCount](005347.html),
[TrackArrivalTime](005351.html),
[Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html)、[Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

Wait until the current position of the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) enters the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

```
Wait TrackInRange(1)
```

Wait until the position of 500 mm upstream from the current position of [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) enters the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

```
Wait TrackInRange(1, -500)
```
