# Parameter Setting

This section describes the parameter setting procedure.

## Parameter Setting Procedure

###### 1 Displaying Detail Setting Window

Press [F12 Detail] on the "Tracking" window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005487_1.png)

Conveyor Tracking window is displayed.

###### 2 Selecting Setting Item

Select an item to set, then press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005487_2.png)

###### 3 Changing Setting Value

Input parameters with the numeric keypad, then press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005487_3.png)

## Parameter List

The parameters described in the table below are not configured automatically in the Detail window.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Tracking Start Range | Refer to the corresponding item of "[Terminology and Definitions](002221.html#ofstMargin)".  Enter a negative value to offset to the upstream direction. |
| Minimum Interval between workpieces (sensor) | This is a threshold value which prevents duplicate data of the work that already exits in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) from being registered by TrackSetSensor command. |
| Low pass filter TC for conveyor pulse | This controls a sudden fluctuation of value by filtering the input value form the encoder.  Setting a value too high lowers the responsiveness to the fluctuation of input value. |
| speed proportional gain | Use this parameter when catch up accuracy of robot deteriorates when the speed of conveyor is increased.  When the robot cannot catch up the workpiece, set this value higher than 1.  When the robot overpasses the workpiece, set this value lower than 1. |
| Stationary deviation compensation | Use this parameter when the robot catches up the workpiece always with a certain amount of shift.  Specify the value with a positive value [mm] when the robot cannot catch up the workpiece.  Specify the value with a negative value [mm] when the robot overpasses the workpiece.  If the stationary deviation compensation is set to a large positive value, the robot may move at a speed faster than the specified external speed to catch up with the conveyor. |

# Parameter Setting

This section describes the parameter setting procedure.

## Parameter Setting Procedure

###### 1 Displaying Detail Setting Window

Press [F12 Detail] in the [Tracking] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005488_1.png)

The [Conveyor Tracking] window appears.

###### 2 Selecting Setting Items

Select an item to set, and press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005488_2.png)

###### 3 Changing Setting Values

Input parameter values using the numeric keypad, and press [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005488_3.png)

## Parameter List

The parameters described in the table below are not configured automatically in the [Detail] window.

| Parameter name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Tracking start range | Refer to the corresponding item of "[Terminology and Definitions](002221.html#ofstMargin)".   Enter a negative value to offset to the upstream direction. |
| Minimum Interval between workpieces (Vision Sensor) | This is a threshold value to prevent the TrackSetVision command from registering data that overlaps with the workpiece existing in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
| Low pass filter TC for conveyor pulse | This controls a sudden fluctuation of value by filtering the input value from the encoder.   Setting a value too high decreases the responsiveness to fluctuations in the input value. |
| Speed proportional gain | Use this parameter when catch up accuracy of robot deteriorates when the speed of conveyor is increased.   When the robot cannot catch up with a workpiece, set this value higher than 1.   When the robot overtakes a workpiece, set this value lower than 1. |
| Stationary deviation compensation | Use this parameter when the robot catches up the workpiece always with a certain amount of shift.   Specify a positive value [mm] when the robot cannot catch up with a workpiece.   Specify a negative value [mm] when the robot overtakes a workpiece.  If the stationary deviation compensation is set to a large positive value, the robot may move at a speed faster than the specified external speed to catch up with the conveyor. |

# TrackOffsetMargin

## Function

In order to define the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin), specify the offset value from the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackOffsetMargin Conveyor number, Offset value
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specifies the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Offset value
:   Specify an offset value from the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange) that is used to define the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin). The value is specified with negative value of [double-precision real type](000453.html.) data.  
    If positive value is specified, the offset is set to the downstream side.  
    The unit is [mm] for conveyor tracking and [deg] for circular tracking (Ver.2.3.\* or higher).

## Description

In order to define the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin), specify the offset value from the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005489_1.png)

## Related Terms

[TrackMinimumIntervalLength](005794.html), [TrackStartArea](005490.html), [TrackCurStartArea](002225.html), [TrackTargetPos](005353.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

* This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.
* Avoid overlapping the shooting area and the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin).  
  Registration overlapping prevention function, which prevents multiple registration of an identical workpiece, is set by the parameter setting of "[Minimum Interval between workpieces (sensor)](005487.html)". This function is effective only when the target workpiece has already existed within the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) area.  
  If the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin) is overlapped with the shooting area, a workpiece data which has been registered in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) may be immediately taken out as a [tracking-target workpiece](002221.html#targetWork) data.  
  In this case, the workpiece that has been taken out from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) may be counted in the buffer area again because the sensor cannot distinguish the taken-out workpiece and the newly counted one as different workpiece. As a result, the registration overlapping prevention function cannot work properly, leading to the unintentional re-registration of workpieces.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005489_2.png)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005489_3.png)

## Example

```
TrackStratArea 1, 500, 800
TrackOffsetMargin 1, -100
```

In this example, the [tracking start range](002221.html#ofstMargin) is 100 mm upstream of the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).

# TrackStartArea

## Function

Configures the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackStartArea Conveyor number, The upstream limit of the tracking range,  
               The downstream limit of the tracking range
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specifies the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

The upstream limit of the tracking range
:   Specifies by [integer type](000451.html) data.

The downstream limit of the tracking range
:   Specifies by [integer type](000451.html) data.

## Description

Set the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange) and [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange).  
When setting the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange), you need to take the conveyor speed and the maximum reach of the robot arm into consideration.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005490_1.png)

## Related Terms

[TrackArrivalTime](005351.html),
[TrackCount](005347.html),
[TrackCurPos](005348.html),
[TrackCurStartArea](002225.html),
[TrackInRange](005355.html),
[TrackOffsetMargin](005489.html),
[TrackStandByPos](005352.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

Set the value of the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange) at 500mm and the value of the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange) at 800mm.

```
TrackStartArea 1, 500, 800
```

# TrackBufferIndexes

## Function

Take out index numbers of data stored in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), and then return them as an array.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackBufferIndexes (Conveyor number [, Count object [, userdata ]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specifies the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Count object
:   Specify data that you intend to obtain by [integer type](000451.html). This is omittable. This will be "-1" if it is omitted.

    | Setting value | Description |
    | --- | --- |
    | -1 | All data |
    | 1 | Read the data specified as a [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) in [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) command.  To perform this operation, [Tracking Buffer Data](005353.html#Mode1) of the fourth argument of "[TrackTargetPos](005353.html)" must be enabled and the [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) data must remain in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
    | 2 | All data except for the data specified by the above "setting value 1".  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher. |
    | 3 | Data whose workpiece's current position is upper than the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher. |
    | 4 | Data whose workpiece's current position is lower than the [upstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackURange).  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher. |
    | 5 | Data whose workpiece's current position is upper than the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange).  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher. |
    | 6 | Data whose workpiece's current position is lower than the [downstream limit of the tracking range](002221.html#trackLRange).  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher. |
    | 7 | Data whose workpiece's current position is within the [tracking range](002221.html#trackRange).  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher. |

Userdata
:   Specify userdata by [integer type](000451.html). User data is not judged when you enter a negative value.  
    This is omittable. This will be "-1" if it is omitted.
    This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\* or higher.

### Return Value

Return the index numbers of the specified target data or user data as one dimensional array of [variant type](005067.html) data.  
If the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) is empty, [variant type](005067.html) data whose internal processing format is "[VT\_EMPTY(0)](005527.html)" will be returned.

| Count object | User data | Return value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pos. | Neg. / No | Return the index number of the specified count object regardless of the user data. |
| Pos. | Pos. | Return the index number of count object specified that belongs to the specified user data. |
| None / -1 | Neg. / No | Return the index number of data within the tracking buffer. |
| None / -1 | Pos. | Return the index number of data in the tracking buffer that belongs to the specified user data. |

Pos. : Positive value entry  
None / -1 : No value entry or "-1" is entered.  
Neg. / No : Negative value entry or no entry.

## Description

From the data stored in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), extract the index numbers that correspond to the specified target data or user data, and then return them as an array. To refer the data with [TrackBufferRead](005492.html) command, use the number obtained and specify the tracking buffer data.

## Related Terms

[TrackBufferDelete](005671.html),
[TrackBufferRead](005492.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html),
[TrackTargetRelease](005567.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

```
Sub Main 

  ' Take out index numbers of all data
  Dim vIndex as Variant    
  vIndex = TrackBufferIndexes(1, -1)
 
  Dim idx as long   
  For idx = LBound(vIndex) To UBound(vIndex)

    'Obtain data specified by tracking buffer by means of the index number    
    Dim vVal as Variant
    vVal = TrackBufferRead(1, vIndex(idx), -1)
                            
    ' Data output  
    PrintDbg "enc=" & vVal(0), _
             "x=" & vVal(1), _
             "y=" & vVal(2), _
             "z=" & vVal(3), _
             "rx=" & vVal(4), _
             "ry=" & vVal(5), _
             "rz=" & vVal(6)
    
  Next
      
End sub
```

The example below shows the case that the process differs depending on whether the element is empty or not.

```
#include "variant.h"

Sub Main

  ' Take out index numbers of all data
　Dim vIndex as Variant
　vIndex = TrackBufferIndexes(1, -1)

  If VarType(vIndex) = VT_EMPTY then
    ' The process where the element is empty
 
'･･･
  ElseIf VarType(vIndex) And VT_ARRAY then
    ' Process in case the elements are not empty (elements constitutes an array).
    If ( UBound( vIndex ) <> -1 ) then
      ' Check that the number of element is not 0, and then read out the data.
      ' Obtain data specified by tracking buffer by means of the index number
      Dim vVal as Variant
      vVal = TrackBufferRead(1, UBound( vIndex ), -1)
'･･･
    End If
'･･･
  End If

End Sub
```

# TrackBufferRead

## Function

From the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), read out specified data.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackBufferRead (Conveyor number, Index number [, Option])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1 to 16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
     (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Index number
:   Specify the Index number obtained by the [TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html) command by [integer type](000451.html) data.

    | Setting value | Description |
    | --- | --- |
    | -1 | Read the data specified as a [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) in [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) command.  This entry is available for Ver.2.0.\*. or higher. |
    | 0 or larger | Read the specified index number. |

Option
:   Specify by [integer type](000451.html) data. The content of return value can be selected. This is an optional value. This should be "-1" if this is omitted.

    | Setting value | Return value | |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | -2 | An array of variant type data corresponding to setting values 0 to 14 (\*1) (Ver. 1.10.\* or higher.) | |
    | -1 | An array of variant type data corresponding to setting values 0 to 10 (\*1) | |
    | 0 | Encoder value at the trigger detection ([integer type](000451.html) data) | |
    | 1 | Current position of the target workpiece. ([Position type](000456.html) data)  (Values are based on the currently selected work coordinate or tool coordinate.) | X[mm] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 2 | Y[mm] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 3 | Z[mm] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 4 | Rx[deg] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 5 | Ry[deg] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 6 | Rz[deg] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 7 | User data ([integer type](000451.html) data) | |
    | 8 | Values are based on the [vision sensor detection coordinate](002221.html#visionCoordinate) of the target workpiece.  (Ver. 1.7.\* or higher.) | X-coordinate[pixel] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 9 | Y-coordinate[pixel] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 10 | Posture angle[deg] ([Single Precision Real Number Type](000452.html) data) |
    | 11 | Attribute data ([integer type](000451.html) data) (Ver. 1.10.\* or higher.) | |
    | 12 | The remaining time until the arrival of the target workpiece at the downstream limit ([integer type](000451.html) data) [msec] (Ver. 2.3.\* or higher.) | |
    | 13 | The distance between the target workpiece and the downstream limit ([integer type](000451.html) data) (Ver. 2.5.\* or higher.) | |
    | 14 | The amount of movement of the target workpiece from the vision sensor detection position to the workpiece's position where the camera captures an image. (\*2) ([integer type](000451.html) data) (Ver. 2.21.2 or higher.) | |

:   \* 1: If the robot controller’s version is old, content unsupported by the version is not available.
:   (Example1) The robot controller with Ver.1.6.\* or lower can obtain only the return values corresponding to the setting values 0 to 7.
:   (Example2) The robot controller with Ver.1.7.\* to Ver.1.10.\* can obtain only the return values corresponding to the setting values 0 to 11.  
    \*2: This is a setting value for vision tracking. In sensor tracking, 0 is always returned.

### Return Value

Values specified by "[Option](#optionSet)" are returned with [variant type](005067.html) data.  
 If the data specified by "[Index number](#indexNo)" does not exist in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf), [variant type](005067.html) data whose [VarType](005519.html) command result is [VT\_EMPTY(0)](005527.html) will be returned.

## Description

Read the data specified by the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf) by means of the index number obtained by the [TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html) command.

## Related Terms

[TrackBufferDelete](005671.html), [TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html), [TrackSetSensor](005375.html), [TrackSetVision](005376.html), [TrackTargetPos](005353.html), [TrackTargetRelease](005567.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

Obtain a one-dimensional array of data Index number stored in the tracking buffer.

```
Dim vIndex as Variant
vIndex = TrackBufferIndexes(1)
```

From the one dimensional array, take out index numbers one by one, and then refer to and output all data of target index.

```
Dim idx as long
For idx = LBound(vIndex) To UBound(vIndex)
  Dim vVal as Variant  
  vVal = TrackBufferRead( 1, vIndex(idx) ,-2)

  PrintDbg "enc=" & vVal(0), _
             "x=" & vVal(1), _
             "y=" & vVal(2), _
             "z=" & vVal(3), _
            "rx=" & vVal(4), _
            "ry=" & vVal(5), _
            "rz=" & vVal(6), _
           "usr=" & vVal(7), _
            "vx=" & vVal(8), _
            "vy=" & vVal(9), _
            "θ=" & vVal(10), _
          "attr=" & vVal(11)
Next
```

From the one dimensional array, take out index numbers one by one, and then refer to and output userdata of applicable index.

```
Dim idx as long
For idx = LBound(vIndex) To UBound(vIndex)
  Dim vVal as Variant  
  vVal = TrackBufferRead( 1, vIndex(idx), 7 )
  PrintDbg "usr=" & vVal
Next
```

From the one dimensional array, take out index numbers one by one, and then refer to and output attribute data of applicable index.

```
Dim idx as long
For idx = LBound(vIndex) To UBound(vIndex)
  Dim vVal as Variant  
  vVal = TrackBufferRead( 1, vIndex(idx), 11 )
  PrintDbg "attr=" & vVal
Next
```

Obtain the remaining time until the arrival of the workpiece which Index number is 5 at the downstream limit.

```
I[0] = TrackBufferRead(1, 5, 12)
```

Obtain the distance between the specified workpiece and the downstream limit.

```
Dim restLength As Float
restLength = TrackBufferRead (1, -1, 13)
```

# TrackTargetOffset

## Function

Set the value for the "Minimum Interval Length of Work Detection", which is a parameter for the conveyor or circular tracking.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackTargetOffset Conveyor number, Offset distance of the steady-state deviation
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [Integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Offset distance of the steady-state deviation
:   Specify by [double precision real number type](000453.html) data.The unit is [mm] for conveyor tracking and [deg] for circular tracking
    (Ver.2.3.\* or higher).

## Description

Set the value for the "Minimum Interval Length of Work Detection", which is a parameter for the conveyor or circular tracking.  
This is used when the robot always follows workpieces with a specified distance away from them.  
Specify by plus value [mm] if the robot cannot pick workpieces.  
Specify by minus value [mm] if the robot passes workpieces.

## Related Terms

[TrackApproach](005346.html),
[TrackDepart](005350.html),
[TrackMove](005356.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html),
[Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html), Parameter Setting Screen (Sensor Tracking([Conveyor](005487.html#MinInterval), [Circular](002877.html#MinInterval)), Vision Tracking([Conveyor](005488.html#MinInterval), [Circular](002888.html#MinInterval)))

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

```
TrackTargetOffSet 1, 10
```

In this example, the target is offset downstream by 10mm.

# TrackEncoder

## Function

Obtain the encoder value of the conveyor or the turntable.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackEncoder (Conveyor number, Mode)
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specify the conveyor number (1-16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Mode
:   Specifies by [integer type](000451.html) data.

    | Setting value | Description |
    | --- | --- |
    | 0 | Obtain the encoder value of the currently used conveyor. |
    | 1 | Obtain the conveyor's encoder value that has been stored at the workpiece detection. |

### Return Value

Return the encoder value of the conveyor or the turntable by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

| Mode | Retuen Value |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Obtain the encoder value of the currently used conveyor. |
| 1 | Obtain the conveyor's encoder value that has been stored at the workpiece detection.  This error will be issued when a workpiece has not been detected.  Even if a workpiece has been detected, an error will be issued when this command is executed after [TrackSetSensor](005375.html) or [TrackSetVision](005376.html) command execution. |

## Description

Obtain the encoder value of the conveyor or the turntable.

## Related Terms

[TrackBufferRead](005492.html),
[TrackInitialize](005354.html), [TrackSetSensor](005375.html),
[TrackSetVision](005376.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

```
-
```

# CONTROLLER PROTECTIVE BOX MANUAL

This manual describes the specifications and usage of the controller protective box and the controller protective box Light.

The controller protective box and the controller protective box Light are optional parts for robot controller. Both of them will protect your robot controller from dust and oil.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Robot controller models | RC8A, RC8 |

The following link destination pages describe the above-mentioned information.

| Title (link destination) | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Controller Protective Box](003447.html) | This product supports RC8 series robot controller.  It will protect your robot controller from dust and oil. |
| [Controller Protective Box Light](003437.html) | This product supports the RC8 series robot controller.   It will protect your robot controller from dust and oil.  (The following models or applications are not supported: VM series, the combination use of VS-068 and Extended-joint, the combination use of VS-087 and extended-joint, MC (total motor capacity is 2000W or higher)). |

To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html) ".

# Overview

The controller protective box and the controller protective box Light, which are equivalent to IP54, are optional parts to protect a controller from dust and fluid by containing a controller. (excluding UL-Listed model)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005497_1.png)

Both controller protective boxes can contain the encoder hub, which is an optional part of controller, as well.

# Specifications

The table below lists the specifications of the controller protective box.

| Item | | Specifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Applicable controller | | RC8 series robot controller (The controller equipped with an I/O conversion box is also applicable.) \*2 |
| Environmental conditions (Temperature and humidity) | In operation | 0 to 40 ℃, 20 to 90% RH (dew condensation not allowed) |
| In storage or during transportation | -10 to 60 ℃, 40 to 75% RH (dew condensation not allowed) |
| Enclosure | | Equivalent to IP54 |
| Installation Type | | Stand-alone Installation \*3 |
| Weight (Mass) | | Approx. 26 kg (RC8 series robot controller is not included) |
| Power supply \*1 | Three-phase | AC185-253 V(AC200 V-7 %～AC230 V+10 %) |
| Single-phase | AC207-253 V(AC230 V±10 %) |
| Heat exchanger | Fans | Internal fan and external fan  External fan: 4715HS-23W-B50-AM0 (Manufactured by Minebea Co.,Ltd)  Internal fan : 4715MS-23W-B50-A00 (Manufactured by Minebea Co.,Ltd) |
| Cooling power | 35 W/K (temperature change 1 ℃ , calculated value) |
| Power supply | Supplied from the controller power and branched by the protective box-incorporated terminal.  Power supply capacity: 0.15KVA |

\*1: The power supply of the controller protective box, unlike that of the controller.

\*2: Not contained in UL-Listed controller.

\*3: Do not place the controller vertically.

# Precautions for Use

1. The controller protective box is a dust- and splash-proof structure equivalent to IP54. However, it has not been designed to withstand explosions, so avoid installing the protective box in any environment where:  
   - there are any flammable gases or liquids,  
   - there are any acidic, alkaline or other corrosive gases,  
   - there are any large-sized inverters, high output/high frequency transmitters, large contactors, welders, or other sources of electrical noise,  
   - the ambient temperature is out of the range from 0°C to 40°C,  
   - the protective box is directly exposed to rains,  
   - the protective box is directly exposed to water, oil, grinding chips or shavings,  
   - there are any grinding or machining chips or shavings.
2. Clean the filter once for two weeks.
3. In the event of water ingress into the controller protective box due to the sealing performance deterioration of the rubber packing, remove the drain hall screws to drain water.
4. The controller protective box has no power switch, so externally turn the controller power on and off.
5. To reduce the risk of electric shock, observe the following precautions.  
   - Do not supply power from the facilities during wiring, controller connection, and controller disconnection.  
   - Do not open the top plate and the rear cover during energizing.  
   - Do not touch the inside parts within 6 minutes from the power OFF.  
   - Do not touch the power terminals (circled area in the image below) during other than wiring operation.  
   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005500_1.png)
6. Using voltage beyond the specified range may damage the controller protective box or reduce the lifetime.
7. If an abnormal temperature is detected, check that whether the internal fan and the external fan of the controller protective box works correctly.
8. Fans are installed in the backside and the inside of the controller protective box.  
   To avoid injury, do not insert fingers or any objects into the fans.

# Preparation of the Power Cable

To connect the power cable shipped with the controller to the controller protective box, you need to process cables as shown below.

The power supply of the controller protective box, unlike that of the controller, does not support 100V and 240V.

###### 1

Cut the cable at a point about 330 mm from the connector end.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_1_1.png)

###### 2

Remove the 60 mm of the outer jacket. (2 parts)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_2_1.png)

###### 3

Remove the 6 mm of outer jackets of each line, then pass the cables through insulation tubes. (8 parts)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_3_1.png)

###### 4

Attach ring terminals to each end, then move the insulation tubes to the position shown below. (8 parts)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005503_4_1.png)

# Storing of the Controller

This section describes the process to store a controller in the controller protective box and to connect wires.

Before operation, make sure that there is no power supply from the facilities.

The following uses RC8 standard specification controller as an example.

Recommended torque : M3:0.6N･m, M4:1.5N･m, M5:3N･m

###### 1

To remove the top panel, unscrew 12 of M4 screws on the top surface.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_1.png)

###### 2

Remove two cable multi-outlet plates, marked by red circles (solid line) in the image below.

Remove six M5 screws for one cable multi-outlet plate.

To use 13 cables or more, remove the cable multi-outlet plate marked by a red circle (broken line) in the image below, as well.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_2.png)

###### 3

Remove the terminal board cover. Lay prepared power cable with M4 screws as shown below.

For the preparation of cables, see "[Preparation of the power cable](005503.html)".

Once the power cable is laid, put the terminal board cover back in place.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_3.png)

###### 4

To use an encoder hub (option part), tighten the encoder hub with four of M4 screws marked by red circles in the image below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_4.png)

###### 5

Attach the left bracket (small) and the right bracket (mounted on the controller protective box) to the left side and right side of the RC8, respectively. Tighten the brackets with M4 screws, marked by six of red circles on the image below.

| Left side of the RC8 | Right side of the RC8 |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |

For the safety I/O less specification, attach the left bracket (large) to the left side of the RC8 as shown below.

| Left side of the RC8 |
| --- |
|  |

###### 6

Connect the FG harness to the earthing point, marked by red circles (solid line) in the image below.![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_8_1.png)

The image below shows the standard specification controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_9.png)

###### 7

Tighten eight of mounting holes on the bracket with M5 screws.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_10.png)

The image below shows the safety I/O less specification controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_11.png)

###### 8

Pass cables through the cable multi-outlet plates which was removed in the STEP2. Attach the plates to the RC8.

For information on how to attach the cable multi-outlet plates, see "[Clamping the Cables](005505.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_12.png)

###### 9

Remove two of M4 screws close to the terminal board. Tighten the FG harness which was mounted in the STEP5 and the FG harness of the motor & encoder cable, by each screws, respectively.

Do not tighten two harnesses together.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005504_13.png)

###### 10

Put the top plate back in place with 12 of M4 screws which was removed in the STEP1.

# Clamp the Cables

This section describes the process to clamp cables with the cable multi-outlet plate.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005505_1.png)

###### 1

Install rubber packings in the ditches of the corner plate and the middle plate.

* Rubber Packing Set

| Model | Application cable dia | Application |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EMSP0 | - | To be used as a blind cover |
| EMSP4 | φ4-φ6 | Communication cable |
| EMSP6 | φ6-φ8 | Pendant cable, Hand I/O cable |
| EMSP8 | φ8-φ10 | Mini I/O cable |
| EMSP10 | φ10-φ12 | Extended parallel I/O cable |

* Rubber Packing Set for Extended-Joint Cables

| Model | Application cable dia | Application |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EMSP8 | φ8-φ10 | Extended-joint encoder cable |
| EMSP12 | φ12-φ14 | Extended-joint motor cable |

Note the following points when installing the EMS packings on the plates.

* Install the EMS packings in the ditches in order starting from both ends of the ditches to the center. (Figure 1)
* Ensure that the ends of the packing seal strings mounted on the plates are neither lifted up by nor caught in the installed EMS packings. (Figure 2)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005505_2.png)![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005505_3.png)

###### 2

Pass the M5 bolts through the hex holes so that the head of bolts go under the hole.

###### 3

Pass the cables through the holes between the corner plate and the middle plate. Adjust both plates to the vertical direction.

###### 4

Attach the M5 nuts to the M5 bolts.

###### 5

Tighten the corner plate and the middle plate with a spanner until no space remains between the plates.

###### 6

Pass the cables through the holes between the middle plate and the corner plate. Adjust both plates to the vertical direction.

###### 7

Attach M5 nuts to the M5 bolts.

###### 8

Tighten the middle plate and the corner plates with a spanner until no space remains between the plates.

###### 9

Pass the cables through the rectangular openings of the controller protective box. Tighten them from the front side with the M6 screws.

# Overview

Mounting a PROFINET IO Device board in the robot controller enables the controller to easily exchange I/O data with PROFINET-compliant network devices. This function is available in Ver.1.6.4 or higher.

For details about PROFIBUS, refer to the PROFIBUS website as shown below.

* PROFIBUS International  
  Home page : <http://www.profibus.com/>

## Operating Environment

To use a PROFINET IO Device board, you need to prepare an expansion board (PROFINET IO Device board) and a function expansion license certificate. For details, refer to "[Options for Robot Controller](001971.html)" and "[Optional Function and License](005476.html)".

> ### Expansion Board
>
> The table below lists the configuration of PROFINET IO Device board.
>
> PROFINET IO Device board is installed in a PCIe slot which is one of an expansion slot in the robot controller. Mini-I/O connector kit is used as an input signal of the safety circuit.

| No. | Components | Remarks | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | PROFINET IO device board  (including No. 2) | Product form ;  • Shipped after mounted on the controller with license  • Shipped separately as a spare part with license  • Shipped separately as a spare part without license | | |
| 2 | Mini I/O connector kit | Connector : PCR-E68FS (Manufactured by HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO CO., LTD.)  Connector cover : PCS-E68LPA-1E (Manufactured by HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO CO., LTD.) | | |
| NPN-type | [Pin assignment](005535.html) | [Configuration of Safety Circuit](001373.html) |
| PNP-type | [Pin assignment](005536.html) | [Configuration of Safety Circuit](001380.html) |
|  | | | | |

### Software License for Function Expansion

To enable the optional function on the robot controller, you need to purchase a license certificate.

| Component |
| --- |
| License certificate for PROFINET IO Device board |

* A license certificate is sold with an expansion board as a set, or is sold individually.
* To purchase a license, a serial number of the robot controller is required.

# Specifications

The table below shows the specifications of the PROFINET on the RC8 series robot controller. For about the specification of the PROFINET IO Device board unit, refer to the instruction manual of the PROFINET IO Device board.

| Item | Specifications | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Communications protocol | PROFINET IO-compliant | | |
| Transmission speed | 10M, 100M (bps) | | |
| Realtime communication | RT | | |
| Support protocol | DCP, SNMP | | |
| Interface connector | RJ-45 connector | | |
| Communications media | Category 5 or above, twisted pair cable | | |
|  | Standard allocation | RC3 Compatible allocation | All-user allocation |
| Number of system inputs | 40 points | 24 points | 0 points |
| Number of system outputs | 32 points | 32 points | 0 points |
| Number of user inputs | 216 to 8152 points | 232 to 8168 points | 8192 points |
| Number of user outputs | 224 to 8160 points | 224 to 8160 points | 8192 points |

# I/O Allocation

I/O port range allocated to the PROFINET IO device is;  
Input: 512-767, 4096-7871, 11648-15807  
Output: 768-1023, 7872-11647, 19904-24063

For other port numbers, refer to [I/O Port Map and Allocation](001328.html).

For available allocations, see "[Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode](001325.html)".

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Standard allocation | [Input Data](005513.html) |
| [Output Data](005514.html) |
| RC3 Compatible allocation | [Input Data](005515.html) |
| [Output Data](005516.html) |

## I/O Port Number corresponding to Input module and Output module

The range of available I/O port number varies depending on the input module and output module settings.

I/O port numbers corresponding to each module are assigned as described in the figure below. From the lowest number of the input port or output port, eight times of the module's byte count are assigned.

![Allocation](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005512_1.png)

# SwapByteArray

## Function

In a one-dimensional array with byte type, change the order of elements according to the byte counts specified.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
SwapByteArray(Variable,Data size,Number of data [,Initial number of element to rearrangement ])
```

### Guaranteed entry

Variable
:   Specify variables to be rearranged by [Variant type](005067.html) data which [Internal processing format](005067.html) is a one-dimensional array of byte type.

Data size
:   Specify the byte count of data rearranged by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

Number of data
:   Specify the number of data by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

Initial number of element to rearrangement
:   Specify an element number which starts the rearrangement by [Integer type](000451.html) data. This is an optional value. This should be "0" if it is omitted.

### Return value

Return the byte count of data rearranged.

## Description

Reverse the order of elements by byte counts specified by the Data size. This function is useful when you change the endianness of data.

The following figure shows an example of SwapByteArray command execution. Each variable is set to Data size= 4, Number of data=3, and Initial number of elements to rearrangement=4.

![SwapByteArray](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005518_1.png)

## Related Terms

[CreateArray](000583.html), [WriteByteArray](005522.html), [ReadByteArray](005523.html), [Comm.Input](000373.html), [Comm.Output](000372.html)

## Attention

-

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Change endianness"
'Change the endianness of variables I[0] and I[1],   
'and then send the binary data of these variables changed. 

#include <Variant.h>

Sub Main
  Dim varData as Variant
  Dim Index as integer
 
  varData = CreateArray( LenB(I0) + LenB(I1) )

  Index = 0
  Index = Index + WriteByteArray(I0, varData, Index)
  Index = Index + WriteByteArray(I1, varData, Index)
  
  'Switch two of I-type variables
  SwapByteArray varData, LenB(I0), 2 
 
  Comm.Open 1

  Comm.Output 1, varData

  Comm.Close 1
End Sub
```

ID : 5519

# VarType

## Function

Return a value which represents the [Internal processing format](005067.html) of variables.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
VarType(Variable)
```

### Guaranteed entry

Variable
:   Specify arbitrary variable. All types of variables are available. Numbers and character strings can be specified directly as well.

### Return value

Return the [Internal processing format](005067.html) by [Integer type](000451.html) data. For about values of the [Internal processing format](005067.html), see [Variant.h](005527.html).

## Description

Return the value which represents [Internal processing format](005067.html) of variable.

If a variable is the [Variant type](005067.html) array, the returned value is a sum of the value representing an array and the value representing a data type. For example, if an integer type array is specified as a variable, 8195 will be returned; that is the sum of the integer type (3) and the array (8192).

## Related Terms

[CreateArray](000583.html), [CreateMultiArray](005521.html), [Comm.Input](000373.html), [Comm.Output](000372.html), [Definition of Variant.h](005527.html)

## Attention

-

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Obtain the internal processing format of variable"
'Check that the internal processing format of variable is I-type data

#include <Variant.h>

Sub Main
  Dim varData as Variant

  Comm.Open 1

  varData = Comm.Input(1)
  If VarType( varData ) And (VT_ARRAY Or VT_UI1) Then
    ' If incoming data is byte array data
    ReadByteArray I0, VarData
  End If

  Comm.Close 1   

End Sub
```

# VarChangeType

## Function

Convert the value into [Variant type](005067.html) data with a specified [Internal processing format](005067.html).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
VarChangeType(Variable,Internal processing format)
```

### Guaranteed entry

Variable
:   Specify a value that you intend to convert. Variables and numeric values can be specified.

Internal processing format
:   Specify an [Internal processing format](005067.html) of converted data by [Integer type](000451.html) data. For about values of the [Internal processing format](005067.html) , see [Variant.h](005527.html).

### Return value

Return a [Variant type](005067.html) data which has been converted into the variable type specified by the internal processing format.

## Description

Convert the specified value into the [Variant type](005067.html) data with a specified [Internal processing format](005067.html).

If you use constants, which are defined by [Variant.h](005527.html), for the internal processing format, embed [Variant.h](005527.html) into [#include](000115.html).

## Related Terms

[CreateArray](000583.html), [CreateMultiArray](005521.html), [Definition of Variant.h](005527.html)

## Attention

Some [Internal processing format](005067.html) which is defined by [Variant.h](005527.html), are not available for VarChangeType. If these are used, an error will occur at VarChangeType execution.

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Convert the internal processing format of variables"
'Date calculation

#include <Variant.h>

Sub Main

  Dim varLaptime as Variant

  varLaptime = VarChangeType(now, VT_DATE) - VarChangeType("2013/07/01", VT_DATE)
  PrintDbg format(varLaptime, "Elapsed time hh:mm:ss")

End Sub
```

# CreateMultiArray

## Function

Create [Variant type](005067.html) arrays with arbitrary [Internal processing format](005067.html). Up to three-dimensional arrays can be created.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
CreateMultiArray(Internal processing format,Elements count of one-dimensional array 
[,Elements count of two-dimensional array [,Elements count of three-dimensional array ]])
```

### Guaranteed entry

Internal processing format
:   Specify the [Internal processing format](005067.html) of arrays that you intend to create by [Integer type](000451.html) data. For about values of the [Internal processing format](005067.html), see [Variant.h](005527.html).

Elements count of one-dimensional array
:   Specify the number of elements in the first dimension of the array by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

Elements count of two-dimensional array
:   Specify the number of elements in the second dimension of the array by [Integer type](000451.html) data. This is an optional value. This will be the one-dimensional array if it is omitted.

Elements count of three-dimensional array
:   Specify the number of elements in the third dimension of the array by [Integer type](000451.html) data. This is an optional value. This will be the two-dimensional array if it is omitted.

### Return value

Return the [Variant type](005067.html) array created.

## Description

Create [Variant type](005067.html) arrays with arbitrary [Internal processing format](005067.html). Up to three-dimensional array can be created.

If the elements count of the one-dimensional array assumes “N”, the index number of the array ranges from 0 through “N-1”. This rule applies to the elements counts of two- or three-dimensional arrays as well.

If you use constants, which are defined by [Variant.h](005527.html), for the internal processing format, embed [Variant.h](005527.html) into [#include](000115.html).

## Related Terms

[CreateArray](000583.html), [Definition of Variant.h](005527.html)

## Attention

Some [Internal processing format](005067.html) which is defined by [Variant.h,](005527.html) are not available for CreateMultiArray. If these are used, an error will occur at CreateMultiArray execution.

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Create two- or more dimensional arrays"
'Create two-dimensional arrays and then assign values 

#include <Variant.h>

Sub Main
	Dim var As Variant

	var = CreateMultiArray(VT_R4, 2, 3) 
	var(0, 0) = POSX( P[0] )
	var(0, 1) = POSY( P[0] )
	var(0, 2) = POSZ( P[0] )
	var(1, 0) = POSRX( P[0] )
	var(1, 1) = POSRY( P[0] )
	var(1, 2) = POSRZ( P[0] )

End Sub
```

# WriteByteArray

## Function

This command stores variables into the one-dimensional array ([Variant type](005067.html)) for every one byte. The byte order is not changed when it is stored in the arrays.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
WriteByteArray(Variables to be stored,Destination array
               [,Element number to start storage [,Destination byte count ]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Variables to be stored
:   Specify values to be stored in Destination array. All types of data (except for array variables of [Variant type](005067.html)) can be specified.

Destination array
:   Specify an array of destination by [Variant type](005067.html) data.

Element number to start storage
:   Specify the element number which is stored first at Destination array. Specify the element number by [Integer type](000451.html) data. This is an optional value. This should be "0" if it is omitted.

Destination byte count
:   Specify the byte count of data which is stored in Destination array by [Integer type](000451.html) data. Up to the size (byte count) of variables to be stored can be stored. This is an optional value. This should be "-1" if it is omitted. If "-1" is specified, all the data of Variables to be stored will be stored in Destination array.

### Return Value

Return the byte count of data which has been stored in Destination array by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

## Description

This command stores values of Variables to be stored into Destination array for every one byte. The byte order is not changed when it is stored in the arrays.

The storage starts from the lowest byte of Variables to be stored in ascending order; the highest byte is stored in the last. The lowest byte of Variables to be stored is stored into the lowest element number of Destination array.

Assuming that Variables to be stored is [Integer type](000451.html), and the hexadecimal number &H4030201, which is equal to 67305985 in decimal numbers, is stored; Destination array will store these data in ascending order. Element number 0, 1, 2 and 3 stores the value of 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively.

If the data type that is used in Variables to be stored includes multiple elements, such as [Vector type](000455.html) and [Position type](000456.html), the order of storage complies with the order of elements.

For example, the order of elements in [Vector type](000455.html) is X, Y and Z.
Therefore, the value of “X” is stored at first, and the value of “Z” is stored last. Also, in each element, the lowest byte is stored first and the highest byte is stored at last.

For about elements order of each type, see [Data Types](000450.html).

## Related Terms

[CreateArray](000583.html), [ReadByteArray](005523.html), [Comm.Input](000373.html), [Comm.Output](000372.html), [LenB](005524.html)

## Attention

You do not need to convert Destination array into a one-dimensional array beforehand by means of [CreateArray](000583.html) or other ways.  
Once WriteByteArray is executed, the values of Destination array are converted to a one-dimensional array of byte counts that will be actually stored. And then, the values of converted Destination array are stored.

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Convertion to Byte arrays
'Send binary data of variables I[0] and I[1] as Byte array

Sub Main
  Dim Var as Variant

  Comm.Open 1

  WriteByteArray I[0], Var, 0
  WriteByteArray I[1], Var, 4

  Comm.Output 1, Var

  Comm.Close 1
End Sub
```

# ReadByteArray

## Function

This command stores the values of a one-dimensional array [(Variant type](005067.html)) of a byte unit into the specified variable for every one byte. The byte order of the array is not changed when it is stored in the variable.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
ReadByteArray(Destination variable,Array to be stored 
              [,Element number to start storage [,Destination byte count]])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Destination variable
:   Specify a variable of the destination.
    All types of data (except for array variable of [Variant type](005067.html)) can be specified.

Array to be stored
:   Specify an Array to be stored by [Variant type](005067.html) data ([Internal processing format](005067.html) is a one-dimensional array with byte type).

Element number to start storage
:   Specify an element number in the Array to be stored that is converted first. Specify the element number by  [Integer type](000451.html) data. This is an optional value. This should be "0" if it is omitted.

Destination byte count
:   Specify the byte count of data which is stored in Destination variable by [Integer type](000451.html) data. Up to the size (byte count) of destination variable can be stored. This is an optional value. This should be "-1" if it is omitted. If "-1" is specified, the data is stored in the same byte size of Destination variable.

### Return Value

Return the byte count of data stored in Destination variable by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

## Description

This command stores values of Array to be stored into estination variable for every one byte. The elements order is not changed when it is stored in the variable.

The storage starts from the lowest byte of Array to be stored in ascending order; the highest byte is stored in the last. The lowest byte of Array to be stored is stored into the lowest element number of Destination variable.

Assume that Array to be stored stores value of elements in order of 1, 2, 3 and 4, where the order of elements number is ascending order which starts from the elements number 0. If Destination variable is [Integer type](000451.html), the hexadecimal number &H4030201, which is equal to 67305985 in decimal number, is stored.

If the data type that is used in Destination variable includes multiple elements, such as [Vector type](000455.html) and [Position type](000456.html), the order of storage complies with the order of elements.

For example, the order of elements in [Vector type](000455.html) is X, Y and Z. Therefore, the value of “X” is stored at first, and the value of “Z” is stored last. Within each element, bytes have the order as well; the lowest byte is stored first and the highest byte is stored at last.

For about elements order of each type, see [Data Types](000450.html).

## Related Terms

[CreateArray](000583.html), [WriteByteArray](005522.html), [Comm.Input](000373.html), [Comm.Output](000372.html)

## Attention

-

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Convert data from the Byte array into each variable type"
'Store received binary data into variables I[0] and I[1]

Sub Main
  Dim Var as Variant

  Comm.Open 1

  Comm.Input 1, Var

  ReadByteArray I[0], Var, 0
  ReadByteArray I[1], Var, 4

  Comm.Close 1
End Sub
```

# LenB

## Function

Return the byte count of character string or numerical value.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
LenB(Data )
```

### Guaranteed entry

Data
:   Specify a character string and numerical value and variable. All data types can be specified.

### Return value

Return the byte counts of Data by [Integer type](000451.html) data.

## Description

Return the byte count of character string or numerical value.

When Data is a character string
:   Return the byte count of character string  
    A single-byte character is regarded as one byte, and a double-byte character is regarded as two bytes.  
    To count both a single-byte character and a double-byte character as one character, use [Len](000281.html) command.

When Data is a variable
:   Return the byte count of a variable type.  
    For example, if [Integer type](000451.html) variable are specified, “4” is returned. However, if [String type](000454.html) variable are specified, the return value is the byte counts of the stored character string.

When Data is a numerical value
:   For example, if “10” is specified, the data is determined as [Integer type](000451.html), and then “4” will be returned.
    If "10.1" is specified, the data is determined as [Double-precision variable of type real](000453.html), and then "8" will be returned.  
    Real number of numerical value is determined as [Double-precision variable of type real](000453.html), not determined as [Floating-point variable of type real](000452.html).

## Related Terms

[Len](000281.html), [CreateArray](000583.html), [CreateMultiArray](005521.html)

## Attention

-

## Example

```
'!TITLE "Obtain the byte count of data"
'Store I-type variable data in the variant type array

Sub Main

	Dim vv as Variant
	Dim ISize As Integer

	iSize = LenB(I0)
	vv = CreateArray(iSize*3)

	For n=0 to 3
		For i=0 to iSize-1
			vv(n*iSize+i) = (I[n] >> i*8) And 0xFF
		Next
	Next

End Sub
```

# Receiving the Provider Event

## Outline of the Provider Event

Provider event is a mechanism to inform a result and status of a procedure on the provider to the main task at arbitrary timings, if the procedure is not synchronized with the main task.  
PacScript provides a dedicated statement to receive the provider event at arbitrary timing.

## Preparation to Receive Provider Events

To receive a provider event, set an event name to receive and a target method by AddHandler statement.

## Standby for Provider Events Receiving

Once an area to receive the event is entered, the main task keeps waiting by using a loop command, which is shown below, until the event is received.

```
Do
Delay 10
If termination condition Then Exit Do
Loop
```

## Procedure for Receiving Provider Events

When the provider issues an event, a method which has been entered by AddHandler is automatically called. By using arguments which are passed to this method, carry out the necessary procedure.

```
Sub OnMessage (ByVal Sender As Object, ByVal Args As Variant)
```

There are two arguments used in this method.

Sender
:   A reference of an object which has issued an event is inserted.

Args
:   A parameter at the event issue is inserted.  
    The value of Arg depends on the object which issues event. Refer to your provider manual.

## Procedure for Receiving Provider Event and Main Task

The main procedure (other than OnMessage) in the task checks event occurrence at the time of going to next line. If an event has been issued, method to receive events (OnMessage) is called. When the procedure of method to receive events has completed, the next line on the main procedure is carried out.  
To run the main procedure in parallel with method to receive event, carry out these procedures in separate tasks.

## Stop of Provider Events Receiving

Soon after the event receiving becomes unnecessary, call RemoveHandler to end the procedure.

```
RemoveHandler object
```

For an object mentioned here, specify the Object which has been entered by AddHandler.

## Sample Program for Receiving Provider Event

This sample program shows how to receive data.  
The data is received when the QR code reader reads the QR code by using the QR code provider. This sample completes by reading three codes.

```
Dim g_Counter As Integer = 0 'Number of data to receive

Sub Main()
Dim ctrl As Object
ctrl = Cao.AddController( "QR", "CaoProv.DENSO.QRCode", "",
      "Conn=com:6:38400:N:8:1, Mode=5, Protocol=0:0:0" )

'Specify the event name and area to receive
AddHandler ctrl, "OnMessage", OnMessage 
g_Counter = 0

'Loop command to keep waiting event receiving
Do
Delay 10
If g_Counter >= 3 Then Exit Do
Loop 

 'Stop event receiving
RemoveHandler ctrl

End Sub

'Event Handler for OnMessage
Sub OnMessage( ByVal Sender As Object, ByVal Args As Variant )
Dim msg as object
msg = Args(0) '::= CaoMessage object
PrintDbg "" & Time & " - CODE = [" & msg.Value & "]"
g_Counter = g_Counter + 1
End Sub
```

# Boundless Rotation of Robot Axis

## Overview

The motion range of the 6th-axis on the 6-axis robots is limited by the software limit, like other axes. If the boundless rotation function on the robot axes is enabled, the software limit is released, that can keep a 6th-axis rotating in the same direction without issuing error.  
 This function is practical especially for the scrubbing and other applications. This function is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Target Robot Models

This function is available for the following robots (except for [the Communication Interface Flange-A type](000016.html)).

| Robot | Axis |
| --- | --- |
| VS-050/060/068/087 series | 6th-axis |

## Usage

With the teach pendant, in [the Path parameter window](001551.html), set [149:Boundless Rotation(J6)] to "1" or "2".

| Value | Description | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Disable | Default value |
| 1 | Enable | - |
| 2 | Enable | Automatically adjust the current angle of the 6th-axis to within the range of plus or minus 360 degree when the robot stops. |

For the setting procedure of the Configuration List, refer to "[Setting Robot Installation Condition](001740.html)" in the TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

If the force sensor-based force control function is activated, even setting the value to 2 will not enable the function that automatically changes the angle to within ± 360 (deg) when the robot stops.

## Maximum Angle and Posclr

The rotation stops when the 6th-axis reaches the maximum angle. Execute Posclr before the 6th-axis reaches the maximum angle.

Posclr changes the current angle as shown below, depending on the mode. For details, see [Posclr](005473.html) in the PROGRAMMER'S MANUAL.

| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Robot axes are not available. |
| 1 | Set the current angle within plus or minus 360 degree. |
| 2 | Set the current angle within plus or minus 180 degree. |
| 3 | Add the specified angle to the current angle (degree).  The calculation value is automatically converted to a multiple of 360 degree. |

The table below shows examples of Mode 3.

| Example | Result |
| --- | --- |
| ``` Posclr 6, 3, 179 ``` | Add 0 degree to the current angle of the 6th-axis |
| ``` Posclr 6, 3, 180 ``` | Add 360 degree to the current angle of the 6th-axis |
| ``` Posclr 6, 3, 360 ``` | Add 360 degree to the current angle of the 6th-axis |
| ``` Posclr 6, 3, -179 ``` | Add 0 degree to the current angle of the 6th-axis |
| ``` Posclr 6, 3, -180 ``` | Add -360 degree to the current angle of the 6th-axis |

## Attention

* If you rotate an axis when the Boundless rotation (J6) setting is "2", or if you run Posclr command, the CALSET value is overwritten.   
   After the CALSET value is overwritten, do not send a project that has been made a backup by WINCAPSIII to the controller. Doing so, the CALSET value will be reset to the value where the backup has been made. As a result, the angle may be changed from that of before the project sending.
* In normal operation at MODE 1 of Posclr or when [Boundless rotation for Robot (J6)] is set to [2:Enable], if the angle of the current position is the multiple of +360 degrees, Posclr will reset the axis to 0 degrees. However, it may set to +360 degrees due to the internal calculation error.  
   Also, the multiple of -360 degrees may set to -360 degrees.  
   Therefore, the motion command that has been written in immediately after Posclr may perform unexpected behavior.
* Also, in normal operation at MODE 2 of Posclr, if the current position is +180 degrees (the multiple of +360 degrees), Posclr will reset the axis to +180 degrees, but it may set to -180 degrees at times.
* If the CP motion is carried out while the rotation angle of either the current position or the target position is the 6th-axis figure Triple (360 degrees <θ6 orθ6≤-360 degrees), a Command speed limit over error might be issued.  
   To avoid this error, execute PosClr before the command execution or operate with PTP motion.

# Definition of Variant.h

Variant.h is a header file to define the value of [Internal processing format](005067.html) which is used in [Variant type](005067.html) data.

Variant.h is a [System header file](000520.html). To use constants defined by Variant.h, read Variant.h with [#include](000115.html).

| Constant | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| VT\_NULL | 1 | Null value (Invalid value) |
| VT\_I2 | 2 | Signed short integer type |
| VT\_I4 | 3 | Integer type(Integer) |
| VT\_R4 | 4 | Floating-point variable of type real(Single) |
| VT\_R8 | 5 | Double-precision variable of type real (Double) |
| VT\_CY | 6 | Money type |
| VT\_DATE | 7 | Date type |
| VT\_BSTR | 8 | String type(String) |
| VT\_DISPATCH | 9 | Object type |
| VT\_ERROR | 10 | Error type |
| VT\_BOOL | 11 | Boolean type |
| VT\_VARIANT | 12 | Variant type（Variant） |
| VT\_UNKNOWN | 13 | Object type |
| VT\_DECIMAL | 14 | Decimal type |
| VT\_I1 | 16 | Character type |
| VT\_UI1 | 17 | Byte type |
| VT\_UI2 | 18 | Unsigned short integer type |
| VT\_UI4 | 19 | Unsigned long integer type |
| VT\_I8 | 20 | Signed 64-bit integer type |
| VT\_UI8 | 21 | Unsigned 64-bit integer type |
| VT\_OBJECT | 9 | Object type |
| VT\_VEC | 256 | Vector type (Vector) |
| VT\_POS | 257 | Position type (Position) |
| VT\_JNT | 258 | Joint type (Joint) |
| VT\_TRN | 259 | Homogeneous transformation type(Trans) |
| VT\_ARRAY | 8192 | Array |
| VT\_BYREF | 16384 | Reference |
| VT\_TYPEMASK | 4095 | Mask constant values |
| VT\_EMPTY | 0 | Not specified |

# ForceSensor

## Function

Reset the force sensor

## Syntax

```
ForceSensor Function Number
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Function Number
:   Specify the processing number along with the force sensor by [Integer type](000451.html) data.
    If "0" is specified, the force sensor is reset, the force sensor is reset.

## Description

Reset the force sensor.  
This command is exclusive to the Compliance Function with Force Sensor.  
For compliance function with force sensor, refer to "[Compliance Function with Force Sensor](005464.html)" of FUNCTION GUIDE.

## Related Terms

[ForceChangeTable](005591.html),
[ForceCtrl](005177.html),
[ForceParam](005176.html),
[ForceValue](005529.html),
[ForceWaitCondition](005530.html)

## Attention

* This command can be used with the models listed in ["Force Sensor Compliance Control"](005464.html#ID005464_ComplianceControl).

## Example

```
Sub Main

 Takearm keep = 1			'Get control authority for the arm group.
 Move P,@E P2				'Move to P2
 ForceParam 1,1,P(100,100,0,100,100,100)'Set force control number, coordinates,
					'and threshold values for external
 :
 ForceSensor 0				'Reset force sensor
 :
 ForceCtrl ON,1				'Enable Force control function
 					'(compliance function)
 Move L,@0 P3				'Move to P3
 :
 'Call the unchuck motion.
 :
 Move L,@0 P2				'Move to P2
 ForceCtrl OFF				'Disable Force control function
 					'(compliance function)
 :

End Sub
```

# ForceValue

## Function

Obtain the force control data.

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
ForceValue ([data number][, Mode])
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Data number
:   Specify a data number that you intend to obtain by [Integer Type](000451.html) data. (See the table below)  
    Data number 1, 4 to 9 and 13 to 15 are available when the Compliance function with Force Sensor is used.

| Data number | Value |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Get the sensor value [N,Nm] on the control coordinate system. |
| 1 | Get the sensor output value [pulse/N.pulse/Nm]. |
| 2 | Acquire the positive peak [N,Nm] of the force and moment on the force control coordinate system. |
| 3 | Acquire the negative peak [N,Nm] of the force and moment on the force control coordinate system. |
| 4 | Acquire the travel distance (command value)[mm,deg] of the tool end from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 5 | Acquire the positive peak (command value)[mm,deg] of the tool end’s travel distance from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 6 | Acquire the negative peaks (command value)[mm,deg] of the tool end’s travel distance from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 7 | Acquire the travel distance (current value)[mm,deg] of the tool end from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 8 | Acquire the positive peak (current value)[mm,deg] of the tool end’s travel distance from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 9 | Acquire the negative peaks (current value)[mm,deg] of the tool end’s travel distance from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 10 | Acquire the deviation [mm,deg] between the command value and the force control command value from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 11 | Acquire the positive peak of the deviation [mm,deg] between the command value and the force control command value from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 12 | Acquire the negative peak of the deviation [mm,deg] between the command value and the force control command value from the start of the force control on the force control coordinate system. |
| 13 | Acquire the force and the moment [N,Nm] of the sensor value. [N, Nm]  (Ver. 1.17.\* or higher.) |
| 14 | Acquire the positive peaks of the force and the moment of the sensor value. [N,Nm]   (Ver. 1.17.\* or higher.) |
| 15 | Acquire the negative peaks of the force and the moment of the sensor value. [N,Nm]   (Ver. 1.17.\* or higher.) |

Mode
:   Specify by [Integer type](000451.html) data. If "0" is specified, acquire data. If "-1" is specified, acquire the data and then reset the buffer data.
    This is omittable. This should be "0" if it is omitted.

### Return Value

Return the value corresponding to the specified data number by one dimensional [array of variant.](005067.html)

## Description

Obtain the force control data.  
For force control function, refer to "[FORCE CONTROL FUNCTION](005169.html)" of FUNCTION GUIDE.

## Related Terms

[ForceChangeTable](005591.html),
[ForceCtrl](005177.html),
[ForceParam](005176.html),
[ForceSensor](005528.html),
[ForceWaitCondition](005530.html)

## Attention

* 5-axis robots do not support this command.
* For the Compliance function with Force Sensor, sensor-related data (data number 1, 13, 14 and 15) are available even if the force control function is disabled. Specifying other data numbers will issue an error "0x81201553 Could not acquire force control data".
* When the force control is enabled by ForceCtrl command, data which are obtained by ForceValue command are initialized to 0s.
  Therefore, if ForceValue command is executed immediately after the force control enablement by ForceCtrl, initialized values may be returned.

## Example

```
Sub Main	                      
  Dim vVal As Variant
  
  Do
  
  vVal = ForceValue( 0 )		'Sensor value[N,Nm]
  
  PrintDbg "X = ", vVal( 0 )
  PrintDbg "Y = ", vVal( 1 )
  PrintDbg "Z = ", vVal( 2 )
  PrintDbg "RX = ", vVal( 3 )
  PrintDbg "RY = ", vVal( 4 )
  PrintDbg "RZ = ", vVal( 5 )

  Delay 1
  
  Loop

End Sub					
```

# ForceWaitCondition

## Function

Wait until the specified conditions of the force control are satisfied.

## Syntax

```
ForceWaitCondition [Position = travel distance][, Force = force and moment] [, Time = elapsed time][, Mode = termination mode][, Timeout = timeout]
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Travel distance
:   Specify the absolute value of travel distance ([mm] or [deg]) of the tool end from the control start by [Position type](000456.html) data. Elements which have specified -1 are not referred. This is omittable. Travel distance is not referred if it is omitted.

Force and moment
:   Specify the absolute value of the force and moment ([N] or [Nm]) converted to the force control coordinate system by [Position type](000456.html) data. Elements which have specified "-1" are not referred. This is omittable. The force and moment is not referred if it is omitted.

Elapsed time
:   Specify the elapsed time [ms] from the control start by [Integer type](000451.html) data. This is omittable. The elapsed time is not referred if it is omitted.

Termination mode
:   Specify the termination mode (see the table below) of the robot and force control when the condition is met by [Integer type.](000451.html) This is omittable. This should be "0" if it is omitted.

| Termination mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | The robot keeps performing a motion with the force control continued. |
| 1 | The robot instantaneously stops performing a motion and then executes the next statement with the force control continued. |
| 2 | The robot instantaneously stops performing a motion and discontinues the force control and then executes the next statement. |

Timeout
:   Specify the timeout period [ms] by [Integer type](000451.html). If the timeout period passes, a Level 1 error occurs and this command ends. This is omittable. This command will not timeout if this option is omitted.

## Description

Wait until the specified conditions of the force control are satisfied.  
 This command is exclusive to the Compliance Function with Force Sensor.  
 For compliance function with force sensor, refer to "[Compliance Function with Force Sensor](005464.html)" of FUNCTION GUIDE.

## Related Terms

[ForceChangeTable](005591.html), [ForceCtrl](005177.html), [ForceParam](005176.html), [ForceSensor](005528.html), [ForceValue](005529.html)

## Attention

* 5-axis robots do not support this command.
* At the start of this command execution, the travel distance from the start of the force control is not reset. Therefore, if you set the travel distance to a condition for termination, the condition can be immediately met, as a result, the command will be terminated.

## Example

```
'This program performs the pressing motion in the Z direction on 
'the tool coordinate system with the force control.

Sub Main 
  TakeArm Keep = 0
	
  ForceParam 1, 1, P(0,0,30,0,0,0),Rate = P(100,100,100,100,100,100)
  ForceParam 2, 1, P(0,0,5,0,0,0),Rate = P(100,100,100,100,100,100)
	
  'Execute CALSET of the sensor
  ForceSensor 0
	
  Motor On
	
  'Start the force control
  ForceCtrl On, 1
	
  'Wait until the force in Z direction comes to 30N
  ForceWaitCondition Force = P(-1,-1,30,-1,-1,-1)
	
  'Change the force control table from 1 to 2
  ForceChangeTable 2
	
  'End the force control
  ForceCtrl Off
	
End Sub
```

# Normal Vector Calculation Function

## Overview

Vertical articulated robots are widely used for loading/unloading operations. However, determining a vertical degree against an angled plane by teaching is difficult.  
This normal vector calculation function determines the vertical vector against a designated plane by specifying three points on the plane. Setting the calculated vector as an approach vector can save the trouble of teaching the robot figure; as a result, operations on angled planes will be easier.

## Description

In the figure below, a normal vector is a vector that is normal to the plane A which is composed of V2 and V3. A normal vector can be calculated by cross product of V2 and V3.

To calculate a normal vector, teach three points Position1, Position2 and Position3 as shown below, and then execute [NormalVector](005532.html) command. For information about how to use NormalVector command, see [NormalVector](005532.html) in the PROGRAMMER'S MANUAL.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005531_1.png)

# NormalVector

## Function

Return a vector which is vertical to a plane where three points belong (normal vector).

## Syntax

```
NormalVector(position1, position2, position3)
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Position1
:   Specify the origin of the vector by [position type](000456.html) data, [vector type](000455.html) data or [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) data. In all data types, elements used for calculation are X, Y and Z.

Position2
:   With Position1, specify a position to determine a vector V1 by [position type](000456.html) data, [vector type](000455.html) data or [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) data. In all data types, elements used for calculation are X, Y and Z.

Position3
:   With Position1, specify a position to determine a vector V2 by [position type](000456.html) data, [vector type](000455.html) data or [homogeneous translation type](000458.html) data. In all data types, elements used for calculation are X, Y and Z.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005532_1.png)

### Return Value

Return a normal vector by [vector type](000455.html) data.

## Description

Return a vector which is vertical to a plane where three points belong (normal vector). The direction of the normal vector is the same as the cross product of V1 and V2. See the figure above.  
By substituting a normal vector into an approach vector of the target position, you do not need to perform a teaching of a robot figure.For details, refer to the "[Normal Vector Calculation Function](005531.html)" of FUNCTION GUIDE. For programming in that case, refer to "Example" shown below.

## Related Terms

[Normal Vector Calculation Function](005531.html)

## Attention

Set Position1, 2 and 3 so that the area of the triangle composed by Position1 to 3 becomes as large as possible.

## Example

```
Sub Main
 Dim aaa As Trans

 'Calculate a normal vector against a plane composed by P10, P11 and P12
 V1 = NormalVector (P10, P11, P12)

 'Convert the loading position P1 to homogeneous translation type data
 aaa = P2T(P1)

 'Substitute the normal vector into the approach vector of P1
 LetA aaa = V1

 'Convert P1 to position type data
 P1 = T2P(aaa)
End Sub
```

# #Pragma Optimize( "wait-idling-time" )

## Function

Specify the length of rest-time on Wait command per task.

## Syntax

```
#Pragma Optimize( "wait-idling-time", time )
```

### Guaranteed entry

Time
:   Specify the length of rest-time on Wait command by an integer of 1 to 1000. Unit is "ms".

## Description

If two or more tasks run Wait command simultaneously, the process of the controller may be overloaded; that may prevent smooth processing. In that case, use #Pragma Optimize command to optimize controller's task processing.   
#Pragma Optimize command adjusts the rest-times on each task so as to reduce the processing load on the controller; that enhances processing speed.

## Related Terms

[Wait](000218.html)

## Attention

-

## Example

```
' In waiting state with Wait command,
' place priority on I/O waiting of Pro1.
' Set rest-time of 100ms for other Pro<n>s so as to reduce processing load.

'Pro1.pcs

Sub Main 

  Wait IO[128] = ON

End Sub


'Pro<n>.pcs

#Pragma Optimize( "wait-idling-time", 100 )
Sub Main 

  Wait I[0] = 1

End Sub
```

# Overview

DeviceNet is a serial communication system which facilitates interconnection between control devices, such as PLCs, PCs, sensors and actuators. By introducing DeviceNet, you can reduce wiring costs by saving wire and establish connection with devices of many manufacturers which support DeviceNet, thus realizing a comfortable and economical system configuration.

This function is available in Ver.1.6.4 or higher.

## DeviceNet Master Board

By inserting the DeviceNet master board into the robot controller and connecting it with a slave device using a DeviceNet cable, DeviceNet system can be configured.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Operating Environment

To use a DeviceNet board, you need to prepare an expansion board (DeviceNet master board) and a function expansion license certificate. For details, refer to "[Options for Robot Controller](001971.html)" and "[Optional Function and License](005476.html)".

### Expansion Board

The table below lists the configuration of DeviceNet master board.

DeviceNet master board is installed in a PCIe slot which is one of the expansion slots of the robot controller. Mini-I/O connector kit is used as an input signal of the safety circuit.

| No. | Components | Remarks | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | DeviceNet master board  (including No. 2) | Product form ;  • Shipped after mounted on the controller with license  • Shipped separately as a spare part with license  • Shipped separately as a spare part without license | | |
| 2 | Mini I/O connector kit | Connector : PCR-E68FS (Manufactured by HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO CO., LTD.)  Connector cover : PCS-E68LPA-1E (Manufactured by HONDA TSUSHIN KOGYO CO., LTD.) | | |
| NPN-type | [Pin assignment](005535.html) | [Configuration of Safety Circuit](001373.html) |
| PNP-type | [Pin assignment](005536.html) | [Configuration of Safety Circuit](001380.html) |
|  | | | | |

### Software License for Function Expansion

To enable the optional function on the robot controller, you need to purchase a license certificate.

| Component |
| --- |
| License certificate for DeviceNet master board |

* A license certificate is sold with an expansion board as a set, or is sold individually.
* To purchase a license, a serial number of the robot controller is required.
