# LED Display

The LED status (turned ON, blinking or turned OFF) indicates the following state.

| LED Name | Color | Status | Definition of status | Description (common errors) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS | Green | Turned ON | Normal state | Unit is in normal state. |
| Green/Yellow | Blinking | Running | Running |
| Yellow | Turned ON | Running | Running |
| - | Turned OFF | No power supply | Controller is turned off. |
| MNS | Green | Turned ON | Connection of communication is completed. | Network is in normal state (communication is established). |
| Blinking | Connection of communication is not completed. | Network is normal, but communication is not established. |
| Green, Red, Turned OFF | Blinking | In self-testing | Power is ON, and self-test is running.Color changes every 0.25 second. |
| Red | Turned ON | Fatal communication error | Communication error (unable to communicate on the network)  ・Node address duplicated  ・Busoff detected |
| Blinking | Minor communication error | I/O Timeout, etc. |
| - | Turned OFF | Off-line state | ・No network power supply  ・No node other than yours |

# Installation of DeviceNet Master Board

The DeviceNet master board is built in an expansion slot of a robot controller.  
A robot controller equips two expansion slots. From these slots, use a connector for PCI Express board to connect DeviceNet master board. For about the way of connection, refer to
"[Installing Expansion Board](001347.html) ".

1. When turn the controller power ON after this installation, "Shutdown since driver installation of the new device was completed." is displayed on the teach pendant.
   Press "OK" to shutdown the robot controller, then turn the motor power ON when "It is now safe to turn off your computer" appears.  
   After reboot is completed, set the Project property setting and the Field bus parameter setting with WINCAPS, and then send these parameters to the robot controller.
2. Connect the shield of DeviceNet cable to the controller housing.  
   ![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005546_1.png)
3. For safety reason and to prevent damage to the devices, disconnect the power cable of the controller or shut down the power supply to the controller from the facilities before disconnecting or connecting cables.

DeviceNet master board also can be used in combination with other extension boards. Selectable allocation mode differs depend on the combination of the extension boards.  
For available allocations, see "[Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode](001325.html)".

# Specifications

## Environmental Requirements

| Item | Specifications |
| --- | --- |
| Operating temperature | 0 to 40℃ |
| Operating humidity | 90% RH or less (without condensation) |

## DeviceNet Communications Specifications

| Item | Specifications | | | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Communications protocol | DeviceNet-compliant | | | |
| Connection supported | Master/slave connection : Polling I/O function, Compliant with DeviceNet communications rules | | | |
| Connection type \*1 | Multi-drop type with possible combination of T-branch (to trunk and branch lines) | | | |
| Bit rate | 500, 250, 125 kbps | | | |
| Communications media | Dedicated cable consisting of 5 wires (2 for signals, 2 for power supply and 1 as a shield wire) | | | |
| Communications cable length | Bit rate | Max. network length \*2 | Branch length | Total branch length |
| 500 kbps | 100 m or less | 6 m or less | 39 m or less |
| 250 kbps | 250 m or less | 6 m or less | 78 m or less |
| 125 kbps | 500 m or less | 6 m or less | 156 m or less |
| Power supply for communication | External supply of 24 VDC ±10% | | | |
| Internal power consumption | Communication power source: 65 mA maximum. | | | |
| Maximum number of connectable nodes | 64 nodes (including configurator (converter) if connected) | | | |
| Error check | CRC | | | |
| \*1 Terminator resistors are needed at both ends of the trunk line. (121 Ω)  \*2 These values may apply when a special thick cable is used as a trunk line. If a special fine cable is used, the maximum network length is 100 m or less. | | | | |

## DeviceNet Master Board Specifications

| Item | Specifications |
| --- | --- |
| Number of user inputs | 0 to 1024 points |
| Number of user outputs | 0 to 1024 points |
| Limitation of I/O point per node | No limit |
| Unit of I/O allocation | The number of I/Os can be set in unit of 8 points. |

# System Construction Procedure

This section shows the configuration procedure of DeviceNet system. This procedure assumes the condition that DeviceNet master board has been installed beforehand.

###### 1

Configure the system

|  |

Make sure that the power supply for communications remains turned off at this stage.

###### 2

Set the communication parameters.

Activate the communication between the robot controller and DeviceNet master board, and between DeviceNet master board and slave devices. For communication between the robot controller and DeviceNet master board, use SYCOM.net that is dedicated software shipped with the Manual pack disc.

###### 3

Check the DeviceNet connection.

Turn on each devices to check connection and operation.

# System Configuration and Configurators

This section describes the network system configuration and configurators in DeviceNet.

|  |
| --- |
| System Configuration Sample |

## Nodes

A DeviceNet network has two kinds of nodes: slaves to which external I/Os are connected, and a master that controls these slaves. Note that their addresses are just network settings, so the master and slaves can be freely arranged on physical sites.

* Up to 63 slaves can be connected.

## Trunk Lines and Drop Lines

The trunk line is a cable whose both ends are terminated with resistors. A drop line is a cable that branches off the trunk line. The trunk line and drop lines can be constructed using DeviceNet thick cables, DeviceNet thin cables, or both.

* Thick cables are used for long-distance trunk lines, strong trunk lines, and drop lines.
* Thin cables are used for trunk lines and drop lines, and for easy termination processing.

### Trunk Line Length

The permissible total length of a trunk line used in a DeviceNet network will differ depending upon the data transmission speed and the type of cables used (thick cable or thin cable).

| Communications speed | Maximum cable length   when only thick cables are used | Maximum cable length   when only thin cables are used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 125 Kbps | 500 m | 100 m |
| 250 Kbps | 250 m |
| 500 Kbps | 100 m |

A DeviceNet network may be constructed with thick and thin cables together. In such a case, the permissible total lengths of thin and thick cables can be obtained according to the calculation formulae below.

“L (thick)” indicates the length of thick cables.  
“L (thin)” indicates the length of thin cables.

| Communications speed | Maximum network length |
| --- | --- |
| 125 Kbps | L (thick) + 5 \* L (thin) ≤ 500 m |
| 250 Kbps | L (thick) + 2.5 \* L (thin) ≤ 250 m |
| 500 Kbps | L (thick) + L (thin) ≤ 100 m |

### Drop Line Length

The drop line length is cable distance between the trunk line tap and the farthest node on the drop line. The permissible overall length of drop lines throughout the network ("total length") depends on the communications speed, and must be within the lengths listed in the table below.

| Communications speed | Drop line length | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum length | Overall length |
| 125 Kbps | 6 m | 156 m |
| 250 Kbps | 78 m |
| 500 Kbps | 39 m |

  

## Terminating Resistors

Terminating resistors must be connected at both ends of the trunk line in a DeviceNet system. The specifications of the terminating resistors are listed below.

* 121Ω
* Metal film resistor with resistance error of less than 1%
* 1/4W

Never connect a terminating resistor to a node. This may result in a failure.

## Communication Power Supply

To operate a DeviceNet network, a communication power must be supplied to each node through DeviceNet cables. The communication power supply, internal circuit power supply, and I/O power supply should be supplied separately.

## DeviceNet Connection Style

As shown below, a variety of connection styles are available for DeviceNet. They include multidrop, star connection, T-ports, daisy chain, and drop line branching.

|  |
| --- |
| DeviceNet connection style |

# I/O Allocation

## Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode

For one robot controller, up to two extension boards can be installed. However, if you install two extension boards, the combination of board must be one PCI board and one PCI-Express board.

For about available combination of I/O extension boards and I/O allocation modes, refer to [Combination of I/O Extension Boards and Allocation Mode](001325.html).

## I/O　Allocation

The following table shows the port number of DeviceNet master board. For about I/O areas of the robot controller, refer to [I/O Port Map and Allocation](001328.html).

| Area | Number of points | I/O port No. |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input | 1024 points | 1024～2047 |
| Output | 1024 points | 2048～3071 |

When you set from the PC, you can allocate the score 1024 but you cannot allocate the score over 1024.

### Node Address

The area of the DeviceNet Master input and output with the RC8 series robot controller are occupied ascending orders with the Node address registered the slave device.

### Limitation of I/O Point per Node

There is no limitation of I/O point for both input and output per node. Make sure to allocate 8 points for one node.

### Slave Status

RC8 series robot controllers do not use this information. Do not read it.

Slave status is added at the end of the input points automatically that are allocated by node. 192 points can be added at the maximum. If the number of points exceeds the DeviceNet Master input areas, which has 1024 points, the exceeded points are not displayed.

### I/O Allocation Example

Assume that two slave devices, node 0 and node 16, are connected.

| Node address | Area | Points | I/O port No. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node 0 | Input | 128 points | 1024～1151 |
| Output | 512 points | 2048～2559 |
| Node 16 | Input | 256 points | 1152～1407 |
| Output | 512 points | 2560～3071 |

|  |
| --- |
| I/O Port Map Sample |

# Installation of SYCON.net

SYCON.net is software to setup the DeviceNet master that is installed in the PC connected to the robot controller. The installation procedure is as follows.

###### 1

Execute the following application file stored in the manual pack disc.

Click \tools\SyconNet\SYCONnet netX setup.exe of manual DVD.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005556_01.png)

###### 2

You can see the display below. Choose the language and click [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005556_02.png)

Start the installation.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005556_03.png)

###### 3

# Software Setting for System Configuration

This section describes the way of network configuration on software of the master device and slave devices which configure the system.

###### 1

Import EDS files.

Start SYCON.net. On the main menu, in [Network] tab, click [Import Device Descriptions].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_1.png)

###### 2

Select [DeviceNet EDS (\*.eds)] from the dropdown list of the file type, and then import EDS file from the connected DeviceNet slave devices. Execute this process for each model of slave devices.

Select desired file and then click [Open].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_2.png)

The following window is displayed. Click [Yes].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_2_1.png)

The following window is displayed. This disappeares when the import is finished.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_2_2.png)

###### 3

Set the DeviceNet master board [CIFX DN/DNM].

From the tree in the right side of the display, click [DeviceNet] - [Master], and then move [CIFX DN/DNM] to the horizontal gray line on the center of display using a drag-and-drop operation.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_3.png)

###### 4

Set the slave device.

Master board CIFX DN/DNM, which has been set in STEP3, is displayed as shown below. From the tree in the right side of the display, click [DeviceNet]-[Slave] and then select desired slave device. Move the slave device to the horizontal yellow line on the center of the window, which comes from the master board icon, using a drag-and-drop operation.

Perform this process for each slave device. In this example, RC8 DeviceNet Slave is connected as a slave device.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_4.png)

An icon of the slave device is displayed as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005559_5.png)

This work should be set each connecting slave device.

This completes the software settings for system configuration.

# Connection Setting between Robot Controller and Master Board

###### 1

# Field Bus Parameter Setting

This section describes the way of node address setting and communication speed setting of DeviceNet master board.

###### 1

From the tree in the left side of the display, click [Configuration] - [Bus Parameters].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005561_1.png)

For [MAC ID] and [Baud Rate] on the right side of the window, select following items.

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MAC ID | Select node address of DeviceNet Master board from the range of 0 to 63 |
| 2 | Baud Rate | Select the communication speed of DeviceNet from 125Kbps, 250Kbps and 500Kbps |

###### 2

With the teach pendant, specify error-related settings.

From the top screen—[F4 I/O]—[F6 Aux.]-[F4 Field Bus parameter]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005561_2.png)

## DeviceNet Master ErrDisplay

This parameter allows you to choose whether the network error will display in "every time" or is display at the "first time" only.

This parameter is set to "0" (EveryTime) by default for safe operation of the facilities. Every time an I/O operation is carried out, an error will display if any.

To check program operations using dummy I/Os for setting up facilities where no connection to the network has been established, set this parameter to "1" (First Time). Doing so will not display errors once detected, allowing you to check program operations.

|  | First Time | EveryTime (Default Setting) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeviceNet ErrDisplay | 1 | 0 |

After completion of setting-up, be sure to set this parameter back to "0."

## DeviceNet Insensitive time to network error [ms]

f the Communication check of DeviceNet communication starts too early after the Robot controller startup, an error [8350200B Prepare for field network communication] might be displayed immediately after booting.  
To prevent such error, adjust "EtherCAT Insensitive time to network error" of Fieldbus parameter longer.

|  | Available range | Default Setting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeviceNet Master Insensitive time to network error　[ms] | 0～65535 | 20000 |

This completes the bus parameter setting.

# I/O Size Setting for Slave Device

This section describes the way of I/O size setting for each slave device connected. Allocate I/O size for each slave device being connected. The layout of this setting window of the following STEP 2 to STEP4 may change depending on the type of DeviceNet slave device.

###### 1

Double click the icon of a slave device connected.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005563_1.png)

###### 2

From the Navigation Area in the left side of the display, click [Configuration]-[Connection].

Select a connection method for slave device connection from ; Poll connection, Change Of state connection, Cyclic connection, and Bit-Strobe connection. A connection method that is not supported by the device will be gray color and it will not be selectable.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005563_2.png)

###### 3

According to the connection method selected at STEP2, click the following items.

| Communication method | Items |
| --- | --- |
| Poll connection | [Configuration]-[Connection]-[Poll] |
| Change of state connection | [Configuration]-[Connection]-[Change of state] |
| Cyclic connection | [Configuration]-[Connection]-[Cyclic] |
| Bit-Strobe connection | [Configuration]-[Connection]-[Bit-Strobe] |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005563_3.png)

###### 4

From the Navigation Area pane, click [Configuration]-[Connection]-[Poll].

[Consumption] in the upper part represents the input of slave device, which corresponds to the output of the robot controller. [Production] in the lower part represents the output of slave device, which corresponds to the input of the robot controller. The setting is performed by a byte-unit. (1 byte = 8 bits) Change the setting of [Connection path], if necessary.

When the setting completes, click [OK].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005563_4.png)

When Bit-Strobe connection is used, the size of "Consumption" may be fixed 8-byte at times. In this case, 64 ports will be occupied for DeviceNet master output.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005563_5.png)

The longer the Production inhibit time, the longer the synchronous time between the master controller and the slave controller.

###### 5

For each slave device, perform STEP 1 to STEP4 to set I/O size..

This completes the I/O size settings for slave device.

# Connection Confirmation

This section describes the way of checking the communication status of network.

## Network Connection Confirmation

Network connection is checked with the Network State in the [Displaying and Operation of I/O](001767.html) window of the teach pendant.

Operation path : Top screen - [F4 I/O]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005565_1.png)

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Network state | Connected | Communication is established  (When multiple slave devices exist, it is recognized as "Connected" if at least one slave device connection is established.) |
| Not connected | Communication is not established |

## Node Connection Confirmation

Node connection status is checked by [Node Diagnosis] in the [I/O Information Display](001100.html) of the teach pendant

Operation path : Top screen - [F4 I/O] - [F6 Aux] - [F1 I/O info]

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005565_2.png)

# Project Property Setting

To use a DeviceNet master board as an I/O expansion board, you need to register the following information from WINCAPSIII.

From the [Project] menu, point to [Property] to open the Property window, and then click .[I/O] tab. For details, refer to "[Configuring a Project](004406.html)".

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005566_1.png)

## Assign

### Device

|  | Setting value |
| --- | --- |
| Device | "DeviceNet Master" or "[Parallel] + [DeviceNet Master]" |

### Mode

Allocation mode is fixed to "All User". For details about allocation mode, refer to "[Functions in Individual Allocation Modes](001326.html)."

|  | Setting value |
| --- | --- |
| Mode | "All User" |

## Options MiniIO

### Power source

If the total maximum capacity of Mini I/O, Hand I/O and Parallel I/O is 1.3 A or lower, the internal power source is available.

|  | Setting value | Defalt setting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Power source | "External" or "Internal" | External |

# TrackTargetRelease

## Function

Delete data of the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork), or return the data to the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

This command is available in Ver.1.6.\* or higher.

## Syntax

```
TrackTargetRelease Conveyor number, Data processing [,UserData]
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Conveyor number
:   Specifies the conveyor number (1 to 16) to be used by [integer type](000451.html) data.  
    (If your robot controller is Ver.1.11.\* or lower, available conveyor number is 1 or 2.)

Data processing
:   Specify Data processing by [integer type](000451.html). True (other than "0") and False ("0") are available. This is omittable. This will be "True (other than 0)" if it is omitted.

    | Setting value | Description |
    | --- | --- |
    | True | Delete data specified as [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |
    | False | Return data specified as [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) to the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). |

UserData
:   Specify a user data value by [integer type](000451.html) data. The user data is used when data is returned to the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf). Retain the current setting value when you enter a negative value. This is omittable. This will be "-1" if it is omitted.

## Description

Delete data of the [tracking target work](002221.html#targetWork) that have been obtained by [TrackTargetPos](005353.html), or return the data to the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).  
Use this command when all the following conditions are met during tracking operation;  
- [Mode 1 of the fourth argument](005353.html#Mode1) of [TrackTargetPos](005353.html) is enabled, and,  
- [tracking-target work](002221.html#targetWork) data remains in the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

## Related Terms

[TrackBufferDelete](005671.html),
[TrackBufferIndexes](005491.html),
[TrackBufferRead](005492.html),
[TrackSetSensor](005375.html),
[TrackSetVision](005376.html),
[TrackTargetPos](005353.html), [Commands for Conveyor Tracking](001122.html), [Commands for Circular Tracking](002898.html)

## Attention

This command is dedicated for conveyor and circular tracking.

## Example

Data are deleted from the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

```
TrackTargetRelease 1, TRUE
```

Change the user data to 20 when data is returned to the [tracking buffer](002221.html#trackBuf).

```
TrackTargetRelease 2, FALSE, 20
```

# General Information

Built-in Vision is a function of a robot controller to process images. Using Built-in Vision allows you to process images without installing other visual controllers.  
To use Built-in Vision, directly connect the FA camera to the robot controller as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005570_1.png)

Connectable FA cameras are the following.

* USB Camera  
  Connect a FA camera to a USB port of the robot controller to use.  
  For RC8 series, a USB camera (manufactured by IDS) is available.  
  USB3.0 is not recommendable because the RC8 series controllers have only USB2.0 ports. (Only USB2.0 cameras have been checked for operation.)
* GigE Camera  
  Connect a FA camera to a LAN port of the robot controller to use.  
  For RC8 series robot controller, GigE-supported area sensor cameras "ace series" manufactured by Basler are available.  
  (GigE: Gigabit Ethernet)
* Network camera  
  Connect a network camera to a LAN port of the robot controller to use.  
  For RC8 series robot controller, network cameras "WebView Livescope series" manufactured by Canon are available.

When connecting a camera (GigE Camera) that uses the robot internal wiring, if a trigger is detected incorrectly with external trigger mode, the parameter setting on the camera could get better the detecting.

## Wiring Instruction for Setting and Adjustment

Setting and adjustment of Built-in Vision are performed by checking the data processing and the processed image with a computer.

### For USB Camera

Connect a computer to a LAN port of the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005570_2.png)

### For Gig-E Camera and Network Camera

Because the robot controller has only one LAN port, you need to use a hub to connect both computer and camera. After setting and adjustment are completed, disconnect the hub and then directly connect the camera to the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005570_3.png)

# Connecting Method

This section describes how to connect hardware.

## Connection of Hardware

For a USB camera, connect the camera to a USB port of the robot controller.   
 For a Basler GigE camera or Canon network camera, connect the camera to a LAN port of the robot controller through a hub when you set up. When using the camera, directly connect it to the LAN port of the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005573_1.png)

* When using a GigE camera (Basler) with the following functions, it is recommended to connect the camera independently to an additional PCI-type LAN port (Type ETG3-PCI, I/O data-made) to avoid data interference.
  + Use a force sensor (LAN connection).
  + Multiple robots perform conveyor tracking.
  + Use a cooperative control function.
* For information about the I/O cable wiring when performing vision tracking with a Basler camera, refer to "[Wiring an I/O cable to a GigE Camera](001214.html)".

## Preparation for Hardware Connection

Before using RC Vision, the following preparations are required.

### Controller, Computer Connection, and IP Address Setting

Connect a computer to a LAN port of the controller. Specify each IP address so that the PC and controller can communicate with each other. For details about the IP address setting of the controller, refer to "[Displaying and Changing Communication Settings Screen](001783.html)" in the TEACH PENDANT GUIDE.

### Activating Visual Option (If Necessary)

Activate "Denso Robot Imaging Library" of the controller. You do not need to perform this step if this is already installed or if you use EVP.  
 To activate this option, a license is required. For details, refer to ["Optional Function and License"](005476.html). For how to activate it, refer to “[Registering License](002685.html)” in OPTION.

# Status Output with User Output Ports

Status of the robot is outputted with user output ports.

For about settings, see "[Displaying and Changing I/O Parameters"](001769.html) of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

| Output Signal | Function |
| --- | --- |
| [Running Stop Processing](005584.html) | When the entire program has stopped by the stop command, such as an emergency stop, pressing STOP button, the program cannot reboot in a certain period of time. This signal turns ON in this period. |
| [Robot controller startup completed](005585.html) | Turns ON at the time of the controller start-up.  The difference between the robot initialization completion signal and this signal is, this signal does not turn OFF even if an error is issued. |
| [Robot Running(Position designation）](005586.html) | This signal turns ON when a command to run the robot has been issued by the controller. |
| [Robot Running(Encoder)](005587.html) | This signal turns ON when the signal returned from the encoder indicates that the robot is running. |
| [Change Battery](005588.html) | This signal turns ON when the encoder battery maintenance data has passed.  The encoder battery maintenance date is checked with the teach pendant.  From the top screen, press [F6 Setting] - [F7 Date and Maintenance]－[F3 Encoder Battery]. |
| [Process of Stopping Motor](005589.html) | After the operation of turning OFF the motor, it takes a certain period of time before the motor completely stops. This signal turns ON when the motor status is going to change from ON to OFF. |
| [32bit Error Code Output](005590.html) | This signal outputs an error code converted from hexadecimal of eight figures into the binary of 32 figures.  "1" represents ON, "0" represents OFF.  "Error number output" of the system output outputs an error code that has been converted into a RC7M error code. However, this function outputs the original error code of RC8 series. |

# Running Stop Processing

## Function

When the entire program has stopped by the stop command, such as an emergency stop, pressing STOP button, the program cannot reboot in a certain period of time. This signal turns ON in this period.

## Usage

If you reboot the program before the stop of all programs, an error message of "83501011 Command is not executable during program stop process" will be displayed.  
This signal is used to check that the entire program has fully stopped and then reboot the program; that prevents the error occurrence.

## ON Condition

This signal turns ON when a stop operation that stops all programs, such as an emergency stop or STOP button, is issued.

## OFF Condition

This signal turns OFF when all programs stop.

# Robot controller startup completed

## Function

Turns ON at the time of the controller start-up.  
The difference between the robot initialization completion signal and this signal is, this signal does not turn OFF even if an error is issued.

## Usage

With this signal and Auto Mode output signal being ON, the OPERATION PREPARATION command must be executed.

## ON Condition

This signal will be turned ON when turning the controller power on normally starts the system program in it and the OPERATION PREPARATION command becomes ready to execute.

## OFF Condition

The signal is OFF until the controller has rebooted after turning ON the controller power.

ID : 5589

# Motor OFF indicator

## Function

After the operation of turning OFF the motor, it takes a certain period of time before the motor completely stops. This signal turns ON when the motor status is going to change from ON to OFF.

## Usage

This command is used to check if the motor OFF is in progress.  
For example, the mode switch from the manual mode to the auto mode includes a motor OFF process. Therefore, the motor ON command is not executed in a certain period of time. This signal is effective to adjust the timing of the auto mode start.

## ON Condition

The ON condition represents the status of the motor OFF is in progress.

## OFF Condition

The OFF condition represents the status of the motor OFF is not in progress.

ID : 5590

# 32bit Error Code Output

## Function

This signal outputs an error code converted from hexadecimal of eight figures into the binary of 32 figures.  
"
1" represents ON, "0" represents OFF.  
"Error number output" of the system output outputs an error code that has been converted into a RC7M error code. However, this function outputs the original error code of RC8 series.

## Usage

This signal is used to use a RC8 series original error number in the external devices.  
The port number which has been designated by the"[32bit Error Code Output IO No](001769.html)"is set to the lowest bit.

## ON Condition

When an error of level 1 or higher has been issued, this signal converts the error number into a binary digit, and then turns ON the port of "1".

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| RC3 Compatible allocation | Turn ON when an error occurs. |
| Standard allocation | Turn ON when an I/O command "[Error Read](001014.html)" is executed. |

## OFF Condition

This signal is OFF when an error of level 1 or higher has not been issued.  
To turn OFF this signal after an error occurrence, clear the error.

## Timing Chart

|  |
| --- |
|  |

ID : 5591

# ForceChangeTable

## Function

Change the force control number used when the force control is performed.

## Syntax

```
ForceChangeTable Force control number
```

### Guaranteed Entry

Force control number
:   Specify the force control number (a parameter table number for the compliance function) by [integer type](000451.html) data from 1 to 10.

## Description

Change the force control number used when the force control is performed.

## Related Terms

[ForceCtrl](005177.html), [ForceParam](005176.html), [ForceSensor](005528.html), [ForceValue](005529.html), [ForceWaitCondition](005530.html)

## Attention

* 5-axis robots do not support this command.
* The command is available only to the force sensor-based force control function. In Compliance Function, which does not use a force sensor, a table cannot be changed.

## Example

```
'This program performs the pressing motion in the Z direction on 
'the tool coordinate system with the force control.

Sub Main 
  TakeArm Keep = 0
	
  ForceParam 1, 1, P(0,0,30,0,0,0),Rate = P(100,100,100,100,100,100)
  ForceParam 2, 1, P(0,0,5,0,0,0),Rate = P(100,100,100,100,100,100)
	
  'Execute CALSET of the sensor
  ForceSensor 0
	
  Motor On
	
  'Start the force control
  ForceCtrl On, 1
	
  'Wait until the force in Z direction comes to 30N
  ForceWaitCondition Force = P(-1,-1,30,-1,-1,-1)
	
  'Change the force control table from 1 to 2
  ForceChangeTable 2
	
  'End the force control
  ForceCtrl Off
	
End Sub
```

# Acquiring, Displaying and Saving Force Control Log

Acquire logs of the following values of each axes, and then display the result in the graph; - Command value of travel distance - Current value of travel distance - Command value of tool end - Current value of tool end - Sensor value

For adjustment procedure by using Force control log, refer to "[Adjustment Procedure](002161.html)".

WINCAPSIII receives the force control log at the same time of the control log reception. You can output the received force control log as a CSV file. To export the log, from the menu bar of the WINCAPSIII, point to [[File]-[Export]](004364.html).

## Displaying the Force Control Log

From the top screen, press [F2 Arm]-[F6 Aux]-[F1 Force Control Log]  
Bold line on the graph indicates the area where the force sensor works.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005592_1.png)

Touching an icon on the upper left will displays a pull down menu that includes operation mode as shown below. There are four types of operation modes available.

| Operation mode | Description | Right/Left arrow keys or Jog dial | UP/Down arrow keys or the combination of Up/Down arrow keys and Jog dial | Screen touch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Move the display | Shifts the display range of the graph axis. | Pressing Right/Left arrow keys will move the display range of the X axis. To adjust the display range with smaller scale, turn the jog dial. | Pressing Up/Down arrow keys will move the display range of the selected Y axis. To adjust the display range with smaller scale, turn the jog dial while pressing Up/Down arrow keys. | The display range of the X axis moves. |
| Change the scale | Expands or contracts the display range of the graph axis. | Pressing the Right/Left arrow keys will expand or contract the display range of the X axis. To adjust display range more precisely, turn the jog dial. | Pressing the Up/Down arrow keys will expand or contract the display range of selected Y axis. To adjust the display range more precisely, turn the jog dial while pressing Up/Down arrow keys. | The display range of the X axis moves. |
| Change the range | For details, refer to the following "[Change the range](#ID005592_check)" section. | Pressing the Right/Left arrow keys will move the selection range cursor on the X axis. To adjust the selection range with smaller scale, turn the jog dial. | Not used. | The selection range on the X axis moves to the position where you touched. |
| Check the current | Value of the selected range. If you select a position where a robot motion command was executed, "Program" and "Line number" are displayed on the upper right. | Pressing the Right/Left arrow keys will move the cursor indicating the current value. To adjust the cursor more precisely, turn the jog dial. | Not used. | The cursor indicating the current value moves to the position where you touched. |

| Keys other than function keys | |
| --- | --- |
|  | Pressing this button will display a pull down menu.  Select desired axis number that you want to display the force control log.  Joint-mode data of X, Y, Z. Rx, Ry, and Rz are available. |
| Dist-Inst | Display the information of Dist-Inst.  The graph shows the value on the force control coordinate system.   Selecting this item will display a line graph with a pink line. |
| Dist-Enc | Display the information of Dist-Enc.  The graph shows the value on the force control coordinate system.  Selecting this item will display a line graph with a purple line. |
| Pos-Inst | Display the information of Pos-Inst.  The graph shows the value on the work coordinate system.  Selecting this item will display a line graph with a yellow line. |
| Pos-Enc | Display the information of Pos-Enc.  The graph shows the value on the work coordinate system.  Selecting this item will display a line graph with a light blue line. |
| Sensor | Display the information of Sensor.  The graph shows the value on the force control coordinate system.  Selecting this item will display a line graph with a red line. |

| Available function keys | |
| --- | --- |
| [F1 Clear Log] | Delete the acquired control log information. |
| [F2 Start Log] | Starts acquiring control log.  REC on the icon of force control log tab turns on when the acquisition of control log is started. |
| [F3 Stop Log] | Stops acquiring control log.  REC on the icon of force control log tab turns off when the acquisition of control log is completed. |
| [F4 Save Log] | Saves the acquired control log information. |
| [F5 Refresh] | Updates the latest information on theforce control log display screen of tech pendant |
| [[F6 Setting]](001734.html) | Displays [Force Control log settings] window.  Confirm and change the Force control log-related settings. |
| [F7 Switch Y-Value display] | Changes the display of Y-axis scale between vertical and horizontal.  Setting the Y-axis scale to the vertical direction will expand the display range of the graph. |
| [F8 Change axis display range] | Changes the display range of the X- or Y-axis.  Pressing [F8 Change axis display range] will display the setting window. Select desired operation from the followings.  * Edit X-axis display range    Specify the display range (start position, end position) of X-axis with numerical values. * Edit selected Y-axis display range    Specify the display range (start position, end position) of Y-axis with numerical values. * Initialize X-axis display range    Initialize the X-axis display range.   (Set the X-axis display range to the default.) * Initialize selected Y-axis display range    Initialize the selected Y-axis display range.   (Set the Y-axis display range to the default.) |

Values displayed in the monitor could differ from the values detected by the force sensor. This is because the displayed values of the force control log or the sensor have been compensated. Therefore, although the detected values actually do not exceed the values you have specified, the displayed value could exceed the value specified, or, conversely, although the displayed values actually do not exceed the values you have specified, the detected value could exceed the value specified.

### Change The Range

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005592_7.png)

| keys | Function |
| --- | --- |
| Start | Set the starting time of logs.  Once the button is pressed, the green lamp turns on so that you can set the log starting time. |
| End | Set the ending time of logs.  Once the button is pressed, the green lamp turns on so that you can set the log ending time. |
| Next | Jump to the beginning of the next force control period. |

## Sample Program

Start the log acquisition before starting the force control. End the log acquisition when the force control ends.

```
Sub Main 

  TakeArm Keep = 0
	
  Motor On

  'Initial position
  Move L, P4+(0,0,10)
	
  SysLog.Ctrl.Clear
  SysLog.Ctrl.Start
	
  'Set the current values to zero. (0N|0Nm)
  ForceSensor 0
	
  Delay 1000

  'Enable the impedance control with the setting of the table number 1
  ForceParam 1,1,P(0,0,30,0,0,0),Damp = P(100,100,100,100,100,100),SPMax = 100
	
  'Start the force control
  ForceCtrl True, 1
	
  'Wait until the conditions are meet
  ForceWaitCondition Force = P(0,0,5)
	
  'Actively change the control parameters
  ForceParam 1,1,P(0,0,10,0,0,0), Damp = P(100,100,100,100,100,100), SPMax = 100
	
  'Rotate around the Rz-axis
  Drive (6,45), Speed = 20, Next
	
  Delay 10000
	
  'End the force control
  ForceCtrl False
	
  'End the motion
  Move P, P4+(0,0,10)
	
  SysLog.Ctrl.Stop
	
End Sub
```

# Motion Check of the Program

You can check the cycle time, trajectory and posture of the robot by running the created program on the program.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005594_1.png)

###### 1

On the [Project window], select a program that you would like to check the motion.  
The selected program is displayed.

###### 2

On the [Debug] menu, click [Simulation mode].

###### 3

Set the external speed.  
On the [TP Status bar], click the speed button which is red-circled in the image above.

###### 4

On the [Debug] menu, select [Start a Task] or [Step in] to execute the program.

###### 5

Check the program flows, the robot posture and the run time in each window.

# Beep sound setting at the vicinity of the singular point

## Operation Path

[F12 Aux]-[Maintenance]-[SnglrBzzr]

## Operation Procedures

Turn ON (sound) or OFF (mute) the beep sound which sounds when the robot passes through the vicinity of the singular point in Auto mode.  
In the Manual mode or the Teach check mode, beep sound is always ON regardless of this setting.

###### 1

The window to turn ON/OFF the beep sound is displayed.

### To turn ON the beep sound

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005595_1.png)

### To turn OFF the beep sound

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005595_2.png)

###### 2

Press the [OK] key to establish the new setting.

# Precautions in Use of Force Sensor Provider

If the Force Sensor Compliance Control option is enabled, replace the following commands of the force sensor providers to the different command as shown below.

| Provider command | Replace / Delete |
| --- | --- |
| AddController method | No need (delete) |
| get\_Value on "@data" variables | ForceValue command |
| 1. WACOH DynPick provider  "OffsetReset" command on CaoController::Execute method 2. ATI Net F/T provider  "BIAS" command on CaoController::Execute method | ForceSensor 0 command |

## Example

In the example program below, provider commands are replaced into the different commands.

### Original Program (Provider Commands are Used)

```
'!TITLE "Pro2.pcs"

 Sub Main
    dim ctrl as object
    dim var as object
    set ctrl = cao.addcontroller("wacoh", "caoprov.wacoh.dynpick", "",
 "conn=tcp:192.168.0.4, @Ifnotmember")
    set var = ctrl.AddVariable("@Data", "@Ifnotmember")

    dim vntVal as variant

    vntVal = var.value

    I11 = vntval(0)
    I12 = vntval(1)
    I13 = vntval(2)
    I14 = vntval(3)
    I15 = vntval(4)
    I16 = vntval(5)
    I17 = vntval(6)

 End Sub
```

### Program Replaced by the Different Commands

* Processing of the line 4-8 are not necessary.
* "var.Value" written in the line 12 is replaced by ForceValue(1).
* Sensor ID is not required when the values are stored in variables.  
  (I17=vnVal(6) will be an error)

```
'!TITLE "Pro2.pcs"

 Sub Main
     dim vntVal as variant

     vntVal = ForceValue(1)

     I11 = vntval(0)
     I12 = vntval(1)
     I13 = vntval(2)
     I14 = vntval(3)
     I15 = vntval(4)
     I16 = vntval(5)

End Sub
```

# Path accuracy enhancement option at high speed operation

## Overview

Enabling this option will enhance [the path accuracy](001622.html) when the High precision control function is enabled at the high speed operation.

## Target Robot Models

This option is available for the 4-Axis robots.

## Usage

This option is enabled when [137 Path accuracy compensation] on [the Configuration List](001551.html) is set to [1: For high speed] by the teach pendant. To disable this option, set to [0: Basic control].

For detailed information about displaying and setting the configuration, refer to [Displaying and Setting the Configuration](001740.html) of the TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

## Precautions for Use

* This option have a only small effect at a low speed operation.
* Enter load settings (mass, center of gravity, inertia) precisely.Entering reversed-gravity direction or the wrong load settings may lead to deteriorate the path accuracy.  
  Be sure not to set incorrect gravity direction.

# TRANSFER ROBOT USER'S MANUAL

The transfer robot is a transportation robot which conveys, casts or takes out workpieces mainly between processes or facilities.

Before use, read and understand this manual thoroughly to ensure safe and efficient operations.

## Robot Types Covered by This Manual

| Series | Robot Types |
| SC series  Transfer robot | LZNN |
| LZZN |
| LYZN |
| LYZZ |
| LSNN |
| LSSN |
| LZSN |
| LZSS |

The alphabetical characters L, Y, Z, S and N in the model names represent the attributes of axes. For details, refer to [LYZS Notation](005608.html).

To ensure operator safety, be sure to read the precautions and instructions in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html)".

* Both robots and controllers imported into South Korea on or after 1st March 2013 are required to have KCs marks.
* "CableVeyor" mentioned in this manual is a registered trademark of Tsubakimoto Chain Co., Ltd.

ID : 5601

# Components 1

## Robot Unit

There are eight types of robot units as shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_1.png)

## Motor and Encoder Cables

These are cables that connect the robot unit and the robot controller.

There are two types: Motor cables and encoder cables. Depending on the robot type and cable length, select one from [Motor and Encoder Cable Selection Table (PDF:60KB)](img/005601/005601_2.pdf).

### Motor Cable

Use a motor cable to connect the robot unit motor and the robot controller.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_3.png)

### Encoder Cable

Use an encoder cable to connect the robot unit encoder and the robot controller. An encoder cable consists of three parts.

#### Encoder Cable

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_4.png)

#### Power Conversion Box Set

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_5.png)

#### Encoder Serial Branch Cable

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_6.png)

## Sheet of Direction Indicator Labels

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_7.png)

These are labels that indicate the motion directions of individual axes.

After installation, affix the direction indicator labels in a position on the robot unit where they can be easily seen.

## Warning and Caution Labels

### Collision Warning Label

Collision warning labels are provided with the robot unit. They inform users that the robot motion range is dangerous and that they should not enter it. Affix the labels in a position where they are easily seen, such as the entrance/exit of the safety fence. If required, provide a plate for affixing the labels.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_8.png)

Serious injury can result from contact with the robot if it is running.

## Encoder Backup Battery

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005601_9.png)

This is a battery for encoder backup.

The position data of the encoder contained in the servomotor is stored in the internal memory of the encoder. The backup battery for each memory retains the above data, while the power to the robot controller is turned OFF.

\*1　Selecting the rain unit

Effective stroke length is calculated by deducting the robot unit length (1600 mm) and two of the mechanical stoppers (450 mm each) from the Full length.  
Use the following format to figure out the necessary rail length.   
From [Rail Unit Combination Table (PDF:67KB)](img/005603/005603.pdf), select Full length longer than the calculated necessary length.

* Necessary Rail length(mm) = Necessary stroke length + (160 + 45 ×2)

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005603_1.png)

\*2 Number of links required for a cableveyor

Use the following format to calculate the number of necessary link. Cableveyor is handled by 8 link-units.

* Number of links required for a cableveyor = (Moving distance / 2 + 75×3.14 + 190×2) / 58

# System Configuration

The whole configuration of the robot system is shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005605_1.png)

## Robot Unit

This is a transportation robot unit which conveys, casts and takes out workpieces mainly between processes or facilities. There are eight types of robot unit that have different axis mechanisms. You can select desired robot unit depending on your needs. For details, see "[Robot Type](005606.html)". Hands or other end effectors should be attached to the flange by the customer.

## Robot Controller

The controller controls the motion of the robot unit according to programs built with signals sent from the connected facilities management equipment. When an operation device is connected, it allows the customer to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

## Operation Devices

The operation devices are optionally available to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

For details about hardware and operation, refer to the "[TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001674.html)" and "[MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001806.html)".

### Teach Pendant (TP)

The teach pendant is a multifunctional operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, program start, programming, and all settings. The teach pendant can also be used as an operation panel by using the teach pendant panel editor.

### Mini-Pendant (MP)

The mini-pendant is a simplified operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, program start, and a part of settings.

## Offline Software

The software enables backing up of project data in the controller and editing, management, movement simulation of programs. WINCAPSIII is an offline software designed for the Denso robot system. The trial version comes with the robot system at no extra charge. For details, refer to "[WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html)".

## Facilities Management Equipment

The management equipment is a system that the customer sets up for managing the facilities. Denso robots can be linked with it via CC-Link, DeviceNet, and other various networks.

# Axis Number and LYZS Notation

The model of the transfer robot is determined by the selected robot type and strokes.   
This page explains the Axis number and the LYZS notation that are related to the robot type and stroke selection.

## Axis Number

The transfer robot allows customers to combine two to four axes, depending on the robot types. Axis numbers, written as J\*, are assigned as shown below.

* The axis at the root, which slides along the rail of the rail unit, is called the J1.
* The one attached to the J1 axis is the J2 axis, followed by the J3 and J4 axes, respectively. If two or more axes are mounted on one axis, the rightmost axis is called the youngest axis number when viewed from the J1 motor.

## LYZS Notation

To express the robot type, use the combination of four alphabets of L, Y, Z and S. The alphabets indicates the axis name, function and the axis number. From the leftmost, each alphabet represents J1, J2, J3 and J4.

Axis names and functions are as follows.

* L　･･･　L axis. Move linearly along the rail on the rail unit
* Y　･･･　Y axis. Move backward and forward
* Z　･･･　Z axis. Move vertically
* S　･･･　S axis. Move backward and forward with expansion and contraction

Since a robot type is expressed in a four-digit notation, a non-existent axis is called N.

Example: LZSN if J1 = L axis, J2 = Z axis, and J3 = S axis.

# Warning and Caution Labels

The robot unit has warning and caution labels pasted as shown below. They alert the user to the dangers of the areas on which they are pasted. Be sure to observe the instructions printed on those labels.

| Warning or caution label | Supplementary information for label | Where labels are affixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Collision warning label | Serious injury can result from contact with the robot if it is running.  (1) Never enter the motion space of the robot when it is running or the power is ON.  (2) When entering the motion space for troubleshooting, be sure to cut off power to the robot motors by activating the emergency stop device, etc. | Collision warning labels are provided with the robot unit. Attach the labels in a position where they are easily seen, such as the entrance/exit of the safety fence. If required, provide a plate for attaching the labels. |
| Motor high temperature caution label | The surface of the motor may become hot depending on the operating conditions, which may give workers a burn if they touch it. |  |

# Precautions When Designing End-effectors

Design an end-effector to meet the requirements described below. Otherwise, a robot failure may result.

If the end-effector design precautions are not observed, the clamped parts of the robot unit may become loose, rattle or be out of position, possibly damaging the robot unit and robot controller.

For Y axis and Z axis, which has a small static allowable moment, an excessive force applied to the end-effector may damage the slider. If the robot comes in contact with an interfering object, a pressing force due to the motor is applied, possibly damaging it. Pay utmost attention to these possibilities when designing end-effectors.

## Maximum Payload

Design the end-effector so that the total mass of the end-effector including a workpiece will be less than the maximum payload capacity of the robot. The total mass includes the wiring, piping, etc. connected to the robot unit and their stays.

| Robot type | LZNN | LZZN | LYZN | LYZZ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum payload | 5 kg/Z　\*1 | | | |

| Robot type | LSNN | LSSN | LZSN | LZSS |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Maximum payload | 3 kg/S　(2kg/S when S axis is 400 mm)　\*1 | | | |

\*1　Check the range of the center of gravity with "[Allowable range for the center of gravity of the payload (PDF:251KB)](img/005610/005610_1 .pdf)". If the center of gravity locates outside of the allowable range, reduce the weight.

# Stopping Time and Distance (Angle) at an Emergency Stop

Pressing the emergency stop button when the robot is in motion stops the robot, the stopping time required from activation of a stop signal and the distance for major three axes vary with the robot speed as shown in the graphs below. When a combination of multiple axes are used, the required stopping time is that of the axis with the longest motion time. There is no variation with the load conditions.

This page shows the stopping time and distance from the activation of a stop signal.

|  | Measurement conditions |
| --- | --- |
| L axis | Maximum speed: 2 m/s, Acceleration: 0.3 G  Maximum payload (total weight): 24 kg |
| Y and Z axes | Robot type LYZZ  Y axis Maximum speed: 0.5 m/s, Acceleration: 0.5 G  Z axis Maximum speed: 0.5 m/s, Acceleration: 0.3 G  Maximum payload: 5 kg / Z |
| S axis | Maximum speed: 1 m/s, Acceleration: 0.5 G  Maximum payload: 3 kg |

# Installation Environment of the Robot Unit

## Preparing a Proper Environment for Installation

Before installing the robot unit and robot controller, confirm that the operating environment is in conformity with each item of SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, "[Installation Precautions](001928.html)". Also, take proper measures to protect the components from vibration.

In an inappropriate environment, the robot will not operate to its full capacity or performance, components may not last long, and unexpected failure may result.

## Connecting the Robot Unit and Robot Controller

Before delivery, the robot unit and the robot controller are configured as a set. If purchasing two or more robot systems, take care not to mistake combination set when connecting robot units and controllers.

The robot unit and robot controller in a set are given the same serial number.

## Installation Environment of the Robot Unit

The installation requirements for the robot unit are shown in the table below. Prepare a highly rigid mount by referring to the figure below.

Do not electric-weld the equipment including the robot. A large current may flow through the motor encoder or robot controller resulting in a failure. If electric welding is required, remove the robot unit and the robot controller from the equipment beforehand.

| Item | Environments and Conditions |
| --- | --- |
| Flatness of the mount | 0.1/500 mm  Refer to "[Mount Example](005620.html)". |
| Rigidity of the mount | Use steel materials.  Refer to "[Mount Example](005620.html)". |
| Installation type | Floor-mount |
| Ambient temperature | During operation: 0 to 40 ℃ |
| During storage and transportation: -10 to 60 ℃ |
| Humidity | During operation: 20 to 90% RH (No dew condensation allowed.) |
| During storage and transportation: 40 to 75% RH (No dew condensation allowed.) |
| Vibration | During operation: 4.9 m/s^2 (0.5 G) or less |
| During storage and transportation: 29.4 m/s^2 (3 G) or less |
| Safe installation environment | Refer to "[Insuring the Proper Installation Environment](001928.html)". |
| Working space, etc. | Sufficient service space must be available for inspection and disassembly.  Keep a wiring route from the robot unit to the controller, and fasten the wiring to the mounting face or beam so that the weight of the cables will not be directly applied to the connectors. |
| Grounding conditions | Refer to the functional ground, "[Grounding of Robot Unit](005627.html)". |

* When the robot operates at high speed, the robot mount undergoes large reaction forces. The mount must be rigid enough so that it will not vibrate or be displaced due to reaction forces. It is also advisable to mechanically join the robot mount with heavy equipment.
* Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling) when the robot is in motion. If this sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or adjust the robot speed.

## Positioning of the Supports

To fasten the rail unit to the supports, each support must be adjusted to the position on the rail unit which the support can be secured beforehand. The position to secure supports on the rail differs according to the length of the rail.

You need to tap as many holes on the support as required when fixing a rail unit to it. For details, refer to "[Positions of Rail Unit Fixing Bolts (PDF:43KB)](img/005620/005620_3.pdf)".

* When the robot operates at high speed, the robot mount undergoes large reaction forces. The mount must be rigid enough so that it will not vibrate or be displaced due to reaction forces. It is also advisable to mechanically join the robot mount with heavy equipment.
* Some mounts may produce a resonance sound (howling) when the robot is in motion. If this sound is loud, increase the rigidity of the mount or adjust the robot speed.

# Transport

This chapter contains a description of transporting the robot unit.

* Before handling or installing the robot unit, be sure to read SAFETY PRECAUTIONS, "[Installation Precautions 1](001928.html)" and this chapter.
* Do not pick up the robot unit by the cables. The robot unit may be broken.
* The Y axis and the S axis which is unscrewed the slide stop bolt move since no brake is equipped. Be careful so that hand or finger does not get caught by an axis or cableveyor.

The way of taking out the robot from the package and the way of transportation differ according to the robot type. Refer to the explanation below before transportation.

| Robot type | Maximum weight | Refer to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LZNN and LZZN | 9 kg | [Taking out and Transport of LZ\*\* robot](#LZ**) |
| LYZN and LYZZ | 12 kg | [Taking out and Transport of LYZ\* robot](#LYZ*) |
| LSNN and LSSN | 13 kg | [Taking out and Transport of LS\*\* robot](#LS**) |
| LZSN and LZSS | 16 kg | [Taking out and Transport of LZS\* robot](#LZS*) |

## Transport Method

1. Make sure that everything is ready for installation.
2. When the package is opened, the robot is placed on its back. Take out the robot as shown in the photograph about "how to take out the robot". After taking it out, transport it as shown in the photograph about "how to transport the robot".
3. Secure a sufficient passage space and make sure that there is no obstacle or hazard on the way.
4. Fix the robot on the mount by referring to "[Installation](005622.html)
   ".  
   [ For S axis only ]
5. Unscrew the slide stop bolt on the S axis. See the blue arrow shown in [Taking Out and Transport of LS\*\* Robot](#LS**).

# Rack Pitch Adjustment

Connecting racks with the end faces in close contact with each other makes the pitch between the teeth in the connecting part too small which may cause a trouble.

Use a counterpart rack in the connecting part to adjust the pitch between teeth.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005623_1.png)

## Adjustment Procedure

Use the following counterpart rack to make adjustment.

| Manufacturer | Name | Catalog symbol |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kohara Gear Industry Co., Ltd. | CP rack | SRCP5-100 |

###### 1

Check that the gap between rails is 1 mm or less.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005623_3.png)

###### 2

While referring to the fixed rack of the rail unit as a guide, use a counterpart rack to adjust the pitch with the rack to be adjusted.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005623_2.png)

This is the end of rack pitch adjustment.

After adjustment, bring them into close contact using a small clamp, and fix the rail unit to the connecting plate. For details about fixing, refer to STEP 9 in "[Robot Installation Procedure (PDF:544KB)](img/005623/005622.pdf)".

# Backlash Adjustment

The backlash must be properly adjusted to prevent vibration and noise and improve the accuracy of stop positions. The below explains the way of backlash adjustment.

###### 1

Place the robot unit between supports.  
Loosen the four bolts which hold the pinion cover and then remove the pinion cover.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005624_1.png)

###### 2

Install the mechanical stopper to the position illustrated below, and then apply the robot unit to the mechanical unit.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005624_2.png)

###### 3

Loosen the motor plate mounting bolts slightly to the extent that the motor plate does not wobble.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005624_3.png)

###### 4

This picture is taken from the opposite side of the motor.  
Turn the pinion clockwise with hand until the teeth of pinion apply to the left side of the teeth of the rack.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005624_4.png)

###### 5

Set the dial gauge on the tooth of the pinion, and then turn the pinion clockwise to check the amount of backlash.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005624_5.png)

###### 6

Using a 7 mm wrench on the adjustment screw, raise or lower the position of the pinion to adjust the backlash.  
Adjust the pinion so that the back lash is set within 0.04 - 0.06 mm.  
One complete turn of the screw (360°) raises or lowers the lead by 0.8 mm.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005624_6.png)

###### 7

When adjustment is finished, tighten the two motor plate mounting bolts.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Tightening torque | 9.8N･m ± 10% |

###### 8

Put the mechanical stopper back where it has been set.

###### 9

Put the pinion cover back.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Tightening torque | 2.9N･m ± 20% |

This is the end of backlash adjustment.

# Connection of Motor and Encoder Cables

The following shows how to connect a motor and encoder cable, as well as the recommended wiring procedures after establishing the connection.

| Robot type | Connection diagram | Recommended treatment after wiring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LZNN | [LZNN (PDF:178KB)](img/005626/005626_1.pdf) | [LZNN (PDF:110KB)](img/005626/005626_a.pdf) |
| LZZN | [LZZN (PDF:192KB)](img/005626/005626_2.pdf) | [LZZN (PDF:111KB)](img/005626/005626_b.pdf) |
| LYZN | [LYZN (PDF:254KB)](img/005626/005626_3.pdf) | [LYZN, LYZZ (PDF:149KB)](img/005626/005626_c.pdf) |
| LYZZ | [LYZZ (PDF:273KB)](img/005626/005626_4.pdf) |
| LSNN | [LSNN (PDF:232KB)](img/005626/005626_5.pdf) | [LSNN, LSSN (PDF:125KB)](img/005626/005626_d.pdf) |
| LSSN | [LSSN (PDF:251KB)](img/005626/005626_6.pdf) |
| LZSN | [LZSN (PDF:253KB)](img/005626/005626_7.pdf) | [LZSN, LZSS (PDF:155KB)](img/005626/005626_e.pdf) |
| LZSS | [LZSS (PDF:290KB)](img/005626/005626_8.pdf) |

* They can be connected in any order.
* Store the motor and encoder cable, user wirings and user pipings neatly so as not to get tangled.
* Inside the cablevayor, do not bind wirings and cables with banding bands or other tools. Doing so will result in wiring disconnection.
* After the motor and encoder cable has been connected to the robot unit, tighten these wirings with referring to "Recommended treatment after wiring" on the table above.
* For about how to fix the power conversion box set, refer to "[How to fix a power conversion box (PDF:108KB)](img/005626/005626_11.pdf)".

To prevent electric shock and damage to the devices, disconnect the power cable of the controller or shut down the power supply to the controller before disconnecting or connecting the motor and encoder cable.

# Grounding of Robot Unit

Ground the grounding terminal of the robot unit with a wire of 5.5 mm2 or more. There are four grounding terminals each on the upper part of a connecting plate.

Use a dedicated grounding wire and grounding electrode. Do not share them with any other electric power or power equipment such as a welder.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Grounding terminal | Four each on the upper part of the connecting plate. Any of the connecting plates or screw holes may be used. |
| Screw | M4, nominal length of 8 mm or less |
| Grounding wire | 5.5 mm² or more |

# Changing the Mechanical End

Different methods are used to change the mechanical ends for the L, Y, Z, and S axes.

## Precautions on Changing Mechanical End

To change the mechanical end, the customer should supply the mechanical stopper suited for the usage conditions following with reference to the descriptions below.

- After changing the mechanical ends using the mechanical stoppers, be sure to also change the software motion limits to prevent the robot arm from coming into contact with the mechanical stoppers when the robot runs.
- If the robot arm collides against any mechanical stopper, it may be damaged. Before use, contact the Denso service representative for inspection and repair. The mechanical stopper installed by the customer may also be damaged. Do not use it again, and replace it before use.
- The robot failures resulting from the mechanical stoppers shall not be covered by the warranty even if the robot is under warranty.

# Changing the L Axis Mechanical End

## Restriction of Motion of L Axis

The motion of the L axis can be restricted using optional mechanical stoppers. The mechanical stoppers consist of two stopper blocks and four stopper bolts.

Change the mechanical stopper installation positions to set a motion range.

## Installation of Mechanical Stoppers

The figure below shows the reference positions for stopper blocks and stopper bolts.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005629_1.png)

###### 1

Loosen the four stopper bolts M12×50 mm and remove the two stopper blocks.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005629_2.png)

###### 2

Move the stopper blocks by 195 mm.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005629_3.png)

###### 3

Install the stopper block with stopper bolts.　Tightening torque: 42.2N･m±20%

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005629_4.png)

This is the end of the mechanical stopper installation.

# Changing the Mechanical End of Y Axis and Z Axis

## Restriction of Motion of Y Axis or Z Axis

The motion of the Y axis or Z axis can be restricted by supplying and installing mechanical stopper bolts.

Install mechanical stopper bolts on the installation taps inside the linear module. Refer to Installation of Mechanical Stopper Bolts shown below to set an appropriate motion range.

## Installation of Mechanical Stopper Bolts

###### 1

Remove the two cross-recessed head bolts on the side of the axis unit

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005630_1.png)

###### 2

Remove the cover on the side of the axis unit.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005630_2.png)

###### 3

Install mechanical stopper bolts on the installation taps inside.

| Target axis | Bolt | Q'ty | Bolt strength | Tightening torque |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Z axis on LZNN or LZZN | M4×8 | 2 | 12.9 | 3.9 ± 0.8 N･m |
| Y axis on all robot types  Z axis on LZS\* | M5×8 | 2 | 12.9 | 8.8 ± 1.8 N･m |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005630_3.png)

When installing the cover, be careful not to let the stainless sheet on the upper surface of the body caught inside.

The edges of the stainless sheet are sharp. Be very careful not to injure hands, etc.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005630_4.png)

###### 4

Using the same procedure described in STEP 1 to 3, remove the cover on the other side and install two stopper bolts in total.

This is the end of the mechanical stopper bolt installation.

# Changing the S Axis Mechanical End

The restriction of the motion range of the S axis is achieved by changing the joint position of the drive timing belt.

If the mechanical end of the S axis needs to be changed, please contact [our sales representatives](001078.html). The warranty does not cover damage or injury resulting from repairs undertaken by other than our service representatives.

## Changing the Joint Position of the Drive Timing Belt

There are two types of timing belts. This section shows how to adjust the joint position of the drive timing belt.

###### 1

Remove the five cross-recessed screws on the body of the S axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005631_1.png)

###### 2

Take out the cover of the S axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005631_2.png)

###### 3

Loosen the two mounting bolts on the hand plate so that the joint position of the drive timing belt and the belt holder can be adjusted.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005631_3.png)

###### 4

Slide the motor plate and hand plate together against the fixed base plate to the blue arrow direction (see image below). Find the joint position of the drive timing belt so that the motion range of the unit will be suitable for the use, and then tighten the unit with the two mounting bolts.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005631_4.png)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Tightening torque | 2.0±0.2 N･m |

###### 5

Attach the stopper bolt on the lateral side of the base plate of the middle slider.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005631_5.png)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Stopper bolt | M4×8　1 piece |
| Tightening torque | 3.9±0.8 N･m |

###### 6

Attach the cover which was taken out in STEP1 and STEP2, then fasten it with the five cross-recessed screws.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Tightening torque | 0.59±0.06 N･m |

This is the end of the setting change procedure.

# Software Motion Limits

To avoid damages that could be caused by collision or contact with mechanical ends, configure the motion space by setting the software motion limits on individual axes.

By default, the software motion limits are configured slightly inside the mechanical ends.

When the robot reaches the software motion limit while it is manually or automatically running, it will stop with an error message displayed. If the robot is in automatic operation, it also cuts off the power to the motors.

This function becomes valid after the robot arm enters the motion space configured by the software motion limits.

Software motion limit setting is not a function complying with a safety standard.

## Factory Defaults

| Axis name | L axis | Y axis or Z axis | S axis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Positive direction | 330 mm \*1 | Stroke value \*2 | Stroke value \*2 |
| Negative direction | 0 mm | 0 mm | 0 mm |

\*1 Set 330 mm regardless of the optional rail length. Change this setting according to the use.

\*2 The same value as the stroke length. Set 100 mm if the stroke length is 100 mm.

## Precautions When Changing the Software Motion Limits

Confirm the robot motion range in actual working environment. Set the software motion limits using the correct unit of measurement.

If the robot arm lies in the position overriding the software motion limits, e.g., immediately after change of the software motion limits, only a manual operation that moves the robot arm towards the motion space is possible. In the manual operation, move the robot arm in Joint mode.

## Software Motion Limits Changing Procedure

Change the values in the software motion limit setting screen on the teach pendant and turn off the robot controller power and then on again.

For details, refer to "[Displaying and Setting the Software Motion Limit](001758.html)" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

Newly entered settings (software motion limits) go into effect after the restart of the controller.

# CALSET

## What Is CALSET?

CALSET refers to calibrating the relation between the actual robot position and the positional information of the controller. CALSET uses a previously determined axis position where an axis can be secured. It creates CALSET data that matches the actual axis position (CALSET position) with the encoder value. The angle of the CALSET position is saved in the robot controller as a RANG value.

CALSET is complete when the user moves each axis of the robot to the CALSET position by hand and use the teach pendant to have the controller recognize the position information.

* The CALSET data is different for each robot.
* CALSET must be performed when any of the motors is replaced or the encoder backup battery goes dead and the position-related data retained in the encoder is lost.
* CALSET data should be managed by the customer.Back up the CALSET data periodically, referring to "[Backup of Projects](006294.html)".

### Factory Defaults of Robot

The robot unit is not equipped with encoder backup batteries at factory shipment. After installing batteries, be sure to perform CALSET as follows:

## Preparation for CALSET

Manually move each axis of the robot until it is pressed against a mechanical stopper or CALSET jig to determine the CALSET position.

### L Axis

| CALSET jig | Manual operation and CALSET position | CALSET position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use of mechanical stopper | Press the L axis against the mechanical stopper at the negative direction end. |  |
| Use of bolt  (Performing CALSET on multiple L axes on one rail) | Install a bolt into a tapped hole on the connecting plate, and press the L axis against it in the negative direction. After performing CALSET, be sure to remove the bolt and keep it carefully.  Bolt: Misumi Corporation product  Model: MSB12-50 |  |

### Y Axis and Z Axis

| CALSET jig | Manual operation and CALSET position | CALSET position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Not needed | Press the slider against the negative direction end. Be careful of dropping when releasing the brake if equipped.  The Z axis falls by its own weight. Make adjustment while pressing it against the CALSET position. |  |

### S Axis

| CALSET jig | Manual operation and CALSET position | CALSET position |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Not needed | Press the slider against the negative direction end. |  |

## Operation Using a Teach Pendant

Set user level "[Maintainer](001772.html)".

Operation path: Press [F2 Arm] - [F12 Maintenance] - [CALSET] (menu) - [CALSET].

###### 1

[CALSET Setting] window is displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005633_5.png)

###### 2

Select [ON] or [OFF] of the CALSET target axis and press [OK]. A system message for confirmation appears.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005633_6.png)

###### 3

Press [OK] to complete CALSET of the relevant axis.

# Grease Lubrication

Lubricate the specified greases to the slideways of the robot with reference to the following table.

## Lubrication Points

| Lubrication points | Lubrication type | Lubricant amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rack | Epinoc AP1 | 1.0 to 1.3 g/m |
| Rail | Epinoc AP1 | 0.5 to 1.0 g/m |
| Two grease nipples on slider | Epinoc AP1 | 2 to 3 cc |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005635.png)

## Grease Feeding Method

* Grease feeding for rack and rail

Apply grease evenly on the entire lubrication area.

* Grease feeding for slider

Using a grease gun, apply grease to the two grease nipples on the sides of the slider.

Improper lubrication points, amount of grease, or lubrication procedure may cause oil drops from the specified points.

## Checking for Oil Drops

Check that there are no oil drops from the lubrication points. Improper environment, amount of grease, or lubrication procedure may cause oil drops.

# Replacement of Cableveyor

This page contains a description of replacing a cableveyor when it is broken or worn out.

Split and reconnect a cableveyor where replacement is needed according to the procedure shown below.

"Cableveyor" is a registered trademark of Tsubakimoto Chain Co., Ltd. This replacement method is quoted from the instruction manual issued by the said company.

## Splitting of Cableveyor

###### 1

Open the two arms at the splitting position.

Insert a flat-blade screwdriver into a gap between the arm edge and the link at the opening-closing side, turn the screwdriver to the right and left to open the two arms.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_1.png)

###### 2

Insert a flat-blade screwdriver into a gap between links as shown in the figure below, pull the screwdriver toward yourself, and remove the pin from the hole.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_3.png)

###### 3

Using the other pin as a pivot, bend the cableveyor into a dogleg shape to split it.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_4.png)

## Reconnection of Cableveyor

###### 1

Replace the worn link with a spare part. Align the split cableveyors with the arms open at the reconnecting position.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_5.png)

###### 2

With the links overlapped, insert a pin into a hole on one side.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_6.png)

###### 3

Insert another pin into a hole on the other side.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_7.png)

###### 4

Either press the arm edge by hand or hit it with a plastic hammer until an audible click is heard.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_8.png)

This is the end of cableveyor replacement.

After an arm is removed, the open and close directions can be changed.

With the arm raised to 90 degrees, move it sideways (arrow directions) to remove and install it.

When installing an arm, hold it with the inscribed side facing outward and attach it to the link.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005636_2.png)
