# Setting the Control Set of Motion Optimization

The optimum speed or acceleration will vary depending upon the payload and center of gravity of an end-effector or workpiece that is to be set at the end of the robot flange. Set the payload and center of gravity position of the end-effector or workpiece and the control set of motion optimization according to the payload and robot posture.

For details, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Optimal Speed Control Function](001542.html)
".

For the operating procedure, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Setting the Load Conditions](001547.html)
".

The mass of payload is a total mass of an end-effector and workpiece, expressed in grams.

Define the payload center of gravity in the TOOL0 coordinates in units of mm.

## 6Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 6axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 6th axis.

The Y component is defined on the orientation vector directed from the center of the flange to the center of the datum hole. The Z component is defined on the approach vector directed from the center of the flange to the normal line of the flange center. The X component is defined on the normal vector directed along the X axis (+) in the right-hand coordinates whose Y axis is an orientation vector and whose Z axis is an approach vector.

Datum hole is a pin hole which exists on the flange surface.

The size of datum hole differs depending on the robot types; φ6H7 for VM series, φ5H7 for other robots.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_1.png)

### Right Hand Coordinate System

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_2.png)

## 4-Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 4axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 4th axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_3.png)

# Product Warranty

## Warranty Information

In the event that a defect resulting from design, manufacture, or material is discovered in a robot, a controller, and their components (hereafter: product), and the defect is confirmed by us or a service dealer designated by us, we will repair the product free of charge (hereafter: warranty repair).  
 Warranty repair is performed by the replacement of related part and/or the repair.  
 In warranty repair, we will cover the costs associated with the following.

* Cost of parts
* Consumable items necessary for repair
* Labor

## Warranty Period

Warranty period shall be a period of 24 months from the shipment of the product.  
 However, even within the said period, the warranty shall be valid for a period of 18 months from the start of use, or up to 6,000 hours of operation (running) time, whichever comes earlier.

For all repairs after the warranty period is over, we will provide repair services at usual and customary rates.

## Replacement Product Warranty Period

Replacement of defective product originally installed in the equipment system pursuant to the warranty shall not extend the warranty period and the replacement product shall be warranted only for the balance of the warranty period remaining on the original product.

Even if the remaining warranty period for the product is ninety (90) days or less, its parts replaced by us or a service dealer designated by us shall be warranted for ninety (90) days from the day when the replacement is completed.

## Items Not Covered

* Failures, which arise from one of the following, shall not be covered by the warranty even if the product is within warranty period:

1. Failures caused by handling, improper programming, maintenance, inspection or installation other than those specified in the related manuals;
2. Failures caused by non-certified disassembling/repair;
3. Failures caused by disassembling/repair by non-authorized personnel;
4. Failures caused by improper modification by you or a third party, or failures caused by the use of any part, oil/grease or software other than those specified by DENSO WAVE;
5. A robot, a controller, a teach pendant, and a mini pendant
   for which a product serial number or production date cannot be confirmed;
6. Failures caused by a fire, salt damage, earthquake, storm/flood, lightning or other acts of God;
7. Failures due to use in an environment outside of the product specifications, such as improper IP rating, dirt/dust, fluid/coolant, improper power supply, high air pressure, and so on;
8. Damages or malfunctions caused by relocation or transportation after installation;
9. Items not covered in related manuals, such as;
- Failures caused by a worn-out consumable (e.g. natural discoloration of paint/plating, deterioration of consumable parts like fan filter);   
 - Failures with no effects on product quality or function (e.g. mechanical noise of controller, motor sound, reducer sound); and10. Products exposed to dangerous and hazardous materials.

* We charge for following costs regardless of the warranty period:

1. Shipping cost;
2. Travel and accommodation (T & A);
3. Maintenance, adjustment and cleaning;
4. Worn-out consumables and oil/grease (grease, battery, filter, bellows and others); and
5. Adjustment or recovery of internal data, such as programs and position variables, created and modified by the customer.

In no event shall we be liable for any other incidental or consequential damages, such as loss of profit, loss of production, psychological damage and damage to property other than our products resulting from product breakdown or failure.

## Warranty Coverage

This warranty is valid within the country where you purchased the product.  
 When transferring your robot to outside of the country of purchase, by doing the user registration of overseas transfer support from the following URL, your robot will be warranted just as in the country of purchase.

* URL of Overseas Transfer Support Registration page in our website

  <https://www.denso-wave.com/en/robot/support/afterservice/page3_2.html>

If your robot has not been registered in the overseas transfer support, you can send the robot back to our dealer in the country of purchase for repair. The transfer fee of your robot shall be paid by customers.

## Disclaimer

* Please contact your local DENSO Robotics sales office for specific questions pertaining to warranty coverage, as it may vary slightly from region to region.
* We continue to improve reliability and performance of our products, and therefore reserves the right to upgrade the product without prior warning.
* We take no responsibility for any erroneous information or errors in writing in this document.

| Total operation | Shows the grand total of the robot controller ON-time counted after the controller leaves the factory. |
| Total running | Shows the grand total of the robot running time counted after the robot leaves the factory. |
| Cumu. operation | Shows the total of the robot controller ON-time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Cumu. running | Shows the total of the robot running time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Operation | Shows the ON-time of the robot controller counted after it is turned ON this time. |
| Running | Shows the running time of the robot counted after the robot controller is turned ON this time. |

Values of "Cumu. operation" and "Cumu. running" can be reset.

# Resetting Encoders

For the encoder resetting procedure, refer to the "[Setting and Changing Encoder](001751.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

In CALSET work, there are "CALSET" and "Recover CALSET data".  
If a motor is changed, execute "CALSET" and in other cases, execute "Recover CALSET data".

# Backing up Projects

You need to periodically back up project data in WINCAPSIII so that you can smoothly recover the robot controller in case of project data loss due to circumstances such as a controller failure.

Be sure to back up and preserve project data, particularly in the following cases:

* at the time of purchase
* after performing CALSET
* after changing RANG values
* after replacing a motor
* after updating robot controller data

DENSO preserves arm data configured at the time of shipment for 10 years. If your arm data is lost, contact our [Sales](001077.html) representatives.

Arm data refers to CALSET and RANG values in project data, which is unique to individual robots and determines the position of each joint.

## Outline

To prevent interference with other devices or entanglement of the end-effector wiring and piping, limit the motion range as needed by setting the mechanical ends for defining the "restricted space" and the software motion limits for defining the "motion space."

After changing the mechanical ends, change also the software motion limits so that the motion space comes within the restricted space.

# Changing RANG Values

A RANG value refers to an angle that determines the relationship between the reference position of the robot arm and the CALSET position, and is also called a reference angle or ready angle.

The factory defaults of RANG values for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd axes are obtained when each axis is in contact with the corresponding mechanical end configured at the time of shipment.

When CALSET is required but mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer cannot be removed so that the robot arm cannot take a posture in the CALSET position determined at the time of shipment, then it is necessary to change the RANG values stored in the controller to the ones obtained by the CALSET position determined by the mechanical stopper parts mounted by the customer.

If the RANG values are changed, the mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer influence the precision of CALSET.

###### 1

Move an axis whose RANG value is to be changed towards the mechanical end by manual operation in Joint mode and slowly press the axis against the mechanical end.

###### 2

Make a note of the RANG value of the corresponding axis in Joint mode which is shown in the current position.

###### 3

On the RANG window, change the current RANG value of the corresponding axis to the value of the note.  
For manner of operation, please refer to "[Manual Input Operation of RANG and CALSET Values](001757.html)"
of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Configurators

The whole configuration of the robot system is shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000820_1.png)

## Robot Unit

This is an industry robot that drives the arms with the motors to assemble and transport workpieces. Hands or other end effectors should be attached to the flange by the customer.

## Robot Controller

The controller controls the motion of the robot unit according to programs built with signals sent from the connected facilities management equipment.

It also allows the customer to teach the robot unit by operating it with any of the operation devices.

## Operation Devices

The operation devices are used to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

For details about hardware, refer to the Operation Guide. For instructions on how to operate these devices, refer to the "[TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001674.html)
" and "[MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001806.html)".

### Teach Pendant (TP)

The teach pendant is a multifunctional operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, programming, and all settings.

The teach pendant can also be used as an operation panel created by the teach pendant panel editor.

### Mini-Pendant (MP)

The mini-pendant is a simplified operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, and a part of settings.

## Offline Software

The software enables backing up of project data in the controller and editing, management, movement simulation of programs. WINCAPSIII is an offline software designed for the Denso robot system. The trial version comes with the robot system at no extra charge. For details, refer to the [WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html).

## Facilities Management Equipment

The management equipment is a system that the customer sets up for managing the facilities. Denso robots can be linked with it via the CC-Link, Ethernet/IP, and other various networks.

# Robot Positioning Time

1. Following figures show the positioning times used to calculate the cycle time.
2. Positioning time means the time from the start of robot operation to the arrival at the target positioning point.
3. After the robot moves to and passes the target positioning point, vibration will be dampened and the robot positioned at the target positioning point as shown in Figure below. This vibration dampening time is not considered in the graph.

1. The vibration dampening time depends on factors such as the weight of the end-effector. If the robot is to be used in such a way that it overshoots or if the vibration damping time is of great concern, test the robot carefully beforehand.
2. If acceleration begins before residual vibration of the robot stops, an overcurrent error may be displayed. In this case, take one of the following measures:  
   Ｘ　Lower the deceleration of the preceding operation with a DECEL command to reduce residual vibration.  
   Ｘ　Keep the robot in stand-by with a DELAY command until residual vibration stops.  
   Ｘ　Lower acceleration with an ACCEL command.
3. Operate the robot with the optimum load setting in accordance with the end-effector weight and workpiece weight. If not, a robot failure may result.

# Setting the Control Set of Motion Optimization

The optimum speed or acceleration will vary depending upon the payload and center of gravity of an end-effector or workpiece that is to be set at the end of the robot flange. Set the payload and center of gravity position of the end-effector or workpiece and the control set of motion optimization according to the payload and robot posture.

For details, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Optimal Speed Control Function](001542.html)
".

For the operating procedure, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Setting the Load Conditions](001547.html)
".

The mass of payload is a total mass of an end-effector and workpiece, expressed in grams.

Define the payload center of gravity in the TOOL0 coordinates in units of mm.

## 6Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 6axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 6th axis.

The Y component is defined on the orientation vector directed from the center of the flange to the center of the datum hole. The Z component is defined on the approach vector directed from the center of the flange to the normal line of the flange center. The X component is defined on the normal vector directed along the X axis (+) in the right-hand coordinates whose Y axis is an orientation vector and whose Z axis is an approach vector.

Datum hole is a pin hole which exists on the flange surface.

The size of datum hole differs depending on the robot types; φ6H7 for VM series, φ5H7 for other robots.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_1.png)

### Right Hand Coordinate System

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_2.png)

## 4-Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 4axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 4th axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_3.png)

# Checking the Controller ON-Time and the Robot Running Time and Resetting Their User Counters

You may check the robot controller ON-time and the robot running time.  
Hours that you can check are the following items.

Refer to the "[Displaying System Information (Robot Tab)](001774.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Total operation | Shows the grand total of the robot controller ON-time counted after the controller leaves the factory. |
| Total running | Shows the grand total of the robot running time counted after the robot leaves the factory. |
| Cumu. operation | Shows the total of the robot controller ON-time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Cumu. running | Shows the total of the robot running time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Operation | Shows the ON-time of the robot controller counted after it is turned ON this time. |
| Running | Shows the running time of the robot counted after the robot controller is turned ON this time. |

Values of "Cumu. operation" and "Cumu. running" can be reset.

# Resetting Encoders

When an error occurs due to run-down encoder backup batteries, or due to a great impact to the robot during turning-off the controller, you need to reset encoders and perform CALSET work.

For the encoder resetting procedure, refer to the "[Setting and Changing Encoder](001751.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

In CALSET work, there are "CALSET" and "Recover CALSET data".  
If a motor is changed, execute "CALSET" and in other cases, execute "Recover CALSET data".

# Backing up Projects

You need to periodically back up project data in WINCAPSIII so that you can smoothly recover the robot controller in case of project data loss due to circumstances such as a controller failure.

Be sure to back up and preserve project data, particularly in the following cases:

* at the time of purchase
* after performing CALSET
* after changing RANG values
* after replacing a motor
* after updating robot controller data

DENSO preserves arm data configured at the time of shipment for 10 years. If your arm data is lost, contact our [Sales](001077.html) representatives.

Arm data refers to CALSET and RANG values in project data, which is unique to individual robots and determines the position of each joint.

# Limiting the Motion Range

## Outline

To prevent interference with other devices or entanglement of the end-effector wiring and piping, limit the motion range as needed by setting the mechanical ends for defining the "restricted space" and the software motion limits for defining the "motion space."

After changing the mechanical ends, change also the software motion limits so that the motion space comes within the restricted space.

# Changing RANG Values

A RANG value refers to an angle that determines the relationship between the reference position of the robot arm and the CALSET position, and is also called a reference angle or ready angle.

The factory defaults of RANG values for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd axes are obtained when each axis is in contact with the corresponding mechanical end configured at the time of shipment.

When CALSET is required but mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer cannot be removed so that the robot arm cannot take a posture in the CALSET position determined at the time of shipment, then it is necessary to change the RANG values stored in the controller to the ones obtained by the CALSET position determined by the mechanical stopper parts mounted by the customer.

If the RANG values are changed, the mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer influence the precision of CALSET.

###### 1

Move an axis whose RANG value is to be changed towards the mechanical end by manual operation in Joint mode and slowly press the axis against the mechanical end.

###### 2

Make a note of the RANG value of the corresponding axis in Joint mode which is shown in the current position.

###### 3

On the RANG window, change the current RANG value of the corresponding axis to the value of the note.  
For manner of operation, please refer to "[Manual Input Operation of RANG and CALSET Values](001757.html)"
of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Configurators

The whole configuration of the robot system is shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000820_1.png)

## Robot Unit

This is an industry robot that drives the arms with the motors to assemble and transport workpieces. Hands or other end effectors should be attached to the flange by the customer.

## Robot Controller

The controller controls the motion of the robot unit according to programs built with signals sent from the connected facilities management equipment.

It also allows the customer to teach the robot unit by operating it with any of the operation devices.

## Operation Devices

The operation devices are used to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

For details about hardware, refer to the Operation Guide. For instructions on how to operate these devices, refer to the "[TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001674.html)
" and "[MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001806.html)".

### Teach Pendant (TP)

The teach pendant is a multifunctional operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, programming, and all settings.

The teach pendant can also be used as an operation panel created by the teach pendant panel editor.

### Mini-Pendant (MP)

The mini-pendant is a simplified operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, and a part of settings.

## Offline Software

The software enables backing up of project data in the controller and editing, management, movement simulation of programs. WINCAPSIII is an offline software designed for the Denso robot system. The trial version comes with the robot system at no extra charge. For details, refer to the [WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html).

## Facilities Management Equipment

The management equipment is a system that the customer sets up for managing the facilities. Denso robots can be linked with it via the CC-Link, Ethernet/IP, and other various networks.

# Setting the Control Set of Motion Optimization

The optimum speed or acceleration will vary depending upon the payload and center of gravity of an end-effector or workpiece that is to be set at the end of the robot flange. Set the payload and center of gravity position of the end-effector or workpiece and the control set of motion optimization according to the payload and robot posture.

For details, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Optimal Speed Control Function](001542.html)
".

For the operating procedure, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Setting the Load Conditions](001547.html)
".

The mass of payload is a total mass of an end-effector and workpiece, expressed in grams.

Define the payload center of gravity in the TOOL0 coordinates in units of mm.

## 6Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 6axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 6th axis.

The Y component is defined on the orientation vector directed from the center of the flange to the center of the datum hole. The Z component is defined on the approach vector directed from the center of the flange to the normal line of the flange center. The X component is defined on the normal vector directed along the X axis (+) in the right-hand coordinates whose Y axis is an orientation vector and whose Z axis is an approach vector.

Datum hole is a pin hole which exists on the flange surface.

The size of datum hole differs depending on the robot types; φ6H7 for VM series, φ5H7 for other robots.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_1.png)

### Right Hand Coordinate System

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_2.png)

## 4-Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 4axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 4th axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_3.png)

# Product Warranty

## Warranty Information

In the event that a defect resulting from design, manufacture, or material is discovered in a robot, a controller, and their components (hereafter: product), and the defect is confirmed by us or a service dealer designated by us, we will repair the product free of charge (hereafter: warranty repair).  
 Warranty repair is performed by the replacement of related part and/or the repair.  
 In warranty repair, we will cover the costs associated with the following.

* Cost of parts
* Consumable items necessary for repair
* Labor

## Warranty Period

Warranty period shall be a period of 24 months from the shipment of the product.  
 However, even within the said period, the warranty shall be valid for a period of 18 months from the start of use, or up to 6,000 hours of operation (running) time, whichever comes earlier.

For all repairs after the warranty period is over, we will provide repair services at usual and customary rates.

## Replacement Product Warranty Period

Replacement of defective product originally installed in the equipment system pursuant to the warranty shall not extend the warranty period and the replacement product shall be warranted only for the balance of the warranty period remaining on the original product.

Even if the remaining warranty period for the product is ninety (90) days or less, its parts replaced by us or a service dealer designated by us shall be warranted for ninety (90) days from the day when the replacement is completed.

## Items Not Covered

* Failures, which arise from one of the following, shall not be covered by the warranty even if the product is within warranty period:

1. Failures caused by handling, improper programming, maintenance, inspection or installation other than those specified in the related manuals;
2. Failures caused by non-certified disassembling/repair;
3. Failures caused by disassembling/repair by non-authorized personnel;
4. Failures caused by improper modification by you or a third party, or failures caused by the use of any part, oil/grease or software other than those specified by DENSO WAVE;
5. A robot, a controller, a teach pendant, and a mini pendant
   for which a product serial number or production date cannot be confirmed;
6. Failures caused by a fire, salt damage, earthquake, storm/flood, lightning or other acts of God;
7. Failures due to use in an environment outside of the product specifications, such as improper IP rating, dirt/dust, fluid/coolant, improper power supply, high air pressure, and so on;
8. Damages or malfunctions caused by relocation or transportation after installation;
9. Items not covered in related manuals, such as;
- Failures caused by a worn-out consumable (e.g. natural discoloration of paint/plating, deterioration of consumable parts like fan filter);   
 - Failures with no effects on product quality or function (e.g. mechanical noise of controller, motor sound, reducer sound); and10. Products exposed to dangerous and hazardous materials.

* We charge for following costs regardless of the warranty period:

1. Shipping cost;
2. Travel and accommodation (T & A);
3. Maintenance, adjustment and cleaning;
4. Worn-out consumables and oil/grease (grease, battery, filter, bellows and others); and
5. Adjustment or recovery of internal data, such as programs and position variables, created and modified by the customer.

In no event shall we be liable for any other incidental or consequential damages, such as loss of profit, loss of production, psychological damage and damage to property other than our products resulting from product breakdown or failure.

## Warranty Coverage

This warranty is valid within the country where you purchased the product.  
 When transferring your robot to outside of the country of purchase, by doing the user registration of overseas transfer support from the following URL, your robot will be warranted just as in the country of purchase.

* URL of Overseas Transfer Support Registration page in our website

  <https://www.denso-wave.com/en/robot/support/afterservice/page3_2.html>

If your robot has not been registered in the overseas transfer support, you can send the robot back to our dealer in the country of purchase for repair. The transfer fee of your robot shall be paid by customers.

## Disclaimer

* Please contact your local DENSO Robotics sales office for specific questions pertaining to warranty coverage, as it may vary slightly from region to region.
* We continue to improve reliability and performance of our products, and therefore reserves the right to upgrade the product without prior warning.
* We take no responsibility for any erroneous information or errors in writing in this document.

# Checking the Odometer and Trip Meter

You may check the odometer which count traversed distance of each axis after shipment.

Refer to the "[Displaying System Information (Robot Tab)](001774.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

## Odometer

Shows the total distance of each axis traversed after the robot leaves the factory. You cannot reset the odometer.

# Checking the Controller ON-Time and the Robot Running Time and Resetting Their User Counters

You may check the robot controller ON-time and the robot running time.  
Hours that you can check are the following items.

Refer to the "[Displaying System Information (Robot Tab)](001774.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Total operation | Shows the grand total of the robot controller ON-time counted after the controller leaves the factory. |
| Total running | Shows the grand total of the robot running time counted after the robot leaves the factory. |
| Cumu. operation | Shows the total of the robot controller ON-time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Cumu. running | Shows the total of the robot running time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Operation | Shows the ON-time of the robot controller counted after it is turned ON this time. |
| Running | Shows the running time of the robot counted after the robot controller is turned ON this time. |

Values of "Cumu. operation" and "Cumu. running" can be reset.

ID : 6088

# Resetting Encoders

When an error occurs due to run-down encoder backup batteries, or due to a great impact to the robot during turning-off the controller, you need to reset encoders and perform CALSET work.

For the encoder resetting procedure, refer to the "[Setting and Changing Encoder](001751.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

In CALSET work, there are "CALSET" and "Recover CALSET data".  
If a motor is changed, execute "CALSET" and in other cases, execute "Recover CALSET data".

# Backing up Projects

You need to periodically back up project data in WINCAPSIII so that you can smoothly recover the robot controller in case of project data loss due to circumstances such as a controller failure.

Be sure to back up and preserve project data, particularly in the following cases:

* at the time of purchase
* after performing CALSET
* after changing RANG values
* after replacing a motor
* after updating robot controller data

DENSO preserves arm data configured at the time of shipment for 10 years. If your arm data is lost, contact our [Sales](001077.html) representatives.

Arm data refers to CALSET and RANG values in project data, which is unique to individual robots and determines the position of each joint.

# Limiting the Motion Range

## Outline

To prevent interference with other devices or entanglement of the end-effector wiring and piping, limit the motion range as needed by setting the mechanical ends for defining the "restricted space" and the software motion limits for defining the "motion space."

After changing the mechanical ends, change also the software motion limits so that the motion space comes within the restricted space.

# Changing RANG Values

A RANG value refers to an angle that determines the relationship between the reference position of the robot arm and the CALSET position, and is also called a reference angle or ready angle.

The factory defaults of RANG values for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd axes are obtained when each axis is in contact with the corresponding mechanical end configured at the time of shipment.

When CALSET is required but mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer cannot be removed so that the robot arm cannot take a posture in the CALSET position determined at the time of shipment, then it is necessary to change the RANG values stored in the controller to the ones obtained by the CALSET position determined by the mechanical stopper parts mounted by the customer.

If the RANG values are changed, the mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer influence the precision of CALSET.

###### 1

Move an axis whose RANG value is to be changed towards the mechanical end by manual operation in Joint mode and slowly press the axis against the mechanical end.

###### 2

Make a note of the RANG value of the corresponding axis in Joint mode which is shown in the current position.

###### 3

On the RANG window, change the current RANG value of the corresponding axis to the value of the note.  
For manner of operation, please refer to "[Manual Input Operation of RANG and CALSET Values](001757.html)"
of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Stopping Time and Distance (Angle) at an Emergency Stop

Pressing the emergency stop button when the robot is in motion stops the robot, the stopping time required from activation of a stop signal and the distance (angle) for major three joints vary with the robot speed as shown in the graphs below. The measuring conditions are: Robot arm extended, 33%, 66% and 100% of the maximum payload.

Acceleration is different depend on the payload. Graphs below show the value of maximum stopping time and distance.

Stop all axis or power supply shuts down in 900ms.

# Stopping Time and Distance (Angle) at an Emergency Stop

Pressing the emergency stop button when the robot is in motion stops the robot, the stopping time required from activation of a stop signal and the distance (angle) for major three joints vary with the robot speed as shown in the graphs below. The measuring conditions are: Robot arm extended, 33%, 66% and 100% of the maximum payload.

Acceleration is different depend on the payload. Graphs below show the value of maximum stopping time and distance.

Stop all axis or power supply shuts down in 900ms.

ID : 6106

# Configurators

The whole configuration of the robot system is shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000820_1.png)

## Robot Unit

This is an industry robot that drives the arms with the motors to assemble and transport workpieces. Hands or other end effectors should be attached to the flange by the customer.

## Robot Controller

The controller controls the motion of the robot unit according to programs built with signals sent from the connected facilities management equipment.

It also allows the customer to teach the robot unit by operating it with any of the operation devices.

## Operation Devices

The operation devices are used to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

For details about hardware, refer to the Operation Guide. For instructions on how to operate these devices, refer to the "[TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001674.html)
" and "[MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001806.html)".

### Teach Pendant (TP)

The teach pendant is a multifunctional operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, programming, and all settings.

The teach pendant can also be used as an operation panel created by the teach pendant panel editor.

### Mini-Pendant (MP)

The mini-pendant is a simplified operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, and a part of settings.

## Offline Software

The software enables backing up of project data in the controller and editing, management, movement simulation of programs. WINCAPSIII is an offline software designed for the Denso robot system. The trial version comes with the robot system at no extra charge. For details, refer to the [WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html).

## Facilities Management Equipment

The management equipment is a system that the customer sets up for managing the facilities. Denso robots can be linked with it via the CC-Link, Ethernet/IP, and other various networks.

# Robot Positioning Time

1. Following figures show the positioning times used to calculate the cycle time.
2. Positioning time means the time from the start of robot operation to the arrival at the target positioning point.
3. After the robot moves to and passes the target positioning point, vibration will be dampened and the robot positioned at the target positioning point as shown in Figure below. This vibration dampening time is not considered in the graph.

1. The vibration dampening time depends on factors such as the weight of the end-effector. If the robot is to be used in such a way that it overshoots or if the vibration damping time is of great concern, test the robot carefully beforehand.
2. If acceleration begins before residual vibration of the robot stops, an overcurrent error may be displayed. In this case, take one of the following measures:  
   Ｘ　Lower the deceleration of the preceding operation with a DECEL command to reduce residual vibration.  
   Ｘ　Keep the robot in stand-by with a DELAY command until residual vibration stops.  
   Ｘ　Lower acceleration with an ACCEL command.
3. Operate the robot with the optimum load setting in accordance with the end-effector weight and workpiece weight. If not, a robot failure may result.

# Changing RANG Values

A RANG value refers to an angle that determines the relationship between the reference position of the robot arm and the CALSET position, and is also called a reference angle or ready angle.

The factory defaults of RANG values for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd axes are obtained when each axis is in contact with the corresponding mechanical end configured at the time of shipment.

When CALSET is required but mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer cannot be removed so that the robot arm cannot take a posture in the CALSET position determined at the time of shipment, then it is necessary to change the RANG values stored in the controller to the ones obtained by the CALSET position determined by the mechanical stopper parts mounted by the customer.

If the RANG values are changed, the mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer influence the precision of CALSET.

###### 1

Move an axis whose RANG value is to be changed towards the mechanical end by manual operation in Joint mode and slowly press the axis against the mechanical end.

###### 2

Make a note of the RANG value of the corresponding axis in Joint mode which is shown in the current position.

###### 3

On the RANG window, change the current RANG value of the corresponding axis to the value of the note.  
For manner of operation, please refer to "[Manual Input Operation of RANG and CALSET Values](001757.html)"
of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Checking the Controller ON-Time and the Robot Running Time and Resetting Their User Counters

You may check the robot controller ON-time and the robot running time.  
Hours that you can check are the following items.

Refer to the "[Displaying System Information (Robot Tab)](001774.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Total operation | Shows the grand total of the robot controller ON-time counted after the controller leaves the factory. |
| Total running | Shows the grand total of the robot running time counted after the robot leaves the factory. |
| Cumu. operation | Shows the total of the robot controller ON-time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Cumu. running | Shows the total of the robot running time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Operation | Shows the ON-time of the robot controller counted after it is turned ON this time. |
| Running | Shows the running time of the robot counted after the robot controller is turned ON this time. |

Values of "Cumu. operation" and "Cumu. running" can be reset.

If a motor is changed, execute "CALSET" and in other cases, execute "Recover CALSET data".

# Backing up Projects

You need to periodically back up project data in WINCAPSIII so that you can smoothly recover the robot controller in case of project data loss due to circumstances such as a controller failure.

Be sure to back up and preserve project data, particularly in the following cases:

* at the time of purchase
* after performing CALSET
* after changing RANG values
* after replacing a motor
* after updating robot controller data

DENSO preserves arm data configured at the time of shipment for 10 years. If your arm data is lost, contact our [Sales](001077.html) representatives.

Arm data refers to CALSET and RANG values in project data, which is unique to individual robots and determines the position of each joint.

# Product Warranty

## Warranty Information

In the event that a defect resulting from design, manufacture, or material is discovered in a robot, a controller, and their components (hereafter: product), and the defect is confirmed by us or a service dealer designated by us, we will repair the product free of charge (hereafter: warranty repair).  
 Warranty repair is performed by the replacement of related part and/or the repair.  
 In warranty repair, we will cover the costs associated with the following.

* Cost of parts
* Consumable items necessary for repair
* Labor

## Warranty Period

Warranty period shall be a period of 24 months from the shipment of the product.  
 However, even within the said period, the warranty shall be valid for a period of 18 months from the start of use, or up to 6,000 hours of operation (running) time, whichever comes earlier.

For all repairs after the warranty period is over, we will provide repair services at usual and customary rates.

## Replacement Product Warranty Period

Replacement of defective product originally installed in the equipment system pursuant to the warranty shall not extend the warranty period and the replacement product shall be warranted only for the balance of the warranty period remaining on the original product.

Even if the remaining warranty period for the product is ninety (90) days or less, its parts replaced by us or a service dealer designated by us shall be warranted for ninety (90) days from the day when the replacement is completed.

## Items Not Covered

* Failures, which arise from one of the following, shall not be covered by the warranty even if the product is within warranty period:

1. Failures caused by handling, improper programming, maintenance, inspection or installation other than those specified in the related manuals;
2. Failures caused by non-certified disassembling/repair;
3. Failures caused by disassembling/repair by non-authorized personnel;
4. Failures caused by improper modification by you or a third party, or failures caused by the use of any part, oil/grease or software other than those specified by DENSO WAVE;
5. A robot, a controller, a teach pendant, and a mini pendant
   for which a product serial number or production date cannot be confirmed;
6. Failures caused by a fire, salt damage, earthquake, storm/flood, lightning or other acts of God;
7. Failures due to use in an environment outside of the product specifications, such as improper IP rating, dirt/dust, fluid/coolant, improper power supply, high air pressure, and so on;
8. Damages or malfunctions caused by relocation or transportation after installation;
9. Items not covered in related manuals, such as;
- Failures caused by a worn-out consumable (e.g. natural discoloration of paint/plating, deterioration of consumable parts like fan filter);   
 - Failures with no effects on product quality or function (e.g. mechanical noise of controller, motor sound, reducer sound); and10. Products exposed to dangerous and hazardous materials.

* We charge for following costs regardless of the warranty period:

1. Shipping cost;
2. Travel and accommodation (T & A);
3. Maintenance, adjustment and cleaning;
4. Worn-out consumables and oil/grease (grease, battery, filter, bellows and others); and
5. Adjustment or recovery of internal data, such as programs and position variables, created and modified by the customer.

In no event shall we be liable for any other incidental or consequential damages, such as loss of profit, loss of production, psychological damage and damage to property other than our products resulting from product breakdown or failure.

## Warranty Coverage

This warranty is valid within the country where you purchased the product.  
 When transferring your robot to outside of the country of purchase, by doing the user registration of overseas transfer support from the following URL, your robot will be warranted just as in the country of purchase.

* URL of Overseas Transfer Support Registration page in our website

  <https://www.denso-wave.com/en/robot/support/afterservice/page3_2.html>

If your robot has not been registered in the overseas transfer support, you can send the robot back to our dealer in the country of purchase for repair. The transfer fee of your robot shall be paid by customers.

## Disclaimer

* Please contact your local DENSO Robotics sales office for specific questions pertaining to warranty coverage, as it may vary slightly from region to region.
* We continue to improve reliability and performance of our products, and therefore reserves the right to upgrade the product without prior warning.
* We take no responsibility for any erroneous information or errors in writing in this document.

# Configurators

The whole configuration of the robot system is shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000820_1.png)

## Robot Unit

This is an industry robot that drives the arms with the motors to assemble and transport workpieces. Hands or other end effectors should be attached to the flange by the customer.

## Robot Controller

The controller controls the motion of the robot unit according to programs built with signals sent from the connected facilities management equipment.

It also allows the customer to teach the robot unit by operating it with any of the operation devices.

## Operation Devices

The operation devices are used to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

For details about hardware, refer to the Operation Guide. For instructions on how to operate these devices, refer to the "[TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001674.html)
" and "[MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001806.html)".

### Teach Pendant (TP)

The teach pendant is a multifunctional operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, programming, and all settings.

The teach pendant can also be used as an operation panel created by the teach pendant panel editor.

### Mini-Pendant (MP)

The mini-pendant is a simplified operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, and a part of settings.

## Offline Software

The software enables backing up of project data in the controller and editing, management, movement simulation of programs. WINCAPSIII is an offline software designed for the Denso robot system. The trial version comes with the robot system at no extra charge. For details, refer to the [WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html).

## Facilities Management Equipment

The management equipment is a system that the customer sets up for managing the facilities. Denso robots can be linked with it via the CC-Link, Ethernet/IP, and other various networks.

# Wire Connection Required in Starting Up the Robot

This section shows the minimum wire connection required for the stand-alone robot unit to turn the motor power ON or run in Auto or Manual mode during adjustment in starting up the robot system.

## Configuration of Safety Circuit

Input signals to the safety circuit are important for safety. Be sure to configure their circuits with contacts as shown below, observing the notes given below.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

For the overall configuration of safety circuits, refer to Mini I/O MANUAL for respective controllers.

RC8A : [[NPN type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002347.html), [[PNP type] Safety Circuit of RC8A](002348.html)

RC8 : [[NPN type] Safety Circuit of RC8](001374.html), [[PNP type] Safety Circuit of RC8](001381.html)

## Wire Connection Required for Motor ON

Short-circuiting both the Emergency Stop input circuits (dual line) only enables the motor to turn ON.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| External Emergency Stop 1 | #2 and #36 on Mini I/O connector |
| External Emergency Stop 2 | #3 and #37 on Mini I/O connector |

Two External Emergency Stop input signals must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the emergency stop state cannot be reset.

## Wire Connection Required for Automatic Operation

Turning this signal ON (shorting) enables switching to Auto mode.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| Enable Auto 1 | #1 and #35 on Mini I/O connector |
| Enable Auto 2 | #31 and #65 on Mini I/O connector |
| Protective Stop 1 | #4 and #38 on Mini I/O connector |
| Protective Stop 2 | #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector |

1. Two Enable Auto and two Protective Stop input signals must be controlled with separate contacts. Two circuits connected in parallel using a single contact or an always-shorted circuit will be interpreted as an external circuit failure so that the circuit will not operate.
2. If no Protective Stop input signals are needed, their circuits can be always short-circuited by terminal connection with jumpers between #4 and #38 and between terminals #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector.

# Operation Modes

The robot offers three operation modes - Manual mode, Teach check mode, and Auto mode.

The Manual mode is used to run the robot manually from the teach pendant and mini-pendant. The Teach check mode provides restricted automatic operation for a final check of programs with the teach pendant after teaching. The Auto mode allows the robot to run automatically.

The teach pendant or mini-pendant supports all of the above three modes.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001527_1.png)

# Setting Connection with WINCAPSIII

## For EtherNet Connection

### Setting Robot Controller

Set robot controller to enable the communication between PC (WINCAPSIII) and robot controller through the Ethernet.This setting is done by teach pendant.

Set communication permission and IP address.

###### 1

Press [F6 Setting] on the basic screen of tech pendant.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_1.png)

[Settings (main)] window will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_2.png)

###### 2

Press [F5 Communication and Token].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_3.png)

[Menu] window of Communication Settings will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_4.png)

###### 3

Press [F2 Network and Permission].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_5.png)

[Communication Settings] window will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_6.png)

###### 4

Select [Permission] by using cursor key or jog dial, or by directly touching the screen.  
This can be also selected by directly touching the screen.  
The selected section will be highlighted.

###### 5

Press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_7.png)

The following system message will be displayed.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_8.png)

###### 6

Select [Read/Write].

Communication permission is defined as follows.  
To use Ethernet, it is necessary to select [Read/Write].

* Disabled : Communication port is not used.
* Read only : Data of robot controller can be read in PC.Data cannot be sent from PC to robot controller.
* Read/Write : Data can be bidirectionally exchangeable between PC and robot controller.

Select, and then press [OK].  
The display will be back to [Communication Settings] window.

###### 7

Select [IP Address] by using cursor key or jog dial, or by directly touching the screen.  
The selected section will be highlighted.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_9.png)

###### 8

Press [F5 Edit].

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_10.png)

Numeric keypad as shown in the next step will be displayed.

###### 9

Enter address using numeric keypad.  
Press [OK] on the numeric keypad after finishing entering the address.  
 Press [OK] to go back to [Communication Settings] window.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/001717_11.png)

If subnet mask is also required to be changed, follow the operation procedure (STEP 7 to STEP 9) to change it.

###### 10

Press [OK] on Communication Settings screen.  
Display will be back to [Menu] window of Communication Settings.

###### 11

Press [Cancel] button twice on the tech pendant.  
Display will be back to the basic screen.

You can use multiple Ethernet IP address by adding a LAN adopter listed in "[RECOMMENDED BOARD LIST](005079.html)".  
Note that communication may fail if IP addresses in the same network are used.

* Incorrect IP address assignment  
  LAN1：192.168.0.1  
  LAN2：192.168.0.2
* Revised IP address assignment  
  LAN1：192.168.0.1  
  LAN2：192.168.1.2

# Wire Connection Required to Prepare a Robot and RC8 (Safety-I/O-Less)

This section shows the minimum wire connection required for the stand-alone robot unit to turn the motor power ON or run in Auto or Manual mode during adjustment in starting up the robot system.

## Configuration of Emergency Stop Circuitry

The *External Emergency Stop* and *Enable Auto* input signals are important for safety. Be sure to configure their circuits with contacts as shown below.

|  |
| --- |
|  |

## Wire Connection Required for Motor ON

Short-circuiting both the *Emergency Stop* input circuits (dual line) only enables the motor to turn ON.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| *External Emergency Stop 1* | #2 and #36 on connector CN5 |
| *External Emergency Stop 2* | #3 and #37 on connector CN5 |

The different status between two emergency stop circuits, if kept for at least approx. one second, will be interpreted as an occurrence of trouble, triggering an error "One of the external emergency stop  
line is disconnected."

## Wire Connection Required for Automatic Operation

1. Turning this signal ON (shorting) enables switching to Auto mode.
2. Turning this signal OFF (opening) enables switching to Manual or Teach check mode.

| Input signal name | Terminal number |
| --- | --- |
| *Enable Auto* | #1 and #35 on connector CN5 |
| *Protective Stop 1* | #4 and #38 on Mini I/O connector |
| *Protective Stop 2* | #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector |

If no *Protective Stop* input signals are needed, their circuits can be always short-circuited by terminal connection with jumpers between #4 and #38 and between terminals #5 and #39 on Mini I/O connector.

# Limiting the Motion Range

## Outline

To prevent interference with other devices or entanglement of the end-effector wiring and piping, limit the motion range as needed by setting the mechanical ends for defining the "restricted space" and the software motion limits for defining the "motion space."

After changing the mechanical ends, change also the software motion limits so that the motion space comes within the restricted space.

# Configurators

The whole configuration of the robot system is shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000820_1.png)

## Robot Unit

This is an industry robot that drives the arms with the motors to assemble and transport workpieces. Hands or other end effectors should be attached to the flange by the customer.

## Robot Controller

The controller controls the motion of the robot unit according to programs built with signals sent from the connected facilities management equipment.

It also allows the customer to teach the robot unit by operating it with any of the operation devices.

## Operation Devices

The operation devices are used to manually operate the robot unit or make various settings.

For details about hardware, refer to the Operation Guide. For instructions on how to operate these devices, refer to the "[TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001674.html)
" and "[MINI PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE](001806.html)".

### Teach Pendant (TP)

The teach pendant is a multifunctional operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, programming, and all settings.

The teach pendant can also be used as an operation panel created by the teach pendant panel editor.

### Mini-Pendant (MP)

The mini-pendant is a simplified operation device that enables robot operation, teaching, mode switching, programmed start, and a part of settings.

## Offline Software

The software enables backing up of project data in the controller and editing, management, movement simulation of programs. WINCAPSIII is an offline software designed for the Denso robot system. The trial version comes with the robot system at no extra charge. For details, refer to the [WINCAPSIII GUIDE](004552.html).

## Facilities Management Equipment

The management equipment is a system that the customer sets up for managing the facilities. Denso robots can be linked with it via the CC-Link, Ethernet/IP, and other various networks.

# Robot Positioning Time

1. Following figures show the positioning times used to calculate the cycle time.
2. Positioning time means the time from the start of robot operation to the arrival at the target positioning point.
3. After the robot moves to and passes the target positioning point, vibration will be dampened and the robot positioned at the target positioning point as shown in Figure below. This vibration dampening time is not considered in the graph.

1. The vibration dampening time depends on factors such as the weight of the end-effector. If the robot is to be used in such a way that it overshoots or if the vibration damping time is of great concern, test the robot carefully beforehand.
2. If acceleration begins before residual vibration of the robot stops, an overcurrent error may be displayed. In this case, take one of the following measures:  
   Ｘ　Lower the deceleration of the preceding operation with a DECEL command to reduce residual vibration.  
   Ｘ　Keep the robot in stand-by with a DELAY command until residual vibration stops.  
   Ｘ　Lower acceleration with an ACCEL command.
3. Operate the robot with the optimum load setting in accordance with the end-effector weight and workpiece weight. If not, a robot failure may result.

# Stopping Time and Distance (Angle) at an Emergency Stop

Pressing the emergency stop button when the robot is in motion stops the robot, the stopping time required from activation of a stop signal and the distance (angle) for major three joints vary with the robot speed as shown in the graphs below. The measuring conditions are: Robot arm extended, 33%, 66% and 100% of the maximum payload.

Acceleration is different depend on the payload. Graphs below show the value of maximum stopping time and distance.

Stop all axis or power supply shuts down in 900ms.

# Setting the Control Set of Motion Optimization

The optimum speed or acceleration will vary depending upon the payload and center of gravity of an end-effector or workpiece that is to be set at the end of the robot flange. Set the payload and center of gravity position of the end-effector or workpiece and the control set of motion optimization according to the payload and robot posture.

For details, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Optimal Speed Control Function](001542.html)
".

For the operating procedure, refer to the FUNCTION GUIDE, "[Setting the Load Conditions](001547.html)
".

The mass of payload is a total mass of an end-effector and workpiece, expressed in grams.

Define the payload center of gravity in the TOOL0 coordinates in units of mm.

## 6Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 6axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 6th axis.

The Y component is defined on the orientation vector directed from the center of the flange to the center of the datum hole. The Z component is defined on the approach vector directed from the center of the flange to the normal line of the flange center. The X component is defined on the normal vector directed along the X axis (+) in the right-hand coordinates whose Y axis is an orientation vector and whose Z axis is an approach vector.

Datum hole is a pin hole which exists on the flange surface.

The size of datum hole differs depending on the robot types; φ6H7 for VM series, φ5H7 for other robots.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_1.png)

### Right Hand Coordinate System

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_2.png)

## 4-Axis Robots

TOOL 0 coordinates of the 4axis robot is defined as the illustration below.

The origin of the TOOL0 coordinates is located in the center of the flange surface on the 4th axis.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/000871_3.png)

# Limiting the Motion Range

## Outline

To prevent interference with other devices or entanglement of the end-effector wiring and piping, limit the motion range as needed by setting the mechanical ends for defining the "restricted space" and the software motion limits for defining the "motion space."

After changing the mechanical ends, change also the software motion limits so that the motion space comes within the restricted space.

# Changing RANG Values

A RANG value refers to an angle that determines the relationship between the reference position of the robot arm and the CALSET position, and is also called a reference angle or ready angle.

The factory defaults of RANG values for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd axes are obtained when each axis is in contact with the corresponding mechanical end configured at the time of shipment.

When CALSET is required but mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer cannot be removed so that the robot arm cannot take a posture in the CALSET position determined at the time of shipment, then it is necessary to change the RANG values stored in the controller to the ones obtained by the CALSET position determined by the mechanical stopper parts mounted by the customer.

If the RANG values are changed, the mechanical stop parts mounted by the customer influence the precision of CALSET.

###### 1

Move an axis whose RANG value is to be changed towards the mechanical end by manual operation in Joint mode and slowly press the axis against the mechanical end.

###### 2

Make a note of the RANG value of the corresponding axis in Joint mode which is shown in the current position.

###### 3

On the RANG window, change the current RANG value of the corresponding axis to the value of the note.  
For manner of operation, please refer to "[Manual Input Operation of RANG and CALSET Values](001757.html)"
of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

# Checking the Controller ON-Time and the Robot Running Time and Resetting Their User Counters

You may check the robot controller ON-time and the robot running time.  
Hours that you can check are the following items.

Refer to the "[Displaying System Information (Robot Tab)](001774.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Total operation | Shows the grand total of the robot controller ON-time counted after the controller leaves the factory. |
| Total running | Shows the grand total of the robot running time counted after the robot leaves the factory. |
| Cumu. operation | Shows the total of the robot controller ON-time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Cumu. running | Shows the total of the robot running time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Operation | Shows the ON-time of the robot controller counted after it is turned ON this time. |
| Running | Shows the running time of the robot counted after the robot controller is turned ON this time. |

Values of "Cumu. operation" and "Cumu. running" can be reset.

# Resetting Encoders

When an error occurs due to run-down encoder backup batteries, or due to a great impact to the robot during turning-off the controller, you need to reset encoders and perform CALSET work.

For the encoder resetting procedure, refer to the "[Setting and Changing Encoder](001751.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

In CALSET work, there are "CALSET" and "Recover CALSET data".  
If a motor is changed, execute "CALSET" and in other cases, execute "Recover CALSET data".

# Backing up Projects

You need to periodically back up project data in WINCAPSIII so that you can smoothly recover the robot controller in case of project data loss due to circumstances such as a controller failure.

Be sure to back up and preserve project data, particularly in the following cases:

* at the time of purchase
* after performing CALSET
* after changing RANG values
* after replacing a motor
* after updating robot controller data

DENSO preserves arm data configured at the time of shipment for 10 years. If your arm data is lost, contact our [Sales](001077.html) representatives.

Arm data refers to CALSET and RANG values in project data, which is unique to individual robots and determines the position of each joint.

# Product Warranty

## Warranty Information

In the event that a defect resulting from design, manufacture, or material is discovered in a robot, a controller, and their components (hereafter: product), and the defect is confirmed by us or a service dealer designated by us, we will repair the product free of charge (hereafter: warranty repair).  
 Warranty repair is performed by the replacement of related part and/or the repair.  
 In warranty repair, we will cover the costs associated with the following.

* Cost of parts
* Consumable items necessary for repair
* Labor

## Warranty Period

Warranty period shall be a period of 24 months from the shipment of the product.  
 However, even within the said period, the warranty shall be valid for a period of 18 months from the start of use, or up to 6,000 hours of operation (running) time, whichever comes earlier.

For all repairs after the warranty period is over, we will provide repair services at usual and customary rates.

## Replacement Product Warranty Period

Replacement of defective product originally installed in the equipment system pursuant to the warranty shall not extend the warranty period and the replacement product shall be warranted only for the balance of the warranty period remaining on the original product.

Even if the remaining warranty period for the product is ninety (90) days or less, its parts replaced by us or a service dealer designated by us shall be warranted for ninety (90) days from the day when the replacement is completed.

## Items Not Covered

* Failures, which arise from one of the following, shall not be covered by the warranty even if the product is within warranty period:

1. Failures caused by handling, improper programming, maintenance, inspection or installation other than those specified in the related manuals;
2. Failures caused by non-certified disassembling/repair;
3. Failures caused by disassembling/repair by non-authorized personnel;
4. Failures caused by improper modification by you or a third party, or failures caused by the use of any part, oil/grease or software other than those specified by DENSO WAVE;
5. A robot, a controller, a teach pendant, and a mini pendant
   for which a product serial number or production date cannot be confirmed;
6. Failures caused by a fire, salt damage, earthquake, storm/flood, lightning or other acts of God;
7. Failures due to use in an environment outside of the product specifications, such as improper IP rating, dirt/dust, fluid/coolant, improper power supply, high air pressure, and so on;
8. Damages or malfunctions caused by relocation or transportation after installation;
9. Items not covered in related manuals, such as;
- Failures caused by a worn-out consumable (e.g. natural discoloration of paint/plating, deterioration of consumable parts like fan filter);   
 - Failures with no effects on product quality or function (e.g. mechanical noise of controller, motor sound, reducer sound); and10. Products exposed to dangerous and hazardous materials.

* We charge for following costs regardless of the warranty period:

1. Shipping cost;
2. Travel and accommodation (T & A);
3. Maintenance, adjustment and cleaning;
4. Worn-out consumables and oil/grease (grease, battery, filter, bellows and others); and
5. Adjustment or recovery of internal data, such as programs and position variables, created and modified by the customer.

In no event shall we be liable for any other incidental or consequential damages, such as loss of profit, loss of production, psychological damage and damage to property other than our products resulting from product breakdown or failure.

## Warranty Coverage

This warranty is valid within the country where you purchased the product.  
 When transferring your robot to outside of the country of purchase, by doing the user registration of overseas transfer support from the following URL, your robot will be warranted just as in the country of purchase.

* URL of Overseas Transfer Support Registration page in our website

  <https://www.denso-wave.com/en/robot/support/afterservice/page3_2.html>

If your robot has not been registered in the overseas transfer support, you can send the robot back to our dealer in the country of purchase for repair. The transfer fee of your robot shall be paid by customers.

## Disclaimer

* Please contact your local DENSO Robotics sales office for specific questions pertaining to warranty coverage, as it may vary slightly from region to region.
* We continue to improve reliability and performance of our products, and therefore reserves the right to upgrade the product without prior warning.
* We take no responsibility for any erroneous information or errors in writing in this document.

The Serial number is a number for the robot unit and the controller that form a pair. Use a pair with the same number.

ID : 6280

# Installation of Encoder Backup Batteries

The two batteries have been removed before the shipment of the robot. Install the batteries in the power conversion box set according to the procedure shown below.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004996_0.jpg)

###### 1

Check that the robot controller power has been turned "OFF".

###### 2

Remove the four bolts and remove the cover of the power conversion box.

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004996_1.png)

Throw away the caution label "No battery contained".

###### 3

Connect the connector and install two batteries. Enclose the batteries in the case.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Tightening torque | 2.0 ± 0.4N･m |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/004996_2.png)

###### 4

Using the four bolts that were removed in STEP2, install the cover of the battery converion box to complete this procedure.

# Limiting the Motion Range

## Outline

To prevent interference with other devices or entanglement of the end-effector wiring and piping, limit the motion range as needed by setting the mechanical ends for defining the "restricted space" and the software motion limits for defining the "motion space."

After changing the mechanical ends, change also the software motion limits so that the motion space comes within the restricted space.

# Encoder Reset

When using the AC servo motor for the first time, you need to initialize the counter circuit in the encoder (encoder reset).

If any of the encoder system down errors 85404671 to 85404674 occurs or, while the controller power is OFF, an excessive impact applied to the motor causes any of the encoder overspeed errors 85404681 to 85404684, user need to reset encoders and perform CALSET.

For the encoder resetting procedure, refer to the "[Setting and Changing Encoder](001751.html)" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

## Operation Using a Teach Pendant

Set user level "Maintainer".

Operation path: [F2 Arm] - [F12 Maintenance] - [Encoder] - [Reset Encoder]

###### 1

The [Encoder Reset Setting] window is displayed.![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005010_1.png)

###### 2

Select [ON] or [OFF] of the axis to be reset and press [OK]. A system message for confirmation appears.![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005010_2.png)

###### 3

Press [OK] to reset the relevant encoder.

This is the end of encoder reset.

After encoder reset is complete, be sure to restart the robot controller.

# Intervals and Purposes of Maintenance and Inspection

Carry out the maintenance and inspection jobs at intervals listed in the table below.

Maintenance and inspection must be carried out by a trained person who possesses the ability to perform these tasks safely.

Before performing maintenance and inspection jobs, read "[Precautions while Robot is Running](001930.html)" and "[Daily and Periodical Inspections](001932.html)" in "[SAFETY PRECAUTIONS](001924.html)" in addition to this section.

| Intervals | Purposes |
| --- | --- |
| Daily Inspections | Inspection jobs to be performed every day to use the robot safely. |
| Quarterly Inspections | Inspection and maintenance jobs to be performed every three months to maintain the precision of the robot and prevent failures caused by overheat of the robot controller. |
| Biennial Inspections | Backup battery replacement to be performed every two years to retain the position data stored in the electronic absolute encoder built in the robot unit. For the transfer unit, check that the cableveyors are normal. |

# Daily Inspections

Before starting operations, check the items listed below every day. The following tables describe the inspection jobs to be performed with the controller power OFF and ON respectively.

Some repair and replacement jobs, shown in "What to do:" column in the tables below, may involve special work. Contact the [DENSO service representative](001078.html).

## Inspections to Be Made with the Power OFF

| Check: | How to check | Criterion | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Connectors (Controllers CN1 to CN10) and their destinations | Visually | No looseness, disengagement, or dirt | Engage the parts properly and clean them. |
| Cables (Controller CN1 to CN10) and robot external cables | Visually | Free of damage or gouges | Repair or replace the parts. |
| Robot unit (excluding lubricated parts) | Visually | No grease leak | Wipe off grease. |

## Inspections to Be Made with the Power ON

| Check: | How to check | Criterion | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LCD on the teach pendant | Visually | Properly displayed | Repair or replace the parts. |
| Pilot lamps on the robot controller | Visually | Should light up. | Repair or replace the parts. |
| Cooling fan in the robot controller | Hold up hand to the exhaust port and check that wind is coming out. | Should work properly. | Repair or replace the parts. |
| EMERGENCY STOP button on the teach pendant, the mini pendant or the emergency stop switch box | Press the EMERGENCY STOP button. | The robot should come to an emergency stop. | Repair or replace the parts. |
| Safety door | Operate the safety door switch and open the switch-wiring door. | The robot should come to an emergency stop. | Check or repair the parts. |

![](DensoRC8_manual_combined_images/005014_2.png)

###### 4

Using the four bolts that were removed in STEP2, install the cover of the battery converion box.

This is the end of replacement of encoder backup batteries.

# Checking the Controller ON-Time and the Robot Running Time and Resetting Their User Counters

You may check the robot controller ON-time and the robot running time.  
Hours that you can check are the following items.

Refer to the "[Displaying System Information (Robot Tab)](001774.html)
" of TEACH PENDANT OPERATION GUIDE.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Total operation | Shows the grand total of the robot controller ON-time counted after the controller leaves the factory. |
| Total running | Shows the grand total of the robot running time counted after the robot leaves the factory. |
| Cumu. operation | Shows the total of the robot controller ON-time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Cumu. running | Shows the total of the robot running time counted after you reset the user counter to zero. |
| Operation | Shows the ON-time of the robot controller counted after it is turned ON this time. |
| Running | Shows the running time of the robot counted after the robot controller is turned ON this time. |

Values of "Cumu. operation" and "Cumu. running" can be reset.

# Backup of Projects

Back up project data periodically in WINCAPSIII in order to recover the robot controller smoothly after loss of project data due to unexpected accidents such as expired service life of memory backup batteries.

Be sure to back up project data and preserve it, in particular:

* at the time of purchase
* after performing CALSET
* after changing RANG values
* after replacement of a motor
* after updating robot controller data.

Arm data refers to CALSET and RANG values in project data, which is unique to individual robots and determines the position of each axis.
